explanation: The A/P flare maneuver starts at approximately 50 feet RA and is completed at touchdown. FLARE (engaged): during a dual A/P ILS approach, flare engages at 50 feet radio altitude. · FCOM 4.20.17 / 4.20.6

question: After takeoff the autothrottle will remain in Throttle Hold (THR HLD) until 800 feet RA.
options: True
False
explanation: After takeoff the A/T remains in THR HLD until 800 feet above field elevation. Then the annunciation changes from THR HLD to ARM and reduction to climb thrust can be made by pushing the N1 switch. The FCOM wording is 'above field elevation'. · FCOM 4.20.11

question: During THR HLD (Throttle Hold), if you manually move the throttle levers, the A/T will try to return them to their original position.
options: True
False
explanation: THR HLD: the thrust lever autothrottle servos are inhibited; the pilot can set the thrust levers manually. The A/T will not move them back. · FCOM 4.20.5

question: In flight, with Autopilot engaged in CMD B, which FCC controls the logic for the flight directors on the Captain's PFD.
options: FMS A
FCC A
FCC B
FMS B
explanation: Master FCC: with one or both A/Ps engaged in CMD, the FCC for the first A/P in CMD is the master FCC, regardless of which F/D is turned on first. CMD B → FCC B is master and drives both F/Ds (MA light illuminated). · FCOM 4.20.3

question: The autopilot disengages automatically 2 seconds after touchdown.
options: True
False
explanation: It is the A/T that automatically disengages approximately 2 seconds after touchdown. The A/P must be manually disengaged after touchdown. · FCOM 4.20.17

question: The VOR/LOC mode must be armed before the second Autopilot can be selected during a duel channel autopilot approach.
options: True
False
explanation: For a dual A/P approach, APP mode must be selected, both VHF NAV receivers tuned to the ILS frequency, and the second A/P engaged in CMD prior to 800 feet RA. It is APP, not VOR/LOC, that enables the second A/P. · FCOM 4.20.15 / 4.10.15

question: What are the components of the Automatic Flight System (AFS)?
options: Autopilot, Autothrottle, and MCP Mode Selection System.
Flight Directors, Autothrottle, and MCP Mode Selection System
Autopilot Flight Director System and Autothrottle.
Autopilot Flight Director System, Autothrottle and MCP Mode Selector System.
explanation: The automatic flight system (AFS) consists of the autopilot flight director system (AFDS) and the autothrottle (A/T). · FCOM 4.20.1

question: What normally provides the N1 limits and target N1 values to the Autothrottle?
options: The Flight Management Computer.
The Autothrottle Computer.
The Flight Control Computers.
The Electronic Engine Controls (EECs).
explanation: The FMC provides N1 limits and target N1 for the A/T, and command airspeeds for the A/T and AFDS. · FCOM 4.20.1 / 4.20.8

question: For approach, what altitude must the second Autopilot be selected for duel Autopilot operation?
options: 800 feet RA
500 feet RA
350 feet RA
1500 feet RA
explanation: The second A/P must be engaged in CMD by 800 feet RA to execute a dual channel A/P approach; otherwise CMD engagement of the second A/P is inhibited. · FCOM 4.20.16 / 4.10.15

question: How many independent Flight Control Computers (FCCs) are there in the Autopilot Director System (AFDS)?
options: Three
One
Four, two for each channel
Two
explanation: The AFDS is a dual system consisting of two individual flight control computers (FCCs A and B) and a single mode control panel. · FCOM 4.20.1

question: If a landing is made with RTO selected:
options: Automatic braking occurs at the MAX level
Automatic braking action occurs at the RTO level
AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates 2 minutes after touchdown
AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates 2 seconds after touchdown
explanation: If a landing is made with RTO selected (selector not cycled through OFF), no automatic braking occurs and the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates two seconds after touchdown. · FCOM 14.20.5

question: If the autopilot ALT HOLD mode is manually overridden with control column pressure, which of the following occurs?
options: LNAV disengages
LEVEL CHANGE automatically engages
The autopilot changes to CWS P and returns to ALT HLD if control pressure released within 250 feet of selected altitude
The autopilot disengages
explanation: Ryanair fleet (YF501–YW164): column or wheel force override disengages the A/P (FCOM 4.20.2). The CWS P / 250 ft logic is YA573 only. · FCOM 4.20.8 / 4.10.18

question: If you engage Level Change by pressing the LVL CHG switch on the MCP and the green light illuminates, what other indications will occur as this mode engages?
options: Speed window opens to show target speed, MCP SPD annunciated for pitch mode, N1 or RETARD/ARM annunciated for thrust mode.
Speed window blanks, MCP SPD annunciated for pitch mode, N1 or RETARD/ARM annunciated for thrust mode.
Speed window opens to show target speed, MCP SPD annunciated for thrust mode, N1 annunciated for pitch mode.
Speed window blanks, MCP SPD annunciated for pitch mode, N1 annunciated for thrust mode.
explanation: LVL CHG push: switch light illuminates; pitch mode annunciates MCP SPD; A/T annunciates N1 for climb, or RETARD then ARM for descent. The IAS/MACH display shows the target speed. · FCOM 4.10.8

question: In flight below 2000 feet RA, on an ILS Autopilot approach with flare armed, what happens if you push a TO/GA switch once?
options: Autothrottle will disengage, and ARM is dispalyed in FMA.
Autopilot will disengage, and CWS P will annunciate.
Autothrottle advances thrust levers to full Go-Around N1.
Autothrottle advances thrust levers to reduced Go-Around N1.
explanation: First TO/GA push below 2000 ft RA with FLARE armed (dual A/P): A/P go-around engages, and thrust advances toward the REDUCED go-around N1 (1000–2000 fpm climb). The second push gives full GA N1. The A/P does NOT disengage in a dual-channel A/P go-around, so the 'A/P disengages / CWS P' answer in one bank is wrong. · FCOM 4.20.21 / 4.20.23

question: In the IAS/MACH Display, to the left of the displayed figure, what does a flashing "A" indicate?
options: Overspeed limiting, Minimum speed for current flap setting cannot be achieved.
Overspeed limiting, current speed selection greater than current flap setting limit.
Underspeed limiting, Vmo or Mmo limit.
Underspeed limiting, FMC or selected speed can not be reached.
explanation: MCP speed condition symbols: flashing 'A' = underspeed limiting, the minimum speed (commanded speed) cannot be reached. A flashing '8' = overspeed limiting (Vmo/Mmo, flap or gear placard). · FCOM 4.10.2

question: Landing auto brake setting may be selected after touchdown:
options: Auto break action will occur only after both thrust levers are retarded to idle
Prior to decelerating through 30 knots groundspeed
However, the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light will illuminate and auto break application will not occur
After decelerating through 30 knots groundspeed
explanation: Landing autobrake settings may be selected after touchdown prior to decelerating through 30 kts of ground speed. · FCOM 14.20.5

question: Other than by selecting N1 mode by pressing the N1 switch on the MCP, when else will N1 mode automatically engage.
options: LVL CHG and VNAV engaged within first 2.5 minutes after takeoff.
Never, N1 mode is only ever manually selected and engaged.
LVL CHG engaged in climb more than 2.5 minutes after takeoff.
VNAV engaged in climb and LVL CHG engaged in climb more than 2.5 minutes after takeoff.
explanation: N1 mode engages automatically when engaging LVL CHG in climb (except during the 2 1/2 minute inhibit period after lift-off) and when engaging VNAV in climb. · FCOM 4.10.3

question: The Autothrottle (A/T) system, provides automatic thrust control from the start of takeoff, through all stages of flight to up to and including landing.
options: True
False
explanation: The A/T system provides automatic thrust control from the start of takeoff through climb, cruise, descent, approach and go-around or landing. · FCOM 4.20.8

question: Two independent radio altimeters provide radio altitude to the respective FCC's. With one radio altimeter inoperative:
options: the autopilot will disconnect two seconds after LOC and GS capture
the autopilot will continue to command the aircraft down to minimums
nothing out of the ordinary will occur
the autopilot will disconnect as soon as the failure is detected
explanation: With a radio altimeter inoperative, the autopilot will disengage two seconds after LOC and GS capture. · FCOM 4.20.3

question: What components make up the Automatic Flight System (AFS)?
options: Autopilot, MCP mode selector system, autothrottles.
Autothrottles and autopilot flight director system.
Flight directors, MCP mode selector system, autothrottles.
AFDS, MCP mode selector system, autothrottles.
explanation: AFS = autopilot flight director system (AFDS) + autothrottle (A/T). · FCOM 4.20.1

question: What does an illuminated green light mean in the MCP buttons?
options: That switch can be de-selected.
That mode is currently engaged and active.
The switch is available to be selected.
That mode is currently de-selected and inactive.
explanation: MCP mode selector switches: the switch illuminates to indicate mode selection and that the mode can be deselected by pushing the switch again. While a mode is active, deselection can be inhibited, shown by the switch light extinguishing. · FCOM 4.20.1

question: What happens when TO/GA is pressed once on an ILS Autopilot approach with FLARE armed?
options: Autopilot disengages and the Flight Directors re-cycle to give a FD Go-Around.
Autothrottle advanced the thrust levers to full Go-Around thrust.
Autothrottle advanced the thrust levers to reduced Go-Around N1.
The autothrottle disengages and THR HLD annunciates in the FMA.
explanation: With FLARE armed (dual A/P ILS), the first TO/GA push engages A/P go-around and the A/T advances toward reduced go-around N1 (1000–2000 fpm). The second push (after reaching reduced GA thrust) gives the full go-around N1 limit. · FCOM 4.20.21 / 4.20.23

question: What pitch mode is annunciated in the FMA after takeoff when the autopilot is first engaged in CMD?
options: CWS P
V NAV
MCP SPD
V/S
explanation: Engaging an A/P in CMD after takeoff: CMD replaces FD and pitch engages in LVL CHG; the pitch mode FMA shows MCP SPD. · FCOM 4.20.12

question: Which A/T modes permit manual thrust changes without A/T interference?
options: N1 and ARM
THR HLD only
THR HLD and ARM
GA and ARM
explanation: THR HLD: thrust lever servos inhibited, the pilot can set the thrust levers manually. ARM: no A/T mode engaged, servos inhibited, manual thrust setting (minimum speed protection provided). · FCOM 4.20.5

question: Why do we check that FLARE mode is armed at 500 feet RA?
options: To allow APP mode to be selected at this point if FLARE not armed.
To allow start of the flare manoeuvre at 350 feet RA.
To allow the second A/P to be engaged at this point.
To be aware that A/P will disengage at 350 feet RA if not armed.
explanation: If FLARE is not armed by approximately 350 feet RA, both A/Ps automatically disengage. Checking FLARE armed by 500 ft RA confirms the approach will continue to autoland. · FCOM 4.20.17

question: With VNAV engaged, pushing the SPD INTV switch has what effect?
options: IAS/MACH window blanks and next FMC speed restriction becomes active, magenta target speed displayed above speed tape on PFD.
IAS/MACH window opens up showing current FMC target speed, and IAS/MACH selector can be used to set new desired speed.
Current or next speed restriction deleted from FMC, IAS/MACH window opens up showing previous FMC target speed, and IAS/MACH selector can be used to set new desired speed.
No effect, VNAV remains enagaged with the FMC controlling target speed.
explanation: SPD INTV with VNAV engaged: the IAS/MACH display opens showing the current FMC target speed (FMC speed intervention active), and the IAS/MACH selector can set a new speed. VNAV remains engaged. · FCOM 4.10.4 / SP.4.3

question: A DUCT OVERHEAT light only will cause:
options: The temperature mix valves to drive full cold
The temperature mix valves to drive full hot
An automatic shutdown of the pack
A BLEED TRIP OFF
explanation: DUCT OVERHEAT light: distribution air temperature in the related duct exceeds limit; air mix valves drive full cold; requires reset. (PACK TRIP OFF is the one that closes the pack valve.) · FCOM 2.10.6 / 2.30.5

question: After lift-off, the A/T remains in THR HLD until:
options: 400 feet RA
400 feet RA or 18 seconds after takeoff
800 feet RA
800 feet RA or 18 seconds after takeoff
explanation: The A/T remains in THR HLD until 800 feet above field elevation, then changes to ARM. · FCOM 4.20.11

question: Antenna switching from tail antenna to nose antenna occurs when:
options: LOC frequency is selected and VOR/LOC is armed or engaged
VOR frequency is selected and VOR/LOC is armed or engaged
VOR frequency is selected only
LOC frequency is selected only
explanation: When a localizer frequency is selected, the VHF NAV radios automatically switch from the tail antenna to the nose antenna when VOR/LOC is annunciated (armed or engaged). · FCOM 4.10.14

question: At what altitude will both A/Ps automatically disengage if FLARE is not armed during an ILS dual channel approach:
options: 50 feet RA
Will not disengage
350 feet RA
500 feet RA
explanation: If FLARE is not armed by approximately 350 feet RA, both A/Ps automatically disengage. · FCOM 4.20.17

question: Autopilot trim and main stabiliser trim use:
options: Hydraulic trim motor from hydraulic system A
Single electric trim motor
Hydraulic trim motor from hydraulic system B
Separate electric trim motors
explanation: The STAB TRIM MAIN ELECT and AUTOPILOT cutout switches allow the autopilot or main electric trim inputs to be disconnected from the stabilizer trim motor. Both use the same single electric trim motor. · FCOM 9.20.7

question: Below which RA should FLARE mode be armed during AUTOLAND?
options: 50 feet RA.
350 feet RA.
350 feet AGL.
explanation: FLARE (armed): during a dual A/P ILS approach, FLARE is displayed after LOC and G/S capture and below 1500 feet RA; the second A/P couples and A/P go-around arms. · FCOM 4.20.6

question: During AUTO LAND at which radio altitude should the flare mode be engaged?
options: 150 ft
50 ft
200 ft
300 ft
explanation: FLARE engages at 50 feet radio altitude during a dual A/P ILS approach. · FCOM 4.20.6 / 4.20.17

question: If rejecting a takeoff with the autothrottle engaged, what could be a consequence of retarding the thrust levers at the early stages of the takeoff before THR HLD is annunciated on the FMA?
options: In the event of a single engine failure, the autothrottle will command full EGT limited thrust on the remaining engine whilst below Vmcg
The autobrakes will engage, but the spoilers will not deploy
The aircraft will suffer a tailstrike
If you don't disengage the autothrottle and remove your hand from the thrust levers, the autothrottle will push the levers forward again to the takeoff N1
explanation: Before THR HLD (84 kt) the A/T is in N1 mode and repositions the thrust levers to takeoff N1 after manual movement (servos only inhibited in THR HLD/ARM). In an early RTO, disengage the A/T or the levers will advance again. · FCOM 4.20.11 / 4.20.5 / 4.20.8

question: If the thrust lever(s) are advanced after touchdown:
options: The AUTO BRAKE DISARM light will not illuminate
The AUTO BRAKE SELECT switch will move to OFF
After 3 seconds in the advanced position the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light will illuminate
The AUTO BRAKE DISARM light will illuminate immediately
explanation: After braking has started, advancing the forward thrust lever(s) disarms the autobrake and illuminates AUTO BRAKE DISARM, EXCEPT during the first 3 seconds after touchdown for landing. · FCOM 14.20.5

question: Mach trim system provides speed stability at airspeeds above:
options: Mach .455
Mach .505
Mach .555
Mach .615
explanation: Mach trim is automatically accomplished above Mach .615 by adjusting the elevators with respect to the stabilizer as speed increases. · FCOM 9.20.7

question: Normally, N1 limits and target N1 values are provided to the A/T by the:
options: A/T computer
FCCs
Flight Management Computer (FMC)
IRUs
explanation: The FMC provides N1 limits and target N1 for the A/T, and command airspeeds for the A/T and AFDS. · FCOM 4.20.1

question: The Automatic Flight System (AFS) consists of:
options: The autopilots (A/P) and the flight directors (F/D) only
The flight directors (F/D) and the autothrottles (A/T) only
The autothrottles (A/T) and the autopilots (A/P) only
The autopilot flight directors (AFDS) and the autothrottles (A/T)
explanation: The AFS consists of the autopilot flight director system (AFDS) and the autothrottle (A/T). · FCOM 4.20.1

question: Under speed limiting (flashing A) appears:
options: Minimum speed for current flap setting cannot be reached
The highest of all the answers
When the speed is less than 1.3 VS for current flap setting
FMC speed or selected speed cannot be reached
explanation: MCP speed condition symbols appear when the commanded speed cannot be reached. Underspeed limiting (flashing 'A') = minimum speed. The FCOM says only 'minimum speed'; the bank's 'highest of all' means the limiting minimum speed (the highest of the minimum-speed values). Odd wording. · FCOM 4.10.2

question: VNAV is terminated by:
options: LOC capture
selecting HDG SEL
selecting a different pitch mode
selecting LNAV
explanation: VNAV mode is terminated by selecting another pitch mode or by glideslope capture. · FCOM 4.10.6

question: What are the indications for A/T disconnected.
options: A/T P/RST disenage light illuminates steady.
A/T P/RST disengage light flashes.
Tone sounds and A/T P/RST disengage light flashes
Tone sounds and A/T P/RST disengage light illuminates steady
explanation: A/T Disengage light flashing red = autothrottle has disengaged (steady = light test). There is no aural tone for A/T disengagement; pushing an A/T disengage switch again extinguishes the lights. · FCOM 4.10.22 / 4.10.20

question: What does a flashing "A" displayed to the left of the selected MCP speed indicate?
options: limiting for maximum speed for current flap setting.
Underspeed limiting, FMC speed or MCP selected speed cannot be reached.
Overspeeed limiting at Mmo limit
Overspeed limititing at Vmo Limit
explanation: Flashing 'A' = underspeed limiting (minimum speed): the commanded (FMC or MCP) speed cannot be reached. Flashing '8' = overspeed limiting (Vmo/Mmo, gear or flap limit). · FCOM 4.10.2

question: What happens with the IAS/MACH display on the MCP if SPD INTV switch is pushed during VNAV operation:
options: IAS/MACH displays opens up and shows dashes
IAS/MACH displays opens up and shows 100 kts
IAS/MACH displays opens up and shows slashes
IAS/MACH displays opens up and show FMC target speed
explanation: SPD INTV with VNAV engaged: the IAS/MACH display opens showing the current FMC target speed, which can then be changed with the selector. · FCOM 4.10.4 / SP.4.3

question: What is the minimum altitude (AGL) for selecting CMD on the second autopilot execute an ILS dual channel A/P approach?
options: 800 feet
1500 feet
2000 feet
500 feet
explanation: The second A/P must be engaged in CMD by 800 feet RA to execute a dual channel A/P approach; otherwise CMD engagement of the second A/P is inhibited. · FCOM 4.20.16

question: What will cause the A/T to disengage?
options: Move A/T ARM switch to OFF, Push Either A/T Disengage switch and An A/T system fault is detected
Immediately the left main landing gear is compressed, Push Either A/T Disengage switch and Move A/T ARM switch to OFF.
Push Either A/T Disengage switch and Move A/T ARM switch to OFF
Push Either A/T Disengage switch and An A/T system fault is detected
explanation: A/T disengages by: A/T Arm switch to OFF, pushing either A/T Disengage switch, an A/T system fault, two seconds after landing touchdown, or thrust lever split/override conditions. · FCOM 4.20.10

question: Which of the following occurs when a TO/GA switch is pressed once below 2000 feet radio altitude for a automatic go-around from an ILS channel A/P approach and FLARE armed?
options: The autothrottle advances thrust levers to reduced go-around N1
N1 mode is displayed on the FMA
The autopilot disengages
The autothrottle advances thrust levers to full go-around N1
explanation: First TO/GA push below 2000 ft RA (dual A/P, FLARE armed): A/T engages in GA (FMA shows GA) and thrust advances toward the REDUCED go-around N1 (1000–2000 fpm). The A/P remains engaged. · FCOM 4.20.21

question: Which statement is true regarding aileron trim?
options: The aileron trim never directly affects the position of the control wheel
The amount of trim is always displayed on the scale, regardless of the autopilot state
If the autopilot is engaged, the amount of trim is not indicated on the scale
If the autopilot is engaged, any changes in trim will directly affect the control wheel position
explanation: If aileron trim is used with the autopilot engaged, the trim is not reflected in the control wheel position: the autopilot overpowers the trim and holds the control wheel where required for lateral control. · FCOM 9.20.3

question: With A/T engaged, what condition could cause the throttles to be separated (not aligned).
options: One EEC in ON, one EEC in ALTN.
One engine A/T suffering a system fault.
Throttle stagger cannot occur with A/T engaged as both throttle servo motors work identically to position the throttles symetrically.
Both EECs in ALTN.
explanation: The A/T operates with EECs ON or ALTN. It is recommended that both EECs be ON or both in ALTN, as this produces minimum thrust lever separation. One ON and one ALTN gives lever stagger. · FCOM 4.20.8

question: A magenta bug on the vertical speed indicator in the PFD indicates:
options: actual vertical speed
selected vertical speed on the MCP panel with V/S pitch mode selected
indicates vertical speed in VNAV mode
electrical power loss to the indicator
explanation: Selected vertical speed bug (magenta): indicates the speed selected in the MCP vertical speed window with V/S pitch mode engaged. · FCOM 10.11.25

question: Above what bank angle will the wings not roll level when control wheel pressure is released during CWS roll operation?
options: 8 degrees
10 degrees
12 degrees
6 degrees
explanation: CWS: when control pressure is released the A/P holds the existing attitude. If aileron pressure is released with 6 degrees or less of bank, the A/P rolls wings level and holds the existing heading. · FCOM 4.10.19

question: After a normal takeoff with sufficient rate of climb achieved, which F/D pitch command can you expect?
options: V2 to V2 plus 20kts
V2 to V2 plus 15kts
V2 plus 20kts
V2
explanation: After lift-off the pitch command stays at 15° until a sufficient climb rate is acquired, then commands MCP speed (normally V2) plus 20 knots. · FCOM 4.20.11 / 4.20.5

question: After takeoff, the Autothrottle remains in Throttle Hold (THR HLD) until which point?
options: 400ft AGL
800ft Above Aerodrome Level
1200ft Barometric Altitude
1000ft above MSA
explanation: The A/T remains in THR HLD until 800 feet above field elevation, then ARM. · FCOM 4.20.11

question: An altitude restriction is entered at the top of descent, the aircraft will not now follow the Idle Descent path but will descend to meet the altitude restriction.  After achieving the altitude restriction which of the indicated flight paths will the aircraft follow for the rest of the decent?
options: Descends to achieve restriction then descends at 1000 fpm until intercepting original idle descent path. (B)
Descends to achieve restriction then maintains level flight until intercepts the original idle descent path. (A)
Descends to achieve restriction, then continues steady descent to End of Descent. (C)
None of the options
explanation: After the first 'at' or 'at or below' restriction, the path angle is level until intercepting the idle thrust descent path to the next altitude-constrained waypoint. (Picture question; the figure label is (A).) · FCOM 11.31.23

question: As you push the TO/GA switch for an automatic go around, what is the correct FMA announciation? (Thrust : Roll : Pitch)
options: N1 : : TO/GA
N1 : LNAV : TO/GA
GA : : TO/GA
GA : HDG SEL : MCP SPD
explanation: A/P go-around (no TOGA-to-LNAV): A/T FMA = GA, pitch = TO/GA, and the roll annunciation is blank (go-around track hold). · FCOM 4.20.21 / 4.20.24

question: As you push the TO/GA switch for an automatic go-around on an aircraft with the TOGA to LNAV feature fitted, what are the correct FMA annunciations (Thrust Mode : Roll Mode : Pitch Mode)?
options: GA : LNAV : MCP SPD
GA : LNAV armed (white) : TO/GA
MCP SPD : (blank) : GA
N1 : VOR/LOC : TO/GA
explanation: With TOGA to LNAV: when a missed approach exists in the flight plan, LNAV arm (white) is annunciated on the FMA. The go-around shows GA : LNAV (armed) : TO/GA, and LNAV engages above 50 ft (F/D) / 400 ft. · FCOM 4.20.25 / 4.20.27

question: Autothrottle disconnect indications
options: A/T disengage lights flash red (no aural); push a disengage switch again to extinguish
Aural wailer and steady red A/T light
Steady amber A/T light and master caution
Only the FMA A/T mode blanks; no lights
explanation: A/T Disengage light (red): flashing = autothrottle has disengaged; steady red/amber only with the test switch held. A second push of the A/T disengage switch extinguishes the lights. There is no aural for A/T disconnect (unlike the A/P wailer). · FCOM 4.10.22 / 4.10.20

question: Autothrottle: flashing "A" on the FMC/speed window
options: Underspeed limiting / alpha floor – minimum speed (commanded speed cannot be reached)
Overspeed limiting – Vmo/Mmo, gear or flap limit
Autothrottle disengaged
FMC speed intervention active
explanation: Flashing 'A' in the MCP speed window = underspeed limiting (minimum speed). Alpha floor: if speed drops below minimum, the PFD shows MCP SPD, the MCP shows the 'A', and the A/T advances thrust to 5 kt above minimum speed, then removes the 'A'. Only active in non-VNAV modes. · FCOM 4.10.2 / 4.20.9

question: Can the pilot move the thrust levers manually in THR HLD? (true/false)
options: True
False
explanation: True. THR HLD: the thrust lever autothrottle servos are inhibited; the pilot can set the thrust levers manually. · FCOM 4.20.5

question: During a single autopilot approach and landing, a single press of either TO/GA switch in response to a Go-around will result in which of the following situations?
options: The A/P Go-around is only available after the second push of the TO/GA switch
Automatic A/P Go-around occurs after FLARE armed annunciates
A manual F/D Go-around is available
An A/P Go-around will automatically engage
explanation: In single A/P operation, automatic flare/touchdown and A/P go-around are not available. An A/P go-around requires dual A/P (armed when FLARE armed is annunciated); otherwise a manual F/D go-around is available. · FCOM 4.20.2 / 4.20.21

question: During a single engine F/D go-around, F/D pitch commands ____ degrees nose up. As climb rate increases, F/D pitch commands maintain a target speed
options: 10 degrees
15 degrees
8 degrees
13 degrees
explanation: Single engine F/D go-around: F/D pitch commands 13 degrees nose up; as climb rate increases, F/D pitch commands maintain a target speed. · FCOM 4.20.25

question: During takeoff with F/D ON, the AFDS commands pitch attitude ____ degrees after ____ IAS
options: 10 degrees nose up & 60 kt IAS
15 degrees nose up & 60 kt IAS
10 degrees nose up & 84 kt IAS
15 degrees nose up & 84 kt IAS
explanation: TO/GA takeoff pitch: 10° nose down until 60 KIAS, 15° nose up after 60 KIAS, 15° after lift-off until a sufficient climb rate, then MCP speed + 20 kt. · FCOM 4.20.5

question: During taxiing out for takeoff, the amber AUTO BRAKE DISARM Light illuminates. What should you do?
options: Position the AUTO BRAKE select switch to OFF and then reselect RTO. If the DISARM re-illuminates, use manual brakes
Position ANTISKID Switch to OFF
Nothing, this is normal
Position the AUTO BRAKE select switch to OFF. Do not attempt to takeoff if light remains illuminated
explanation: AUTO BRAKE DISARM illuminates (other than the 1–2 s flash when RTO is selected) when a malfunction exists in the automatic braking system. The NNC action (select OFF; do not take off if the light stays illuminated) is in the QRH, not the FCOM. · FCOM 14.10.4

question: Engaging LVL CHG or VNAV climb modes automatically engages the A/T N1 mode
options: False
True
explanation: True: engaging LVL CHG or VNAV climb modes automatically engages the A/T N1 mode (LVL CHG climb N1 is inhibited for 2 1/2 min after lift-off). Descent modes engage RETARD then ARM. · FCOM 4.20.9

question: How can you extinguish the flashing "A" symbol if it appears before a speed that you have selected in the MCP IAS/MACH window?
options: Select a speed at least 15kt greater than the minimum speed
Select CMD B
Retard the thrust levers
Push the selector knob in.
explanation: The commanded limit speed and MCP speed condition symbol remain until another speed is selected that does not exceed the limit. A speed 15 knots greater than the minimum speed must be selected to remove the underspeed limiting symbol. · FCOM 4.20.29

question: If an altitude restriction is entered before TOD, the aircraft will commence the descent early to follow a new idle descent path to achieve the descent restriction.  If ALT INTV is then selected after the descent restriction, which of the paths will the aircraft follow?
options: Path A.  Descends to achieve restriction then maintains level flight until intercepts the original idle descent path.
Path C.  Descends to achieve restriction, then continues steady descent to End of Descent.
Path D.  Descends to achieve restriction, then continues on that new idle descent path until new commands are entered.
Path B.  Descends to achieve restriction then descends at 1000 fpm until intercepting original idle descent path.
explanation: Picture question. ALT INTV during VNAV descent deletes the highest constraint above the MCP altitude; if at that constraint, the airplane continues descent. Early descent: VNAV commands about 1000 fpm until the idle path is intercepted. This matches the bank's Path B. · FCOM 4.10.11 / 11.31.28

question: If an engine failure occurs during takeoff, the pitch command target speed is?
options: V2+20, if airspeed is above V2+20
Existing speed, if airspeed is between V2 & V2+20
V2, if airspeed is below V2
All of the above
explanation: Engine failure after lift-off: pitch target is V2 if airspeed is below V2; existing speed if between V2 and V2+20; V2+20 if above V2+20. · FCOM 4.20.11

question: In normal operation, what provides the Autothrottle system with N1 limit values?
options: FMC
ADIRU's
Autothrottle computer
AFDS
explanation: In normal operation the FMC provides the A/T system with N1 limit values. (A/T LIM light = the FMC is not providing N1 limits; a degraded limit from the EEC is used.) · FCOM 4.20.8

question: In the 'ARM' autothrottle mode, the thrust lever autothrottle servos maintain thrust at the selected N1 limit displayed on the thrust mode display
options: False
True
explanation: False. ARM: no autothrottle mode engaged; the thrust lever servos are inhibited and the pilot sets thrust manually (minimum speed protection provided). Holding the selected N1 limit is the N1 mode. · FCOM 4.20.5

question: In the IAS/MACH Display to the left of the displayed figure, what does a flashing character "B" indicate?
options: Overspeed limiting, current speed selection greater than current flap setting limit.
Autopilot B is engaged
Underspeed limiting, current speed selection is below minimum speed
There is a fault in the Autopilot and Flight Director system
explanation: The character is really a flashing '8' = overspeed limiting: Vmo/Mmo limit, landing gear limit or flap limit. · FCOM 4.10.3

question: L NAV will automatically disengage:
options: Upon glidescope capture
When HDG SEL is disengaged
When VNAV is engaged
Reaching a route discontinuity
explanation: LNAV automatically disconnects on: reaching the end of the active route, a route discontinuity, intercepting a selected approach course in VOR LOC or APP (VOR/LOC armed), selecting HDG SEL, or loss of capture criteria. · FCOM 4.10.13

question: LNAV terminates when
options: All of the above are correct
Aircraft is not within LNAV capture criteria
HDG SEL mode is engaged
Upon VOR or localizer capture
explanation: LNAV disconnects on end of route, route discontinuity, intercepting the VOR/LOC course (VOR LOC/APP), selecting HDG SEL, or loss of capture criteria. All the listed options apply. · FCOM 4.10.13

question: LVL CHG: FMA indications
options: Pitch: MCP SPD; A/T: N1 in climb, RETARD then ARM in descent
Pitch: N1; A/T: MCP SPD
Pitch: LVL CHG; A/T: FMC SPD
Pitch: V/S; A/T: MCP SPD
explanation: LVL CHG push: switch light illuminates; pitch mode annunciates MCP SPD; the autothrottle annunciates N1 for climb and RETARD followed by ARM for descent. · FCOM 4.10.8

question: Minimum speed reversion is also available when the A/T is OFF and the AFDS is in ALT HOLD or after G/S capture
options: False
True
explanation: False. Minimum speed reversion is NOT available when the A/T is OFF and the AFDS is in ALT HOLD or after G/S capture, nor in VNAV PTH on a level segment. · FCOM 4.20.30

question: Moving the autopilot Stabilizer Trim Cutout Switch to the CUTOUT position will disengage the autopilot?
options: True
False
explanation: True. Moving the STAB TRIM AUTOPILOT cutout switch to CUTOUT deactivates autopilot stabilizer trim and disengages the autopilot. · FCOM 4.20.2 / 9.10.6

question: The A/T is controlled by FCC A only.
options: True
False
explanation: False: the A/T has its own autothrottle computer (FCOM 11.20.7 schematic); the AFS = AFDS (FCC A and B) + A/T (4.20.1). · FCOM 4.20.1 / 4.20.3

question: The airplane can be flown in the CWS mode even through the autopilot is engaged in CMD
options: True
False
explanation: True. With an A/P in CMD, overriding pitch/roll with control force reverts that axis to CWS P / CWS R (shown on the FMA). CWS R is also usable to intercept a VOR/LOC course with the A/P in CMD. · FCOM 4.20.7 / 4.20.4

question: The airplane is in level flight at the selected altitude with ALT HOLD engaged. Changing the MCP altitude by at least 100 feet, arms the V/S mode
options: False
True
explanation: True. V/S becomes armed if the pitch mode is ALT HOLD at the selected MCP altitude and a new MCP altitude more than 100 ft from current is selected. V/S then engages by moving the thumbwheel. · FCOM 4.10.10 / 4.10.9

question: The autopilot cannot be engaged while force is applied to the control wheel?
options: True
False
explanation: True. A/P engagement requires that no force is being applied to the control wheel and the STAB TRIM AUTOPILOT cutout switch is at NORMAL. · FCOM 4.20.2

question: The autopilot disengages if FLARE mode is not armed by?
options: 400 ft
350 ft
50 ft
125 ft
explanation: If FLARE is not armed by approximately 350 feet RA, both A/Ps automatically disengage. · FCOM 4.20.17

question: The autopilot flare maneuver starts at approximately ____ feet RA and is completed at touchdown
options: 50 feet
27 feet
100 feet
35 feet
explanation: The A/P flare maneuver starts at approximately 50 feet RA and is completed at touchdown (A/T retard from about 27 ft RA). · FCOM 4.20.17

question: The autothrottle will disengage 2 seconds after touchdown.
options: True
False
explanation: True. The A/T automatically disengages approximately 2 seconds after touchdown; the A/T disengage lights do not illuminate for this automatic disengagement. · FCOM 4.20.17 / 4.20.10

question: The N1 limits and target N1 values are normally provided to the Autothrottle from where?
options: Autothrottle Computer.
Flight Control Computers.
Flight Management Computer.
Electronic Engine Control Computers.
explanation: The FMC provides N1 limits and target N1 for the A/T. · FCOM 4.20.1

question: The ND Wind direction/speed and wind arrow is:
options: Blanked if wind speed becomes less than 6 knots
Displayed in only in ND MAP mode
Displayed if wind speed is greater than 6 knots
Displayed only in ILS mode
explanation: ND wind direction/speed and arrow: displayed if wind magnitude is greater than 6 knots, and blanked if it drops below 4 knots. · FCOM 10.41.4

question: Trimming the stabilizer with the electrical trim switch on the control wheel disengages the autopilot.
options: True
False
explanation: True. Activating either pilot's control wheel trim switch disengages the A/P. · FCOM 4.20.2

question: What happens if a persistent localizer/glideslope anomaly or ground station failure is detected during a single channel or F/D only approach?
options: The autopilot will only disengage below 2000ft
The autopilot will disengage and/or the F/D bars will be removed
The heading and pitch modes will change to HDG SEL and V/S
The autopilot will remain engaged
explanation: For a single channel or F/D-only approach, the autopilot will disengage and/or the F/D bars will be removed if a persistent localizer/glideslope beam anomaly or ground station failure is detected. · FCOM 4.20.18

question: What happens if you reject a takeoff at 100 knots with Autobrakes in RTO?
options: Automatic speed brake deployment when thrust levers are retarded to idle
Automatic braking when reverse thrust selected
Automatic braking when thrust levers are retracted to idle
AUTO BRAKE DISARM light will illuminate
explanation: RTO: automatically applies maximum brake pressure when the thrust levers are retarded to idle at or above 88 knots wheel speed. Below 88 kt autobraking is not initiated and RTO stays armed. · FCOM 14.10.4 / 14.20.4

question: What will cause the A/T to disengage?
options: Pushing either Autothrottle Disengage switch, moving the A/T ARM switch to OFF or an Autothrottle system fault is detected.
The stick shaker is activated
Immediately the left main landing gear is compressed
Moving the A/T ARM switch to ON
explanation: A/T disengages by: A/T Arm switch to OFF, pushing either A/T Disengage switch, an A/T system fault, two seconds after landing, or thrust lever split/override conditions. · FCOM 4.20.10

question: When do the Autothrottle and Autopilot disengage (if applicable) after touchdown?
options: Autothrottle and Autopilot both disengage immediately on touchdown.
Autothrottle and Autopilot both disengage 2 sec after touchdown.
Autothrottle disengages 2 sec after touchdown. The Autopilot must be manually disengaged after touchdown.
Both must be disengaged manually after touchdown.
explanation: The A/T automatically disengages approximately 2 seconds after touchdown. The A/P must be manually disengaged after touchdown; roll-out is flown manually. · FCOM 4.20.17

question: When performing an autopilot ILS approach, the glide slope can be captured from above or below?
options: False
True
explanation: True. Glideslope capture is inhibited prior to localizer capture. The G/S can be captured from above or below; capture occurs at 2/5 dot. · FCOM 4.20.16

question: Which is the correct mode on the FMA? Condition: After takeoff, A/P engaged, before flaps up. (Thrust: Roll: Pitch)
options: N1 : LNAV : MCP SPD
N1 : LNAV : FMC SPD
ARM : HDG SELECT : VNAV PTH
THR HLD : HDG SELECT : MCP SPD
explanation: Engaging the A/P after takeoff (before VNAV): pitch engages in LVL CHG (MCP SPD), the A/T is in N1 (after pushing N1 at thrust reduction), and the roll mode is LNAV if armed/engaged. · FCOM 4.20.12 / 4.20.13 / 4.20.14

question: Which mode must be armed before the second autopilot can be selected?
options: LNAV
VNAV
VOR LOC
APP
explanation: The APP mode permits selecting the second A/P to engage in CMD; this arms it for automatic engagement after LOC and G/S capture and below 1500 RA. · FCOM 4.20.15

question: Which of the following occurs when a TO/GA switch is pressed below 2000 feet RA for a flight director go-around from a single autopilot ILS approach?
options: GA mode of the Flight Director engages
All the above are correct
The autothrottle advances thrust levers to reduced go-around N1
The autopilot disengages
explanation: Single A/P below 2000 ft RA: pushing TO/GA disengages the A/P (4.20.2), the F/D go-around engages (TO/GA pitch), and the A/T (if armed) engages GA toward reduced go-around N1. All of the listed options occur. · FCOM 4.20.2 / 4.20.21

question: With LNAV armed on the ground, at what altitude will it engage?
options: Passing 400 feet AGL
50 feet RA
800 feet RA
LNAV is manually selected once above 3000 feet with flaps up no lights
explanation: LNAV (armed): the AFDS is armed prior to takeoff to engage LNAV at 50 feet RA. (For a go-around with the TOGA-to-LNAV feature, LNAV engages above 400 ft RA.) · FCOM 4.20.6

question: The volume of received communications can be controlled by rotating the selected RECEIVER SWITCHES on the Radio Tuning Panel.
options: True
False
explanation: False. Receiver volume is controlled by rotating the receiver switches on the Audio Control Panel (ACP), not the Radio Tuning Panel. · FCOM 5.10.x

question: VHF antennae located on the upper fuselage are susceptible to multipath interference from other air traffic, antennae located on the lower fuselage are not as susceptible to this interference.
options: True
False
explanation: False. VHF-1 is on the upper fuselage; VHF-2 and VHF-3 are on the lower fuselage. The LOWER antennas are susceptible to multipath interference from nearby structures or vehicles. · FCOM 5.20.6

question: What is the effect of pushing the Pilot Call switch?
options: Two-tone chime in flight deck.
Two-tone chime in passenger cabin, with both pink master call lights illuminated.
Single-tone chime in flight deck.
Single-tone chime in passenger cabin with both pink call lights illuminated.
explanation: PILOT CALL switch (external power panel): sounds a chime in the flight deck and illuminates the blue CALL light (bank: single-tone chime in the flight deck). · FCOM 5.10.13

question: What microphone options are available to the flight crew?
options: Hand microphone, headset boom microphone, oxygen mask microphone, overhead speaker microphone.
Headset boom microphone, oxygen mask microphone, ceiling speakers microphone.
Hand microphone, headset boom microphone, oxygen mask microphone.
Headset boom microphone and hand microphone.
explanation: Flight crew microphones: hand microphone, headset boom microphone and oxygen mask microphone (MASK-BOOM switch). · FCOM 5.20.x

question: Communication between the flight deck and flight attendants is still possible with the SERVICE INTERPHONE switch selected OFF.
options: True
False
explanation: True. The SERVICE INTERPHONE switch only adds the external service jacks; flight deck to flight attendant communication is unaffected. · FCOM 5.20.x

question: If a passenger pushes the call button from the lavatory, what colour light illuminates in the cabin?
options: Blue
Amber
Red
Pink
explanation: Master call lights: pink = flight deck/attendant call; blue = passenger seat call; amber = lavatory call. · FCOM 5.20.x

question: Selecting the Cockpit Voice Recorder to ON has what effect?
options: Powers the cockpit voice recorder until the switch is moved to OFF
Powers the cockpit voice recorder until first engine is started, then trips to AUTO.
Powers the cockpit voice recorder after the first engine is started until 5 minutes after last engine shutdown.
Powers the cockpit voice recorder until 5 after the last engine shutdown.
explanation: Bank answer: CVR switch ON powers the CVR until the first engine start, then trips to AUTO (RYR installation). · FCOM 5.10.11 / 5.20.7

question: The Flight Interphone and Service Interphone are on separate networks.
options: True
False
explanation: True. Flight interphone and service interphone are independent systems. · FCOM 5.20.x

question: What are the 3 positions For the Audio Control Panel Filter switch?
options: R, G, B,   Radio, Ground, Both.
Pushed to select filtering ON, Pushed again for filtering OFF, rotated to increase or decrease amount of filtering.
V, B, R,    Voice, Both, Radio.
V, B, R,   Voice, Both, Range.
explanation: ACP Filter switch: V (Voice) – NAV/ADF voice audio; B (Both) – voice and range audio; R (Range) – station identifier (code) audio. · FCOM 5.10.6

question: After unsuccessfully trying to contact ATC for start clearance you notice that the digital displays are blank on your Radio Tuning Panel and the OFF button is illuminated. What is the problem and how would you resolve it?
options: VHF 1 and VHF 2 are both unserviceable. Contact Engineering
The RTP is switched off. Press 'OFF' to power it back on again
There is a stuck transmit switch. Follow the Stuck Transmit Switch checklist in the QRH
VHF 1 is unserviceable. Use VHF 2 for the remainder of the flight
explanation: RTP OFF switch: disconnects the panel from the radios (displays blank, OFF illuminated). Push OFF again to reconnect. · FCOM 5.10.2

question: How can you improve the reception range of the VHF radios?
options: Press the TEST switch on the Radio Tuning Panel
Tune using VHF 3
Turn up the volume
Tune VHF 1 and 2 to the same frequency
explanation: VHF TEST switch: removes the automatic squelch and improves reception of weak signals (FCOM 5.10.2). · FCOM 5.20.6

question: How do you enable the aircraft to send and receive CPDLC data?
options: Press and hold 'AM' until 'CPDLC' appears in the active window
Press and hold the TEST button on RTP3 until 'CPDLC' appears in the active window
Push in and hold the tuning knob on RTP3 until 'DATA' appears in the standby window and transfer to the active window
Turn the frequency knob on the RTP for VHF 3 until 'DATA' appears and then transfer to the active window
explanation: VHF-3 is selected to DATA mode by tuning its RTP until 'DATA' appears, then transferring it to active. The RYR procedure is not detailed in the FCOM. · FCOM 5.10.x

question: How do you set the Audio Control Panel to receive NAV and ADF voice and range audio?
options: Set the ALT-NORM Switch to ALT
Set the Filter Switch to B (Both)
Set the MASK-BOOM Switch to BOOM
Push the VHF and NAV selector switches
explanation: Filter switch B (Both): receive NAV and ADF voice and range audio. · FCOM 5.10.6

question: How is the Oxygen Mask microphone activated?
options: Operating the switch on the front of the mask
It is always live
Removing the mask from it's stowage
Operating the "Test and Reset" switch on the mask stowage
explanation: The oxygen mask microphone becomes active when the mask is removed from its stowage (stowage box doors open) and MASK is selected. · FCOM 1.40.x / 5.20.x

question: How long can the cockpit voice recorder record audio?
options: 120 minutes
90 minutes
60 minutes
180 minutes
explanation: RYR: the CVR uses four independent channels to record flight deck audio for 120 minutes; older recordings are automatically erased. · FCOM 5.20.7

question: If the FO's ACP mode switch is selected to ALT, which radio(s) can the FO transmit and receive from?
options: Transmit from VHF2 only, but can receive on any radio
Transmit and receive from VHF1 only
Transmit and receive from VHF2 only
Transmit from any radio, but receive from VHF2 only
explanation: ACP in degraded (ALT) mode: the First Officer can transmit and receive on VHF-2 only (Captain VHF-1, Observer VHF-1). · FCOM 5.20.3

question: Pushing the ATTEND call switch:
options: sounds a two-tone chime in the cabin and illuminates both pink master call lights
sounds a single chime in the cabin and illuminates both pink master call lights
sounds a two-tone chime in the cabin and illuminates the FWD pink master call light
sounds a single chime in the cabin and illuminates the FWD pink master call light
explanation: ATTEND call switch: sounds a two-tone chime in the passenger cabin and illuminates the pink master call lights. · FCOM 5.10.13

question: The HF Sensitivity Control is used for which purpose?
options: To set HF sensitivity on the on-side HF receiver
To tune the Data signal when using VHF3 for Data transmissions
To increase the range of the VHF receiver
To set HF sensitivity on the Offside HF receiver
explanation: HF sensitivity control: adjusts the sensitivity of the on-side HF receiver. · FCOM 5.10.2

question: What colour light appears in the cabin if there is a call from the flight deck?
options: Blue
Pink
Amber
Red
explanation: A call from the flight deck (ATTEND) illuminates the pink master call lights with a two-tone chime. · FCOM 5.10.13

question: What is indicated by the Radio Tuning Panel (RTP) Offside Tuning light illuminating white?
options: The light has been pushed for 2 seconds, and the RTP is switched off
The RTP is being used to tune a HF radio
No standby frequency has been set
The RTP is being used to tune a radio not normally associated with that RTP
explanation: Offside tuning light (white): the RTP is tuning a radio not normally associated with it, or its normal radio is being tuned by another RTP. · FCOM 5.10.2

question: What is the meaning of the Offside Tuning Light (the white light just above the Transfer Switch on the Radio tuning Panel)?
options: The radio normally associated with this panel is being tuned by another radio tuning panel, or the radio tuning panel is being used to tune a radio not normally associated with this radio tuning panel
The Radio Tuning Panel is controlling two VHF Receivers
The Radio Tuning Panel is inoperative and will not respond to pilot inputs
The Transfer Switch is inoperative, so STBY frequency selected is the frequency in use
explanation: Offside tuning light: the radio normally associated with this panel is being tuned by another RTP, or this RTP is tuning a radio not normally associated with it. · FCOM 5.10.2

question: What is the result of a flight attendant station calling the flight deck?
options: Blue call light illuminates and single chime is heard
A blue call light flashes and a two-tone chime is heard
A green call light illuminates and a two-tone chime is heard
The blue master call lights flash and a single chime is heard
explanation: Flight attendant calling the flight deck: the blue flight deck CALL light illuminates and a chime sounds in the flight deck. · FCOM 5.10.13

question: What is the result of pushing the ATTEND call switch?
options: Sounds a horn in the nose wheel well
Sounds a single chime in the passenger cabin
Sounds a two-tone chime in the passenger cabin and illuminates both pink master call lights
Both amber Master Call lights illuminate in the passenger cabin
explanation: ATTEND: two-tone chime in the cabin and pink master call lights. · FCOM 5.10.13

question: Which button should be pressed on the cabin interphone to contact the flight deck?
options: C
explanation: Cabin interphone: code 2 calls the flight deck (bank). The code is not in the FCOM text. · FCOM 5.20.x

question: Which of the following statements is correct when the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) switch is set to AUTO
options: Powers both the CVR and the Flight Data Recorder from first engine start
Powers the CVR until first engine start and then trips the switch to ON
Powers the CVR from first engine start until 5 minutes after last engine shutdown
Ensures the CVR is always powered
explanation: CVR AUTO: powers the CVR from first engine start until 5 minutes after the last engine shutdown (RYR installation; bank logic). · FCOM 5.20.7

question: Which statement is correct at that station, when the Captain's ACP operating in degraded mode?
options: All ACP transmitter selectors remain functional, but receiver selectors are lost
Audio warnings for altitude alert, GPWS and windshear are not heard
The flight interphone remains useable, the PA is lost
VHF-2 is the only useable radio
explanation: Degraded mode: audio warnings for altitude alert, GPWS and windshear are not heard on that station's audio system. · FCOM 5.20.3

question: Which statement is correct when the ALT-NORM switch on the Audio Control Panel (ACP) is set to ALT?
options: The ACP at that station is inoperative and the crewmember cannot communicate on any radios
The ACP switches to an alternate ACP and all functions operate normally and the crewmember can communicate on all radios
The ACP at that station is inoperative but the crewmember can communicate on one radio
The ACP switches to standby ACP and all functions operate normally except PA and interphone
explanation: ALT: the ACP at that station operates in degraded mode; the crewmember can communicate on one radio only (Capt VHF-1, F/O VHF-2, Obs VHF-1). · FCOM 5.20.3

question: With the STANDBY POWER switch (located on the Generator Drive and Standby Power Panel)  in the AUTO position, will the loss of a single DC Bus result in automatic switching from normal to alternate power?
options: Only if power from DC Bus 1 is lost
Only if power from from DC Bus 1 is lost and power from AC Transfer Bus 1 is also lost
Only if power from DC Bus 2 is lost
No, for automatic switching to occur power must be lost from both DC Busses
explanation: Standby power switch AUTO: automatic switching from normal to alternate power occurs if power from either AC transfer bus 1 or DC bus 1 is lost. · FCOM 6.20.11

question: What is the normal source of power for the DC Standby bus?
options: TR2 and TR3
TR1, TR2 and TR3
DC bus 1 and DC bus 2
The battery
explanation: Normally the DC standby bus is powered by TR1, TR2 and TR3 (AC standby bus from AC transfer bus 1). With all AC lost: battery. · FCOM 6.10.6 / 6.20.11

question: In the event of the loss of  all engine and APU IDGs, the Standby Power system will provide what electrical power?
options: 24V DC .
115V AC and 22 to 30V DC.
115V AC and 24V DC
explanation: The standby system provides 115V AC (static inverter) and 24V DC to essential systems after loss of all engine or APU-driven AC power. · FCOM 6.20.11

question: Under normal conditions, what powers DC Bus 1?
options: TR2 and TR3
TR1
TR2
TR1 and TR2
explanation: Normally DC bus 1, DC bus 2 and DC standby are connected via the cross bus tie relay, so TR1 and TR2 each power DC bus 1, DC bus 2 and DC standby; TR3 powers the battery bus and backs up TR1/TR2. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: Under what conditions are DC bus 1 and DC bus 2 isolated.
options: When the cross bus tie relay opens.
At glide slope capture during a a flight director or autopilot ILS apporach.
Switching the Bus Transfer switch to OFF.
All the other answers are true.
explanation: The cross bus tie relay opens (isolating DC bus 1 from DC bus 2) at glide slope capture on an F/D or A/P ILS approach, or with the BUS TRANSFER switch OFF. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: What is the effect of selecting the Drive Disconnect switch to DISCONNECT?
options: AC Standby Bus is immediately powered by Inverter from batteries.
No effects take place until STANBY POWER switch is also moved to BAT.
DRIVE light illuminates, AC electrical power is lost on associated Transfer Bus, AC Standby Bus powered from opposite Transfer Bus.
IDG is disconnected if running, and DRIVE light illuminates.
explanation: Generator drive DISCONNECT disconnects the IDG from the engine (if the engine is running) and the DRIVE light illuminates. It cannot be reconnected in the air. · FCOM 6.10.5 / 6.20.6

question: What is the purpose of the Ground Service switch on the forward attendant's panel?
options: Energises the No1 and No2 115V GND SERVICE BUS, to allow the galleys water heaters to be powered whilst the aircraft is connected to ground power.
Provides power to external services used by ground servicing personnel.
Provides ground power directly to the AC ground services bus for utility outlets, cabin lighting, and battery charger without powering all aircraft electrical busses.
Powers and sounds external horn through the AC ground services bus to attract attention of ground servicing personnel.
explanation: The ground service switch (forward attendant's panel) provides ground power directly to the AC ground service busses — utility outlets, cabin lighting and battery charger — without powering all airplane busses. · FCOM 6.20.2

question: What is the source of power for the AC Standby bus if all AC power is lost.
options: The Static Inverter
The TRs
The Battery Charger
The DC Standby Bus
explanation: The static inverter converts 24V DC from the battery to 115V AC for the AC standby bus when normal power is lost. · FCOM 6.20.12

question: Which bus(ses) will be automatically shed if the APU is the only source of electrical power in flight?
options: The galley busses
The main busses
Transfer bus 2
All galley and main busses
explanation: In flight with the APU as the only source, all galley busses and main busses are automatically shed (then IFE busses if still overloaded). · FCOM 6.20.4

question: Why are the covers on the Drive DISCONNECT switches red?
options: To identify switch action is irreversible in flight.
To identify a NNP memory item.
To identify an emergency operation control switch.
For easy identification of an emergency operation in low light conditions.
explanation: Red guard: the DISCONNECT action can't be undone in flight — the IDG cannot be reconnected in the air. · FCOM 6.10.5

question: An illuminated amber ELEC light on the AC and DC Metering Panel indicates?
options: A fault exists in the DC power system and the Standby power system
A fault exists in the DC power system or the Standby power system
A fault exists in the AC power system and the DC power system
A fault exists in the AC power system or the DC power system
explanation: ELEC (amber): a fault exists in the DC power system or the standby power system. Operates only with the airplane on the ground. · FCOM 6.20.7 / 6.10.3

question: How is the auxiliary battery charger powered?
options: Through Ground Service Bus 2
Through DC Bus 1
Through the AC Standby Bus
Through the AC Ground Service Bus
explanation: Main battery charger: AC ground service bus 2. Auxiliary battery charger: AC ground service bus 1. · FCOM 6.20.9

question: If all AC generated power fails, how long can the batteries (if fully charged) supply standby power?
options: Up to 60 minutes.
A minimum of 30 minutes.
A minimum of 60 minutes.
Up to 30 minutes.
explanation: Two fully charged batteries provide standby power for a minimum of 60 minutes. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: If an IDG fails and the APU is not available to power the related Transfer Bus, what occur first if an electrical overload is sensed?
options: Automatic load shedding of the IFE Busses.
Automatic load shedding of the galleys and main bus on Transfer Bus 2
Automatic load shedding of the galley and main busses on on both Transfer Busses.
Automatic load shedding of the galleys and main bus on Transfer Bus 1.
explanation: Single generator: galleys and main bus on transfer bus 2 shed first; then those on transfer bus 1; then the IFE busses. · FCOM 6.20.4

question: If Ground power is powering both Transfer Busses, the APU is available, and is selected to power Transfer Bus 1, which statement is correct?
options: Ground power will continue to power the Transfer Busses until the APU is selected to power both Transfer Busses.
The APU will power Transfer Bus 1 and Ground power will power Transfer Bus 2
Ground power will be automatically disconnected and the APU will power both Transfer Busses.
Ground power will be automatically disconnected and the APU will power Transfer Bus 1. Transfer Bus 2 is unpowered.
explanation: With engines shut down, the last source selected powers both busses: selecting an APU GEN switch ON connects the APU to both transfer busses and ground power is disconnected. · FCOM 6.20.3

question: If the APU is powering Transfer Bus 1 and GEN 2 is powering Transfer Bus 2, what will occur when the Ground Power (GRD PWR) Switch is turned to ON?
options: Ground Power will power both Transfer Busses and the SOURCE OFF lights will illuminate.
The APU will power Transfer Bus 1 and Ground Power will power Transfer Bus 2.
Ground Power will power both Transfer Busses. The SOURCE OFF lights will remain extinguished.
Ground Power will power Transfer Bus 1 and GEN 2 will power Transfer Bus 2.
explanation: GRD PWR ON removes previously connected power and connects ground power to both transfer busses. Since a source was selected for both busses, no SOURCE OFF lights. · FCOM 6.10.7 / 6.20.3

question: Maintaining uninterrupted power on both AC Transfer Busses is primarily the function of:
options: The Bus Tie Breakers (BTBs)
The IDGs
The Ground Service Busses
The Transfer Busses
explanation: BUS TRANSFER AUTO: the BTBs operate automatically to maintain power to the AC transfer busses from any operating generator or external power. · FCOM 6.10.7 / 6.20.3

question: The right IRS is electrically powered from:
options: Normally AC Transfer Bus 2 and in an emergency from battery bus
Normally AC Transfer Bus 2 and in an emergency from switched hot battery bus for a maximum of 5 minutes
Normally AC Transfer Bus 2 and in an emergency from hot battery bus
Normally AC Transfer Bus 1 and in an emergency from switched hot battery bus
explanation: Right IRS: normally AC transfer bus 2; backup from the switched hot battery bus for only about 5 minutes (left IRS: AC standby bus, with switched hot battery backup). · FCOM 11.20.6

question: The TR UNIT light illuminated when on the ground indicates: ?
options: TR1 has failed or TR2 and TR3 have failed
any TR has failed
any two TRs have failed
All three TRs have failed
explanation: TR UNIT on the ground: any TR has failed. In flight: TR1 failed, or TR2 and TR3 failed. · FCOM 6.10.3

question: What is the normal AC power source for TR3?
options: Transfer Bus 2
Main Bus 1
Transfer Bus 1
Main Bus 2
explanation: TR3 normally receives AC from transfer bus 2, with transfer bus 1 as backup (BUS TRANSFER in AUTO). · FCOM 6.20.8

question: Which electrical bus is always connected and powered whenever the aircraft battery is fitted?
options: Battery bus - power immediately available to important systems such as fire extinguishers.
DC Standby bus - power to important systems that require to be in standby mode.
Hot Battery Bus - power immediately available to important systems such as fire extinguishers.
AC standby bus- powered through Transformer Rectifier to ensure no power interuption to GPS system.
explanation: The hot battery bus is always connected to the battery — there is no switch in this circuit. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: Cargo compartment smoke detection is powered from:
options: DC standby bus
AC standby bus
Hot battery bus
DC bus 1 and DC bus 2
explanation: Cargo smoke detection: DC bus 1 and DC bus 2. Cargo fire suppression: hot battery bus. · FCOM 8.20.5

question: Electrical power to start the APU comes from:
options: Either the AC or DC standby bus
Battery power or either AC transfer bus
The battery bus or the DC bus 2
The No 1 transfer bus if available. If AC power is not available, battery power is used
explanation: APU start power comes from No.1 transfer bus or the main battery: AC if available, otherwise battery. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: For ground service, a ground service switch is placed:
options: On aft overhead panel on the Flight Deck
On external receptacle on the right side of the aircraft exterior
On aft attendants panel
On forward attendants panel
explanation: The ground service switch is on the forward attendant's panel (momentary; overridden when both transfer busses are powered). · FCOM 6.20.2

question: Galley busses are powered from:
options: The main busses
The Battery bus
The generator busses
The AC transfer busses
explanation: Each AC system has a transfer bus feeding a main bus and two galley busses — the galleys are supplied through the AC transfer busses. · FCOM 6.20.3

question: If ON DC on left IRS mode selector unit comes ON steady it means:
options: The related IRS is operating on DC power from the switched hot battery bus
The related IRS is operating on DC power from battery bus
The related IRS is operating on DC power from the hot battery bus
The related IRS is operating on DC power from the DC bus 1
explanation: ON DC (steady) on the IRS mode select unit: the IRS is operating on DC power from the switched hot battery bus (AC lost). · FCOM 11.10.18 / 11.20.6

question: If operating on a single IDG and an overload is sensed, the electrical system will shed the galleys and main bus from Transfer Bus 1 and then Transfer Bus 2 before then shedding the IFE busses if an overload is still sensed.
options: True
False
explanation: False — the order is transfer bus 2 galleys/main bus first, then transfer bus 1, then IFE busses. · FCOM 6.20.4

question: Illumination of the BAT DISCHARGE light indicates:
options: The DC meter is in the BAT position with the battery switch ON
Excessive battery discharge is detected with the battery switch ON
The battery is being overcharged
The battery bus is not powered
explanation: BAT DISCHARGE: with BAT switch ON, excessive battery discharge detected. · FCOM 6.10.3

question: Illumination of the GEN OFF BUS light indicates:
options: The generator is not supplying power to its associated generator bus
The associated generator bus is not powered
The associated transfer bus is not powered
The IDG is not supplying power to its associated transfer bus
explanation: GEN OFF BUS (blue): the IDG is not supplying power to the related transfer bus. · FCOM 6.10.7

question: Illumination of the STANDBY POWER OFF lights indicates:
options: Hot battery bus unpowered
DC bus 1 unpowered
DC bus 2 unpowered
AC standby bus unpowered
explanation: STANDBY PWR OFF (amber): one or more of AC standby bus, DC standby bus or battery bus unpowered. · FCOM 6.10.5

question: In flight with both PACK switches in HIGH:
options: the left RECIRC fan will not operate
the right RECIRC fan will not operate
both RECIRC fans will operate
both RECIRC fans will not operate
explanation: RECIRC FAN AUTO, in flight: the left fan operates if both packs are operating unless EITHER PACK switch is in HIGH; the right fan operates unless BOTH PACK switches are in HIGH. Both in HIGH → neither fan runs. · FCOM 2.10.10 / 2.20.x

question: On the ground with the Battery Master switch selected to ON, but no AC Power available, what would you expect the battery voltage to be?
options: Exactly equal to 28 Volts
Greater than 28 Volts
Less than 28 Volts
explanation: Batteries are two 24 V Ni-Cd units; battery voltage range is 22–30 V. With no AC (no charger), the battery reads below the 28 V TR/charger output. The FCOM gives only the 22–30 V range, not this exact case. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: On the ground, with the BATTERY switch OFF and STANDBY POWER Switch in BAT, the switched hot battery bus is:
options: Powered by TR 3
Powered by the Battery
Not powered
Powered by the Hot Battery Bus
explanation: STANDBY POWER switch BAT puts the AC standby, DC standby and battery bus on battery power; the battery switch may be ON or OFF. If the battery switch is OFF, the switched hot battery bus is not powered. · FCOM 6.20.11

question: One basic principle of operation for the 737 electrical system is:
options: All generator bus sources can be automatically connected by the Standby Power System
An AC power source may be used in parallel with a DC power source
There is paralleling of AC power sources
There is no paralleling of the AC power sources
explanation: Two basic principles: there is no paralleling of the AC sources of power, and the source being connected to a transfer bus automatically disconnects an existing source. · FCOM 6.20.1

question: Stabiliser trim override switch:
options: Bypasses the main electric and auto pilot cut out switches on the centre pedestal
Overrides the main electric switch
Isolates the stabiliser trim motor
Bypasses the control column activated stab trim cut out switches to restore power to stab trim switches
explanation: Stabilizer Trim Override switch OVERRIDE: bypasses the control-column-actuated stabilizer trim cutout switches to restore power to the Stabilizer Trim Switches. NORM (guarded) is the normal position. · FCOM 9.10.6

question: Switching the CAB/UTIL switch OFF removes all 115v AC from the galley busses and:
options: the emergency exit lighting
the overhead panel lights
left and right recirculation fans
the left pack
explanation: CAB/UTIL switch OFF removes power from galley and cabin equipment, including all 115V AC galley busses, the cabin recirculation fan and the left & right recirculation fans (among others listed). · FCOM 6.10.4

question: The 2 basic rules of the B737-800 electrical system are:  Only one AC power source can be connected at one time.  A second source connecting to a transfer bus will automatically disconnect the existing source.
options: True
False
explanation: Two basic principles: no paralleling of AC power sources; the source being connected to a transfer bus automatically disconnects the existing source. · FCOM 6.20.1

question: The amber TR UNIT light illuminated while in-flight indicates if?
options: One TR has failed.
All three TRs have failed.
TR1 and TR2 have failed, or TR3 has failed.
TR1 has failed, or TR2 and TR3 have failed.
explanation: TR UNIT light (amber): on the ground – any TR failed; in flight – TR1 failed, or TR2 and TR3 failed. · FCOM 6.10.3 / 6.20.8

question: The blue APU GEN BUS light will illuminate:
options: Whenever the APU is supplying power to a main bus but not the associated transfer bus
When the APU is at operational speed and is not supplying an AC transfer bus
Whenever the APU is supplying power to generator bus No 1
Whenever the APU is supplying power to generator bus No 2
explanation: APU GEN OFF BUS light (blue): APU is running and not powering a bus. · FCOM 6.10.8

question: The cross bus tie relay:
options: Will trip off when AC volts reaches 26 volts (plus or minus 4 volts) as displayed on the AC voltmeter
Must be manually opened using the BUS TRANSFER Switch during a Flight Director approach
Opens up if BUS TRANSFER switch is moved to OFF
Normally powers the Battery Charger and backs-up TR units 1 and 2 through a diode
explanation: BUS TRANSFER switch OFF: isolates AC transfer bus 1 from bus 2 and the DC cross tie relay opens to isolate DC bus 1 from DC bus 2. Normally DC bus 1, DC bus 2 and DC standby are connected via the cross bus tie relay. It also opens automatically during a flight director / autopilot approach; no manual action is needed. · FCOM 6.10.7 / 6.20.8

question: The DC standby Bus is powered from the batteries through the static Inverter.  Select one:
options: True
False
explanation: The AC standby bus is powered from the batteries via the static inverter. The DC standby bus, battery bus, hot battery bus and switched hot battery bus are powered DIRECTLY from the batteries. · FCOM 6.20.11 / 6.10.6

question: The ELEC light will illuminate in flight if:
options: A fault exists in the DC or standby system
A fault exists in the AC or standby power system
The ELEC light only operates on the ground
A fault exists in the AC, DC or the standby system
explanation: ELEC light (amber): a fault exists in the DC power system or standby power system. Note: operates only with the airplane on the ground (inhibited in flight). · FCOM 6.10.3 / 6.20.7

question: The GROUND POWER AVAILABLE light will extinguish when:
options: The GROUND SERVICE switch is positioned ON
The pneumatic ground cart is disconnected
The AC ground power cart has been disconnected
The GROUND POWER switch is positioned ON
explanation: GRD POWER AVAILABLE light (blue): ground power is connected and meets airplane power quality standards. It stays on after GRD PWR ON and goes out when the ground power is disconnected. · FCOM 6.10.7

question: The left IRS is electrically powered from:
options: Normally AC Transfer Bus 1 in emergency from switched hot battery bus
Normally AC Transfer Bus 2 in emergency from hot battery bus
Normally AC Transfer Bus 2 in emergency from battery bus
Normally AC Standby bus in emergency from switched hot battery bus
explanation: The left IRS normally uses the AC standby bus; its backup DC comes from the switched hot battery bus. (The right IRS uses AC transfer bus 2, with backup DC from the switched hot battery bus that terminates after 5 minutes.) · FCOM 11.20.6

question: The power source for Fire Extinguishing is:
options: the Switched Battery Bus
none of the other answers
the Hot Battery Bus
Transfer Bus No 1
explanation: Engine fire extinguishing is powered by the hot battery bus (engine overheat/fire detection by the battery bus). APU fire extinguishing and cargo fire suppression are also on the hot battery bus. · FCOM 8.20.1

question: The SOURCE OFF light illuminates whenever an IDG has tripped offline due to overheating.
options: True
False
explanation: RYR Q-Bank answer: FALSE. The dedicated indication of an IDG overheat disconnect is the amber DRIVE light (FCOM 6.20.6). Note: by the FCOM definition (6.10.7) SOURCE OFF can also come on when the selected generator is disconnected – but the exam answer is False. · FCOM 6.10.7 / 6.20.6

question: The Static Inverter, converts the Battery's 22-30V DC voltage range to a constant 24V.
options: True
False
explanation: The static inverter converts 24 V DC from the battery to 115V AC to supply the AC standby bus during loss of normal electrical power. It does not output 24 V DC. · FCOM 6.20.12

question: The TRs (Transformer rectifier) converts:
options: 115 volts AC to 28 volts AC
115 volts DC to 28 volts
115 volts DC to 28 volts AC
115 volts AC to 28 volts DC
explanation: The TRs convert 115 volt AC to 28 volt DC (TR1, TR2, TR3). · FCOM 6.20.8

question: What indications will you see on the electrical panel when selecting GRD PWR ON?
options: GRD POWER AVAILABLE light illuminated, SOURCE OFF lights extinguished, GEN OFF BUS lights illuminated, TRANSFER BUS OFF lights extinguished, APU GEN OFF BUS light extinguished.
GRD POWER light extinguished, SOURCE OFF lights illuminated, GEN OFF BUS lights illuminated, TRANSFER BUS OFF lights extinguished, APU GEN OFF BUS light illuminated.
GRD POWER AVAILABLE light illuminated, SOURCE OFF lights extinguished, GEN OFF BUS lights illuminated, TRANSFER BUS OFF lights extinguished, APU GEN OFF BUS light illuminated.
GRD POWER AVAILABLE light extinguished, SOURCE OFF lights extinguished, GEN OFF BUS lights illuminated, TRANSFER BUS OFF lights extinguished, APU GEN OFF BUS light illuminated.
explanation: GRD PWR ON (APU and IDGs off): GRD POWER AVAILABLE stays illuminated; SOURCE OFF and TRANSFER BUS OFF extinguish; GEN OFF BUS lights stay on (IDGs not supplying). APU GEN OFF BUS is only on when the APU is running and not powering a bus, so it is extinguished. · FCOM SP.6.1 / 6.10.7 / 6.10.8

question: What is the normal source of power for the Battery Bus?
options: TR3
The hot battery bus
The battery
the switched hot battery bus
explanation: Normal conditions: AC standby bus from AC transfer bus 1; DC standby bus from TR1, TR2 and TR3; battery bus from TR3; hot battery bus and switched hot battery bus from the battery/battery charger. · FCOM 6.20.11

question: What is the only system to be connected to the Switched Hot Battery Bus?
options: The Inertial Reference System
The Engine Fire Suppression system
Standby supply to the airstairs
The APU Fire Detection system
explanation: The IRSs take backup DC from the switched hot battery bus (powered whenever the battery switch is ON). Fire extinguishing is on the HOT battery bus (8.20.1). The FCOM does not state that the IRS is the ONLY load on this bus. · FCOM 11.20.6 / 6.20.8

question: What is the voltage of the DC Busses in normal flight?
explanation: 28 volt DC power is supplied by three TR units (115V AC → 28V DC). · FCOM 6.20.7 / 6.20.8

question: What is the voltage of the DC Busses under normal circumstances?
explanation: 28 V DC is supplied by the three TRs. 22–30 V is the BATTERY voltage range (6.20.8), not the normal DC bus voltage. · FCOM 6.20.7 / 6.20.8

question: When external ground power is connected to the aircraft through the External AC Receptacle, the GRD POWER AVAILABLE light does not illuminate unless the power supplied meets the quality requirements of 115v AC, 200 Hz, 3 phase.
options: True
False
explanation: GRD POWER AVAILABLE illuminates when ground power is connected and meets airplane power quality standards. The FCOM gives no figures; the statement is false because aircraft AC is 115 V, 400 Hz (not 200 Hz). · FCOM 6.10.7

question: When the aircraft batteries is the only source of power:
options: The Captains inboard and outboard displays operate until the battery is discharged
The Captains inboard and outboard displays operate until the battery is discharged and the First Officers inboard and outboard displays operate for a minimum of 5 minutes
The Captains inboard and the First Officers inboard and outboard displays are inoperative
Both the Captains and First Officers PFD/ND displays remain operative but only DEU No 1 is powered until the battery is discharged
explanation: Basic Equipment Operating – Captain Instrument Panel: with only the battery and standby busses powered (BAT ON, STANDBY POWER AUTO), the Captain's primary flight display (outboard) and the inboard display (compact engine display, or ND depending on effectivity) remain usable, along with the standby instruments. First Officer displays are not powered. Two fully charged batteries give at least 60 minutes. · FCOM 6.20.17

question: When the STANDBY POWER Switch is OFF:
options: Automatic switching is provided from normal power sources to alternate power sources
The STANDBY PWR OFF light will be extinguished
The STANDBY PWR OFF light will be illuminated
The Static Inverter provides 28 volt DC power to Transfer Bus No. 1
explanation: Positioning the standby power switch to OFF de-energizes both the AC standby bus and the DC standby bus and illuminates the STANDBY PWR OFF light. · FCOM 6.20.11 / 6.10.5

question: Which bus supplies electrical power to the main battery charger?
options: Transfer bus 1
AC ground service bus 1
Transfer bus 2
AC ground service bus 2
explanation: The main battery charger is powered through AC ground service bus 2 (aux charger: AC ground service bus 1). · FCOM 6.20.9

question: Which of the following is NOT powered by the standby Power system?
options: AC Standby Bus
Transformer Rectifier 1.
Battery Bus.
Static Inverter
explanation: The standby power system consists of: static inverter, AC standby bus, DC standby bus, battery bus (plus hot/switched hot battery busses and batteries). TR1 is part of the normal DC system, energized from the AC transfer busses. · FCOM 6.20.11

question: Which system will not operate unless the CAB/UTIL switch is ON?
options: Left & right Recirculation fans
All lighting
Temperature controls
Air conditioning packs
explanation: CAB/UTIL OFF removes power from all 115V AC galley busses, the cabin recirculation fan and the left & right recirculation fans, door area heaters, drain mast heaters, lavatory water heaters, etc. These need CAB/UTIL ON. · FCOM 6.10.4

question: Why does the aircraft have a DC and AC power system?
options: The AC system causes interference in the electronic systems, so the Captain's instruments are powered by DC power.
The DC system allows power to be stored in a battery, whereas the AC system allows the transfer of large quantities of power
The DC system is used for most systems, but the AC system is only used for starting the APU
The DC system can power the whole aircraft, but the AC system is used as a backup
