explanation: AC (IDGs/APU gen, 115V) carries the main electrical load; 28 V DC comes from TRs fed by the AC transfer busses, and the batteries (DC) provide stored backup power. The FCOM does not state the 'why'; this is basic electrical theory. · FCOM 6.20.1 / 6.20.7

question: With normal power source on the buses, placing the battery switch to OFF will remove power from:
options: The battery bus
The standby buses
The battery bus, switched hot battery bus and standby buses
The battery bus and switched hot battery bus
explanation: BAT switch OFF: removes power from the battery bus and switched hot battery bus when operating with normal power sources available. When the battery is the only source, it also removes the DC standby bus, static inverter and AC standby bus. · FCOM 6.10.3

question: With the BUS TRANSFER switch in the AUTO position; how do the BTBs operate?
options: BTBs isolate Transfer Bus 1 from Transfer Bus 2, if only 1 IDG is supplying power, DC Cross Tie Relay closes to connect DC Bus 1 to DC Bus 2.
BTBs automatically maintain power to AC Transfer busses from any operating generator or external power.
BTBs automatically maintain power to DC Bus 1 and DC Bus 2 through the DC Cross Tie Relay.
BTBs isolate Transfer Bus 1 from Transfer Bus 2, if only 1 IDG is supplying power, DC Cross Tie Relay opens to isolate DC Bus 1 from DC Bus 2.
explanation: BUS TRANSFER AUTO (guarded): BTBs operate automatically to maintain power to the AC transfer busses from any operating generator or external power; the DC cross tie relay automatically gives normal or isolated operation as required. · FCOM 6.10.7

question: With the STANDBY POWER switch in the AUTO position, loss of both engine driven generators and APU generator will result in that AC standby bus is powered by battery through static inverter and DC standby bus is powered by battery:
options: In flight only
Either in flight or on the ground
On the ground only
Will not occur
explanation: STANDBY POWER AUTO: in flight OR on the ground, with loss of all AC power, the AC standby bus is powered by the battery through the static inverter, and the DC standby bus and battery bus directly by the battery. · FCOM 6.10.6 / 6.20.11

question: A take off is performed with the APU powering both transfer buses
options: The generators will come on line automatically if the APU is either shut down or fails
During climb, after passing 1500 feet AGL generators will automatically come on line
Both AC and DC Standby bus will disconnect after lift-off
Both transfer busses will disconnect automatically after lift-off
explanation: Automatic generator on-line feature: if the airplane takes off with the APU powering both transfer busses and the APU is then shut down or fails, the engine generators automatically come on line. · FCOM 6.20.3

question: After the loss of all generators, full charged batteries can provide standby power for a minimum of:
options: 5 minutes
60 minutes
90 minutes
30 minutes
explanation: Two fully charged batteries have sufficient capacity to provide standby power for a minimum of 60 minutes. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: As part of the preflight procedure you are about to test the STALL warning. For this to be possible, an AC source must have powered the Aircraft for a minimum of approximately
options: 2 minutes
1 minutes
4 minutes
3 minutes
explanation: Preflight note: the stall warning test requires that the AC transfer busses have been powered for up to 4 minutes. · FCOM NP.21.8

question: Blue illumination of APU GEN OFF BUS means:
options: APU is running but not powering transfer busses
APU is running
APU is not running
APU is running and powering transfer busses
explanation: APU GEN OFF BUS light (blue): APU is running and not powering a bus. · FCOM 6.10.8

question: If an AC Generator disconnects in flight, what may also happen?
options: The related SOURCE OFF light will extinguish
The Autopilot may disconnect
The Electric Hydraulic Pumps will trip off
The Master Fire Warning will illuminate
explanation: AFDS: power interruption or loss may cause disengagement of the AFDS and/or A/T. A generator dropping off-line causes a momentary bus transfer, so the autopilot may disconnect. · FCOM 4.20.3

question: If electrical demand exceeds generator supply, load shedding occurs. When another generator comes online or demand decreases, power to the main and galley buses is normally restored automatically. If not, they can be reconnected manually by:
options: Selecting both engine driven generators to OFF and then ON again
Hold the GEN 1 or GEN 2 switch in the ON position for up to 5 seconds
Recycling the CAB/UTIL switch
Select the APU generator to ON
explanation: Automatic load shedding: if power is not restored automatically, manual restoration of galley and main bus power can be attempted by moving the CAB/UTIL power switch to OFF, then back ON. · FCOM 6.20.4

question: If the APU is the only source of electrical power:
options: In flight, the APU attempts to carry the full electrical load
On the ground, the main busses are shed first if an overload condition is sensed
On the ground, the galley busses are automatically shed
In flight, the galley busses are automatically shed
explanation: APU load shedding: in flight, if the APU is the only source of electrical power, all galley busses and main busses are automatically shed (then both IFE busses if still overloaded). On the ground, the APU attempts to carry the full load; if overloaded, the galleys are shed first. · FCOM 6.20.4 / 7.30.4

question: If the STANDBY POWER switch is set to BAT, what does it mean if the STANDBY PWR OFF light now extinguishes?
options: Standby Power is not available
The battery has been disconnected from the Standby System
The battery is supplying the Standby System, and Standby Power is available
The battery is no longer being charged by the Standby System
explanation: STANDBY PWR OFF (amber) illuminates when the AC standby bus, DC standby bus or battery bus is unpowered. In BAT, the battery powers the AC standby (via the inverter), DC standby and battery busses, so the light extinguished = standby power available from the battery. · FCOM 6.10.5 / 6.10.6

question: If the TR UNIT light illuminates in flight, why should you not use the AFDS Approach Mode on an ILS approach?
options: The ILS receivers are fed directly from TR1 and TR2
On Glideslope capture, the Cross Bus Tie Relay will open, resulting in part of the DC system losing power
The autopilot may disengage on localizer capture
This light indicates that the Standby DC system is unavailable
explanation: The cross bus tie relay automatically opens at glide slope capture during a flight director or autopilot ILS approach. TR UNIT light in flight = TR1 failed (or TR2 and TR3). With the busses split, DC bus 1 (or 2) could lose its power source. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: If you move the BUS TRANSFER switch to OFF, what effect will this have on the electrical system?
options: BUS TIE BREAKER 1 and 2 open, and the CROSS BUS TIE relay closes
BUS TIE BREAKER 1 and 2 and the CROSS BUS TIE relay all open
BUS TIE BREAKER 1 and 2 close, and the CROSS BUS TIE relay opens
explanation: BUS TRANSFER OFF: isolates AC transfer bus 1 from AC transfer bus 2 (BTBs open), the DC cross tie relay opens to isolate DC bus 1 from DC bus 2, and TR3 input is inhibited from connecting to AC transfer bus 1. · FCOM 6.10.7

question: Illumination of the amber generator DRIVE light indicates low oil pressure caused by which of the following?
options: IDG failure
IDG automatic disconnect due to high oil pressure
Loss of the associated engine-driven hydraulic pump
Failure of the associated AC transfer bus
explanation: DRIVE light (amber): IDG low oil pressure caused by IDG failure, engine shutdown, IDG automatic disconnect due to high oil TEMPERATURE (not pressure), or IDG disconnected through the DISCONNECT switch. · FCOM 6.10.5 / 6.20.6

question: Illumination of the GND POWER AVAILABLE light indicates:
options: The external power bus is powered by a ground power supply
Ground power is connected and meets aircraft power quality standards
Ground power is connected however no aircraft power quality is measured
The ground service bus is powered by a ground power supply
explanation: GRD POWER AVAILABLE light (blue): ground power is connected and meets airplane power quality standards. · FCOM 6.10.7

question: In flight if APU is the only source of electrical power:
options: No galley busses are automatically shed
Only galley bus A and B are automatically shed
Only galley bus C and D are automatically shed
All galley busses are automatically shed
explanation: In flight, if the APU is the only source of electrical power, all galley busses and main busses are automatically shed. · FCOM 6.20.4

question: In the event of a total failure of AC electrics, which of these will occur?
options: All pitot heating is lost
VHF Com 1 will be unavailable
The Flap Position Indicator will stop at it's current position and will not respond to subsequent flap position changes
The Left IRS will only operate for 5 minutes
explanation: Elimination: on standby power the captain's pitot probe is still heated (3.20.5), so not all pitot heat is lost. The LEFT IRS stays on battery; it is the RIGHT IRS DC backup that stops after 5 minutes (11.20.6). VHF 1 is on standby power. The flap indicator behaviour is not stated in the FCOM. · FCOM 3.20.5 / 11.20.6

question: In the event of a total loss of AC power, which systems will be available?
options: All ice protection systems will be available, but the Weather Radar will be unavailable
The Weather Radar will remain available, but all ice protection systems will be lost
All ice protection systems and Weather Radar will be unavailable
Some ice protection systems will be unavailable, the Weather Radar will be unavailable
explanation: On standby power, only the captain's pitot probe is heated (3.20.5), so SOME ice protection remains. The weather radar is not on standby power, so it is unavailable. The FCOM shows the basic equipment operating on 6.20.17–18; WXR is not among it. · FCOM 3.20.5 / 6.20.17

question: In the event that a GEN OFF BUS light illuminates in flight, what may occur as an indirect consequence?
options: The Autopilot cannot be engaged in APP mode
If the Autopilot is engaged on the affected side, it may disconnect due to the momentary loss of power
The AC fuel pumps in the main tank on the affected side will not be available
Only the Captain's and Standby instruments will be available
explanation: Power interruption or loss may cause disengagement of the AFDS and/or A/T. A GEN OFF BUS (generator dropping off) gives a momentary power transfer, so an engaged autopilot may disconnect. · FCOM 4.20.3

question: Normal DC indications are
explanation: The RYR FCOM gives no tolerance figure (TRs supply 28 V DC; battery range 22–30 V). 26 ± 4 V is the classic Boeing normal DC voltmeter indication. · FCOM 6.20.6 / 6.20.8

question: On the ground the TR UNIT amber light illuminates if:
options: Only if TR 2 and TR 3 have failed
TR 3 has failed
Any TR has failed
TR 1 has failed
explanation: TR UNIT light: on the ground – any TR failed; in flight – TR1 failed, or TR2 and TR3 failed. · FCOM 6.10.3 / 6.20.8

question: On the ground, what does the illumination of the ELEC light tell you?
options: There is a fault within the DC or Standby Electrical System
The Standby System is operating on DC power
The battery voltage is excessively low
There is a failure of TR1, TR2 or TR3
explanation: ELEC light (amber): a fault exists in the DC power system or standby power system. Operates only on the ground (inhibited in flight). · FCOM 6.10.3 / 6.20.7

question: The AC Standby Bus is powered by:
options: The AC Transfer Bus No 2 under normal conditions
The Battery Bus through the Static Inverter under normal conditions
The AC Transfer Bus No 1 under normal conditions
The Battery through the Static Inverter with a failure of one engine driven generators
explanation: Under normal conditions the AC standby bus is powered from AC transfer bus 1. With loss of ALL AC power it is powered by the battery through the static inverter. · FCOM 6.20.11 / 6.10.6

question: The aircraft is on the ground and the Flight Recorder Switch is in NORMAL:
options: The Flight Recorder operates when electrical power is available and with engines operating
The Flight Recorder operates anytime electrical power is available and start switch in GROUND position
The Flight Recorder operates whenever the Battery Switch is ON
The Flight Recorder operates anytime electrical power is available
explanation: Flight recorder switch NORMAL: in flight – operates anytime electrical power is available; on the ground – operates when electrical power is available and either engine is operating (TEST also allows it on the ground). · FCOM 10.16.24 / 14.20.8

question: The SOURCE OFF light is the only indication that an IDG has tripped offline due to overheating.
options: False
True
explanation: False. An IDG auto-disconnect for high oil temperature gives the amber DRIVE light (IDG low oil pressure) and the GEN OFF BUS light, as well as SOURCE OFF. · FCOM 6.10.5 / 6.10.7

question: The TR Unit light will illuminate in flight if:
options: TR3 fails
TR1 fails
TR2 fails
DC bus 2 fails
explanation: In flight the TR UNIT light illuminates if TR1 fails, or TR2 AND TR3 fail. A single TR2 or TR3 failure does not light it in flight. · FCOM 6.10.3 / 6.20.8

question: What is the overall function of the Static Inverter?
options: To convert DC electrical power to AC electrical power
To convert a low AC voltage into a higher AC voltage
To remove static interference from the Ground Power Supply.
To convert a fluctuating DC voltage into a steady 28 Volts DC
explanation: The static inverter converts 24 volt DC power from the battery to 115V AC power to supply the AC standby bus during loss of normal electrical power. · FCOM 6.20.12

question: What would you see on the flight deck as a direct result of low oil pressure in the No2 IDG?
options: No immediate affect noticeable as the Bus Tie Breakers (BTB) automatically connect the No1 IDG to drive both AC Transfer Bus 1 and AC Transfer Bus 2
Electrical power automatically transfers to the STANDBY system
Power is lost on the First Officer's displays after a delay of 5 minutes
The No2 Drive light illuminates amber
explanation: DRIVE light (amber): IDG low oil pressure (IDG failure, engine shutdown, auto-disconnect for high oil temperature, or DISCONNECT switch). Low oil pressure in IDG 2 illuminates the No 2 DRIVE light. · FCOM 6.10.5 / 6.20.6

question: When AC power is not available, the main battery energizes the hot battery and?
options: The DC bus 1
The Standby bus
The AC transfer bus 1
The switched hot battery bus
explanation: Hot battery bus: always connected to the battery. Switched hot battery bus: powered whenever the battery switch is ON. With no AC, DC busses on the battery are the battery bus, DC standby bus, hot battery bus and switched hot battery bus. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: When Ground Power is available and selected ON, which AC Transfer Bus(es) are powered?
options: AC Transfer Bus 2 only
AC Transfer Bus 1 and AC Transfer Bus 2
AC Standby Bus only
AC Transfer Bus 1 only
explanation: On the ground with both generator switches OFF or both engines shut down, selecting the GRD PWR switch ON connects external power to BOTH transfer busses. · FCOM 6.20.3

question: When operating on standby power:
options: Only the captains pitot probe is heated and the CAPT PITOT amber light will not illuminate for a failure
Only the captains pitot probe is heated and the CAPT PITOT amber light will illuminate in case of failure
Only the F/Os pitot probe is heated
Both captains and F/Os primary pitot are heated
explanation: On standby power only the captain's pitot probe is heated, and the CAPT PITOT light does not illuminate for a failure. The standby airspeed pitot probe is not heated on standby power. · FCOM 3.20.5

question: When will the ELEC Light illuminate on the ground?
options: The ELEC light only operates in flight
When a fault exists in the AC, DC or the standby system
When a fault exists in the DC or standby system
When a fault exists in the AC or standby power system
explanation: ELEC light (amber): a fault exists in the DC power system or standby power system. Operates only with the airplane on the ground. · FCOM 6.10.3 / 6.20.7

question: When will the TR UNIT light illuminate in flight?
options: When TR1 has failed
When TR1 and TR2 have failed
If any TR has failed
The TR UNIT light only illuminates when the aircraft is on the ground
explanation: TR UNIT light in flight: TR1 failed, or TR2 and TR3 failed. On the ground: any TR failed. · FCOM 6.10.3 / 6.20.8

question: Which air conditioning system will not operate unless the CAB/UTIL switch is ON?
options: Air conditioning packs
All 115V AC galley busses
Temperature controls
Left & right Recirculation fans
explanation: CAB/UTIL OFF removes power from the left & right recirculation fans (the air-conditioning item) as well as the galley busses, door heaters, etc. Packs and temperature controls are unaffected. · FCOM 6.10.4

question: Which bus supplies electrical power to the auxiliary battery charger:
options: Transfer bus 2
AC ground service bus 2
Transfer bus 1
AC ground service bus 1
explanation: The auxiliary battery charger is powered through AC ground service bus 1 (main charger: AC ground service bus 2). · FCOM 6.20.9

question: Which of these conditions would cause an IDG "DRIVE" light to illuminate in flight?
options: Generator overload
IDG low oil temperature
Generator Breaker open
IDG low oil pressure
explanation: DRIVE light (amber) = IDG low oil pressure (IDG failure, engine shutdown, auto-disconnect for high oil temperature, or DISCONNECT switch). · FCOM 6.10.5

question: Which statement is correct for an aircraft taking off with the APU powering both transfer buses?
options: The AC and DC Standby buses will automatically disconnect after lift-off
The engine generators are automatically connected to their related transfer buses if the APU is shut down
The engine generators are automatically connected to their related transfer buses after passing 1500 feet AGL
Both transfer buses will automatically disconnect after lift-off
explanation: Automatic generator on-line feature: after takeoff with the APU powering both transfer busses, if the APU is shut down or fails, the engine generators automatically connect to their transfer busses. · FCOM 6.20.3

question: With the BUS TRANSFER switch in AUTO, if one IDG fails in flight, what happens next?
options: The Generator Circuit Breaker on the failed side will open. The AC Transfer Bus on the failed side will remain unpowered until the APU is selected to that side
The Generator Circuit Breaker on the failed side will open. The AC Transfer Bus on the failed side will remain unpowered until the Generator on the failed side is selected OFF

The Generator Circuit Breaker on the failed side opens, the Bus Tie Breaker on the failed side opens and the Bus Tie Breaker on the functional side closes. The AC Transfer Bus on the failed side is powered by the AC standby system
The Generator Circuit Breaker on the failed side opens, Bus Tie Breakers 1 and 2 close. Both AC Transfer Buses are powered by the remaining IDG
explanation: BUS TRANSFER AUTO: if the source powering a transfer bus is disconnected or fails (its GCB opens), the source powering the opposite transfer bus automatically picks up the unpowered bus through the BTBs. One IDG then powers both. · FCOM 6.20.3

question: Fuel for the APU is normally supplied from the:
options: Centre tank
No 2 main tank
Left side of the fuel manifold
Aux. Tank
explanation: APU fuel comes from the left side of the fuel manifold when the AC fuel pumps are operating; with no AC pumps it is suction fed from main tank No.1. · FCOM 7.30.1 / 12.20.3

question: If both the ON and ALTN lights in the EEC switch are illuminated, what does this indicate?
options: The EEC has been manually switched to the soft alternate mode
The soft alternate mode is armed.
The EEC has automatically switched to the soft alternate mode.
The EEC is inoperative for that engines.
explanation: Both ON and ALTN in view = the EEC has automatically switched to the soft alternate mode. When ALTN is selected manually the ON indication is blanked. · FCOM 7.15.4 / 7.20.4

question: If the APU GEN OFF BUS light fails to illuminate by the end of the start cycle:
options: The APU failed a self test and the OVERSPEED light will illuminate
There is no light associated with this malfunction
The FAULT light illuminates
The MAINT light illuminates
explanation: If the start fails or the APU GEN OFF BUS light fails to illuminate by the end of the start cycle (up to 120 s), a system failure has occurred and the FAULT light illuminates. · FCOM 7.30.3

question: Raising an engine start lever to the IDLE position opens which fuel valve(s)?
options: The related engine-mounted fuel shutoff valve.
The related spar fuel shutoff valve and engine-mounted fuel shutoff valve.
The related engine-mounted fuel shutoff valve and engine bypass valve.
The related spar fuel shutoff valve.
explanation: Start lever IDLE: energizes ignition through the EEC, electrically opens the spar fuel shutoff valve and the engine-mounted fuel shutoff valve (via the EEC). CUTOFF closes both. · FCOM 7.15.5

question: The Master Caution lights and ENG system annunciator lights will illuminate if the EEC automatically enters the soft alternate mode.
options: True
False
explanation: True. When the EEC automatically reverts to soft alternate, the amber ALTN in the EEC switch illuminates (ON stays visible); the amber light triggers MASTER CAUTION and the ENG annunciator. · FCOM 7.20.4 / 15.20.4

question: When is the EGT Start Limit Redline displayed?
options: The EGT start Limit Redline is only displayed if the EGT exceeds the Start Limit.
Until the engine achieves stabilised idle (approx 59%)
Until starter cutout speed (approx 56%)
Until the engine achieves self sustaining idle (approx 50%)
explanation: EGT start limit redline (red) is displayed until the engine achieves stabilized idle (approximately 59% N2). · FCOM 7.11.7

question: Which ENGINE START switch position will provide ignition to both igniters regardless of igniter selector switch position when the engine start lever is in IDLE?
options: CONT
CONT and FLT
GRD
FLT
explanation: FLT: provides ignition to both igniters when the engine start lever is in IDLE, regardless of the ignition select switch. CONT uses the selected igniter(s). · FCOM 7.15.1

question: APU cooling air enters along with APU engine air through the APU intake located on the right rear fuselage.
options: True
False
explanation: False. APU engine air enters through an automatic inlet door on the right side of the fuselage; cooling air enters through a separate cooling air inlet above the APU exhaust outlet. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: As well as the indication on the Lower DU, engine oil quantity can be physically checked using the gauges located in the Main Undercarriage Wheel Well.
options: True
False
explanation: False per the banks. FCOM: oil quantity is a secondary engine indication on the DU; physical checking is done at the engine oil tank (sight gauge on the engine), not in the main wheel well. · FCOM 7.20.1

question: At what rotational speed is the Start Lever moved to the IDLE position?
options: Starter cutout speed - 56% N1.
Max Motoring - 25% N2.
Max motoring - 56% N1.
Starter cutout speed - 56% N2.
explanation: When the engine accelerates to 25% N2 or max motoring, the start lever is moved to IDLE (opens spar and engine fuel valves, ignition on). Starter cutout is at about 56% N2. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: Can reverse thrust be deployed if the aircraft has not touched down?
options: Yes, if the forward thrust levers are in the idle position and both radio altimeters sense less than 10 feet RA.
Yes, if the forward thrust levers are in the idle position and either radio altimeter senses less than 10 feet RA.
No, the air/ground safety sensor must be in the ground mode and either radio altimeter senses zero ft RA
No, the air/ground safety sensor must be in the ground mode
explanation: The reverser can deploy when EITHER radio altimeter senses less than 10 ft, OR the air/ground sensor is in ground mode. Reverse levers are mechanically blocked until forward levers are at idle. · FCOM 7.20.13

question: During an in-flight start the EGT Start Limit Redline is never displayed.
options: True
False
explanation: False. During in-flight starts the EGT start limit redline can be shown, depending on the EEC start logic. If both redlines show, the start limit redline is the in-flight start limit. · FCOM 7.20.10

question: During an In-flight start, if a wet start is detected, when will the EEC turn off ignition and fuel to the engine?
options: No in-flight abnormal start protection.
As soon as the wet start is detected by the EEC.
15 seconds after start lever moved to Idle.
10 seconds after start lever moved to Idle.
explanation: Abnormal start protection is for GROUND STARTS ONLY. In flight there is no automatic wet/hot start cutoff — the crew monitors. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: If the forward thrust lever is reduced to idle while the EEC is in the soft alternate mode, what is the result?
options: The EEC will remain in the soft alternate mode, the ALTN switch illuminates and the ON indication remains visible.
The EEC enters the hard alternate mode, the ALTN switch remains illuminated and the ON indication remains visible.
The EEC enters the hard alternate mode, the ALTN switch remains illuminated and the ON indication is blanked.
Approach idle is commanded by the EEC.
explanation: Retarding the thrust lever to idle in soft alternate puts the EEC into hard alternate; the ALTN switch stays illuminated and ON remains visible. (Manual ALTN blanks ON.) · FCOM 7.20.4

question: In flight, with the APU as the only source of electrical power; if the electrical load exceeds the APU Generator design limit, the galley busses and the IFE busses are the first to be automatically shed.
options: True
False
explanation: False. In flight with the APU as the only source, all galley AND main busses are shed automatically; only if the load still exceeds limits are the IFE busses shed too. · FCOM 7.30.4

question: Moving the battery switch to OFF automatically shuts down the APU:
options: on the ground or in the air
on the ground only
never
in the air only
explanation: Moving the battery switch to OFF on the ground or in the air automatically shuts down the APU (power loss to the electronic control unit). · FCOM 7.30.2

question: Of the four lights located on the APU control panel, which light will NOT cause an automatic shutdown of the APU when it illuminates?
options: MAINT
LOW OIL PRESSURE
OVERSPEED
FAULT
explanation: Protective shutdown shows one of three lights: FAULT, OVERSPEED or LOW OIL PRESSURE. MAINT is only a maintenance indication — no shutdown. · FCOM 7.30.3 / 7.15.8

question: On a ground start, if a Wet start is detected, when will the EEC turn off ignition and shut off fuel to the engine.
options: 15 seconds after the start lever moved to Idle
10 seconds after start lever moved to idle
15 seconds after throttle lever moved to Idle
The EEC does not turn off ignition and fuel - this is a crew responsibility.
explanation: Ground start: if a wet start (no EGT rise) is detected, the EEC turns off ignition and shuts off fuel 15 seconds after the start lever is moved to IDLE. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: The APU can operate and supply bleed air only, up to the aircraft operating ceiling of 41, 000 feet.
options: True
False
explanation: False. The APU starts and operates up to the airplane maximum certified altitude and can supply electrical power AND bleed air (bleed for one pack in flight, two on the ground). · FCOM 7.30.1

question: The APU engine air inlet door is located at the rear of the fuselage just below and forward of the left horizontal stabiliser.
options: True
False
explanation: False. The APU air inlet door is on the RIGHT side of the fuselage. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: The APU switch to OFF position has an automatic shutdown delay of:
options: 120 seconds
60 seconds
135 seconds
30 seconds
explanation: APU switch OFF: trips the APU generator, closes the APU bleed valve, GEN OFF BUS light goes out; shutdown occurs automatically after 60 seconds (cooling). · FCOM 7.30.3

question: The engine start valve closes and the START VALVE OPEN alert on the upper DU extinguishes at approximately ?
explanation: At starter cutout (about 56% N2) the start switch returns to OFF, the bleed valve returns to the selected position and the start valve closes (START VALVE OPEN alert goes out). · FCOM 7.20.9

question: The REVERSER light located on the aft overhead panel illuminated during a normal reverse sequence indicates ?
options: A normal indication if the light extinguishes 10 seconds after the thrust reverser is commanded to stow.
One or more faults in the system if the light illuminates at the start of the sequence.
A normal indication until the reverser sleeves are stowed at the completion of the reverse sequence.
The isolation valve has failed to open and the thrust reverser control valve has not moved to the deploy position.
explanation: REVERSER light: illuminates when the reverser is commanded to stow and goes out 10 s later when the isolation valve closes — normal. If on for more than about 12 s, a malfunction (MASTER CAUTION + ENG). · FCOM 7.20.14

question: What condition causes the A/T LIM indication to illuminate WHITE on the upper centre display panel?
options: The FMC is not providing the A/T system with N1 limit values
The A/T system is no longer sending an EGT limit values to the FMC.
The Forward Thrust Levers have been advanced to the fully forward position by the A/T system.
The Forward Thrust Levers have been manually advanced to the fully forward position.
explanation: A/T LIM (white): the FMC is not providing N1 limit values to the A/T; the A/T uses a degraded N1 thrust limit from the related EEC. Replaces the thrust mode display. · FCOM 7.11.4

question: What effect does moving the N1 SET Outer Knob to BOTH have on A/T operation?
options: Causes the A/T system to set a reduce Max Thrust bug for both engines.
Has no effect on the A/T system operation.
Causes the A/T system to disengage.
Causes the A/T system to set an increased Max Thrust bug for both engines.
explanation: N1 SET outer knob BOTH: both reference N1 bugs/readouts are set manually with the inner knob — it has no effect on A/T operation. · FCOM 7.11.4

question: What is the indication of an impending oil filter bypass due to contamination?
options: Illumination of the Master Caution and ENG system annunciator lights.
Illumination of the FILTER BYPASS warning light on the Fuel Panel.
An amber OIL FILTER BYPASS alert illuminates on the upper display unit.
An amber OIL FILTER BYPASS alert illuminates on the upper display unit and illumination of the Master Caution and ENG system annunciator lights.
explanation: Amber OIL FILTER BYPASS alert on the upper DU: impending bypass of the scavenge oil filter (blinking during the alert period). · FCOM 7.11.9 / 7.20.7

question: What is the indication that the thrust reverser sleeves have moved from the stowed position and have reached the deployed position?
options: The amber REV thrust reverser indication located on the upper display unit illuminates.
The REVERSER light on the aft overhead panel illuminates.
The REV thrust reverser indication located on the upper display unit illuminates green.
The reverse thrust lever may be moved beyond the interlock position.
explanation: REV on the upper DU: amber = reverser moved from the stowed position; green = reverser deployed. · FCOM 7.11.6

question: When GRD is selected and the eng start switch is selected to either 1 or 2, how are the crew alerted to the start valve opening?
options: The blue START VALVE light illuminates bright blue then goes dim blue once the start valve is fully open.
The only indication is the N2 gauge increasing to Max Motoring (25%).
An amber START VALVE OPEN alert is displayed on the lower DU.
A START VALVE OPEN alert is displayed on the upper DU.
explanation: When the start valve opens, an amber START VALVE OPEN alert is shown on the upper DU (blinking = uncommanded opening). · FCOM 7.11.8 / 7.20.9

question: Where in the engine oil system is the oil filter located?
options: In the engine oil supply after leaving the oil tank
In the engine bearings supply line
In the oil tank
In the engine oil return line before reaching the oil tank
explanation: Oil returns to the tank via scavenge pumps through the scavenge filter, then the main engine oil cooler (fuel cooled), before reaching the tank. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: Which bus powers the right igniter plug?
options: DC Bus 1
AC Transfer Bus 1
The AC Standby Bus
AC Transfer Bus 2
explanation: Left igniter: associated AC transfer bus. Right igniter: AC standby bus. · FCOM 7.20.10

question: Which indication is NOT supplied to the Secondary Engine Indications on the lower DI via the EEC?
options: Oil temperature
Oil pressure
Fuel flow
Oil quantity
explanation: When the EEC is not powered, N1, N2, oil quantity and engine vibration are displayed directly from the engine sensors — so oil quantity does not come via the EEC (oil pressure/temperature and fuel flow do). · FCOM 7.20.2

question: A TA symbol showing on the ND has, alongside it, a down arrow and "-07". This indicates:
options: The traffic is above your position
The traffic is descending at a minimum of 500fpm
The traffic is another 737
The traffic is below your position but is ascending at 700fpm
explanation: -07 = traffic 700 ft below. The arrow shows the traffic is climbing or descending at 500 fpm or more (no arrow below 500 fpm); down arrow = descending. · FCOM 10.41.22

question: After normal engine start, what should be done if the DUAL BLEED light is illuminated:
options: Pack switch, affected side, OFF
Isolation valve to close, bleed air switch(es) affected side off
Engine start lever affected side to cut off
Place the APU bleed switch to OFF
explanation: DUAL BLEED: APU bleed valve open together with an engine bleed (possible backpressure of the APU). After engine start the APU BLEED switch goes OFF and the light extinguishes. · FCOM 2.10 / NP After Start

question: After starting the engine and it achieving Stabilised Idle (59% N2), a low oil pressure condition would be identified by the amber LOW OIL PRESSURE annunciation on the upper DU, and the Lower DU displaying OIL PRESS Pointer in the Amber band.
options: True
False
explanation: False. The oil pressure amber band varies with N2 above 65% N2 and is NOT displayed below 65% N2 — so at ~59% idle you would not see the pointer in an amber band. · FCOM 7.11.13

question: An amber Display Source Annunciation below the speed tape indicates:
options: A single EFIS control panel has been selected as the source for all six DUs
The altimeter is receiving inputs from a source other than the ADIRU and is unreliable
A single DEU has been manually or automatically selected to all six display units
A non-dispatchable CDS fault has occurred
explanation: If the displays are automatically or manually switched to a single DEU source, a DSPLY SOURCE annunciation appears on both PFDs. · FCOM 10.21.2

question: An auto relight protection is provided by EEC activating both igniters when a flameout is detected and there is a rapid uncommanded decrease in:
options: Fuel flow
N1 or N1 below idle
EGT
N2 or N2 below idle
explanation: Auto-relight: the EEC activates both igniters when a flameout is detected — an uncommanded rapid decrease in N2, or N2 below idle RPM. · FCOM 7.20.10

question: Approach idle is selected in flight by the EECs under what normal conditions(s)?
options: Landing gear extended
Below 15,000 feet
Flaps are in landing configuration or engine anti-ice is ON
Below 2,000 feet
explanation: Approach idle in flight if: cowl anti-ice ON for either engine, OR below 19,000 ft MSL with main gear down, OR flaps in approach configuration (≥ 15). Maintained until after touchdown. · FCOM 7.20.5

question: APU cooling air:
options: Enters through the air inlet door
Is supplied by the air conditioning packs
Enters through the ram air system
Enters through a cooling air inlet above the APU exhaust outlet
explanation: APU cooling air enters through a cooling air inlet above the APU exhaust outlet, circulates through the compartment and oil cooler, and vents through the exhaust. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: At what point during a normal start is the EEC supplied with electrical power?
options: When the engines accelerates to a speed greater than 15% N2
When the engines accelerates to a speed greater than 25% N2 or max motoring
When the engine start switch is positioned to GRD
When the battery switch is placed ON
explanation: Positioning the engine start switch to GRD supplies electrical power to the EEC and displays pointers/digits for all engine parameters. · FCOM 7.20.2

question: Both, ON and ALTN visible on EEC, indicate EEC has automatically changed to soft alternate mode, and remains in soft mode until:
options: Thrust lever retarded to idle or manually selecting ALTN with EEC switch on AFT overhead panel
Thrust levers are both advanced to full throttle
The N2 of any engine drops below 57%
The N1 of any engine drops below 57%
explanation: Soft alternate remains until hard alternate is entered by retarding the thrust lever to idle or manually selecting ALTN with the EEC switch (aft overhead). · FCOM 7.20.4

question: Can an engine be started if the aircraft does not have AC power applied?
options: Only if the APU is running
No
Yes, even if the battery switch is placed OFF
Yes, provided an air source is available for starting
explanation: Yes — a battery start is possible with a pneumatic source: the start switch uses battery power to open the start valve, and the EEC is powered by its alternator once N2 exceeds 15%. · FCOM 7.20.3 / 7.20.9

question: During battery start, when does the EEC start to operate?
options: When the start switch is positioned to GND
When the fuel cutoff lever is positioned to IDLE
explanation: Battery start with no power: only N1, N2 and oil quantity are shown. The EEC is not powered until N2 exceeds 15%, then it energizes and all parameters appear. · FCOM 7.20.3

question: During engine start, the EGT exceeds the starting limit, when does the EEC automatically turns off ignition and shuts off fuel to the engine?
options: In the air only
On the ground only
Never
On the ground and in the air
explanation: Abnormal start protection (impending hot start, stall, EGT start limit exceedance, wet start) is for ground starts only. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: During primary charge cycle operation, battery voltage can be as high as:
options: 40 volts
115 volts
30 volts
400 volts
explanation: Battery voltage range is 22–30 V; the charger runs a primary charge cycle then reverts to constant voltage. Bank answer: up to 30 V. · FCOM 6.20.8 / 6.20.9

question: How is fuel heated prior to reaching the engine?
options: The IDG oil cooler
The main engine oil cooler.
An electrical fuel heater
The main engine oil cooler and the IDG oil cooler
explanation: After the first stage fuel pump, fuel passes through two fuel/oil heat exchangers where IDG oil and main engine oil heat the fuel. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: How is the accessory gearbox connected to the engine?
options: It is mechanically linked to the N2 rotor
It is mechanically linked to the N1 rotor
It is not connected to the engine
Through a liquid clutch mechanism
explanation: The N2 rotor (HP compressor + HP turbine) drives the engine gearboxes; the bleed-air starter is connected to the N2 rotor. · FCOM 7.20.1

question: How is the EEC affected the failure of one DEU (Display Electronic Unit) ?
options: Both EECs are rendered inoperative and the EEC ON indication extinguishes.
The EEC for the related side reverts to soft alternate mode and the ALTN switch illuminates.
Failure of a single DUE has no effect on the EECs.
Both EECs revert to soft alternate mode and the ALTN switch illuminates.
explanation: Loss of either DEU results in loss of signal to both EECs: both EEC ALTN lights illuminate and each EEC reverts to the alternate mode (prevents engines running on a single source of data). · FCOM 7.20.4

question: How is the engine fuel heated prior to entering the engine?
options: Heated by passing through engine oil heat exhanger only.
Heated by passing through IDG oil heat exchanger and engine oil heat exchanger.
Engine fuel is not heated until it is burnt in the engine combustion chamber.
Heated only by Kinetic energy imparted due to pressure increase passing through the 1st and 2nd stage engine fuel pumps.
explanation: Fuel passes through two fuel/oil heat exchangers where IDG oil and main engine oil heat it, then the fuel filter. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: How is the hard alternate mode entered?
options: It cannot be manually selected
When in normal mode, retard the thrust lever to idle
When in Soft Alternate mode, retard the thrust lever or push the EEC switch
It activates automatically when a failure occurs
explanation: Hard alternate is entered from soft alternate by retarding the thrust lever to idle, or by manually selecting ALTN with the EEC switch. · FCOM 7.20.4

question: How is the oil for each engine cooled?
options: By a main engine oil cooler using engine fuel.
By the Hydro-mechanical unit (HMU).
By an oil cooler located in the engine cowling using N1 air flow (bypass air).
By an oil cooler located within the related oil tank.
explanation: Before returning to the tank, oil passes through the main engine oil cooler where it is cooled by engine fuel. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: How many fire extinguishing bottles are there totally for engine and APU fires?
explanation: Two engine fire extinguisher bottles (either can go to either engine) plus one APU bottle = 3. (Cargo has its own bottle.) · FCOM 8.20.2 / 8.20.3

question: How many spark igniters are there on each engine?
explanation: Each engine has two igniter plugs (left: associated AC transfer bus; right: AC standby bus). · FCOM 7.20.10

question: If a crossbleed start is required during in flight starting, the X-BLEED START indication will be displayed above:
options: Above FF dial
Above N1 dial
Above N2 dial
Above EGT dial
explanation: If crossbleed starting is required in flight, X-BLD (magenta) is displayed above the N2 dial (XB on the compact display) — airspeed below that needed for a windmilling start. · FCOM 7.20.10 / 7.11.12

question: If an outboard display unit fails, the PFD is automatically displayed:
options: Never. It can only be displayed manually with the MAIN PANEL DU selectors
On the inboard display unit
On the ENGINE SECONDARY display
On the ENGINE PRIMARY display
explanation: If an outboard DU fails, the PFD is automatically displayed on the inboard DU and the outboard DU blanks. · FCOM 10.21.5

question: Illumination of amber FAULT light with the overheat detector switch in NORMAL indicates:
options: One of the detector loops for an engine has failed
One detector loop for each engine has failed
There is a fault in APU engines for cargo hold detector loops
Both detector loops for an engine have failed
explanation: FAULT with OVHT DET switch in NORMAL: both detector loops for an engine have failed. With the switch in A or B: the selected loop has failed. · FCOM 8.10.4

question: Impact fittings located in the opening of each main gear well:
options: Provide positive uplock during main gear retraction
Are intended to provide automatic braking to main gear wheels during retraction
Allows the landing gear transfer unit to use hydraulic system B pressure to raise the gear if hydraulic system A fails
Are intended to provide protection to wheel well components during gear retraction by preventing a gear with a spinning tire and loose tread from entering the wheel well
explanation: A spinning tire with loose tread impacts a fitting in the wheel well opening; that gear stops retracting and free falls back down, protecting the wheel well (gear can't be retracted until the fitting is replaced). · FCOM 14.20.1

question: In case of an engine overheat:
options: Both fire warning lights the related engine OVHT/DET system annunciator lights illuminate.
Only the related ENGINE OVERHEAT light illuminates
The Master caution OVHT/DET light will illuminate during Recall only
Both master caution lights, the related ENGINE OVERHEAT light and the OVHT/DET system annunciator lights illuminate
explanation: Engine overheat: both MASTER CAUTION lights, the OVHT/DET annunciator and the related ENG OVERHEAT light illuminate. Fire adds the bell, master FIRE WARN and the fire switch light. · FCOM 8.20.2

question: In the event of an elevator jam, an override mechanism allows:
options: Apply force against the jam will break out only the captains control column
The elevator feel and centring unit to transfer proper aerodynamic forces to the control column
Lighter than normal control forces to be used for take off and landing
The control columns to be physically separated
explanation: Control column jam: the override mechanism allows the columns to be physically separated; force breaks out either column and the free one controls the elevator. · FCOM 9.20.6

question: Once the thrust reverse auto-stow circuit is activated:
options: the thrust reversers remain in the uncommanded position
reverse thrust cannot be reselected
the isolation valve remains open and the control valve is held in the stow position
the isolation valve closes and the control valve is held in the stow position
explanation: Once auto-restow activates, the isolation valve remains open and the control valve is held in the stow position until reverse is commanded again or maintenance action is taken. · FCOM 7.20.14

question: Placing the TEST Switch, on fire protection panel to FAULT/INOP position tests:
options: The cargo extinguishing circuits
The fault detection circuits for both engines and the APU
The squib continuity
Both engines overheat detectors
explanation: FAULT/INOP test: tests the fault detector circuits for both engines and the APU (MASTER CAUTION, OVHT/DET, FAULT and APU DET INOP lights). · FCOM 8.10.1 / 8.20.8

question: Pulling up the APU fire warning switch:
options: Trips the generator control relay and breaker, arms the ssociated extinguisher and closes the bleed air valve, closes the fuel shutoff valve, and the APU inlet door
Discharges the APU fire extinguisher and closes the bleed air valve
Discharges the APU fire extinguisher
Discharges the APU fire extinguisher and shuts down the APU
explanation: APU fire switch UP: arms the APU bottle squib, closes the APU fuel shutoff valve, bleed air valve and inlet door, trips the APU generator control relay and breaker, and allows the switch to be rotated to discharge. · FCOM 8.10.2 / 8.20.4

question: Reverse thrust can be selected with the forward thrust levers in what position?
options: Forward thrust position
Maximum thrust position
Idle thrust position
Any position
explanation: Reverse thrust cannot be selected unless the related forward thrust lever is at IDLE. · FCOM 7.15.6

question: The accessory gearboxes receive drive from:
options: ENG HYD Pumps
N2 Rotor
IDG
N1 Rotor
explanation: The N2 rotor drives the engine gearboxes. · FCOM 7.20.1

question: The amber DUAL BLEED light is illuminated before starting engines. What should you do?
options: Nothing, this is normal condition before engine start
Shutdown the APU
Do not start the engines
Use a pneumatic ground cart for starting engines
explanation: Before start the APU bleed is ON with engine bleed switches ON, so DUAL BLEED is normally illuminated. Thrust must be limited to idle while it is on; it goes out when the APU bleed is switched OFF after start. · FCOM 2.10 / NP

question: The APU can supply both transfer busses:
options: on the ground or in the air
in the air only
on the ground only
never
explanation: The APU generator can power both AC transfer busses on the ground or in flight. · FCOM 7.30.1 / 6.20.1

question: The APU may be used as a pneumatic source up to:
options: 25,000 feet
17,000 feet
41,000 feet
10,000 feet
explanation: APU limits (EASA): bleed + electrical max 10,000 ft; bleed only max 17,000 ft; electrical only max 41,000 ft. · FCOM L.10.7

question: The APU may be used as electrical and bleed source simultaneously up to:
explanation: APU bleed + electrical load simultaneously: max 10,000 ft (bleed only 17,000 ft, electrical only 41,000 ft). · FCOM L.10.7

question: The APU starts, operates and can supply electrical power alone up to:
explanation: The APU starts and operates up to the airplane maximum certified altitude; electrical load only: max 41,000 ft. · FCOM L.10.7 / 7.30.1

question: The B737-800 has no In-Flight Abnormal Start Protection.
options: True
False
explanation: True. Abnormal start protection is for ground starts only — it does not function during in-flight starts. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: The blue APU MAINT light means that:
options: APU has to be shut down manually in flight or on ground
APU shuts down automatically
APU has to be shut down manually on ground only
APU may be operated
explanation: MAINT (blue): APU maintenance problem exists — the APU may still be operated. Disarmed with the APU switch OFF. · FCOM 7.15.8

question: The decision height (DH) display on the CDS is set:
options: Independently by each pilot using his/her EFIS control panel
By using the DH selector knob on the forward instrument panel
By entering the desired DH on the FMC CDU APPROACH REFERENCE page
Automatically when APPROACH is selected on the MCP panel
explanation: Each pilot sets the minimums on his/her own EFIS control panel (MINS selector, RADIO or BARO). With BOTH ON 1 or 2, one EFIS panel controls both sides. · FCOM 10.11.24 / 10.11.31

question: The display selector on the IRS Display Unit (ISDU) is moved to position HDG/STS during alignment. What is shown in the right window.
options: Right window displays wind speed
Right window displays minutes remaining until alignment is complete
Right window display true track
Right window displays ground speed
explanation: ISDU HDG/STS: left window true heading; right window maintenance status codes — during alignment, minutes remaining until alignment is complete (shows 15 until 14 minutes remain). · FCOM 11.10.18

question: The EEC automatically selects approach idle in flight anytime:
options: Flaps are in the landing configuration and thrust lever angle is above 34 degrees for either engine
The aircraft descends below 15,000 feet
Flaps are in the landing configuration or engine anti-ice is ON for either engine
Flaps are in the landing configuration or engine start switches are placed to CONT or FLT
explanation: Approach idle in flight: cowl anti-ice ON for either engine, OR below 19,000 ft MSL with main gear down, OR flaps in approach configuration (≥ 15). · FCOM 7.20.5

question: The EEC provides redline overspeed protection for:
options: N2 only in both the normal and alternate modes
N1 only in both the normal and alternate modes
N1 and N2 in both the normal and alternate modes
N1 and N2 in the normal mode only
explanation: The EEC provides N1 and N2 redline overspeed protection in both normal and alternate modes. It does NOT protect EGT — the crew must observe the EGT limit. · FCOM 7.20.5

question: The flight spoilers will start to extend on the down going wing with a control wheel deflection at approximately:
options: 15 degrees
20 degrees
5 degrees
10 degrees
explanation: When the control wheel is displaced more than approximately 10°, flight spoiler deflection is initiated (on the wing with up aileron). · FCOM 9.20.4

question: The LOCKOUT PIN is installed in the steering depressurisation valve. What does this do?
options: It locks the nose wheel in center position
Allows aircraft pushback or towing without depressurising the hydraulic systems
Bypasses the standby hydraulic system
It locks the pedals in neutral position
explanation: The lockout pin in the towing lever depressurizes nose wheel steering, allowing pushback or towing without depressurizing the hydraulic systems. · FCOM 14.20.3

question: The number of ground spoilers on each wing are:
explanation: System A powers all four ground spoilers, two on the upper surface of each wing. (Four flight spoilers per wing.) · FCOM 9.20.16

question: The number of LE slats located on each wing are:
explanation: Leading edge devices: four slats and two Krueger LE flaps per wing (slats 1–8 in total). · FCOM 9.20.21

question: The thrust reverser may be deployed:
options: In flight with radio height less than 30 feet
When the air/ground sensor is in the ground mode
In flight when the thrust lever is at idle
Always in flight with throttles at idle
explanation: Reverser deploys when either radio altimeter senses less than 10 ft, or the air/ground safety sensor is in ground mode; forward levers must be at idle. · FCOM 7.20.13

question: To receive NAV and ADF voice and range audio:
options: set the filter switch to BOTH
press the TEST button on the VHF panel
set the filter switch to V
set the filter switch to R
explanation: ACP filter switch: V = voice; B (Both) = NAV/ADF voice and range audio; R = range (station identifier code) only. · FCOM 5.10.6

question: What abnormal start protection is available?
options: On the ground only and for hot, wet, stall and EGT exceedances
On the ground and in flight for hot, wet, stall and EGT exceedances
In flight only for hot, wet, stall and EGT exceedances
None
explanation: Abnormal start protection (ground starts only): impending hot start, engine stall, EGT start limit exceedance and wet start. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: What are the indications that the engine starter has disengaged?
options: Start switch rotates to FLT, N1 rpm 17-20% and N2 rpm stabilized
The fuel LOW PRESSURE lights extinguish with N1 rpm 56%
The start switch automatically returns to OFF, and the START VALVE OPEN light extinguishes
An immediate increase in the N1 indication due to closure of the compressor bleed valves
explanation: At starter cutout (about 56% N2) the start switch returns to OFF, the bleed valve returns to the selected position and the start valve closes (START VALVE OPEN alert extinguishes). · FCOM 7.20.9

question: What does a Red Box around an N1 RPM Digital Readout mean when the aircraft is on the ground and the engine has been shut down?
options: The N1 RPM display has suffered a malfunction in flight.
An operating limit is currently being exceeded. The box will no longer show when the limit is not being exceeded.
The N1 Limit Bug has been set manually.
An exceedance has occurred at some point in the flight.
explanation: On the ground after engine shutdown, a red box around the N1 readout indicates that an in-flight exceedance occurred. · FCOM 7.11.5

question: What is the maximum authorised thrust reduction below any certified rating?
explanation: Assumed temperature reduced thrust: maximum reduction authorized is 25% below any certified rating (not with contaminated runways, etc.). · FCOM 11.32.3

question: What is the recommended value of engine RPM that the engine must accelerate to prior to moving the engine start lever to the IDLE position?
options: 56% N2 or maximum motoring speed
25% N2 or maximum motoring speed
At the first indication of N1 rotation
25% N1 or maximum motoring speed
explanation: Move the start lever to IDLE at 25% N2 or max motoring. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: What modes can the EECs operate in?
options: Normal and Degraded
On and Degraded
On, Soft Alternate and Hard Alternate
Normal, Soft Alternate and Hard Alternate
explanation: EEC modes: normal, soft alternate and hard alternate. · FCOM 7.20.4

question: What start protection do the engines have in flight?
options: N1 overspeed only
EGT exceedance only
The engines have no engine start protection in flight
Wet start protection only
explanation: Abnormal start protection does not function during in-flight starts — no start protection in flight. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: When are the NO SMOKING signs illuminated?
options: The NO SMOKING signs are always illuminated
When the landing gear is up
When the flaps are up and above 1000 RA
When the landing gear and flaps are up
explanation: YF501–YW164: the NO SMOKING signs are permanently illuminated (switch placarded INOP). · FCOM 1.40.5 / 1.30.9

question: When does the amber DUAL BLEED Light illuminate
options: When the APU bleed valve is open and the No 2 engine bleed switch is on and the isolation valve is closed
When the APU bleed valve is open and the No 1 engine bleed switch is off
When the APU bleed valve is open
When the APU bleed valve is open and the No 1 engine bleed switch is on
explanation: DUAL BLEED: APU bleed valve open and engine No.1 BLEED switch ON, or engine No.2 BLEED switch ON with the APU bleed valve AND isolation valve open. · FCOM 2.10.2

question: When does the OIL FILTER BYPASS alert illuminate on the upper display unit?
options: Once the oil filter bypass has opened and oil is bypassing the filter.
If the oil filter bypass has failed in the closed position and oil pressure is beginning to increase.
Illuminates to warn that the oil filter is partially blocked
when an oil pump has failed
explanation: Prior to the oil bypassing the saturated scavenge filter, the OIL FILTER BYPASS alert illuminates — i.e. the filter is becoming blocked (impending bypass). · FCOM 7.20.7

question: When selecting reverse thrust, when can the reverse thrust levers be increased beyond the idle detent?
options: On main wheel spin up greater than 60kts
Once the reverser sleeves approach the fully deployed position
Immediately after selecting reverse idle
When the air ground sensor senses the ground mode
explanation: An interlock blocks the reverse lever at reverse idle until the sleeves approach the deployed position (more than 60% deployed); REV turns green and the lever can be raised to detent No.2. · FCOM 7.20.13 / 7.15.5

question: When the EEC is not powered, following engine indications are displayed directly from the engine sensors:
options: Fuel flow and oil pressure
Oil temperature, pressure and quantity indications
Oil temperature and engine vibration
Oil quantity and engine vibration
explanation: With the EEC unpowered, N1, N2, oil quantity and engine vibration come directly from engine sensors. · FCOM 7.20.2

question: Where in the engine oil system is the main engine oil cooler located?
options: In the engine oil supply after leaving the oil tank
In the engine oil return line before reaching the oil tank
In the engine accessory section
In the oil tank
explanation: After the scavenge pumps and filter, oil passes through the main engine oil cooler (fuel cooled) before returning to the tank. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: Which bus powers the left igniter plug on the number one engine?
options: AC Transfer Bus 1
AC Transfer Bus 2
DC Bus 1
The AC Standby Bus
explanation: Left igniter = associated AC transfer bus (engine 1 → AC transfer bus 1). Right igniter = AC standby bus. · FCOM 7.20.10

question: Which part of the engine does the starter motor drive?
options: The HP rotor (N2)
To the APU
Directly to the N1 rotor via a reduction gearbox
The front fan
explanation: The bleed-air-powered starter motor is connected to the N2 (HP) rotor. · FCOM 7.20.1

question: Which window(s) are heated with the LEFT FWD WINDOW HEAT switch ON?
options: L1 only
explanation: FWD WINDOW HEAT switches control window No.1; SIDE switches control window No.2. Window No.3 is not electrically heated. · FCOM 3.20.2

question: Whilst on the ground with wing anti-ice selected ON, advancing the thrust levers for take-off will cause:
options: Both wing anti-ice valves to close and the WING ANTI-ICE switches to remain ON
Both wing anti-ice valves to close and the WING ANTI-ICE switches to change to OFF
Both wing anti-ice valves to open and the WING ANTI-ICE switches to remain ON
Both wing anti-ice valves to open and the WING ANTI-ICE switches change to OFF
explanation: On the ground, wing anti-ice valves close if either engine's thrust is above the takeoff warning setting; the switch stays ON (it trips OFF at liftoff on some airplanes). · FCOM 3.10.6

question: Why is the fuel heated prior to entering the fuel filter?
options: To prevent ice crystals in the fuel from blocking the fuel filter.
To make the engine easier to start
To improve the operation of the fuel nozzles
To increase the combustion temperature
explanation: Fuel is heated by the IDG and engine oil heat exchangers before the fuel filter, to prevent ice crystals from blocking the filter. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: Why must the battery remain switched on for at least a minute after shutting down the APU?
options: DC Power is needed to run the APU Fuel Pump
The APU uses DC power to close the APU Air Inlet Door after the cooling cycle is complete
The IRSs need DC power for 30 seconds after losing AC power to shut down properly
The Fire Extinguisher for the APU can't be used if the battery has been switched off.
explanation: After shutdown (60 s cooling), the APU air inlet door closes automatically — it needs DC power, so keep the battery ON until the door has closed. · FCOM 7.15.8 / 7.30.3

question: With ENGINE START switch in OFF, automatic ignition will occur:
options: If ENG ANTI-ICE is selected ON
Will never occur
If N1 is between 57% and 50%
If N2 is between 57% and 50%
explanation: Start switch OFF: both igniters are activated (start lever IDLE) when an uncommanded rapid decrease in N2 occurs, N2 is between 57% and 50%, or in flight N2 between idle and 5%. · FCOM 7.15.1

question: With the APU running, how can it be stopped immediately?
options: Move the APU START switch to OFF.
Pull the APU Fire Switch
Select Ground Power On
Switch off all AC powered fuel pumps
explanation: The APU switch OFF gives a 60 s cooling delay. Pulling the APU fire switch closes the APU fuel shutoff valve immediately (also bleed valve, inlet door, generator). · FCOM 8.10.2

question: With the APU running, how can it be stopped immediately?
options: Rotate APU FIRE switch
Switch the battery off.
All of the above.
Move the APU START switch to OFF.
explanation: Moving the battery switch to OFF automatically shuts down the APU (power loss to the ECU) — immediately. APU switch OFF has a 60 s cooling delay. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: With the AUTO BRAKE select switch at RTO, autobraking is initiated when:
options: Wheel speed 90 knots or more and thrust levers at IDLE
Automatically when thrust levers are set to IDLE
Wheel speed 60 knots or less and thrust levers at IDLE
AUTO BRAKE ARM light on, wheel speed 90 knots or more and thrust levers at IDLE
explanation: RTO: maximum braking applied when the thrust levers are retarded to idle at or above 88 kt wheel speed (the option says 90 — closest answer). · FCOM 14.10.4

question: With the CONTROL PANEL select switch on the Displays Source Panel in the BOTH ON 2 position:
options: ADIRU inputs for both the L and R ADIRU are being received from the First Officers pitot probe
DEU 2 controls all six display units
The First Officers EFIS control panel is supplying identical inputs to the Captains and First Captains displays
Both pilots displays are using the No 2 DEU
explanation: CONTROL PANEL BOTH ON 2: both pilots' displays are set to the First Officer's EFIS control panel. (DEU selection is the separate DISPLAYS SOURCE switch.) · FCOM 10.21.2 / 10.16.6

question: With the fuel pumps off, where does the APU fuel supply come from?
options: Left side of the Fuel Manifold.
No 1 Main Tank.
Suction fed from Centre Tank.
From tapping in left engine supply line.
explanation: With no AC fuel pumps operating, APU fuel is suction fed from main tank No.1. · FCOM 7.30.1

question: All window heat is selected ON. The green window heat ON light for the Right Side Window extinguishes. The likely reason is:
options: system is at correct temperature
the window heat has not yet reached the required temperature
the window heat has failed
the window heat is taking power from another source
explanation: Window heat ON light extinguished with the switch ON = window at correct temperature (or system failed/switch OFF). Normally it cycles as the controller holds temperature. · FCOM 3.10.1

question: An amber CDS FAULT in the left lower corner of PFD indicates:
options: A dispatchable CDS FAULT has occurred on the ground before staring second engine
A dispatchable CDS fault (comes on 10 seconds after landing)
A non-dispatchable fault has occurred after starting both engines
A non-dispatchable fault has occurred on the ground before starting second engine
explanation: CDS FAULT (amber): a non-dispatchable CDS fault — shown on the ground only, prior to start of the second engine. CDS MAINT (white) = dispatchable fault. · FCOM 10.11.30

question: An Amber PACK light illumination during Master Caution recall, that extinguishes when master caution is reset, indicates:
options: Failure of both standby pack controllers
Failure of either primary or standby pack controller
Failure of either left or right standby controller
Failure of the zone temp controller
explanation: PACK light during Master Caution recall (extinguishes on reset) = failure of either the primary or standby pack control. Steady = pack trip off or failure of both controls. · FCOM 2.10.10

question: An auto-relight capability is provided for flame-out protection. Whenever the EEC detects an engine flameout, both igniters are activated. A flameout is detected when?
options: An uncommanded rapid decrease in N1 occurs
An uncommanded rapid decrease in N1 occurs or N2 is below idle RPM
An uncommanded rapid decrease in N2 occurs or N2 is below idle RPM
An uncommanded rapid decrease in N1 occurs or N2 is below idle RPM or EGT is below 200°C
explanation: Flameout detected when an uncommanded rapid decrease in N2 occurs or N2 is below idle RPM — then both igniters are activated. · FCOM 7.20.10

question: Approach idle is maintained?
options: Until after touchdown (60 KIAS)
Until Reverser selection
Until 84 KIAS
Until after touchdown, when ground minimum idle is selected
explanation: Approach idle is maintained until after touchdown, when ground minimum idle is selected. · FCOM 7.20.5

question: Approach idle is selected in flight by the EECs under what normal conditions(s)?
options: Below 19,000 ft MSL - Main landing gear is down and locked AND flaps are in the approach configuration (greater than or equal to 15)
Below 2,000 feet RA.
Below 19,000 feet MSL.
Cowl thermal anti-ice switch is ON for either engine.
explanation: Approach idle if ANY of: cowl anti-ice ON for either engine; below 19,000 ft MSL AND either main gear down; or flaps in approach configuration (≥ 15). Option A wrongly needs gear AND flaps. · FCOM 7.20.5

question: APU operation requires the following?
options: APU fire switch on the overheat/fire panel must be IN All of the above
APU fire control handle on the APU ground control panel must be IN
Battery switch must be ON
All of the answers are correct
explanation: APU operation requires: APU fire switch IN, APU fire control handle on the ground control panel IN, battery switch ON. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: Below what altitude will the approach idle schedule begin if the EECs lose flap or anti-ice signals?
options: Below 15,000 feet MSL
Below 19,000 feet MSL
Below 2,500 feet RA
Approach idle must be manually selected by the crew in these circumstances
explanation: If a fault prevents the EEC receiving flap or main gear position signals, the approach idle schedule begins below 19,000 ft MSL. · FCOM 7.20.5

question: During a battery engine start:
options: Only oil pressure and engine vibration are available prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
The EEC is not powered until the engine accelerates to a speed greater than 15% N2
Only N1, N2, oil quantity and engine vibration are available prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
Only round dials are visible for engine indications prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
explanation: Battery start with no power: only N1, N2 and oil quantity available; the EEC is not powered until N2 exceeds 15%. · FCOM 7.20.3

question: During a normal engine start, which of the following statements is true?
options: Only round dials are visible for engine indications prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
Only N1, N2, oil quantity indications are available until the engine accelerates to a speed greater than 15% N2
Only oil pressure and engine vibration are available prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
Only N1, N2, oil quantity and engine vibration are available prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
explanation: Before the start switch goes to GRD the EEC is unpowered, so only N1, N2, oil quantity and engine vibration are displayed (directly from sensors). · FCOM 7.20.2

question: During a normal engine start:
options: Only oil pressure and engine vibration are available prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
Only round dials are visible for engine indications prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
The EEC is not powered until the engine accelerates to a speed greater than 15% N2
Only N1, N2, oil quantity and engine vibration are available prior to placing the engine start switch to GRD
explanation: Before GRD: only N1, N2, oil quantity and vibration. GRD powers the EEC and shows all parameters. · FCOM 7.20.2

question: During alternate brake operation, the following protection is provided:
options: Skid, locked wheel and hydraulic plane only
None of the above
Skid and hydraulic plane only
Skid, locked wheel, touchdown and hydroplane
explanation: Both normal and alternate brake systems provide skid, locked wheel, touchdown and hydroplane protection (alternate on wheel pairs). · FCOM 14.20.4

question: During an impending hot start the flashing white box surrounding EGT digital read out resets:
options: When the start lever is moved to CUT OFF or engine reaches idle N2
Engine reaches idle N1
At starter cutout
When the EGT is stabilized
explanation: Impending hot start or stall (ground start): the white box around the EGT readout flashes; it resets when the start lever is moved to CUTOFF or the engine reaches idle N2. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: During APU operation, fuel is automatically heated to prevent icing
options: True
False
explanation: True — during APU operation, fuel is automatically heated to prevent icing. · FCOM 7.30.1

question: During APU start, EGT may fluctuate between 0° and 1100°C before normal rise, and the LOW OIL PRESSURE light may cycle several times. These are normal indications and do not affect the start. EGT monitoring is not required.
options: True
False
explanation: True. During the APU start cycle EGT may fluctuate 0–1100°C before the normal rise and LOW OIL PRESSURE may cycle; no adverse effect, and it is not necessary to monitor EGT during start. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: During engine ground start, how long before the EEC detects a Wet Start and shuts off ignition and fuel if there is no rise in EGT after the start lever is moved to IDLE?
options: Until starter cut out
10 seconds
15 seconds
20 seconds
explanation: Wet start (no EGT rise): the EEC turns off ignition and fuel 15 seconds after the start lever is moved to IDLE (ground starts). · FCOM 7.20.9

question: During engine start the maximum time allowance for EGT indication after start lever is moved to idle is:
options: 10 seconds
20 seconds
15 seconds
Unit starter cut out
explanation: RYR NP: accomplish ABORTED ENGINE START if there is no increase in EGT within 15 seconds of raising the start lever to IDLE (same as the EEC wet start logic). One bank says 10 s — the RYR FCOM says 15. · FCOM NP.21.50 / 7.20.9

question: During normal operation with the OVHT DET Switch in NORMAL, an alert is initiated if:
options: Only FIRE can be detected
Loop A is sensing a FIRE or OVHT
Loop B is sensing a FIRE or OVHT
Both loop A and B is sensing a FIRE or OVHT
explanation: With OVHT DET in NORMAL, both loops must sense the fire or overheat to give an alert. If one loop fails it is automatically deselected and the other works alone. · FCOM 8.20.1

question: Each engine has two igniter plugs. The EEC arms the igniter plug(s) selected by the ignition select switch. The Left igniter plug receives power from the DC Standby bus while the Right igniter plug receives power from the AC standby bus
options: True
False
explanation: False. Left igniter: associated AC TRANSFER bus (not DC standby). Right igniter: AC standby bus. · FCOM 7.20.10

question: Engine oil pressure is in the yellow band at take off thrust. Which of the following is true
options: Acceptable, no action is necessary
Do not take off
Normal, but requires continuous monitoring of the oil pressure
Normal, but requires continuous monitoring of the oil temperature
explanation: Amber oil pressure = caution range. At takeoff thrust an amber-band oil pressure is not acceptable for departure — bank answer: do not take off. · FCOM 7.11.13

question: Following an unpressurised takeoff, when is the first engine Bleed Switch positioned to ON?
options: After the gear is up and obstacle clearance has been achieved
Prior to 400 feet above the ground
At not less than 400 feet, and prior to 2000 feet above field elevation
After passing through 2000 feet above the ground
explanation: No engine bleed (unpressurized) takeoff: at not less than 400 ft and prior to 2,000 ft above field elevation, engine No.2 BLEED switch ON (then packs, then engine 1 after cabin pressure stabilizes). · FCOM SP.2.4

question: How can you tell if an engine EEC is operating in Alternate Mode?
options: The N1 indication will flash amber
The N2 indication will have a white box around it.
The amber "ALTN" caption is illuminated on the related EEC mode switch
All indications for that engine will turn amber on the upper DU
explanation: Amber ALTN in view on the EEC switch = EEC in alternate mode (automatic or manual; ON blank if manual). · FCOM 7.15.4

question: If a wet start is detected, the EEC will automatically turn off ignition and shut off fuel to the engine:
options: 15 seconds after the start valve opens during ground starts
10 seconds on the ground or 30 seconds in flight after the start lever is moved to idle
no automatic shutdown is provided for a wet start
15 seconds after the start lever is moved to idle during ground starts
explanation: Wet start: EEC shuts off ignition and fuel 15 s after the start lever goes to IDLE — ground starts only. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: If an engine fails during flight:
options: Execution of the ENGINE OUT page disengages VNAV and all subsequent performance predictions are blanked
The ENGINE OUT page cannot be executed because engine out information is informative only
VNAV immediately disengages and cannot be re-engaged
Execution of the ENGINE OUT page disengages VNAV and all performance data must be re-entered before VNAV can be re-engaged
explanation: ENG OUT CLB/CRZ pages are advisory/information only — once selected they cannot be executed. · FCOM 11.41.33 / 11.42.30

question: If an engine start switch is in GRD and an engine start has to be aborted, what must be done before shutting down the engine?
options: Move the engine start lever to cutoff
Lift up the fire switch for the affected engine
Motor the engine for 60 seconds
Advance the thrust lever
explanation: Aborted start: start lever to CUTOFF (closes fuel and ignition), keep the start switch in GRD and motor the engine for the full 60 seconds to cool it and clear unburned fuel. · FCOM QRH ABORTED ENGINE START / NP.21.51

question: If the aircraft is at FL270, what can the APU supply?
options: AC Electrical power only
Bleed air and AC electrical power
Bleed air only
Unable to supply bleed air or AC electrical power
explanation: APU limits: bleed only up to 17,000 ft, bleed + electrical up to 10,000 ft, electrical only up to 41,000 ft. At FL270: AC electrical power only. · FCOM L.10.7

question: If the APU is running and all AC fuel pumps are operating, where will the APU draw its fuel from?
options: Left main tank
Right main tank
The tank with the greatest quantity
Centre tank
explanation: APU fuel comes from the left side of the fuel manifold. With all pumps on and fuel in the center, the center pumps (higher pressure) feed the manifold — so it's center tank fuel. · FCOM 7.30.1 / 12.20.2

question: If the Thrust Reverser Auto Restow function is operating, can the reversers be deployed normally?
options: No, can only be deployed to Detent 1
Yes.
No, can only be deployed to Detent 2
explanation: Yes. After auto-restow the isolation valve stays open and control valve at stow 'until the thrust reverser is commanded to deploy' — so normal deployment is still possible. · FCOM 7.20.14

question: If the Thrust Reversers are set to Detent Number 2, how is the engine thrust set?
options: Set automatically by the Hydromechanical Unit (HMU)
It is set automatically by the EEC
Forward movement of the thrust levers to set 70% N1
Set by Flight Control Computer No. 1
explanation: The EEC uses thrust lever inputs to automatically control forward and reverse thrust. · FCOM 7.20.3

question: Illumination of the APU DET INOP Light will cause following lights to illuminate:
options: No lights
Only OVHT/DET
Only MASTER CAUTION
Both MASTER CAUTION and OVHT/DET
explanation: APU DET INOP (amber): APU detector loop failed. MASTER CAUTION and OVHT/DET illuminate. · FCOM 8.10.4

question: In addition to the ALTN caption being illuminated for the EEC on engine number 1, what other associated warning may you see?
options: DSPLY SOURCE 1
A/T P/RST
A/P P/RST
ALT DISAGREE
explanation: One EEC in ALTN gives more thrust for the same lever position, so the levers split. The A/T disengages if the levers separate by more than 10°, and the red A/T P/RST light flashes. Keep both EECs in the same mode. · FCOM 4.20.8 / 7.15.4

question: In normal operation, what provides the A/T system with N1 limit values?
options: ADIRUs
A/T computer
AFDS
FMC
explanation: In normal operation, the FMC provides the A/T system with N1 limit values (A/T LIM = degraded limit from the EEC). · FCOM 4.20.8

question: It is recommended to operate the APU for _____ before using it as a bleed air source.
options: 20 seconds
30 seconds
60 seconds
120 seconds
explanation: Operate the APU for two full minutes before using it as a bleed air source (stabilization extends APU service life). · FCOM 7.30.3

question: Once activated, the APU DC operated fuel pump operates automatically until:
options: APU shutdown
The completion of the APU start cycle
An AC fuel pump pressurises the manifold
Once the APU is at governed speed, ready to accept a load
explanation: The APU DC fuel pump runs during start/operation until an AC fuel pump pressurizes the manifold (bank answer). NP: position an AC fuel pump ON with AC power to extend APU fuel control unit life. · FCOM 7.30.1 / NP.21.147

question: Placing the TEST Switch in the FAULT/INOP position tests:
options: The engine overheat detectors only
The APU overheat detectors only
The fault detection circuits for both engines and the APU
The APU DET INOP Light, FAULT Light and APU BOTTLE DISCHARGE Light
explanation: FAULT/INOP: tests the fault detector circuits for both engines and the APU. · FCOM 8.10.1

question: Prior to returning to the oil tank engine oil passes through:
