options: the scavenge filter and IDG fuel-cooled oil cooler
main engine oil cooler and IDG fuel-cooled oil cooler
first stage fuel pump and main engine oil cooler
the scavenge filter and main engine oil cooler
explanation: Scavenge pumps → scavenge filter → main engine oil cooler (fuel cooled) → oil tank. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: Starter cutout speed is:
options: Approximately 56% N2
Approximately 50% N2
explanation: Starter cutout speed: approximately 56% N2. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: Starter Cutout speed is?
options: Approximately 50%
Approximately 56%
explanation: Starter cutout speed: approximately 56% N2. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: The amber LE FLAPS TRANSIT light:
options: Indicates LE slats are fully extended
Provides TE flaps asymmetry protection
Indicates all LE devices are fully extended
Is inhibited during Autoslat operation in flight
explanation: LE FLAPS TRANSIT: LE device in transit or not in programmed position. The light is inhibited during autoslat operation in flight. · FCOM 9.10.15

question: The APU OVERSPEED light illuminated indicates
options: APU RPM limit has been exceeded resulting in an automatic shutdown
The overspeed shutdown protection feature has failed a self-test during a normal APU shutdown
The overspeed shutdown protection feature has failed a self-test during a normal APU shutdown or APU RPM limit has been exceeded resulting in an automatic shutdown
None of the answers are correct
explanation: APU OVERSPEED (amber): RPM limit exceeded causing automatic shutdown, OR the overspeed shutdown protection failed its self-test during a normal shutdown. · FCOM 7.15.8

question: The APU requires an AC power supply for starting.
options: True
False
explanation: False. Power to start the APU comes from No.1 transfer bus OR the main battery; with no AC the starter generator uses battery power. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: The APU starter cycle may take up to:
options: 135 seconds
120 seconds
180 seconds
60 seconds
explanation: The APU start cycle may take as long as 120 seconds. · FCOM 7.30.3

question: The EEC automatically selects ground minimum idle, flight minimum idle and approach idle. Approach idle is selected in flight?
options: Below approximately 12000 ft
If flaps are greater than 1 or engine & wing anti-ice are ON
If flaps are in landing configuration or engine anti-ice is ON for either engine
Below 1500 ft, f flaps are greater than 1 or engine anti-ice is ON
explanation: Approach idle in flight: cowl anti-ice ON for either engine, OR below 19,000 ft MSL with main gear down, OR flaps in approach configuration (≥ 15). · FCOM 7.20.5

question: The EGT display, both box and dial, turn red and the EEC automatically turns off ignition and shut off fuel to the engine if:
options: The EGT exceeds the starting limit during ground or in flight starts
The EGT exceeds the starting limit during ground starts
An impending hot start is detected during ground starts
An impending hot start is detected during ground starts or in flight starts
explanation: Ground starts: if EGT exceeds the starting limit the EGT box and dial turn red and the EEC turns off ignition and fuel. (Impending hot start: flashing white box, auto cutoff on current software.) None of this works in flight. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: The ISOLATION VALVE switch is to AUTO, both engine bleeds are ON and both pack switches are in AUTO. The isolation valve:
options: opens if there is AC power available
is fully open
is fully closed
is half open
explanation: Isolation valve AUTO with both engine bleeds ON and both packs AUTO or HIGH: the isolation valve is closed. It opens automatically if any bleed or pack switch is OFF. · FCOM 2.20.2

question: The loss of one DEU results in activation of both the EEC's in alternate mode. In this situation, which of the following statements is correct?
options: If the thrust levers are reduced the hard mode is entered and last valid flight conditions will be used for the engine parameters
You can only enter the hard mode by manually selecting it on the engine control panel
The soft alternate mode is entered first, using last valid flight condition to define engine parameters
The EEC's automatically switch into hard mode and the engines might overboost
explanation: Loss of a DEU puts both EECs in alternate. The soft alternate mode is entered first, using the last valid flight conditions so thrust does not change; hard alternate follows when the lever is retarded to idle or ALTN is selected. · FCOM 7.20.4

question: The number of flight spoilers located onn each wing are:
explanation: Four flight spoilers on each wing (plus two ground spoilers per wing). · FCOM 9.20.4

question: The operation of the over-wing emergency exits depends on:
options: engine speed, thrust position, air/ground sensors
engine speed, thrust position
engine speed, thrust position, air/ground sensors, door status, DC power
engine speed, thrust position, air/ground sensors, door status
explanation: Overwing exit flight locks lock/unlock depending on engine speed, thrust lever position, air/ground mode and door open/closed status; they unlock if any condition is not met or DC power is lost. · FCOM 1.40.51

question: The R ELEV PITOT Light is illuminated and PROBE HEAT switches are ON. What does this indicate?
options: System A hydraulic pressure is low
System B hydraulic pressure is low
The right elevator pitot is blocked
The right elevator pitot is not heated
explanation: Probe heat lights (amber): related probe not heated. (On standby power the lights do not indicate status.) · FCOM 3.10.3

question: The wing ANTI-ICE:
options: Is used for de-icing or anti-icing when icing conditions exist
Should be on during ground operation with temperature less than 15C and visible moisture
Is required in the climb or cruise with SAT below -40
Should only be used in flight
explanation: In flight the wing anti-ice system may be used as a de-icer or anti-icer; on the ground it is used between engine start and takeoff when icing conditions exist or are anticipated (unless protected by Type II/IV fluid). · FCOM SP.16.12 / SP.16.6

question: True or false - If both batteries on the aircraft are completely discharged and there is no ground power available, you can still start the APU
options: True
False
explanation: False. APU start power comes from transfer bus 1 or the main battery, and the battery switch must be ON (the ECU needs DC). Flat batteries and no ground power = no APU start. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: What condition would cause an automatic shutdown of the APU?
options: The APU has no automatic shutdown protection - shutting down the APU is always Flight Crew initiated.
An APU high oil temperature condition occurs or The APU overspeeds.
An APU high oil temperature condition occurs or The APU overspeeds or APU fuel control unit failure.
The APU overspeeds or APU fuel control unit failure
explanation: The ECU makes a protective shutdown for faults that could damage the APU, shown by FAULT, OVERSPEED or LOW OIL PRESSURE. Causes include overspeed, high oil temperature and fuel control unit failure (FAULT light). Bank answer. · FCOM 7.30.3 / 7.15.8

question: What condition would cause an automatic shutdown of the APU?
options: APU fuel control unit failure, An APU high oil temperature condition occurs.
APU fuel control unit failure, The APU overspeeds
The APU has no automatic shutdown protection - shutting down the APU is always Flight Crew initiated.
APU fuel control unit failure, The APU overspeeds, An APU high oil temperature condition occurs.
explanation: Protective shutdowns: overspeed (OVERSPEED light), low oil pressure, and faults such as high oil temperature or fuel control unit failure (FAULT light). Bank answer. · FCOM 7.30.3 / 7.15.8

question: What condition would cause an automatic shutdown of the APU?
options: The APU has no automatic shutdown protection - shutting down the APU is always Flight Crew initiated
The APU air inlet becomes stuck in the open position
APU low fuel temperature detected
An APU high oil temperature condition occurs
explanation: An APU high oil temperature triggers a protective shutdown (FAULT light). Bank answer. · FCOM 7.30.3

question: What does a Red Box around an N1 RPM Digital Readout mean - when the aircraft is on the ground and the engine has been shut down?
options: The N1 Limit Bug has been set manually.
An inflight exceedance has occurred.
The N1 RPM display has suffered a malfunction in flight.
This situation cannot occur - the Red Box only occurs in flight to indicate an operating limit is currently being exceeded.
explanation: On the ground after shutdown, a red box around the N1 readout = an in-flight exceedance occurred. · FCOM 7.11.5

question: What is the effect on the flight of seeing an OIL FILTER BYPASS indication whilst airborne?
options: The engine has to be immediately shut down
The engine can be run at a reduced thrust setting if the alert extinguishes
There is no effect on the flight, but no further takeoffs are allowed
The engine can be run for another 45 minutes before being shut down
explanation: QRH: retard the thrust lever; if the OIL FILTER BYPASS alert extinguishes the engine may be operated at the reduced thrust setting, otherwise shut it down. FCOM 7.11.9: impending bypass of the scavenge filter. · FCOM QRH OIL FILTER BYPASS / 7.11.9

question: What may cause the EEC to enter Soft Alternate mode?
options: EGT limit exceedance
A rapid uncommanded drop in N1
If the EEC loses the required signals to operate in Normal Mode
A total loss of AC power
explanation: If required signals are not available to operate in the normal mode, the EEC automatically changes to soft alternate. · FCOM 7.20.4

question: What power source is required to start the APU?
options: Hydraulic power
DC electrical power
AC electrical power
Bleed air
explanation: The APU needs the battery switch ON (DC for the ECU); the starter-generator uses transfer bus 1 AC if available, otherwise battery DC. DC is always required. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: What prevents the reverser mechanism actuators from deploying if not commanded?
options: An electromechanical lock and a hydraulic isolation valve
The mechanical lock on the Thrust Reverse levers prevents uncommanded motion of the reverser sleeves
A mechanical lock connected to the main landing gear
explanation: After stowing, the isolation valve closes and the electro-mechanical lock engages — together they prevent uncommanded deployment. · FCOM 7.20.13

question: When does the OIL FILTER BYPASS alert illuminate on the upper display unit?
options: Illuminates prior to oil bypassing the scavenge filter.
Illuminates just prior to oil pump bypass opening as pressure gets near to pressure required to open the bypass.
Once the oil filter bypass has opened and oil is bypassing the filter.
If the oil filter bypass has failed in the closed position and oil pressure is beginning to increase.
explanation: The OIL FILTER BYPASS alert illuminates prior to the oil bypassing the scavenge filter (impending bypass). · FCOM 7.20.7

question: When does the RAD ALT display a digital readout?
options: Below 1000ft AGL
Below 2500ft AGL
Below 1500ft AGL
Between 2500ft AGL and 1000ft AGL
explanation: Radio altitude shows below 2,500 ft AGL: digital between 2,500 and 1,000 ft; below 1,000 ft a round dial. · FCOM 10.31.3

question: When is the ENGINE ANTI-ICE turned on if icing condition exists on the ground?
options: During taxi out
Before engine start
As part of the after start checks
When starting the takeoff roll
explanation: RYR: engine anti-ice must be selected ON immediately after both engines are started and remain ON during ground operations when icing conditions exist or are anticipated. · FCOM SP.16.5

question: When the APU is started using battery power only, there is a normal indication on the electrical metering panel that the APU generator has come on line and is ready to be selected
options: True
False
explanation: False. With battery-only start, CPS FREQ is blank and AC VOLTS reads 0 (APU GEN selected) until the APU completes the start and the APU GEN OFF BUS light comes on. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: When the Audio System is operating in the degraded mode:
options: All stations are available to all crew members
First Officer can only transmit and receive on VHF 2
Captain can only transmit and receive on VHF 2
Observer can only transmit on VHF 2
explanation: Degraded mode radio at that station: Captain VHF-1, First Officer VHF-2, Observer VHF-1. · FCOM 5.20.4

question: When using the APU in flight, which of the following statements is true?
options: The APU may only be used as a bleed air source up to 10,000 feet
The APU may be used to feed two air conditioning packs up to 41,000 feet
The APU may be used as an electrical and bleed air source simultaneously up to 10,000 feet
The APU may be used as an electrical and bleed air source simultaneously up to 17,000 feet
explanation: APU: bleed + electrical simultaneously up to 10,000 ft; bleed only 17,000 ft; electrical only 41,000 ft; one pack in flight. · FCOM L.10.7

question: Where is the Engine Fuel Flow is measured?
options: After passing through the fuel filter
After passing through the engine fuel shutoff valve
Before the fuel reaches the HMU
Before passing through the second stage engine fuel pump
explanation: Fuel flow is measured after passing through the engine fuel shutoff valve, displayed on the DU and provided to the FMS. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: Which engines power the 737-800
options: Pratt Whitney JT9-3 engines
CFM 56-7 engines
Pratt Whitney JT9-7 engines
CFM 56-3 engines
explanation: 737-800: CFM56-7 engines (typical rating CFM56-7B27; RYR performance data uses -7B26). · FCOM 7.20.4

question: Which of the following actions would cause a displayed ENG FAIL Alert to extinguish?
options: Engine fire switch pulled
EEC set to ALTERNATE
Engine fire bottle discharged
Start lever moved to IDLE
explanation: ENG FAIL (amber, below 50% N2 with start lever IDLE) remains until the engine recovers, the start lever is moved to CUTOFF, or the engine fire switch is pulled. · FCOM 7.11.8

question: Which of the following statements is true, when the Thrust Reverser (REV) indication is displayed Amber?
options: Thrust reverser is moved from stowed position
The thrust reverser is deployed
That reverse thrust must not be selected
The reverse thrust lever is not in the commanded position
explanation: REV amber: thrust reverser moved from the stowed position. Green: deployed. · FCOM 7.11.6

question: Which of the following statements is true, when the Thrust Reverser (REV) indication is displayed green?
options: The reverser sleeve is unlocked
The reverser blocker door is fully stowed
The thrust reverser is deployed
The reverse thrust lever has reached detent 2
explanation: REV green: thrust reverser is deployed (lever can then go to detent No.2). · FCOM 7.11.6

question: With all electrically powered fuel pumps switched on and fuel in all tanks, where would the fuel for the APU be fed from?
options: Left main tank
Both main tanks simultaneously
Centre tank
Right main tank
explanation: APU feeds from the left side of the fuel manifold; with all pumps on and fuel in the center, the higher-pressure center pumps supply the manifold — center tank fuel. · FCOM 7.30.1 / 12.20.2

question: With the electrically driven fuel pumps switched off, which tank does the APU draw it's fuel from?
options: No 1 Main Tank.
Suction fed from Centre Tank.
Left side of the Fuel Manifold.
Number 2 main tank
explanation: With no AC fuel pumps operating, APU fuel is suction fed from main tank No.1. · FCOM 7.30.1

question: With the Multifunction Display Switch (MFD) is SYS in lower DU shows:
options: Hydraulic pressure and quantity only
Door annunciations
Brake temperature on all fours wheels
Hydraulic pressure and quantity only and flight ctrls surfaces
explanation: MFD SYS: hydraulic quantity and pressure on the lower DU (on the -800 there is no flight control surface display). · FCOM 13.10.2

question: How can the Fire Warning Bell be silenced on the flight deck?
options: Push the master caution warning lights, press the horn cutout of the APU ground control panel, push fire warning bell cutout switch.
Push the Master Fire Warn lights, press the Horn Cutout of the APU Ground Control Panel.
Fire bell can only be silenced by pressing either master fire warn light.
Push the master fire warn lights, push fire warning bell cutout switch.
explanation: Fire warning bell: silenced by pushing either master FIRE WARN light or the BELL CUTOUT switch on the overheat/fire protection panel (both also extinguish the master FIRE WARN lights and reset the system). · FCOM 8.10.1 / 8.20.10

question: The Engine Fire DISCH switches are mechanically locked in the Down position and can only be pulled Up when an Overheat or Fire is detected and the switch has illuminated.
options: True
False
explanation: False. The engine fire switch is mechanically locked in when there is no fire signal, but it can also be unlocked manually with the fire switch override (button under the handle / aft electronic panel). · FCOM 8.10.2 / 8.10.3

question: After pressing the DISCH switch, how long does it take for the cargo fire DISCH light to illuminate to indicate that the Cargo Fire Suppression system has been fully activated?
options: Immediately.
195 minutes.
Up to 60 seconds.
Up to 30 seconds
explanation: The cargo fire DISCH light illuminates once the bottle is discharged (system fully activated); it may take up to 30 seconds. · FCOM 8.20.6

question: As well as using the DISCH switch on the Fire Protection panel in the flight deck, an APU fire can be extinguished by discharging the APU fire extinguisher using the APU Ground Control Panel, which is located in a quick release access panel immediately forward and below the APU.
options: False
True
explanation: False as worded. The APU ground control panel (APU FIRE CONTROL handle, discharge) is in the RIGHT MAIN WHEEL WELL, not forward of the APU. · FCOM NP.21.13 / 7.30.2

question: Fire extinguishers provide a means of extinguishing of the engine, APU, cargo, wheel well and lavatory fires:
options: Only engine fire and lavatory fires
Only engine fire, cargo, APU fire and lavatory fires
Only engine fire and wheel well fire
Only engine fire and cargo
explanation: Extinguishing systems: engines, APU, cargo compartments (suppression) and lavatories. The main gear wheel well has fire detection but NO extinguishing system. · FCOM 8.20.1

question: How many fire extinguisher bottles are fitted for the Cargo compartments?
options: 1 fire extinguisher bottle that can only be discharged into forward cargo hold.
2 fire extinguisher bottles, one for forward cargo hold, and one for rear cargo hold.
2 fire extinguisher bottles, 1 rapid discharge bottle and one smaller slow discharge bottle.
1 fire extinguisher bottle, that can be selected to be discharged into either cargo hold.
explanation: YF501–YW164: a single cargo fire extinguisher bottle that can be discharged into either the forward or aft compartment (ARMED switch selects). · FCOM 8.20.6

question: How might it be possible to determine if the toilet fire extinguisher has been discharged?
options: Discharge indicator panel above lavatory door illuminated and Temperature indicator placard in lavatory changes colour from white to black.
Steady red light remains illuminated on Lavatory ceiling smoke detector panel after alarm tone has silenced and Lavatory Fire warning illuminated on flight deck.
Discharge nozzles changed colour from black to grey and Pressure gauge on fire bottle in the red zone.
Discharge nozzles changed colour from black to grey and Temperature indicator placard in lavatory changes colour from white to black.
explanation: Lavatory extinguisher operation is automatic and gives no flight deck indication. Discharge is checked locally (nozzle colour change / temperature placard; bank answer). · FCOM 8.20.8

question: If after moving the FAULT/INOP - OVHT/FIRE TEST switch to the OVHT/FIRE TEST position,  one engine fire switch fails to illuminate. How would you determine which detector loop had failed?
options: Move to FAULT/INOP - OVHT/FIRE switch to the central TEST position, then test one loop at a time using the OVHT DET switch selected first to A and then B.
Carry out the test again one loop at a time using the OVHT DET switch selected to A and then B.
This indication only occurs when BOTH loops have failed.
Carry out the test again with the switch selected to FAULT/INOP testing each loop individually with the OVHT DET switch at A then B.
explanation: With OVHT DET in A or B the system works as a single loop and the FAULT light indicates the selected loop has failed. Re-test one loop at a time with the switch at A, then B. · FCOM 8.10.4 / 8.20.1

question: Pushing cargo fire TEST switch:
options: Test the fwd and aft cargo fire loops only
Test the fwd and aft cargo fire loops only and continuity of the extinguisher bottle squib circuit
Only test the lamps on the cargo fire panel
Test the continuity of the extinguisher bottle squib circuit only
explanation: Cargo fire TEST: tests the forward and aft detector loops (warning lights) and the extinguisher bottle squib circuits (green EXTINGUISHER lights); the DISCH light also illuminates. · FCOM 8.20.10

question: The engines and APU have fire extinguishing systems, but the cargo holds and wheel well have only suppression systems.
options: True
False
explanation: False. Cargo compartments have smoke detection and fire suppression, but the main gear wheel well has fire detection only, no extinguishing. · FCOM 8.20.1

question: The engines each have an overheat light and an illuminated fire switch. The APU has an illuminated fire switch but no overheat light. The cargo compartments and the main wheel well have only fire warning light(s).
options: True
False
explanation: True. Engines: overheat and fire detection; APU: fire detection (fire switch) only; cargo: smoke detection; wheel well: fire detection only. · FCOM 8.20.1 / 8.10.x

question: The engines have both Overheat and Fire warnings, the APU, cargo holds and wheel well have ONLY Fire warnings.
options: True
False
explanation: True. Only the engines have overheat detection in addition to fire detection; APU, cargo (smoke) and wheel well have fire warnings only. · FCOM 8.20.1

question: What is the effect of pulling up the No1 Fire DISCH switch?
options: Closes engine and spar fuel shutoff valves, closes inlet valve to both Air Conditioning Packs, trips IDG control relay, arms both Squibs on both on both engine fire bottles, and allows the DISCH switch to be rotated left or right.

Closes engine fuel shutoff valve, closes engine bleed air valve, trips IDG control relay, closes hydraulic fluid shutoff valve and isolates EDP low pressure warning light, disables thrust reverser, arms Squib on No1 engine fire bottle, and allows the DISCH switch to be rotated to the left to discharge bottle into N01 engine.

Closes engine and spar fuel shutoff valves, closes engine bleed air valve, trips IDG control relay, closes hydraulic fluid shutoff valve and isolates EDP low pressure light, disables thrust reverser, arms one Squib on both engine fire bottles, and allows the DISCH switch to be rotated left or right.
Extinguishes Master Caution and Fire Warning lights, silences Fire Warning Bell, shuts down No1 engine, and discharges No1 Fire Bottle into No1 engine.
explanation: Engine fire switch UP: arms one squib on each engine bottle; closes fuel (engine and spar), hydraulic shutoff and engine bleed air valves; disables the thrust reverser; trips the generator control relay and breaker; deactivates the EDP LOW PRESSURE light; allows rotation. · FCOM 8.10.2

question: When a lavatory fire is detected:
options: the OVHT/DET light on the annunciator panel illuminates
the OVHT/DET light on the annunciator panel illuminates along with the MASTER CAUTION. The fire extinguisher operates automatically
the OVHT/DET light on the annunciator panel illuminates along with the MASTER CAUTION. The fire extinguisher is discharged by the cabin crew
the fire extinguisher operates automatically
explanation: Lavatory fire extinguisher operation is automatic and there is no flight deck indication of discharge. · FCOM 8.20.8

question: After pushing the DISCH switch to discharge the extinguisher into the selected cargo compartment, how long may it take for the cargo fire DISCH light to illuminate?
options: A few seconds
It illuminates immediately
Up to 2 minutes
Up to 30 seconds
explanation: Cargo fire DISCH light may take up to 30 seconds to illuminate. · FCOM 8.20.6

question: After rotating a fire switch to discharge the associated extinguisher, how long may it take for the BOTTLE DISCHARGED light to illuminate?
options: Less than 5 seconds
Up to 2 minutes
Up to 30 seconds
Less than 1 second
explanation: BOTTLE DISCHARGED: the related bottle has discharged or its pressure is low. The FCOM gives no timing; a few seconds is typical. · FCOM 8.10.4

question: After rotating a fire switch to discharge the extinguisher into the related engine, how long may it take for the L or R BOTTLE DISCHARGED light to illuminate?
options: Less than 1 second
Up to 2 minutes
A few seconds
Up to 30 seconds
explanation: BOTTLE DISCHARGED: illuminates within a few seconds when the bottle discharges (or its pressure is low). No timing in the FCOM. · FCOM 8.10.4

question: B737-800 aircraft only have 1 cargo fire extinguisher bottle fitted
options: False
True
explanation: True for RYR airplanes (YF501–YW164): one cargo fire extinguisher bottle. Two bottles are only on YA573. · FCOM 8.20.6 / 6.20.15

question: Boeing provide the option for 2 Cargo Fire extinguisher bottles to be fitted, one is a rapid discharge bottle which is fully discharged immediately upon pressing the DISCH switch on the Cargo Fire Panel, the second bottle is a slow discharge bottle that is released 1 minute after the discharge of the first bottle, and discharges slowly over several minutes to provide a total of 195 minutes of fire suppression in the cargo holds.  This second slow discharge fire extinguisher bottle is NOT fitted in any Ryanair B737-800 aircraft.
options: True
False
explanation: True. Two bottles (YA573 only); RYR (YF501–YW164) has a single bottle giving 75 minutes of suppression. · FCOM 8.20.6

question: During normal operation with the OVHT DET Switch in NORMAL, when will a fire alert be triggered?
options: Both loop A and B sense a FIRE
Loop A senses a FIRE or OVHT
Loop B is sensing a FIRE or OVHT
Loop A is sensing FIRE and loop B is sensing an OVHT
explanation: OVHT DET NORMAL: loops A and B are both active and both must sense the condition (if one loop fails it is automatically deselected and the other acts as a single loop). · FCOM 8.10.1 / 8.20.1

question: For approximately how long will the discharge of a cargo fire bottle provide fire suppression?
options: 30 minutes
12 minutes
195 minutes
75 minutes
explanation: Cargo bottle discharge gives fire suppression for 75 minutes (60 min to land + 15 min for go-around, landing and passenger unloading). · FCOM 8.20.6

question: For the APU Fire Bottle, apart from it being discharged in the event of a fire, what else may cause the APU BOTTLE DISCHARGED light to illuminate?
options: A low pressure within the bottle
The APU has automatically shut down due to a high EGT
Discharging either Engine Fire Switch
The APU Fire Detection System is inoperative
explanation: APU BOTTLE DISCHARGED: the bottle has discharged or its pressure is low. · FCOM 8.10.5

question: How can you determine if the toilet fire extinguisher has been discharged?
options: Lavatory Fire warning illuminated on flight deck
Steady red light remains illuminated on Lavatory ceiling smoke detector panel after alarm tone has silenced
Extinguisher discharge nozzle will have changed colour
Pressure gauge on fire bottle in the green zone
explanation: No flight deck indication of lavatory extinguisher discharge; the discharge nozzle tips change colour (bank). Not detailed in the FCOM. · FCOM 8.20.8

question: How can you tell if the lavatory extinguisher has discharged?
options: The extinguisher discharge nozzles will be grey in colour instead of black
A red light will illuminate above the lavatory door
The pressure gauge will read zero
An amber DISCH light will illuminate on the FWD and AFT Attendant's panel
explanation: The discharge nozzles change colour (black to grey) when discharged; there is no flight deck indication. · FCOM 8.20.8

question: How many smoke detectors are in the AFT and FWD cargo compartments?
options: AFT: 5- FWD: 4
AFT: 4 - FWD: 6
AFT: 6- FWD: 4
AFT: 3 - FWD: 8
explanation: Each cargo compartment has dual-loop smoke detectors; the FCOM does not give the number per compartment. Unverified answer. · FCOM 8.20.5

question: If a FWD cargo fire warning light re-illuminates within 120 seconds of a cargo fire bottle discharge into that compartment, will both Master FIRE WARN lights illuminate again and will the fire bell sound?
options: The Master FIRE WARN lights will illuminate, but the bell will not sound
The bell will sound, but the Master FIRE WARN lights will not illuminate
No
Yes
explanation: If a cargo fire warning light re-illuminates, both master FIRE WARN lights also re-illuminate and the fire warning bell sounds. · FCOM 8.20.6

question: Illumination of the amber APU DET INOP Light will cause what else to also illuminate?
options: MASTER CAUTION lights and the OVHT/DET System Annunciator light
No other lights will illuminate
Only the MASTER CAUTION lights
Only the OVHT/DET System Annunciator light
explanation: APU DET INOP (amber): APU detector loop has failed; MASTER CAUTION and OVHT/DET system annunciator lights also illuminate. · FCOM 8.10.4

question: In the event of a fire being detected in the APU, the fire bell will sound on the flight deck.An external APU Fire Horn will also sound in the wheel well to alert ground crew
options: False
True
explanation: True. APU fire: master FIRE WARN lights and bell on the flight deck; in the main wheel well the APU fire warning horn sounds and the APU fire light flashes (on the ground only). · FCOM 8.10.2

question: The fire detectors located in the forward and aft cargo holds detect a fire by what means?
options: Detecting smoke only
Forward cargo compartment set to detect smoke only, due to hot air from cabin conditioning system being discharged into forward cargo hold, aft cargo compartment set to detect both smoke and heat.
Detecting either smoke or heat above a pre-set value.
Detecting heat above a pre-set value only.
explanation: The forward and aft cargo compartments have smoke detectors (dual loop). Detection is by smoke only. · FCOM 8.20.5

question: To extinguish an APU fire from outside of the flight deck, the APU fire control handle needs to be pulled down first before the fire bottle discharge switch is operated
options: False
True
explanation: True (bank logic). On the APU ground control panel (right main wheel well) the APU fire control handle is pulled to arm the bottle before the discharge switch is used. Details are not in the FCOM. · FCOM 7.30.2 / NP.21.13

question: What do the 2 green illuminated EXTINGUISHER TEST lights on the cargo fire panel indicate?
options: The cargo fire extinguisher bottle is at the required pressure
Both squibs for the one cargo fire extinguisher bottle have passed the electrical circuit test
Fire warning system test completed satisfactorily
Each squib for both of the cargo fire extinguisher bottles have passed the electrical circuit test
explanation: The green EXTINGUISHER test lights show the squib circuits of the single cargo bottle (forward and aft discharge squibs) passed the continuity test. · FCOM 8.20.10

question: What is the first item on the CARGO FIRE checklist, and what is the effect of this action?
options: Press the FWD or AFT CARGO FIRE ARM switch. The extinguisher will discharge into the FWD or AFT cargo compartment
Push and hold the cargo DISCH switch for at least 30 seconds until the DISCH caption appears. This will arm the extinguisher, but it will not operate
Push and hold the cargo DISCH switch for at least one second. This will arm the squib for discharge and then discharge the extinguisher into the relevant compartment
Press the FWD or AFT CARGO FIRE ARM switch. The white ARMED caption will illuminate and the fwd or aft squib will be armed, but not discharge
explanation: First step: push the FWD or AFT cargo fire ARMED switch, which arms the squib for that compartment (white ARMED). Discharge happens only when the DISCH switch is pushed. · FCOM 8.20.6

question: What precaution regarding the use of the APU should you take if the APU DET INOP light is illuminated?
options: The APU can be used for bleed air, but not for electrical supply
Do not run the APU
The APU can be used on the ground, but not in the air
The APU can be used for electrical supply, but not for bleed air
explanation: Do not operate the APU if the APU DET INOP light fails to illuminate during the test (detection is inoperative). · FCOM NP.21.4 / SP.6.2

question: Which statement is correct when both loops in the cargo compartment fire detection system are operating normally?
options: Both loops must detect the presence of smoke to cause an alert
One loop must detect the presence of heat to cause an alert
One loop must detect the presence of smoke to cause an alert
Both loops must detect the presence of heat to cause an alert
explanation: Cargo smoke detectors are dual loop: normally both detection loops must detect smoke to cause an alert (single loop if one is deselected/failed). · FCOM 8.20.5

question: Why does the bell silence when the FIRE/WARN button is pressed?
options: To indicate to the crew the fire has extinguished
To allow the crew to communicate whilst actioning the memory items and checklist and also so that additional fire warnings will be heard
To prevent the bell from sounding again for the rest of the flight
This only occurs during the Fire Warning test
explanation: Pushing the master FIRE WARN light or BELL CUTOUT silences the bell and resets the system for additional warnings, letting the crew communicate while doing the checklist. · FCOM 8.10.1

question: Why is there a Fire Warning AND a Master Caution for an Engine fire, but only a Fire Warning for an APU fire?
options: An APU fire does not need immediate attention from the crew
The failure of the engine will trigger a MASTER CAUTION warning
The MASTER CAUTION doesn't illuminate for an APU fire, as extinguishing is fully automatic
Prior to an Engine Fire detection, an Engine Overheat would have been sensed. However, there is no overheat detection for the APU
explanation: Engine overheat illuminates MASTER CAUTION and OVHT/DET; engines have overheat and fire detection. The APU has fire detection only, so no overheat caution. · FCOM 8.10.4 / 8.20.1

question: With all AC power removed from the aircraft and the Battery Master switch in the OFF position, can the engine fire extinguishers be activated by operating the flight deck Fire Switches?
options: Yes, but the Engine Fire switches will need to be unlocked manually before they are able to be pulled up
The Engine fire extinguishers cannot be operated in this case, but the APU extinguisher will operate
The Engine fire extinguishers can be operated in this case, but the APU extinguisher cannot
No. The Battery Master must be in the ON position for the extinguishers to operate
explanation: Engine fire extinguishing is powered by the hot battery bus (works with BAT OFF), but detection is on the battery bus. With no fire signal the switches stay locked, so they must be unlocked with the override first. · FCOM 8.20.1 / 8.10.3

question: You have armed the FWD Cargo Fire switch, seen the white ARMED caption on the switch and then pressed the Cargo Fire DISCH for more than one second and released it. You don't see the amber DISCH caption immediately. Does this indicate a fault?
options: This would indicate that the extinguisher has failed to arm
This may be normal. You should allow up to 30 seconds for the DISCH light to illuminate
May be normal. If the Cargo Fire Warning has stopped, the FIRE caption will extinguish and the DISCH caption will also extinguish
This is not normal. The DISCH light should illuminate within one second of pressing the DISCH switch. You should assume that the fire extinguisher has not operated
explanation: Normal: the cargo fire DISCH light may take up to 30 seconds to illuminate after discharge. · FCOM 8.20.6

question: What should the maximum flap extension altitude be?
options: 20,000 feet
41,000 feet
Field elevation plus 1000 feet.
2500 feet RA
explanation: To prevent excessive structural loads from increased Mach at higher altitude, flap extension above 20,000 feet should not be attempted. · FCOM 9.20.19 / L.10.x

question: How does the Stall Identification system help the pilot identify and prevent further movement into a stalled condition?
options: The elevator feel shift module prevents the yaw damper from making any rudder movement, and the stick shaker activates.
Elevator Feel Shift Module increase, hydraulic system A pressure to the Elevator Feel and Centering Unit, moving the elevator to provide at least 15 degrees of nose down pitch.

Elevator Feel Shift Module increase, hydraulic system A pressure to the Elevator Feel and Centering Unit, significantly increasing the force required to move the control column rearwards to continue into a stalled condition.
The yaw damper provides 2 degrees of rudder movement, and the speed trim system automatically pushes the control column forward to warn the pilot that a stall condition was being approached.
explanation: Stall identification: yaw damper, Elevator Feel Shift module and speed trim work together. EFS increases hydraulic system A pressure to the elevator feel and centering unit, significantly increasing the column force needed to pull further aft. · FCOM 9.20.12

question: On landing, when do the ground spoilers extend?
options: Compression of the left main landing gear strut.
Compression of the right main landing gear strut.
Compression of the nose landing gear.
Compression of any landing gear strut.
explanation: The ground spoilers extend only when the right main gear strut is compressed (ground spoiler interlock valve), in addition to flight spoilers deploying on ground mode/wheel spin-up. · FCOM 9.20.16

question: What does the SPEED BRAKE DO NOT ARM light (located on the left forward panel) indicate when illuminated amber?
options: Illuminated whenever forward thrust levers are advanced beyond takeoff thrust whilst aircraft on the ground
Indicates an abnormal condition or test input in the speed brake system.
Indicates that the wheel speed has dropped below 60 kts on landing and the speedbrake lever has not been moved to the down position.
Indicates an abnormal condition or test input in the speed brake system, OR that the wheel speed has dropped below 60 kts on landing and the speedbrake lever has not been moved to the down position.
The speed brakes must not be extended as airspeed currently too high for safe operation.
explanation: SPEED BRAKE DO NOT ARM (amber): abnormal condition or test inputs to the automatic speed brake system, OR during landing wheel speed below 60 kt with the speedbrake lever not moved to DOWN. · FCOM 9.10.11

question: What happens to the speed brakes if the SPEED BRAKE lever is left in the DOWN position during landing.
options: The ground spoilers will deploy on landing if all other conditions are met, but flight spoilers will not deploy.
The speed brake lever will automatically move to the up position and the spoilers will deploy as normal if all other required conditions are met.
The spoilers will not deploy regardless of all other required conditions being met.
The flight spoilers will deploy on landing if all other conditions are met, but ground spoilers will not deploy.
explanation: Lever DOWN at landing: if the thrust reversers are raised (both reverse thrust levers), the SPEED BRAKE lever automatically moves UP and the spoilers deploy (with the other conditions met). · FCOM 9.20.16

question: What is the purpose of the ALTERNATE FLAPS master switch, and why is the cover red?
options: Fully extends the leading and trailing edge flaps. Red because the action cannot be reversed, leading and trailing edge devices cannot be retracted once extended.

Closes the trailing edge flap bypass valve, activates standby pump, and arms ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch.  Red because the action of extending the trailing edge devices cannot be reversed in flight.

Closes the trailing edge flap bypass valve, activates standby pump, and arms ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch.  Red because the action of extending the leading edge devices cannot be reversed in flight.

Fully extends the leading edge devices, and can extend and retract the trailing edge flaps. Red because the action cannot be reversed, leading and trailing edge devices cannot be retracted once extended.
explanation: ALTERNATE FLAPS master ARM: closes the TE flap bypass valve, activates the standby pump and arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch. Guard is red because LE devices extended by the standby system cannot be retracted. · FCOM 9.10.x / 9.20.x

question: What will cause the STBY RUDDER ON light to illuminate?
options: Standby rudder system is commanded on, to pressurise the standby rudder PCU, by selecting YAW DAMPER switch to OFF.

Only illuminated when the standby rudder system has been automatically commanded on - not illuminated when standby rudder system has been manually commanded on by selecting the FLT CONTROL switch to STBY RUD.
Standby rudder system is commanded on, either manually or automatically, to pressurise the standby rudder PCU.
Only illuminated when the standby rudder system has been manually commanded on by selecting a FLT CONTROL switch to STBY RUD - not illuminated when standby rudder system automatically commanded on.
explanation: STBY RUD ON (amber): the standby rudder system is commanded on to pressurize the standby rudder PCU, manually (FLT CONTROL to STBY RUD) or automatically. · FCOM 9.10.x

question: If wheel spinup is not detected on landing with the speed brake ARMED the flight spoilers will deploy automatically:
options: Only when the right main landing gear strut compresses
When the ground spoilers deploy
Flight spoilers do not deploy on landing, only ground spoilers deploy
When the air/ground system senses the ground mode (any strut compresses)
explanation: If wheel spin-up is not detected, the flight spoilers deploy when the air/ground system senses ground mode; ground spoilers additionally need the right main strut compressed. · FCOM 9.20.16

question: On Short Field Performance aircraft, the leading edge slats do not move from the extended to the fully extended position until the Flap lever is moved beyond the Flap 25 position
options: False
True
explanation: True. YW098–YW164: flap lever 1 to 25 → LE flaps full extended, slats EXTEND position; slats go to FULL EXTEND only beyond 25 (30/40). · FCOM 9.20.19

question: Selecting the ALTERNATE FLAPS master switch to...
options: ON, activates the standby pump and arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch
ARM, closes trailing edge flap bypass valve, activates standby pump and arms ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch.
Correct answer
OFF, activates the PTU and arms the primary flap selector.
STBY, activates the standby pump and arms ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch
explanation: ALTERNATE FLAPS master switch ARM: closes the TE flap bypass valve, activates the standby pump and arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch. · FCOM 9.10.x

question: Selecting the Flap lever to the FLAP 1 position causes the LE Flaps inboard of the engines to move to which position?
options: Partially extended until selecting greater than Flap 25
Partially extended until selecting Flap 10 or greater
Fully Extended
Remain fully retracted until Flap 10 is selected
explanation: Flap lever 1 and beyond: LE flaps extend to the FULL extended position (slats to EXTEND). · FCOM 9.20.19

question: The ALTERNATE FLAPS Master Switch selected to ARM:
options: Fully extends the LE Devices using Standby Hydraulic pressure
Arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS Master Switch, activates the Standby Hydraulic Pump, and closes the Trailing Edge Flaps Bypass valve
Closes the Flight Spoiler Shutoff valve
Activates the Standby Hydraulic Pump and pressurises the Standby Rudder Control Unit
explanation: ARM: arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch, activates the standby hydraulic pump and closes the TE flap bypass valve. · FCOM 9.10.x

question: The Autoslat system:
options: Is normally powered by Transfer Bus No 2
Provides slat development above Vmo/Mmo if necessary
Drives the slats to FULL EXTEND when TE Flaps 1 through 5 are selected and the aircraft approached a stall
Is normally powered by Hydraulic System A
explanation: Autoslat: at flaps 1, 2 and 5 (YW098+: 1–25), the LE slats move to full extended if the airplane approaches a stall. Powered by system B (PTU backup). · FCOM 9.20.21

question: The flap slat electronic unit (FSEU) provides flap load relief for all aircraft from Flap 10 through to Flap 40.
options: True
False
explanation: False. Flap load relief is armed at flaps 30 and 40 (YA573–YW097); only YW098–YW164 have 10, 15, 25, 30 and 40. · FCOM 9.10.13

question: The flap slat electronic unit (FSEU) will close the trailing edge bypass valve if it detects trailing edge flap asymmetry, skew or uncommanded motion; thus stopping the movement of the flaps via the normal system.  However, the flaps can still be moved by means of electric motors.
options: True
False
explanation: True. On TE asymmetry, skew or uncommanded motion the FSEU closes the TE bypass valve, stopping normal flap movement (alternate flaps are still possible). · FCOM 9.20.24

question: The flap/slat electronics unit (FSEU) provides:
options: Protection for LE devices and TE flaps if two or more LE flaps or LE slats moves from commanded position
Skew detection for LE flaps
Slat and skew protection during auto-slat operation
LE skew detection for slats 1 through 8
explanation: LE uncommanded motion: if two LE flaps or two or more slats on one wing move with no command, the FSEU shuts down LE control and illuminates LE FLAPS TRANSIT. · FCOM 9.20.25

question: What is the function of Flap Load Relief system?
options: Prevent damage to the flaps from excessive aerodynamic loads
Prevent an excessive nose-down pitch tendency from high airspeeds with high flap settings
Automatically reduce the flap setting to 15 during a single-engine go-around
Prevent excessive hydraulic pressures being fed back to the hydraulic system
explanation: Flap load relief protects the flaps from excessive aerodynamic loads by retracting to a smaller setting when the placard speed is exceeded. · FCOM 9.20.x

question: Which statement is correct in relation to the Yaw Damper?
options: Provides Gust Dampening, Dutch roll prevention and Turn coordination. The rudder pedals are displaced by yaw damper operation to provide feedback to the pilot.
Provides Gust Dampening, Dutch roll prevention and Turn coordination. The rudder pedals are not displaced by yaw damper operation.
Provides Gust Dampening and Turn coordination. The rudder pedals are not displaced by yaw damper operation.
Provides Gust Dampening and Turn coordination. The rudder pedals move to match rudder movement for feedback to the pilot.
explanation: The yaw damper provides gust dampening, Dutch roll prevention and turn coordination; rudder pedals are not displaced by yaw damper inputs (unlike rudder trim). · FCOM 9.20.13

question: Yaw damper inputs (main or standby) can be overridden:
options: Only when the yaw damper switch is off
By rudder pedals inputs but not trim inputs
By trim inputs but not rudder pedals inputs
By either trim or rudder pedals inputs
explanation: Yaw damper inputs (main or standby) can be overridden by rudder pedal or rudder trim inputs. · FCOM 9.20.13

question: How many flight spoilers are there in total?
explanation: Four flight spoilers on each wing = 8 flight spoilers in total (plus 4 ground spoilers). · FCOM 9.20.4

question: How many flight spoilers are there on each wing?
explanation: Four flight spoilers are located on the upper surface of each wing. · FCOM 9.20.4

question: How many spoilers are there in total?
explanation: 8 flight spoilers + 4 ground spoilers (two per wing) = 12 spoilers in total. · FCOM 9.20.4 / 9.20.16

question: If the Captain's control wheel were to become jammed in roll, how could the First Officer maintain roll control?
options: Roll control is only available from the Captains control wheel
Apply sufficient roll force to "break out" the FO's control wheel, and then roll can be controlled through the flight spoilers
Manually removing the hydraulic power from the flight controls will un-jam the controls and allow the Captain's wheel to turn freely and control the ailerons in Manual Reversion
Roll control will remain unavailable for the remainder of the flight. Roll can only be maintained by the use of rudder
explanation: Aileron transfer mechanism: if the aileron system is jammed, force on the First Officer's control wheel gives roll control through the spoilers (Captain's wheel jammed → F/O wheel via spoilers). · FCOM 9.20.3

question: Select the correct statement
options: The secondary flight controls are powered by hydraulic system A, with backup from the standby hydraulic system for the rudder and manual reversion for the rest
The secondary flight controls are powered by hydraulic system B, with backup from the A hydraulic system for the rudder and manual reversion for the rest
The primary flight controls are powered by hydraulic systems A and B and manual reversion for the rest if system A and B are lost
The primary flight controls are powered by hydraulic systems A and B, with backup from the standby hydraulic system for the rudder and manual reversion for the rest
explanation: Primary flight controls are powered by hydraulic systems A and B; the standby system backs up the rudder; ailerons and elevators can be operated by manual reversion. · FCOM 9.20.1

question: Selecting the Flap lever to the FLAP 1 Gate causes the LE Flaps to move to what position?
options: Takeoff setting
Fully Extended
Flap 15 position.
Flap 1 position
explanation: Flap 1: LE flaps go to fully extended. · FCOM 9.20.19

question: The flap load relief system is operational at:
options: Flaps 15, 30 and 40
Flaps 40 only
Flaps 30 and 40
All flap settings
explanation: Flap load relief is armed at flap lever 30 and 40 (YA573–YW097); YW098+ also at 10, 15 and 25. · FCOM 9.10.13

question: The FSEU controls FLAP LOAD RELIEF when flaps are in position(s)
options: 40 only
30 only
explanation: Flap load relief: flaps 30 and 40 (YW098+: 10, 15, 25, 30, 40). · FCOM 9.10.13

question: The yaw damper provides inputs to the rudder to provide which of the following, and what effect does it have on the rudder pedals?
options: Provides Gust Dampening and Turn coordination. The rudder pedals move to match rudder movement for feedback to the pilot.
Provides Gust Dampening, Dutch roll prevention and Turn coordination. The rudder pedals are not displaced by yaw damper operation.
Provides Gust Dampening and Turn coordination. The rudder pedals are not displaced by yaw damper operation.
Provides Gust Dampening, Dutch roll prevention and Turn coordination. The rudder pedals are displaced by yaw damper operation to provide feedback to the pilot.
explanation: Yaw damper: gust dampening, Dutch roll prevention and turn coordination; the rudder pedals are not displaced by yaw damper operation. · FCOM 9.20.13

question: Under what conditions does the YAW DAMPER switch automatically move to OFF and cannot be reset to ON?
options: When aircraft is on ground with both yaw dampers engaged
When electrical power is cycled and hydraulic system A pressure drops
When SMYD detects a fault, yaw damper is unresponsive, or FLT CONTROL B is OFF or in STBY RUD
When hydraulic system A pressure is lost and SMYD input is inactive
explanation: The YAW DAMPER switch trips OFF (and cannot be reset to ON) when the SMYD detects a fault, the yaw damper is unresponsive, or FLT CONTROL B is OFF or in STBY RUD. · FCOM 9.10.x

question: What are the operational considerations when using speed brakes in flight?
options: Deploying speed brakes in an intermediate position increases roll rate significantly. Movement beyond FLIGHT DETENT causes buffeting and is prohibited
Speed brakes have no effect on roll rate during turns and may be deployed beyond the FLIGHT DETENT for maximum effectiveness
Speed brakes can be used freely during flight with no operational limitations
Deploying speed brakes in a turn has no impact on aircraft handling
explanation: In flight, speed brakes increase roll rate (spoilers assist roll); using beyond the FLIGHT DETENT in flight causes buffeting and is prohibited. · FCOM 9.20.16 / L.10.x

question: What does a FLT CONTROL "LOW PRESSURE" light illuminated amber indicate?
options: Related hydraulic system pressure to ailerons, elevator and rudder is low.
This light is illuminated whenever the associated FLT CONTROL switch is in the OFF position.
The STBY RUD system pressure is low.
Both hydraulic systems pressure to ailerons, elevator and rudder are low.
explanation: FLT CONTROL LOW PRESSURE (amber): low hydraulic pressure from the related system (A or B) to the ailerons, elevator and rudder. Deactivated when the switch is in STBY RUD and the standby rudder shutoff valve opens. · FCOM 9.10.x

question: What effect will moving the STAB TRIM OVERRIDE switch to the OVERRIDE position have?
options: Removes power to the Stabilizer Trim motor
Allows the electric stabiliser trim to be used regardless of control column position
Removes the autopilot inputs to the Stabiliser Trim system
Deactivates all Stabiliser Trim inputs
explanation: STAB TRIM OVERRIDE: bypasses the control-column-actuated stabilizer trim cutout switches, so electric trim works regardless of column position. · FCOM 9.10.6

question: What is the function of the Force Fight Monitor in the main Rudder PCU?
options: To assist the with Rudder operation
It reduces rudder deflection at airspeeds above approximately 135kt
If it detects a difference in force being applied by the Main Rudder PCU and the Standby Rudder PCU

It monitors the pressures being applied to the A and B actuators. it automatically turn on the Standby Hydraulic pump and open the standby rudder shutoff valve to pressurize the standby rudder PCU if opposing forces are detected
explanation: The Force Fight Monitor detects opposing pressure between the A and B rudder actuators (one system failed) and automatically starts the standby pump and opens the standby rudder shutoff valve to pressurize the standby rudder PCU. · FCOM 9.20.x

question: What is the function of the Speed Trim system?
options: To improve speed stability above M0.615 with autopilot engaged
To increase the rate at which the trim wheel operates with Flaps not up
Provide trim inputs to improve speed stability characteristics during manual flight
To increase control column forces when approaching Vmo / Mmo
explanation: Speed trim provides stabilizer trim inputs to improve speed stability during manual flight (low weight, aft CG, high thrust); it operates most frequently during takeoff, climb and go-around. · FCOM 9.20.x

question: What is the maximum permitted lever position of the speed brake lever in flight?
options: DOWN (Speed brake use is prohibited in flight)
UP
FLIGHT DETENT
ARMED
explanation: In flight the SPEED BRAKE lever must not be moved beyond the FLIGHT DETENT. · FCOM 9.10.11 / L.10.x

question: What is the result of selecting the ALTERNATE FLAPS master switch to ARM?
options: Arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch, activates the standby hydraulic pump and closes the TE flap bypass valve
Fully extends the LE devices using electric motors
Closes the flight spoilers shut off valve
Activates the standby hydraulic pump and pressurizes the standby rudder control unit
explanation: ARM: arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch, activates the standby pump and closes the TE flap bypass valve. · FCOM 9.10.x

question: What will cause the FEEL DIFF PRESS light to illuminate?
options: Flaps are not up and an excessive hydraulic pressure imbalance between hydraulic System B and the Standby hydraulic system is sensed
Flaps are up and an excessive hydraulic pressure imbalance between hydraulic System A and the Standby hydraulic system is sensed
Flaps are either up or down and either hydraulic system fails or either elevator pitot system fails, and an excessive hydraulic pressure imbalance is sensed
Captain's pitot system fails
explanation: FEEL DIFF PRESS (amber): excessive differential pressure in the elevator feel computer (e.g. hydraulic system or elevator pitot failure). Flaps up or down; YF501+ also possibly erroneous EFS activation. · FCOM 9.10.3

question: When extending the flaps using ALTERNATE FLAPS switch, why should you carefully monitor the Flap Position Indicator as the flaps extend?
options: No asymmetry protection is provided when using the Alternate Flap system
If you operate the switch to the "DOWN" position, the switch will latch on and the flaps will fully extend until you move the switch back to the center position
Only the "L" needle indicates flap position when using Alternate Flaps
Only the "R" needle indicates flap position when using Alternate Flaps
explanation: Alternate (electric) flap extension provides no asymmetry/skew protection, so monitor the flap position indicator closely. · FCOM 9.20.x

question: Which statement is correct in the event of an elevator control column jam, and the override mechanism has been operated?
options: Applying force against the jam will break out only the captain's control column
Lighter than normal control forces must be used for take off and landing
The elevator feel and centring unit will transfer proper aerodynamic forces to the control column
The control columns are physically separated. The column which is free to move will be able to provide elevator control
explanation: Elevator jam: the override mechanism lets the control columns be physically separated; the column that is free to move provides elevator control. · FCOM 9.20.x

question: Which statement is true regarding aileron trim?
options: If the autopilot is engaged the amount of trim is not indicated on the scale
It repositions the ailerons by using aileron balance tabs
The amount of trim is indicated on the scale on top of control column with or without autopilot engaged
Aileron trim is not available with the autopilot engaged
explanation: If aileron trim is used with the autopilot engaged, the trim is not reflected in the control wheel or the trim scale; the A/P overpowers it. · FCOM 9.20.3

question: With reference to the illumination of the LE FLAPS TRANSIT light, which statement is correct?
options: Indicates all LE Devices are fully extended
Is inhibited during Autoslat operation in flight
Indicates LE Slats are fully extended
Indicates that TE Flaps asymmetry protection is being provided
explanation: LE FLAPS TRANSIT: any LE device in transit or not in programmed position (or LE uncommanded motion); inhibited during autoslat operation in flight. · FCOM 9.10.15

question: With the speed brake lever at ARMED, if a wheel spin-up signal is not detected on landing, will the flight spoilers deploy automatically?
options: The flight spoilers will not deploy unless wheel spin up of 60kts or greater is detected
They will deploy only when the right main landing gear strut is compressed
They will deploy only after the Ground Spoilers have deployed
They will deploy automatically when the Air /Ground system senses ground mode
explanation: Without wheel spin-up, the flight spoilers deploy automatically when the air/ground system senses ground mode; ground spoilers additionally need the right main strut compressed. · FCOM 9.20.16

question: On the navigation display, how is the display presented in VOR, Approach and Plan modes?
options: VOR = true north up, Approach = heading up, Plan = heading up.
VOR = heading up, Approach = heading up, Plan = true north up.
VOR = true north up, Approach = true north up, Plan = heading up.
VOR = heading up, Approach = true north up, Plan = heading up.
explanation: Centre/expanded VOR and APP modes are heading-up; PLAN mode is true-north-up (true north up arrow). · FCOM 10.16.3 / 10.11.47

question: What condition causes an Amber IAS DISAGREE alert to appear at the bottom of the speed tape?
options: Selected V Ref is not correct for current aircraft configuration.
V Ref has not been entered
Captain's and First Officer's airspeeds disagree by more than 5 kts for more than 5 seconds.
Difference of more than 10 kts for more than 10 seconds between Captain's and First Officer's airspeed indications.
explanation: IAS DISAGREE (amber): Captain's and First Officer's airspeed indications disagree by more than 5 knots for 5 continuous seconds. · FCOM 10.11.29

question: What does the top of the amber bar indicate at the lower end of the speed tape?
options: Minimum manoeuvre speed (1.3g manoeuvre capability to stick shaker above approximately 30,000 feet) - (1.3g manoeuvre capability to low speed buffet below approximately 30,000 feet).
Minimum manoeuvre speed (1.3g manoeuvre capability to stick shaker below approximately 20,000 feet) - (1.3g manoeuvre capability to low speed buffet above approximately 20,000 feet).
Minimum manoeuvre speed (1.3g manoeuvre capability to stick shaker below approximately 30,000 feet) - (1.3g manoeuvre capability to low speed buffet above approximately 30,000 feet).
Minimum manoeuvre speed (1.3g manoeuvre capability to stick shaker above approximately 20,000 feet) - (1.3g manoeuvre capability to low speed buffet below approximately 20,000 feet).
explanation: Top of the amber bar = minimum maneuver speed: 1.3 g maneuver capability to stick shaker below about 20,000 ft, and to low-speed buffet above about 20,000 ft. · FCOM 10.11.x

question: Dotted red areas on terrain display indicate:
options: Terrain more than 2,000 ft above airplane altitude
Terrain more than 2,000 ft above Radio altitude
Terrain 500 ft below (250 with gear down) to 2,000 ft above airplane altitude
Terrain 2,000 ft below to 55 ft above (250 with gear down) airplane altitude
explanation: Dotted red: terrain more than 2,000 ft above the airplane. Dotted amber: 500 ft (250 ft gear down) below to 2,000 ft above. Dotted green: 2,000 ft below to 500/250 ft below. Solid red/amber: look-ahead warning/caution. · FCOM 15.10.12

question: During an ILS approach the captain observes his BARO minimum reference altitude turns from green to flashing amber for three seconds, this means:
options: A windshear has been encountered
The aircraft has descended below captains selected minimum altitude (DA)
The aircraft has descended below 1000 feet
Radio altitude data is unreliable
explanation: BARO minimums pointer and line turn amber (flashing) when the airplane descends below the selected minimum altitude; reset with the RST switch. · FCOM 10.11.23

question: On the PFD, what does the amber annunciation "DISPLAYS CONTROL PANEL" indicate?
options: The Displays Source Control Panel on the side the annunciation is displayed has failed.
The PFD the annunciation is displayed on has an error and information displayed may be erroneous.
The Display Select Panel on the the side the annunciation is displayed has failed.
The EFIS control panel on the side the annunciation is displayed has failed
explanation: DISPLAYS CONTROL PANEL (amber): a failed EFIS control panel on the affected side. · FCOM 10.11.31

question: The bug below that indicates V2 + 15 is displayed at what stage of flight, and when is it removed?
options: Displayed at Takeoff, removed at first flap retraction or when Vref entered in CDU.
Displayed on Approach, removed once right main landing gear is compressed, throttle levers at Idle, and engines have spooled down from Approach Idle to Ground Idle.
Displayed at Approach, removed when flaps at Flap 1 or greater.
Displayed at takeoff, removed when Pitch Flight director moves to 15 degrees nose up.
explanation: The V2+15 bug is shown for takeoff and removed at the first flap retraction or when VREF is entered in the CDU. · FCOM 10.11.x

question: What does a white CDS MAINT message in the lower left corner of the PFD indicate?
options: A non-dispatchable CDS fault has occurred post second engine start.
A dispatchable CDS fault has occurred prior to second engine start.
A dispatchable CDS fault has occurred prior to first engine start.
A non-dispatchable CDS fault has occurred prior to second engine start
explanation: CDS MAINT (white): a dispatchable CDS fault, displayed on the ground only, prior to start of the second engine. CDS FAULT (amber) = non-dispatchable. · FCOM 10.11.30

question: What does the Magenta figure displayed above the Speed Tape signify?
options: Maximum airspeed for current flap settings.
FMC computed airspeed if the IAS/MACH window is blank.
Current or next speed restriction in the FMC.
Airspeed manually selected in the IAS/MACH window and FMC computed airspeed if the IAS/MACH window is blank.
Airspeed manually selected in the IAS/MACH window.
explanation: Selected speed readout (magenta) above the speed tape: speed selected in the MCP IAS/MACH window, or the FMC computed speed when the window is blank. · FCOM 10.11.x

question: The amber annunciation "INSTR SWITCH" indicates what?
options: Captain's and First Officer's displays are using separate sources of IRU data.
The IRS switch on the Forward Overhead panel is not selected to NORMAL
Captain's and First Officer's displays are using the same source of IRU data with the IRS switch selected to OFF.
The IRS switch on the Aft Overhead panel is not selected to NORMAL.
explanation: INSTR SWITCH (amber): both pilots' displays use the same IRU source, shown when the IRS transfer switch on the (forward) overhead panel is not in NORMAL. · FCOM 10.11.32

question: An amber IAS DISAGREE alert in the bottom of the speed tape indicates:
options: The Captains and First Officers airspeeds disagree by more than 5 KTS for more than 5 seconds
The selected V REF is not correct for actual airplane gross weight
The selected V REF is not correct for actual airplane configuration
There is a difference of more than 10 KTS between the MCP and FMC speeds
explanation: IAS DISAGREE: Captain's and First Officer's airspeeds disagree by more than 5 kt for 5 seconds. · FCOM 10.11.29

question: How many DEUs are installed on the aircraft?
explanation: Two DEUs (DEU 1 and DEU 2), selectable with the DISPLAYS SOURCE selector. · FCOM 10.16.5 / 10.11.30

question: If the Airspeed indicator fails
options: There are no indications on the PFD
The SPD flag shows on the PFD
The aural warning 'SPEED SPEED' sounds
The FAIL flag shows on the PFD
explanation: Speed flag (amber, SPD) on the PFD: speed indication is inoperative. · FCOM 10.11.28

question: The digital readout of the vertical speed in white shown at the bottom (when descending) of the vertical speed indication will show when the vertical speed exceeds what figure?
options: 500 feet per minute
400 feet per minute
250 feet per minute
1000 feet per minute
explanation: Vertical speed (white) digital readout appears when greater than 400 fpm; above the indication when climbing and below when descending. · FCOM 10.11.25

question: What does a magenta bug on the vertical speed indicator display show?
options: Displays vertical speed when greater than 400 feet per minute
Indicates vertical speed with VNAV pitch mode engaged
The vertical speed selected in the MCP vertical speed window with V/S pitch mode engaged
Actual vertical speed
explanation: Selected vertical speed bug (magenta): the speed selected in the MCP V/S window with V/S pitch mode engaged. · FCOM 10.11.25

question: What does an amber MAP RANGE DISAGREE annunciation on the ND indicate?
options: The selected range on the EFIS control panel is different from the weather radar display range
Range information is not being fed to the map display
The selected range on the EFIS control panel is different from the map display range
Range information cannot be read from the EFIS control panel
explanation: MAP RANGE DISAGREE: selected range on the EFIS control panel differs from the MAP display range. · FCOM 10.11.62

question: What does the acronym FPV stand for?
options: Flight Patch Velocity
Final Path Vector
Flight Pitch Vectoring
Flight Path Vector
explanation: FPV = Flight Path Vector (selected on the EFIS control panel). · FCOM 10.11.x

question: What does the ATT:RST annunciation displayed on an ISFD mean?
options: Self realignment in progress
Attitude must be reset using the Attitude Reset (RST) switch
Power has been lost to the ISFD
Attitude information is being recalculated
explanation: ISFD ATT:RST (amber): attitude must be reset using the attitude reset switch. ATT 10s = realignment in progress; WAIT ATT = temporary self-correcting loss of attitude. · FCOM 10.16.16

question: What is the result if the airplane pitch attitude reaches the Pitch Limit Indication?
options: Initial buffet occurs before stick shaker activation
Stick shaker activates for existing flight conditions
The speed trim system pushes the control column forward
The airplane stalls
explanation: Pitch limit indication shows the pitch attitude at which the stick shaker activates for the existing flight conditions. · FCOM 10.11.x

question: When does the Rad Alt display a digital readout with no circular display around it?
options: Below 1,000ft AGL
From 1,000ft AGL to 300ft AGL
From 2,500ft AGL to 1,000ft AGL
Below 2,500ft AGL
explanation: Radio altitude: digital display from 2500 to 1000 ft AGL; round dial below 1000 ft AGL. · FCOM 10.11.19

question: When does the Rad Alt display the aircraft's height above ground?
options: The airplane has descended below the selected radio altitude minimums
There is difference of more than 10 feet between the captain's and first officer's radio altimeters
Radio altitude data is unreliable
The airplane has descended below 1,000 ft radio altitude
explanation: Radio altitude is displayed below 2500 ft AGL (digital), and with the round dial below 1000 ft. Of the options, below 1000 ft RA (round dial) is the intended answer. · FCOM 10.11.19

question: When is the current Mach number displayed at the bottom of the airspeed indications tape on the PFD?
options: When above 10,000 feet and airspeed is 0.35 Mach and above
When airspeed is 0.40 Mach and above
When above 20,000 feet
When airspeed is 0.615 Mach and above
explanation: Current Mach is displayed below the airspeed tape when Mach is .40 or greater. · FCOM 10.11.x

question: Which statement is correct when the airplane has descended below the radio altitude minimums?
options: The Rad Alt display dial perimeter, numeric readout and pointer flash for 5 seconds
The Rad Alt numeric readout and pointer turn amber and flash for 5 seconds
On the Rad Alt display on the PFD, the dial display and pointer turn amber and flash for 3 seconds
The Rad Alt dial perimeter, numeric readout and pointer turn green and flash for 3 seconds
explanation: Below radio altitude minimums the remaining dial perimeter and pointer turn amber and flash for 3 seconds; the numeric readout does not flash. · FCOM 10.11.19

question: With the range set greater than 20 nm, how far is the aircraft from the point arrowed (second line on Position Trend Vector)?
options: 20 seconds flight time
60 seconds flight time
2 nautical miles
4 nautical miles
explanation: Position trend vector: segments at 30, 60 and 90 seconds (range > 20 NM); the second line = 60 seconds. · FCOM 10.41.10

question: If the aircraft present position cannot be entered through the FMC CDU, it can be entered using the ISDU keyboard.
options: True
False
explanation: Present position is normally entered through the FMC CDU (POS INIT). If it cannot be entered through the CDU, it can be entered using the ISDU keyboard. · FCOM 11.20.4 / 11.20.6

question: If alignment is lost in flight, what action can be taken?
options: The navigation mode remains unavailable for the rest of the flight, but ALIGN mode can be selected to provide attitude reference.
The IRS mode selectors must be moved to OFF to allow FMC to hold all GPS and navigation data for remainder of the flight.
The navigation mode remains unavailable for the rest of the flight, but ATT mode can be selected to provide attitude reference.
IRS mode selector can be selected to ALIGN for 30 seconds then back to NAV to reset the system.

ATT mode can be selected to relevel the system and attain attitude reference, the system can then be returned to ALIGN for the 30 second Fast Align, then returned to NAV once the ALIGN light extinguishes.
explanation: If alignment is lost in flight, the navigation mode (present position and ground speed) is inoperative for the remainder of the flight. Selecting ATT allows the attitude mode to provide an attitude reference after about 30 s of straight, level, unaccelerated flight. · FCOM 11.20.5

question: On the DEP/ARR page on the FMC, can more than one Arrival be entered?
options: True
False
explanation: The DEP/ARR index gives ARR prompts for the Route 1 and Route 2 destinations (and an OTHER airport), so an arrival can be selected for each route. The FCOM does not state this as a yes/no rule. · FCOM 11.40.23

question: Setting the ADF mode selector switch to ANT has what effect?
options: ADF bearing data switched to keel antenna only, to minimise multipath interference.
ADF bearing pointer slews to 135 degrees relative bearing.
No ADF bearing data available and audio reception optimised.
ADF bearing data sent to Standby Radio Magnetic Indicator as well as the DUs
explanation: ADF mode selector ANT: audio reception optimized; no ADF bearing data available. ADF position: audio possible and bearing sent to the DUs and the standby RMI. · FCOM 11.10.23

question: A total of 99 numbered waypoints cannot be exceeded for any single route.
options: True
False
explanation: False. When the quantity of numbered waypoints exceeds 99, the identifier uses the first two characters of the entry followed by the smallest three-digit sequence number, so more than 99 are possible. · FCOM 11.31.16

question: After performing the FMC/CDU preflight, the flight crew notices that the ACTIVE NAV DATA base is expired and must be changed. Which will the RTE page look like after the NAV DATA base change?
options: Same, no action required
Route discontinuity will be gone, everything else remain the same
Black, requiring reloading
The NAV DATA base cannot be changed after pre-flight
explanation: The navigation database date can be changed only on the ground. Changing the navigation database removes all previously entered route data, so the RTE page is blank and the route must be re-entered. · FCOM 11.40.7

question: Below what altitude are windshear alerts available for aircraft fitted with IntuVue weather radar?
options: 1200 feet RA and below.
1800 feet RA and below
2300 feet AGL and below.
1500 feet AGL and below.
explanation: Predictive windshear alerting below 1,200 ft RA. IntuVue: windshear detection operates automatically below 1800 ft AGL, with alerts available at 1200 ft and below. · FCOM 11.20.11 / 11.20.13

question: During VNAV PATH DESCENT and below the Speed Restriction Altitude, the FMC Alerting Message OVERSPEED DISCONNECT means:
options: The FMC has disengaged the autothrottles due to excessive N1
VNAV has disengaged because airspeed has exceeded FMC Speed Restriction by more than 15kts
VNAV has disengaged at Vmo
VNAV has disengaged because airspeed has exceeded FMC Target Speed by more than 10kts
explanation: OVERSPEED DISCONNECT: during path descent, above or below the speed restriction altitude, VNAV disengages when airspeed exceeds the FMC speed restriction by more than 15 knots. Action: manually reduce speed and re-engage VNAV. · FCOM 11.60.9

question: How long are the navigation databases valid for?
options: Valid until next update
48 Hours
21 Days
28 Days
explanation: The FMC contains two sets of navigation data, each valid for 28 days. · FCOM 11.32.2

question: On the IRS panel, if the DC FAIL light illuminates in flight all alignment data is lost and the system cannot be re-set until the aircraft is parked on the ground.
options: True
False
explanation: False. DC FAIL (amber) = DC power for the related IRS is not normal. If the other lights are extinguished, the IRS is operating normally on AC. Alignment is lost only if the IRS loses BOTH AC and DC power (11.20.5). · FCOM 11.10.21

question: On which page of the FMC is the IRS position initially set?
options: RTE page.
POS INIT page
INIT REF page.
DEP ARR page.
explanation: POS INIT page (via INIT REF/POS): used for IRS initialization. SET IRS POS entry is required to initialize the IRS. · FCOM 11.40.5 / 11.40.9

question: Positioning the WING ANTI-ICE switch to ON in flight:
options: Adjusts FMC displayed Vref automatically when WING-ANTI ICE switch is ON
Sets stick shaker logic for icing conditions for the remainder of flight
Have no influence on stick shaker logic
Sets stick shaker logic for icing conditions only when WING-ANTI ICE switch is ON
explanation: WING ANTI-ICE ON in the air: wing anti-ice valves open and stick shaker logic is set for icing conditions. It remains set for the remainder of the flight, regardless of subsequent switch position. · FCOM 3.10.6

question: What colour is the Outer Marker Beacon (OM) displayed on the PFD?
options: OM appears Magenta in lower right corner of Attitude Indicator.
OM appears Cyan in top right corner of AI.
OM appears White in top right corner of AI
OM appears in Magenta in top right corner of the Attitude Indicator.
explanation: Marker beacon indications appear at the upper right of the attitude display: OM cyan, MM amber, IM white. · FCOM 11.10.26 / 11.20.9

question: What colour is the route on the Nav display when you activate a route by pressing the R6 switch?
options: Dashed Magenta
Magenta.
Dashed Cyan
White
explanation: Inactive route = cyan dashed line; activated but not yet executed = cyan dashed line; active route = magenta; modifications = white dashed. · FCOM 11.31.16

question: A valid FMC PERF INIT page Scratch Pad entry for actual FUEL is:
options: Actual fuel is entered manually before every flight
Actual fuel is entered manually before the first flight in the morning
Actual fuel is entered manually before last flight at nightstop for next day
Actual fuel is displayed automatically and cannot be entered manually
explanation: Fuel quantity values come automatically from the fuel quantity system to PERF INIT and PROGRESS 1/3. Manual entry is only possible when fuel data is invalid (VERIFY GW AND FUEL, FUEL line shows dashes). · FCOM 11.32.4

question: During VNAV operations the Fuel Quantity Indicating System fails:
options: VNAV operation is not possible
The pilots enter and periodically update manually calculated fuel weight on the FMC PERF INIT page in order to keep gross weight and performance data accurate
VNAV disengages
The scratchpad message: CHECK FMC FUEL Quantity is displayed
explanation: VERIFY GW AND FUEL: fuel data invalid, the PERF INIT fuel value is replaced with dashes. Enter fuel weight on PERF INIT 1/2; periodic update of fuel weight is required to keep gross weight and performance data valid. · FCOM 11.60.13 / 11.32.4
