question: For the IntuVue  Radar, Predictive Windshear mode is automatically turned on in which of the following specific aircraft conditions?
options: In flight below 1500 feet AGL, on ground with both engines running.
In flight below 2300 feet AGL, on ground with throttle levers at takeoff position setting.
In flight below 1800 feet AGL, on ground with throttle levers set for takeoff.
In flight above 1200 feet RA, on ground with throttle levers at takeoff position setting.
explanation: IntuVue automatic windshear activation: in the air below 1800 ft AGL, or on the ground with the thrust levers set for takeoff. · FCOM 11.10.36

question: If a storm cell is displayed on the weather radar, up to what distance away may turbulence associated with the storm be present?
options: More than 20nm
Up to 10nm
Up to 5nm
Up to 2 nm
explanation: Turbulence associated with a storm can extend well beyond the visible echo; standard practice is to avoid cells by at least 20 nm. The FCOM gives no distance: WX/TURB shows turbulence within 40 nm, and clear air turbulence cannot be detected. · FCOM 11.10.34 / 11.20.10

question: If IRS alignment is lost in flight, the navigation mode becomes inoperative for the remainder of the flight.
options: True
False
explanation: True. If alignment is lost in flight, the navigation mode (position and ground speed) is inoperative for the remainder of the flight; ATT mode can give attitude. · FCOM 11.20.5

question: If the GPS position varies considerably from the radio and IRS computed position, how does the FMC calculate the aircraft's position?
options: GPS updating is suspended until the GPS position can be determined to be reasonable.
The FMC will only use the IRS position for the remainder of the flight
The calculated position will be the average of the GPS position and IRS position
The GPS update will be removed for the remainder of the flight
explanation: If the GPS position update is excessive, GPS updating is suspended until the GPS position can be determined to be reasonable. · FCOM 11.31.6

question: Manual IRS entries of present position or magnetic heading are normally accomplished on the:
options: POS SHIFT page 3/3
POS SHIFT page 1/3
POS SHIFT page 2/3
POS INIT page or the ISDU
explanation: Manual IRS entries of present position or magnetic heading are normally accomplished on the POS INIT page of the FMC/CDU. The ISDU may also be used. · FCOM 11.20.5

question: On later aircraft YW130 through YW164, the VHF NAV switch changes the source of the data that the DEUs use for the NDs.  What data is transferred by this switch?
options: VOR, GBAS, MCP course
DME, GBAS, VOR, Autothrottle, MCP Course.
DME, ILS, VOR, MCP course.
DME, ILS/GLS, VOR, MCP course
explanation: YW130–YW164: the VHF NAV transfer switch transfers DME, ILS/GLS, VOR and MCP course data for the NDs (earlier airplanes: DME, ILS, VOR, MCP course). · FCOM 11.10.30

question: On the FMC FIX INFO page the RAD/DIS FR indicates:
options: The radial and distance of your next abeam point
The radial and distance from the fix to the airplane, this information will update as the aircraft changes position
The radial and distance of the destination field
the radial and distance from the airplane to the fix, this is not updated as the airplane changes position
explanation: RAD/DIS FR: displays the radial and distance from the fix to the airplane, continually updated as the airplane position changes. · FCOM 11.42.51

question: On the ground, what is the primary source of position data for the FMC?
options: GPS
VOR/DME
VOR
IRS
explanation: On the ground, the FMC calculates present position based on GPS data. If GPS data is not available, it uses IRS data. · FCOM 11.31.4

question: On which CDU page is the ground speed displayed?
options: PROGRESS page 1
PROGRESS page 2
POS REF page 2
CRUISE
explanation: POS REF page 2/3 shows the latitude/longitude calculated by each system; ground speed is displayed for the FMC and each IRS. · FCOM 11.40.11

question: The Air Data Inertial Reference System (ADIRS) produces following flight data:
options: Attitude and speed only
Position and speed only
Position, attitude, altitude and speed
Altitude and speed only
explanation: The ADIRS produces flight data such as position, speed, altitude and attitude for the flight displays, FMCs, flight controls, engine controls and other systems. · FCOM 10.21.12

question: The Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) can be erased:
options: Pushing erase button for 2 seconds and aircraft in flight with parking brake ON
Pushing erase button for 2 seconds and aircraft in flight
Pushing erase button for 2 seconds and aircraft on ground with parking brake ON
Pushing erase button for 2 seconds and aircraft on ground with parking brake OFF
explanation: CVR ERASE switch (red), push 2 seconds: all four channels erased; operative only when the airplane is on the ground and the parking brake is set. · FCOM 5.10.11

question: The curved trend vector extending from the aircraft symbol on ND MAP and MAP CTR is divided into three segments, it represents with range greater than 20 NMs:
options: Predicts position at the end of 10, 20 and 30 second intervals
Predicts position at the end of 20, 40 and 60 second intervals
Predicts position at the end of 30, 60 and 90 second intervals
Predicts position at the end of 60, 90 and 120 second intervals
explanation: Position trend vector (MAP, MAP CTR): predicts position at the end of 30, 60 and 90 second intervals; each segment represents 30 seconds (range > 20 NM: 3 segments). · FCOM 10.41.10

question: The FMC Advisor Message DRAG REQUIRED indicates the aircraft is:
options: Within 15 knots of Vmo/Vmmo
5 knots or less above the FMC target speed
10 knots or more below the FMC target speed
10 knots or more above the FMC target speed or within 5 knots of Vmo/Vmmo
explanation: DRAG REQUIRED: airspeed is 10 kts or more above the FMC target speed, or within 5 kts of Vmo/Mmo. Action: use speedbrakes, trim or reduced thrust to come within 5 kts of target. · FCOM 11.60.18

question: The FMC advisory Message BUFFET ALERT indicates:
options: Current conditions result in a manoeuvre margin less than specified
Clear air turbulence has been detected in the intermediate flight path
The flight deck crews dinner is being prepared in the galley
The aircraft is in a partial or full stall
explanation: BUFFET ALERT (only with flaps retracted): current conditions result in a maneuver margin less than specified. Bring the airplane back within the operating envelope. · FCOM 11.60.18

question: The FMC Alerting Message INSUFFICIENT FUEL means:
options: You will have less than 900kg (2000lbs) of fuel at the destination
You will not reach your destination before running out of fuel
The APU is running out of fuel
It is necessary to increase the thrust setting
explanation: INSUFFICIENT FUEL: FMC fuel at the destination is predicted to be less than 2000 lbs / 900 kg. Modify the route, cruise altitude, or divert for additional fuel. · FCOM 11.60.6 / 11.32.4

question: The FMC alerting message RESET MCP ALT means:
options: Aircraft within 2.5 NM of the FMC calculated Top of Descent (TOD) point without selecting lower altitude on the MCP
Aircraft within 5 NM of the FMC calculated Top of Climb (TOC) point without selecting higher altitude on the MCP
Aircraft within 5 NM of the FMC calculated Top of Descent (TOD) point without selecting lower altitude on the MCP
Aircraft within 15 NM of the FMC calculated Top of Descent (TOD) point without selecting lower altitude on the MCP
explanation: RESET MCP ALT: during cruise with VNAV engaged, within 5 NM of the top-of-descent point without selecting a lower altitude on the MCP. · FCOM 11.60.9

question: The IntuVue weather radar fitted in aircraft YF662-YF695 and YW001-YW164, gives clutter-free viewing of significant weather out to what range?
options: 420 nautical miles.
120 nautical miles.
320 nautical miles
220 nautical miles
explanation: IntuVue (RDR-4000) software eliminates ground clutter, giving clutter-free viewing of significant weather out to 320 nm (and from ground level to 60,000 ft MSL). · FCOM 11.20.11

question: The scratch pad message VERIFY GW AND FUEL appears:
options: When gross weight is out of limit
When fuel data is invalid causing V NAV to disengage
When fuel data is invalid and fuel has to be entered manually
You will not reach your destination before running out of fuel
explanation: VERIFY GW AND FUEL: total fuel quantity data is invalid; the PERF INIT FUEL line changes to dashes. Enter fuel weight manually on PERF INIT and update it periodically. · FCOM 11.32.4 / 11.60.13

question: The supplemental and temporary data bases has storage capacity for:
options: 20 navaids and 2 airports
unlimited navaids and 6 airports
unlimited airports and 40 navaids
40 navaids and 6 airports
explanation: The supplemental and temporary navigation databases share storage capacity for forty navaids and six airports (first come, first served). · FCOM 11.32.1

question: To see both left and right GPS position in latitude and longitude you select:
options: POS REF page 3/3
POS REF page 2/3
POS REF page 1/3
PROG page 3/3
explanation: POS REF page 2/3 shows the left and right GPS latitude/longitude. POS SHIFT 3/3 shows GPS position relative to the FMC position. · FCOM 11.20.2

question: To see both left and right GPS position relative to the FMC position you select:
options: POS INIT page 1/3
POS SHIFT page 3/3
POS REF page 1/3
POS REF page 2/3
explanation: POS SHIFT page 3/3 shows the left and right GPS position (bearing/distance) relative to the FMC position. · FCOM 11.20.2 / 11.42.34

question: What are the 2 databases the FMC uses for operation?
options: Terrain and Airports
Peformance and Terrain
Navigation and Airports
Navigation and Performance
explanation: The FMC contains two databases: the performance database and the navigation database. · FCOM 11.32.1

question: What are the LNAV engagement criteria when more than 3 miles from the active route?
options: The aircraft can be on any heading
The aircraft must be on an intercept heading, but not necessarily before the active waypoint
The aircraft must be on a heading that will intercept the active route before the active waypoint
LNAV cannot be engaged if more than 3 miles from the active route
explanation: LNAV engages within 3 NM of the active leg on any heading. Outside 3 NM, it engages if on an intercept heading of 90° or less and the intercept will occur before the active waypoint. · FCOM 11.31.10 / 4.10.13

question: What components comprise the Flight Management System?
options: FMCS, AFDS, MCP, IRS, GPS.
FMCS, AFDS, A/T, MCP, EFIS, ADIRS.
FMCS, A/P, A/T, MCP, EFIS, IRS.
FMCS, AFDS, A/T, IRS, GPS.
explanation: The FMS is comprised of: flight management computer system (FMCS), autopilot/flight director system (AFDS), autothrottle (A/T), inertial reference systems (IRS) and the global positioning system (GPS). · FCOM 11.20.1

question: What does LRC on the FMC CRZ page mean?
options: Low Route Climb
Low Route Cruise
Lost Radio Contact
Long Range Cruise
explanation: Three primary cruise modes: economy (ECON), long range cruise (LRC), and a manually selected speed. · FCOM 11.42.17 / 11.31.21

question: What forward arc does the weather radar antenna sweep?
explanation: On the ground or in flight below 2,300 ft RA with PWS enabled, the radar scan is limited to 120 degrees; above that it reverts to 180 degrees (the normal sweep). · FCOM 11.20.11

question: What information is available with the IRS mode selector in ATT?
options: Only altitude information
Only attitude information
Only heading information
Only attitude and heading information
explanation: IRS mode selector ATT: provides only attitude and heading information. Heading is available after entry of the initial magnetic heading (POS INIT SET HDG or ISDU). · FCOM 11.10.21

question: What may cause the CDU message "DRAG REQUIRED" to be displayed?
options: Autothrottle is not responding
The descent has been commenced more than 5 miles before the Top of Descent point
An unexpected tailwind results in a significant increase in airspeed to maintain path.
The FMC is unable to determine the current flap setting
explanation: The CDU message DRAG REQUIRED is displayed if an unexpected tailwind results in a significant increase in airspeed to maintain the path. · FCOM 11.31.25

question: When setting up the FMC, what Pre-flight information is required.
options: Initial Position, Performance Data, Route, Takeoff Data.
Initial Position, SID, Route, Performance Data, Takeoff Data.
Performance Data, Navigation Database, Route, Takeoff Data.
Initial Position, Takeoff and Climb Thrust Limits, Route, Cruise Wind.
explanation: Required preflight information: initial position, performance data, route of flight, takeoff data. Optional: navigation database, RTA data, SID, cruise wind. · FCOM 11.31.1

question: Which statement is correct if an engine fails in flight?
options: Execution of the engine out cruise (ENG OUT CRZ) page disengages VNAV
The engine out cruise (ENG OUT CRZ) page is information only and the EXEC light will not illuminate
Execution of the engine out cruise (ENG OUT CRZ) page will change the VNAV speed to drift down speed
VNAV immediately disengages and can not be re-engaged
explanation: Selecting LT/RT ENG OUT changes the display to the ENG OUT CRZ page, which is information only. The crew flies the driftdown manually: A/T off, MCT, MCP speed to ENG OUT SPD, MCP altitude to max altitude, LVL CHG. · FCOM 11.42.30 / 11.31.33

question: With VNAV engaged, the AFDS pitch and A/T modes are commanded by the:
options: MCP
FCC
CWS
FMC
explanation: With a VNAV mode engaged, the FMC commands AFDS pitch and A/T modes to fly the vertical profile. · FCOM 4.20.6

question: After completing the FMC CDU pre-flight action, you look at the POS INIT page again. The SET IRS POS line is missing. What is required?
options: The alignment was not performed Cycle the IRSs to OFF and start a new alignment, then re-enter PPOS LAT/LONG
Re-enter PPOS LAT/LONG into the FMC
Return to ALIGN, then NAV and enter the PPOS LAT/LONG into the left or right IRS unit
Nothing. This is a normal indication once both IRSs have entered the NAV mode
explanation: SET IRS POS: box prompts are displayed when either IRS is in ALIGN mode and the present position has not been entered. The line blanks when the IRS transitions from alignment to the navigation mode, so this is normal. · FCOM 11.40.9

question: Arrivals can be selected on the FMC for either the origin or destination airport on the DEP/APR page:
options: Only origin airport is available until passing 120 NM from origin airport
Only origin airport is available until passing 60 NM from origin airport
Both origin and destination airport are available
Only destination airport is available
explanation: DEP/ARR INDEX: departure and arrival prompts are available for the origin airport; destination airports have only arrival prompts. Arrivals can therefore be selected for both origin and destination. · FCOM 11.40.22 / 11.40.23

question: During cruise the FMC Alerting Message VERIFY POSITION indicates:
options: The Captain has left the cockpit for an excessive period of time
Position information is contradictory
You are routing to the wrong airfield
The aircraft is excessively off the flight planned course
explanation: VERIFY POSITION: position information is contradictory. Refer to the FMC/IRS-radio navigation check supplementary procedure. · FCOM 11.60.14

question: During the PRELIMINARY COCKPIT PREPARATION, the IRS Mode Selector is moved from OFF to ATT instead of OFF to NAV. How can normal IRS operation be regained?
options: Switch to OFF wait for ALIGN light to extinguish then perform full alignment
Switch directly to NAV from ATT position
Switch to OFF position for 1 minute and then to ALIGN
Switch to ALIGN position than to NAV
explanation: Inadvertent selection of ATT on the ground: IRS mode selectors OFF, observe the ALIGN lights extinguish, then initiate a full alignment. · FCOM SP.11.4

question: During the PRELIMINARY COCKPIT PREPARATION, the IRS Mode Selectors are normally positioned to:
options: NAV
First NAV then ATT after 30 seconds
ALIGN
ATT
explanation: Preliminary preflight: IRS MODE SELECTORS ... NAV (the system aligns automatically). The airplane must be parked and not moved until alignment is complete. · FCOM NP.21.9

question: How are flight crew alerted that the current position and heading will not allow LNAV engagement?
options: There is no visual indication
The FMC will display the message 'NOT ON INTERCEPT HEADING'
You will see a ROUTE DISCONTINUITY message
The LNAV button will not illuminate
explanation: NOT ON INTERCEPT HEADING: the airplane is not within the LNAV capture criteria (LNAV pressed or LNAV disengages). Manually place the airplane on an intercept heading and re-engage LNAV. · FCOM 11.60.20

question: How long should a fast realignment take to complete?
options: 30 seconds
10 minutes
5 minutes
1 minute
explanation: During transits with brief ground times, a thirty second fast realignment and zeroing of ground speed error may be performed by selecting ALIGN while parked. · FCOM 11.20.5

question: How many ILS receivers are installed in Ryanair B737-800 aircraft?
options: 4 receivers.
1 receiver with 2 seperate channels.
2 receivers.
2 main receivers and a standby single channel receiver.
explanation: Two ILS receivers are installed, tuned manually on the VHF navigation control panels. · FCOM 11.20.8

question: If GROSS WT is not available from the FMC, the APPROACH REF page will be:
options: Flashing
Box prompts
Dashes
Blank
explanation: APPROACH REF GROSS WT: normally the FMC calculated weight; displays box prompts when gross weight is not available from the FMC. · FCOM 11.43.19

question: If power to the FMC is lost for more than 10 seconds in flight whilst using VNAV and LNAV, what will you need to do once power to the FMC has been restored?
options: Ensure that the appropriate Autothrottle, Roll and Pitch modes are engaged and select the active waypoint
Flight can be continued as normal
You will need to continue the remainder of the flight without VNAV or LNAV, as they will no longer be available
All FMC data will be lost, so you will need to re-enter the route
explanation: Power lost more than 10 s in flight: LNAV and VNAV disengage; all data is retained. On restoration the RTE LEGS page shows SELECT ACTIVE WPT/LEG; the FMC must be told how to return to the route, and appropriate modes re-engaged. · FCOM 11.32.5

question: If the FAULT Light on the IRS Mode Selector Unit illuminates, it indicates:
options: A failure of a symbol generator
That DC power for the respective IRS is not normal
A system fault affecting the respective IRS ATT and/or NAV mode has been detected
An entry of an invalid present position
explanation: FAULT light (amber): a system fault affecting the related IRS ATT and/or NAV modes has been detected. · FCOM 11.10.21

question: If the Fuel Quantity Indicating System fails during VNAV operations
options: PERF INIT page in order to keep gross weight ans performance data accurate
VNAV operation is not possible
The Scratchpad message: CHECK FMC FUEL is displayed
The flight crew should enter & periodically update manually estimated fuel weight
explanation: VERIFY GW AND FUEL: when fuel data is invalid, the crew enters fuel weight on PERF INIT and periodically updates it to keep gross weight and performance data valid. · FCOM 11.32.4 / 11.60.13

question: If the ND is showing data other than weather (such as ground proximity terrain data) when a Windshear warning is generated, what mode does the weather radar display revert to?
options: No warning messages will be displayed
There will be no change to the display, except that the "WINDSHEAR" message will be displayed
The display will show weather information
explanation: If the display shows data other than weather (e.g. GPWS terrain) when a windshear event occurs, it automatically switches to weather mode to present the windshear icon. · FCOM 11.20.13

question: If the ON DC light on left IRS Mode Selector Unit illuminates it means the related IRS is operating on DC power. Which bus is supplying the power?
options: DC bus1
The battery bus
The hot battery bus
The switched hot battery bus
explanation: IRS backup DC comes from the switched hot battery bus (right IRS backup terminates after 5 min). ON DC illuminates and the ground-call horn sounds on the ground. · FCOM 11.20.6

question: If you push both thrust levers fully forward whilst using a 22K Thrust is selected in the FMC, the engines will produce
options: Full 26K thrust
22K thrust
VMCG limited thrust
Manually advancing the thrust levers with Autothrottle engaged will have no effect on N1
explanation: The FMC derate only sets the target N1; in normal mode the EEC limits thrust to the engine's maximum rating at full forward thrust lever, so full rated (26K) thrust is produced. The FCOM does not state this directly. · FCOM 7.20.4

question: Illumination of amber AUTO SLAT FAIL light that can be reset, during recall indicates:
options: Failure of a single stall management yaw damper (SMYD) computer
Failure of both AUTO SLAT systems
Failure of both stall management (SMYD) computers
Failure of single AUTO SLAT system
explanation: AUTO SLAT FAIL: failure of the auto slat system; on MASTER CAUTION recall (resettable) it indicates failure of a single SMYD computer. · FCOM 9.10.4

question: In a climb on which FMC page is MAX ANGLE selected?
options: CRZ
PERF
PROG
CLB
explanation: MAX ANGLE (and MAX RATE) climb speeds are selected on the CLB page: maximum altitude over the shortest horizontal distance. · FCOM 11.41.8 / 11.41.10

question: In a VNAV descent, what would be the risk associated with setting the Missed Approach Altitude when within less than 300ft of the MAA?
options: Would transition from VNAV PTH to VNAV SPD
May cause engagement of ALT ACQ
May cause a transition to ALT HLD
Would transition from VNAV SPD to VNAV PTH
explanation: RYR: the MAA must be set when 300 ft above MDA/DA (or 300 ft below the MAA) to avoid inadvertent ALT ACQ. · FCOM NP.21.122

question: In addition to the ON DC light, what other indication is there that the IRSs are operating on DC power?
options: 'IRS PWR' appears in amber on the Captain's Navigation Display
On the ground, the Ground Call Horn will sound
'ON DC' appears in the HDG/STS window on the IRS panel
'IRS L' appears in amber on both of the Navigation Displays
explanation: On DC (battery) power the ON DC light illuminates and, on the ground, the ground-call horn in the nose wheel well sounds to alert maintenance. · FCOM 11.20.6

question: In degraded mode, what are the combinations for transmission and reception at the degraded station?
options: Capt. VHF 1, F.O. VHF 2, Observer VHF 2
All stations will use VHF 1
Capt. VHF 1, F.O. VHF 2, Observer VHF 1
Capt. VHF 2, F.O. VHF 1, Observer VHF 2
explanation: ACP degraded mode: the Captain uses VHF 1, the First Officer VHF 2, and the observer VHF 1. · FCOM 5.20.3

question: In normal operation, what are the power supplies for the Left and Right IRS?
options: Left IRS is fed by AC Transfer Bus 1, the right IRS is fed by the AC Standby Bus
Both IRSs are fed by the DC Standby Bus
Left IRS is fed by AC Transfer Bus 1, the right IRS is fed by AC Transfer Bus 2
Left IRS is fed by the AC Standby Bus, the right IRS is fed by AC Transfer Bus 2
explanation: Left IRS: AC standby bus; right IRS: AC transfer bus 2. Backup DC for both comes from the switched hot battery bus. · FCOM 11.20.6

question: In the event of a failure of both GPS Receivers, in addition to the GPS L INVALID and GPS R INVALID messages on the scratchpad, what other indication will you see
options: VERIFY POSITION in amber on the ND
ENTER POSITION scratchpad message
TERR POS displayed in amber on the ND
UNABLE REQD NAV PERF – RNP on FMC scratchpad
explanation: Both GPS failed: amber GPS light. TERR POS (amber) on the ND = look-ahead terrain unavailable due to position uncertainty, which is typical after loss of both GPS. The FCOM does not link the two directly. · FCOM 10.11.57 / 11.10.15

question: In turbulence mode, at what velocity of horizontal flow of precipitation towards or away from the weather radar will the target display turn magenta?
options: 2.5 meters per second or greater
10 meters per second or greater.
7.5 meters per second or greater
5 meters per second or greater.
explanation: Turbulence mode: precipitation moving horizontally at 5 or more meters per second toward or away from the antenna displays magenta (heavy turbulence). · FCOM 11.20.10

question: On aircraft with a mode selector selection of TEST, WX, WX/TURB and MAP,  selecting WX/TURB displays what?
options: Weather radar returns, and windshear out to 40 miles.
Weather radar returns, and turbulence out to 10 miles whilst on the ground only.
Weather radar returns, turbulence out to 40 miles, and windshear out to 20 miles.
Weather radar returns and turbulence within 40 miles.
explanation: WX/TURB: shows weather radar returns and turbulence within 40 miles. Turbulence detection needs precipitation; clear air turbulence cannot be detected. · FCOM 11.10.34

question: On later aircraft YW059 through YW164, what is the default Vertical Required Navigational Performance (VRNP) used by the FMC for oceanic, en route, and terminal phases of flight?
options: 400 feet below, 250 feet above the aircraft planned altitude.
250 feet below, 400 feet above the aircraft planned altitude.
250 feet.
400 feet.
explanation: YW059–YW164: the FMC uses 400 feet as the default VRNP for oceanic, en route and terminal phases. · FCOM 11.31.9

question: One of the purposes of the FMC FIX INFO page is to:
options: Establish your position relative to any unknown fix
Create a new waypoint at the intersection of the active route with a radial or distance from a known fix
Establish a fix relative to arrival airport position
Create new waypoints and using place bearing /place bearing or along track fix methods, monitor flight progress
explanation: FIX INFO: radial/distance from a fix; the route intersection point can be copied into the route as a waypoint on the LEGS page. · FCOM 11.42.50 / 11.42.51

question: Predictive Windshear alerts are triggered from:
options: Common Display System
Weather Radar System
Aural Warning Module
EGPWS
explanation: Predictive windshear (PWS) alerts are generated by the weather radar system. · FCOM 11.20.11 / 11.20.13

question: Regardless of what range you select on the Navigation Display, the range at which turbulence is detected is automatically limited to 40 nautical miles.
options: True
False
explanation: True. Turbulence is shown only within 40 miles regardless of the selected range. · FCOM 11.10.34

question: Some Ryanair B737-800 aircraft have a weather radar with the ability to be tilted a selected number of degrees above or below the horizon?
options: True
False
explanation: True. The tilt control tilts the antenna up or down to the selected degrees above or below the horizon. · FCOM 11.10.34

question: Some weather radar (WXR) panels have an manual altitude control switch (ALT) - when in MAN mode, this can be used to achieve which of the following:
options: Controls weather analysis alitude from 0 - 41,000 feet MSL in 100 feet increments
Manual altitude control is NOT available on any WXR control panels.
Controls weather analysis altitude from 0 - 60,000 MSL in 1000 feet increments
Controls weather analysis alitude from 500 - 60,000 feet MSL in 100 feet increments
explanation: Manual altitude control (MAN mode): ALT selects the weather analysis altitude from 0 to 60,000 ft MSL in 1000 ft increments. · FCOM 11.10.35 / 11.20.12

question: The aircraft is not certified for operations:
options: Above 78N or below 78S
The aircraft is certified for operations at all latitudes
Above 82N or below 82S
Above 73N or below 60S
explanation: Maximum flight operating latitude: 82° N and 82° S (with regional exceptions, e.g. 70° N between 80° W and 130° W). · FCOM L.10.2 / 11.20.4

question: The AUTO FAIL light on the cabin pressurization panel is illuminated alone:
options: This indicates that the alternate pressurization will automatically assume control
Indicates you should switch the pressurization to ALTN then back to AUTO to reset the system
This indicates a dual controller failure
Indicates the PAX OXY system has activated
explanation: AUTO FAIL alone = dual controller failure. AUTO FAIL + ALTN = single controller failure with automatic transfer to ALTN. · FCOM 2.10.14 / 2.10.15

question: The image below shows the IRS panel located on the AFT overhead panel, for later aircraft YW130 through YW164.  Other than OFF, what are the switch positions in the clockwise order?
options: ALIGN, NAV, ATT.
NAV, ALIGN, GLS
NAV, ALIGN, ATT.
ATT, ALIGN, NAV.
explanation: Picture question. IRS mode selector: OFF, then clockwise ALIGN, NAV; ATT is on the other side of OFF. · FCOM 11.10.20

question: The minimum equipment requirement for RA's to be generated is:
options: The other aircraft has a Mode C transponder
The other aircraft has a Mode S transponder
The other aircraft has ADS-B
The other aircraft is visible on primary radar
explanation: TCAS RAs require the intruder to report altitude (at least a Mode C transponder); Mode A only gives TAs. The FCOM does not state the minimum equipment. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: Under what circumstances will the V Speeds be removed from the FMC, the No V Speeds Flag reappear on the PFD, and the Scratchpad message TAKEOFF SPEEDS DELETED appear?
options: If the MFRA is adjusted before TO/GA is pressed
After first engine start, if the sensed OAT differs by more than 6 degrees C from the OAT entered on the TAKEOFF REF page
If the FMC generated QRH V Speeds differ by more than 1kt from the entered OPT calculated V Speeds
OAT has been changed on the TAKEOFF REF page after the V Speeds have been entered
explanation: TAKEOFF SPEEDS DELETED: change to runway/thrust/performance data after V speeds are selected, OR after first engine start the entered OAT differs from sensed OAT by ±6 °C. Enter corrected OAT on N1 LIMIT and reselect V speeds. · FCOM 11.60.11

question: Up to what range will the weather radar detect turbulence?
options: 40 nautical miles
420 nautical miles.
120 nautical miles.
220 nautical miles
explanation: Turbulence is displayed within 40 nautical miles. · FCOM 11.10.34

question: What does a flashing white ALIGN light on the overhead IRS panel tell you?
options: The last known position or the position in the FMC is different to that calculated by the IRS
All power to the IRS has been lost and it is using it's own internal battery
The align process has initiated. The lights will flash for a further two minutes
The selector is in ATT and the align process will not give position data
explanation: ALIGN flashing: alignment cannot be completed due to a significant difference between previous and entered positions, an unreasonable present position entry, or no present position entry. · FCOM 11.10.21

question: What does an amber FAULT light mean on the IRS panel?
options: A system fault affecting the related IRS ATT and/or NAV modes has been detected
AC Power to the IRS is not present
The selector knob is in the ATT position
DC power to the IRS is not present
explanation: FAULT light (amber): a system fault affecting the related IRS ATT and/or NAV modes has been detected. · FCOM 11.10.21

question: What does the GPS light illuminating indicate when either annunciator panel is pushed to initiate a recall?
options: IRS left or right selector switch selected to ATT.
Single GPS sensor unit failure.
GPS left and right system running in degraded mode.
Failure of both GPS sensor units
explanation: GPS light on recall: single GPS sensor unit failure (extinguishes when recall is reset). Steady GPS light: both failed. · FCOM 11.10.15

question: What is the minimum pavement width for a 180 degree turn?
explanation: 737-800: minimum width of pavement for a 180° turn = 79.7 ft (24.3 m) in the current FCOM; 24.1 is the closest option. 20.4 m is the 737-700. · FCOM 1.10.5 / 1.10.6

question: What will be the result on the APPROACH REF page if airplane gross weight is not available from the FMC?
options: GROSS WT will display box prompts
GROSS WT will display dashes
GROSS WT will be flashing
GROSS WT will be blank
explanation: APPROACH REF GROSS WT displays box prompts when gross weight is not available from the FMC. · FCOM 11.43.19

question: What will cause the ANP scales to expand out to the centre and turn amber?
options: Loss of one GPS and one IRS
The ANP is equal to RNP. The bars turn amber once the deviation is within the ANP bar limit for 5 continuous seconds
Loss of one GPS Receiver
Loss of one GPS, one IRS and one DME
explanation: ANP bars expand inward as ANP increases relative to RNP, just touch at the centre when ANP equals RNP, and turn from white to amber if the deviation is within the ANP bar limits for 5 continuous seconds. · FCOM 10.11.14

question: What would be the most likely cause of the following indications in flight?Disengagement of LNAV and VNAV, FMC ALERT light illuminates, FMC/CDU FAIL light on left CDU, VTK displayed in amber on the left Nav Display
options: Loss of power to both ADIRUs
Failure of the Left FMC
End of Descent deleted from the active route
Loss of both IRSs
explanation: Single (left) FMC failure: LNAV/VNAV disengage, FMC alert light, FAIL light on the left CDU, and failure indications on the left ND. Loss of IRS/ADIRU would give attitude/heading flags instead. · FCOM 11.32.5 / 11.10.14

question: When flying between storm cells, how much separation should you allow?
options: At least 40nm
10nm
6nm
20nm
explanation: Avoid storm cells by at least 20 nm each, so allow at least 40 nm between two cells. The FCOM gives no figure; this is FCTM/radar guidance. · FCOM 11.20.10

question: When will the FMC Alerting Message VERIFY GW AND FUEL be shown in the CDU scratchpad?
options: When gross weight is out of limit
When fuel quantity data is invalid and estimated fuel weight has to be entered manually
The FMC has detected an unexpected drop in fuel quantity
When fuel quantity data is invalid causing VNAV to disengage
explanation: VERIFY GW AND FUEL: fuel quantity data invalid; the PERF INIT fuel shows dashes and fuel weight must be entered manually and updated periodically. · FCOM 11.32.4 / 11.60.13

question: When will you see the FMC Alerting Message 'VERIFY POSITION' ?
options: On the ground only, if position information is sensed as being incorrect
If the position does not correspond to an airport in the database
In the cruise only
The aircraft is excessively off the flight planned course
explanation: VERIFY POSITION (on ground): position information is contradictory. Check manually entered data and crosscheck IRS, GPS and FMC positions; re-align the IRSs if needed. (In flight the messages are VERIFY POS: xxx-xxx.) · FCOM 11.60.14

question: Where on the FMC CDU are the GPS latitude and longitude displayed?
options: NAV DATA
POS REF page 2
INIT REF
POS INIT page 1
explanation: POS REF page 2/3 shows the left and right GPS latitude and longitude. · FCOM 11.20.2

question: Which indications are correct for a failure of the left FMC?
options: FMC CDU FAIL light illuminates, left FMC CDU screen blanks, left ND screen blanks, LNAV diengages with VNAV remaining available
FMC P/RST amber light illuminates, normal operation continues with remaining functioning FMC automatically driving both ND screens
FMC P/RST amber light illuminates, FAIL light on FMC CDU illuminates, LNAV and VNAV disconnect if engaged, failure information displayed on left ND after delay of approximately 25 to 30 seconds
FMC P/RST amber light illuminates, A/P P/RST light illuminates, LNAV and VNAV disconnect if engaged, left ND not available
explanation: Single FMC failure: FMC alert light, FAIL light on the related CDU, LNAV and VNAV disconnect if engaged, failure information on the related ND after a short delay. The FMC source select switch can transfer to the other FMC. · FCOM 11.10.14 / 11.32.5

question: Which statement is correct for the fuel quantity displayed on the FMC PROGRESS Page 1?
options: Displays wing tank fuel only
Displays total fuel used since engine start, based on fuel flow inputs to the FMC
Displays center tank fuel only
Displays present total fuel remaining, as obtained from the fuel quantity indication system
explanation: PROGRESS page 1 FUEL QTY: displays the present total fuel quantity remaining as obtained from the airplane fuel quantity indication system. · FCOM 11.41.19

question: Which statement is correct when an active navigation database expires in flight?
options: Both LNAV and VNAV will disengage
The alerting message UNABLE REQD NAV PERF - RNP will appear in the CDU scratchpad
The expired database continues to be used until the active date is changed after landing
All LNAV information is lost and waypoints have to be created manually in the temporary navigation database
explanation: When an active database expires in flight, the expired database continues to be used until the active date is changed after landing. · FCOM 11.40.7

question: With VNAV SPD engaged when climbing toward an 'at' altitude restriction, what FMA transition would you see?
options: Transition to ALT HLD
Transition to VNAV PTH
Would remain in VNAV PTH
Transitions to VNAV SPD
explanation: In a VNAV SPD climb, on reaching an altitude constraint the AFDS levels off and the pitch FMA changes to VNAV PTH (VNAV constrained altitude annunciates VNAV PTH). · FCOM 11.31.23 / 4.10.6

question: For landing, what is the maximum fuel imbalance between the No.1 and No.2 main tanks?
options: 553 Kgs.
653 Kgs.
726 Kgs.
453 Kgs.
explanation: Limitations: lateral imbalance between main tanks 1 and 2 must be scheduled to be zero. Random fuel imbalance must not exceed 453 kg for taxi, takeoff, flight or landing. · FCOM L.10.10

question: How many fuel measuring sticks are installed?
explanation: Six fuel measuring sticks in each main tank and four in the center tank = 16. · FCOM 12.10.8

question: In flight a fuel imbalance between No1 and No2 tanks can be corrected by:
options: Increase thrust setting on the side with higher amount of fuel and decrease thrust setting on side with lower amount of fuel.

Opening the crossfeed valve, turning OFF the fuel pumps for the tank with lower fuel and allowing the pumps from the tank with the higher amount of fuel to transfer fuel to the other tank until the IMBAL amber warning light extinguishes, then close the Crossfeed valve and turn back on the pumps.
Open the Crossfeed cock, turn off the pumps on the low side until the Fuel Quantity Indicators are balanced.
A Fuel imablance cannot be rectified in flight, as fuel transfer between tanks can only be carried out on the ground using the Ground Refuelling Panel switches.
explanation: QRH: open the CROSSFEED and switch OFF the fuel pumps of the LOW tank, so both engines feed from the high tank until balanced, then restore. Fuel is not 'transferred' into the other tank — the high tank just feeds both engines. (FCOM 12.20.2: crossfeed lets one main tank feed both engines.) · FCOM QRH FUEL IMBALANCE / 12.20.2

question: What does a blue light mean on the Nitrogen Generation System (NGS).
options: NGS system functioning in a degraded condition.
Bright blue means NGS valve closed or disagrees with commanded position
Dim blue means NGS valve agrees with commanded position.
Bright blue means NGS valve closed.
explanation: NGS indicator (main wheel well): OPERATIONAL green = fully operational; DEGRADED blue = operating in a degraded condition; INOPERATIVE amber (no lights also = inoperative). Fitted YF501–YF695, YK885–YW164. · FCOM 12.10.10

question: Which fuel valves are Flight Crew made aware of their position by means of flight deck indications?
options: Fuel valves are automatic with no flight deck indications.
Centre, No1 and No2 Tanks Fuel Pump Valves, Engine Fuel Shutoff Valve, Cross Feed valve.
Engine Fuel Shutoff valves, Spar Fuel Shutoff valves, Crossfeed valve.
Engine Fuel Shutoff valves, Spar Fuel Shutoff valves, Crossfeed valve, Centre, No1 and No2 tanks Fuel Pump valves.
explanation: Flight deck valve-position lights exist for the ENG VALVE CLOSED (engine fuel shutoff), SPAR VALVE CLOSED and crossfeed VALVE OPEN. Fuel pumps only have LOW PRESSURE lights — there are no pump 'valves'. · FCOM 12.10.1 / 12.10.2

question: After the Centre Tank has emptied the auto shutoff logic stops the pumps, how do the pumps then function?
options: Switching the pumps to OFF and then back to ON recycles the auto shutoff logic and the pumps will again activate.
The pumps will not funtion again until the Centre tank has been refueled above 453 kg.
The pumps can be activated if necessary by tripping the auto shutoff circuit breaker on Panel P6-1 behind the First Officer.
There is no shutoff logic, the pumps continue to run with the amber LOW PRESSURE light illuminated until the Flight Crew switch the pumps to OFF.
explanation: Setting a center tank pump switch OFF resets its auto shutoff logic. When set ON again after being OFF, the pump activates again until switched OFF or the auto shutoff logic deactivates it. · FCOM 12.10.2

question: During cruise you note both center tank fuel pumps have failed as indicated by the illumination of both center tank fuel pump LOW PRESSURE lights. You still have 320 kg of fuel in the center tank and both main tanks are full. You will see:
options: a CONFIG indication on the CDS
a LOW indication on the CDS
There will be no indication on CDS
a pump LOW PRESSURE indication on the CDS
explanation: No CDS indication: CONFIG needs both CTR pump switches OFF with > 726 kg; LOW is for main tanks < 453 kg. Only the LOW PRESSURE lights, then MASTER CAUTION + FUEL after 10 s of continuous illumination (or up to 5 min of flickering at low quantity). · FCOM 12.10.2 / 12.10.5

question: How many fuel pumps does each tank have, and where are they located?
options: The centre tank has 1 AC fuel pump located on the front wall of the centre tank and 1 located on the rear wall of the centre tank.  The No1 main tank has 1 pump located on the rear wall of the No1 tank and 1 pump located on the front wall of the No1 tank .  The No2 tank has 1 pump located on the rear wall of the No2 tank and 1 pump located on the front wall of the No2 tank..

The centre tank has 2 AC pumps located on the forward wall of the centre tank.  The No1 main tank has 2 AC pumps located on the rear wall of the No1 tank.  The No2 main tank has 2 AC pumps located on the rear wall of the No2 tank.

The centre tank has 2 AC pumps located on the forward wall of the centre tank.  The No1 main tank has 1 AC pump located on the rear wall of the No1 tank.  The No2 main tank has 1 AC pump located on the rear wall of the No2 tank.

The centre tank has 2 AC fuel pumps mounted on the rear wall of the centre tank.  The No1 tank has 2 AC pumps mounted in the centre tank - 1 on the front wall and one one the rear wall.  The No2 tank has 2 AC pumps mounted in the centre tank - 1 on the front wall and 1 on the rear wall.  There is also a Jet pump mounted in the centre tank discharging into No1 tank
explanation: FCOM confirms each tank has two AC pumps and a center tank scavenge jet pump feeding main tank 1; pump mounting locations are not given in the FCOM — answer from the banks. · FCOM 12.20.2 / 12.20.3

question: In-flight, the two fuel pump LOW PRESSURE Lights for main tank No.1 illuminate. What happens to the No.1 engine?
options: it receives fuel from main tank No. 2 automatically
it receives fuel from main tank No.1 through a suction feed line that bypasses the pumps
it will shut down due to fuel starvation
it continues to operate due to the metering of fuel by the Fuel Control Unit
explanation: When main tank pump pressure is low, each engine can draw fuel from its own main tank through a suction feed line that bypasses the pumps. At high altitude dissolved air may restrict flow (thrust loss or flameout possible). · FCOM 12.20.2

question: Pulling an engine FIRE WARNING switch up:
options: closes both the engine fuel shutoff valve and the spar fuel shutoff valve
automatically discharges the fire extinguisher if fire is detected
closes the spar fuel shutoff valve; the fuel cutoff lever has to be moved to cutoff to close the engine fuel shutoff valve
closes the engine fuel shutoff valve; the fuel cutoff lever has to be moved to cutoff to close the spar fuel shutoff valve
explanation: Pulling the engine fire switch closes both the engine fuel shutoff valve and the spar fuel shutoff valve (same as start lever to CUTOFF). Discharge needs the switch to be rotated. · FCOM 8.20.2 / 12.20.3

question: The fuel imbalance alert is only displayed when the aircraft is in the air.
options: True
False
explanation: False. IMBAL (amber) is displayed when the airplane is on the ground or in the air, when main tanks differ by more than 453 kg. · FCOM 12.10.6

question: What is the indication of the Crossfeed VALVE OPEN Light when the CROSSFEED selector is positioned OPEN and the crossfeed valve is closed?
options: illuminated dim blue
extinguished
illuminated amber
illuminated bright blue
explanation: Crossfeed VALVE OPEN light: bright blue = valve in transit OR position disagrees with selector; dim blue = valve open; extinguished = valve closed. · FCOM 12.10.2

question: What is the source of electrical power for the engine fuel shutoff valves?
options: the AC Standby Bus
the Battery Bus
the Hot Battery Bus
the DC Standby Bus
explanation: Engine fuel shutoff valves: fuel actuated, solenoid controlled, powered from the battery bus. Spar valves: DC motor from the hot battery bus. Crossfeed: DC motor from the battery bus. · FCOM 12.20.3

question: Where is the fuel temperature sensor located?
options: In each engine supply line adjacent to the Fuel Flow Meter
1 in the inboard rear of each main tank
In the No1 main tank.
In each engine Hydro-Mechanical fuel control unit.
explanation: A sensor in main tank No.1 provides the FUEL TEMP indication (AC powered). · FCOM 12.20.3

question: With the Centre (CTR) tank FUEL PUMP switches ON, if an amber LOW PRESSURE light illuminates, it also immediately illuminates MASTER CAUTION and a FUEL system annunciator lights.
options: True
False
explanation: False. With CTR pump switches ON, continuous illumination of one LOW PRESSURE light for 10 seconds is needed before MASTER CAUTION and FUEL illuminate. · FCOM 12.10.2

question: With the engines running, the fuel CONFIG alert will be displayed by the No1 and No2 Fuel Quantity Indicators turning Amber, when the Centre tank quantity is greater than 726kg and the Centre tank pump switches are off
options: True
False
explanation: False. CONFIG (either engine running, CTR > 726 kg, both CTR pump switches OFF) shows on the CENTER tank indicator — its digits (and arc on YA573–YW063) turn amber, not tanks 1 and 2. · FCOM 12.10.5

question: Aircraft in flight. You have 2500 kg of fuel in the No 1 main tank and 3060 kg of fuel in the No 2 main tank. You will see:
options: The fuel quantity arc and digits on main tank No 2 turn amber
An amber IMBAL indication below main tank No 1 accompanied by a Master Caution Light and system annunciation for fuel
An amber IMBAL indication below main tank No 1, fuel quantity arc and digits on tank with lower quantity also turns amber
An amber LOW indication below main tank No 1 accompanied by a Master Caution Light and system annunciation for fuel
explanation: Difference 560 kg > 453 kg, so IMBAL is shown below the lower tank (No.1) and that tank's digits turn amber (arc and digits on YA573–YW063). No Master Caution for IMBAL. · FCOM 12.10.6

question: Center fuel tank fuel is used before main tank fuel because:
options: Center tank check valves open at a higher differential than main tank check valves
Main tank pumps cannot produce pressure until the center tank LOW PRESSURE light illuminate and center tank pumps are turned OFF
Centre tank fuel pumps produce higher pressure than main tank pumps
Center tank check valves open at a lower differential than main tank check valves
explanation: Center tank pumps produce higher pressure than main tank pumps, so center tank fuel is used first even with all pumps operating. · FCOM 12.20.2

question: During an engine start , when an engine start lever is positioned to IDLE detent, which of the following statements is correct?
options: The related SPAR VALVE CLOSED light is unaffected by the engine start lever position.
The related blue SPAR VALVE CLOSED light transitions from extinguished, to bright, and then dim.
The related blue SPAR VALVE CLOSED light transitions from dim, to bright, and then extinguished.
The related blue SPAR VALVE CLOSED light transitions from dim to extinguished.
explanation: Start lever to IDLE: SPAR VALVE CLOSED light goes dim (closed) → bright (in transit) → extinguished (open). · FCOM SP.12.2 / 12.10.1

question: Engine Fuel Flow is measured:
options: before the fuel filter
after passing through spar fuel shutoff valve
before the first stage fuel pump
after passing through the engine fuel shutoff valve
explanation: Fuel flow is measured after passing through the engine fuel shutoff valve, displayed on the DU and sent to the FMS. · FCOM 7.20.7

question: In flight both centre tank fuel pumps selected OFF with 760 kg remaining in the centre tank, and both main tanks are full. What will be displayed on the Upper Display Unit?
options: A CONFIG alert under the centre fuel contents gauge
A CONFIG alert indication under the left and right fuel contents gauges
A fuel LOW alert indication below the centre tank contents gauge
The centre tank pump LOW PRESSURE lights will be illuminated
explanation: CONFIG: either engine running, center tank more than 726 kg and both center pump switches OFF → amber CONFIG at the center tank indicator. · FCOM 12.10.5

question: In the unlikely situation of total generator failure, at high altitude thrust deterioration may occur. Why?
options: When on STBY power the fuel pumps run a little slower
The fuel will be suction fed, which may cause dissolved air released from the fuel to restrict fuel flow in the suction feed line.
When on STBY power the HMU will be unreliable, therefore thrust deterioration might occur at high altitude
Loss of AC power will affect the ignition system and therefore create a potential risk of flameout
explanation: With no AC the fuel pumps stop and engines suction feed. Dissolved air released as the airplane climbs can collect in the suction line and restrict fuel flow — thrust deterioration or flameout at high altitude. · FCOM 12.20.2

question: In which fuel tanks are bypass valves located?
options: Both main tanks
None
Center tank
All tanks
explanation: The suction feed line in each MAIN tank has a bypass valve around the pumps; the main tank bypass valves can also be used for suction defueling. · FCOM 12.20.2

question: The amber fuel IMBAL alert will remain displayed until the imbalance is reduced to:-
options: 726 kgs
91 kgs
453 kgs
363 kgs
explanation: IMBAL appears above 453 kg difference and remains until the imbalance is reduced to 91 kg. · FCOM 12.10.6

question: The engine fuel shutoff valve:
options: And the spar fuel shutoff valve require AC power to operate
Is the only fuel shutoff with an associated blue light on the forward overhead fuel panel
Is controlled by both the Engine Fire Warning switch and the Engine Start Lever, however, the spar fuel shutoff valve is controlled only the Engine Start Lever
And the spar fuel shutoff valve close when the respective Engine Start Lever is placed to CUTOFF
explanation: Both the spar and engine fuel shutoff valves close when the start lever goes to CUTOFF or the engine fire switch is pulled. Both have blue lights; both are DC powered. · FCOM 12.20.3

question: What does an illuminated main tank fuel pump LOW PRESSURE Light indicate?
options: Low fuel pressure in the affected tank
Low fuel pump input pressure
Low pressure in the fuel manifold
Low fuel pump output pressure
explanation: Main tank pump LOW PRESSURE light: pump output pressure is low, or the FUEL PUMP switch is OFF. · FCOM 12.10.3

question: What is the purpose of the centre tank fuel scavenge jet pump?
options: Transfer fuel from the left main tank to the centre tank
Transfer the last remaining fuel from the centre tank to the left main tank
Transfer fuel from the centre tank to the right main tank
Feed Engine number 1 if both left main tank pumps fail
explanation: The scavenge jet pump transfers any remaining center tank fuel to main tank No.1 (left). · FCOM 12.20.3

question: What operates the spar fuel shutoff valve?
options: DC motor from Hot Battery Bus
AC motor from Standby Bus
Pushrods and cranks
Cables and pulleys
explanation: Spar fuel shutoff valves are DC motor operated from the hot battery bus. · FCOM 12.20.3

question: When the engine start lever is placed to CUTOFF:-
options: The engine fuel shutoff valve only closes.
The spar fuel shutoff valve only closes.
The spar fuel shutoff valve and engine fuel shutoff valve both close.
The spar fuel shutoff valve, engine fuel shutoff valve and engine bypass valve all close.
explanation: Both the spar fuel shutoff valve and the engine fuel shutoff valve close whenever the engine start lever is placed to CUTOFF or the engine fire switch is pulled. · FCOM 12.20.3

question: Which statement is correct in relation to the amber fuel IMBAL alert?
options: The centre tank pumps should be switched on
It will be displayed when the main tanks imbalance is 363 kgs.
The fuel pumps should be switched off in the tank with the greatest quantity
It will remain displayed until the imbalance reduces to 91 kgs or less.
explanation: IMBAL: main tanks differ by more than 453 kg, shown below the tank with less fuel, on the ground or in the air, until the imbalance is reduced to 91 kg. · FCOM 12.10.6

question: With all fuel tanks full and all electrically driven fuel pumps switched on, which tank feeds which engine?
options: Both engines will be fed by the centre tank
Number 1 engine fed by the right tank, Number 2 engine fed by the left tank.
Number 1 engine fed by the left tank, Number 2 engine fed by the right tank.
explanation: Both engines are normally pressure fed from the center tank until it is near zero (center pumps produce higher pressure), then each engine from its own main tank. · FCOM 12.20.1

question: With fuel in the center and main tanks, both engines operating and all fuel pump switches ON, fuel from which tank(s) is used first?
options: No 2 main tank
Center tank
Not main tank
Both main tanks
explanation: Center tank pumps produce higher pressure than main tank pumps, so center fuel is used first even with all pumps ON. · FCOM 12.20.2

question: During cruise both centre tank fuel pumps have failed. There is still 460 kg in the centre tank, and both main tanks are full. The upper Display Unit will show:
options: A CONFIG Alert indication.
A pump low pressure indication.
A LOW Alert indication under centre tank.
There will be no indication on the CDS
explanation: CONFIG needs both CTR switches OFF with > 726 kg; LOW applies to main tanks < 453 kg. With 460 kg and pumps failed (switches ON) nothing appears on the CDS — only the LOW PRESSURE lights and MASTER CAUTION/FUEL. · FCOM 12.10.5

question: During the cruise (with all FUEL PUMP switches on), if both centre tank fuel pump LOW PRESSURE lights illuminate but you still have 320 kg of fuel in the centre tank and both main tanks are full, what other indication(s) would you see in this scenario?
options: A pump LOW PRESSURE indication on the CDS
There will be no indications on the CDS, but both the MASTER CAUTION and FUEL system annunciator lights will illuminate
A CONFIG indication on the CDS
A LOW indication on the CDS
explanation: No CDS alert (CONFIG needs switches OFF and > 726 kg). With CTR switches ON, continuous LOW PRESSURE for 10 seconds brings on MASTER CAUTION and FUEL. · FCOM 12.10.2

question: During the cruise, both centre tank fuel pump LOW PRESSURE lights illuminate. You still have 320 kg of fuel in the center tank and both main tanks are full. Will you see any other indication?
options: A pump LOW PRESSURE indication on the CDS
A LOW indication on the CDS
There will be no indication on the CDS, but the Master Caution will illuminate
A CONFIG indication on the CDS
explanation: No CDS indication; after 10 s of continuous LOW PRESSURE (CTR switches ON) MASTER CAUTION and FUEL illuminate. · FCOM 12.10.2

question: If the Centre Tank is empty, the Centre Tank pumps are switched off, all four Main Tank pumps are switched on and the CROSSFEED Valve is left in the OPEN position, what may occur?
options: A CONFIG alert will be displayed
The Centre Tank LOW PRESSURE lights may flicker and then illuminate for 10 seconds
The CROSSFEED VALVE light will extinguish
A fuel IMBAL may occur
explanation: FCOM: continued crossfeed use will result in a progressive fuel imbalance — with crossfeed open one side's pumps can end up feeding both engines. · FCOM 12.20.2

question: If you take off with the fuel panel in the standard configuration and then the LEFT centre tank pump fails, what will happen to the fuel levels in the tanks if no switch positions are changed?
options: Fuel from the right main tank will feed the right engine, fuel from the left main tank will feed the left engine
Fuel from the centre tank will feed the left engine, fuel from the right main tank will feed the right engine
Fuel from the centre tank will feed the right engine, fuel from the left main tank will feed the left engine
Fuel from the centre tank will continue to feed both engines
explanation: Each center pump pressurizes its own side of the manifold (crossfeed closed). With the left CTR pump failed, the left engine is fed by main tank 1 pumps, while the right engine is still fed from the center tank — an imbalance builds. · FCOM 12.20.1 / 12.20.2

question: In flight if the indicated fuel temperature on the FUEL TEMP gauge were to descend to below -43 degrees Celsius, what warnings would you see on the flight deck?
options: There would be no additional warnings
MASTER CAUTION and FUEL
MASTER CAUTION and OVHD
FUEL TEMP warning on the MFD
explanation: The FUEL TEMP indicator only displays tank 1 temperature — there is no caution light or alert for low fuel temperature. The limit (–43°C or freezing point +3°C, whichever higher) is monitored by the crew. · FCOM 12.10.1 / L.10.10

question: In flight, if there was 1500Kg of fuel in the centre tank with both centre tank pumps switched OFF, what warning would you see?
options: LOW FUEL
Master Caution and FUEL annunciator
The will be no warning
CONFIG
explanation: CONFIG: either engine running, center tank more than 726 kg, both center pump switches OFF. · FCOM 12.10.5

question: Minimum in-flight tank fuel temperature is:
options: 3 degrees above the fuel freezing point or -43 degrees, whichever is higher
-43 degrees
3 degrees above the fuel freezing point or -43 degrees, whichever is lower
3 degrees above the fuel freezing point
explanation: Minimum tank fuel temperature prior to takeoff and inflight: –43°C, or 3°C above the fuel freezing point, whichever is higher. FSII additives do not change it. · FCOM L.10.10

question: On an NG aircraft, what is the correct sequence regarding the SPAR VALVE CLOSED light during a normal engine shutdown procedure after the START LEVER is positioned to CUTOFF?
options: Transitions from extinguished to bright
Transitions from extinguished, to bright and then dim
Transitions from extinguished to dim
Transitions from dim, to bright and then extinguishes
explanation: Start lever to CUTOFF: SPAR VALVE CLOSED light goes extinguished (open) → bright (in transit) → dim (closed). · FCOM SP.12.2

question: On the B737-800, what are the USABLE FUEL capacities of the aircraft fuel tanks?
options: Centre = 20,025 ltr, No1 = 4,876 ltr, No2 = 4,876 ltr
Centre 13,066kg, No1 = 3,915kg, No2 = 3,915kg
Centre = 12,726kg, No1 = 3,453kg, No2 = 3,453kg
Centre = 3915kg, No1 = 13,066kg , No2 = 13,066kg
explanation: Usable fuel (0.8029 kg/l): No.1 and No.2 4,876 l / 3,915 kg each; center 16,273 l / 13,066 kg; total 26,025 l / 20,896 kg. · FCOM 12.20.4

question: The BOOST PUMPS are located in
options: In the avionics bay
In the Hydraulic reservoir
The CENTER TANK
The MAIN TANK
explanation: FCOM says only that each tank has two AC pumps. Bank answer (matches the other bank question on pump location): the boost pumps are physically mounted in the center tank area. · FCOM 12.20.2

question: The CONFIG warning is inhibited with less than_ kg in the center tank
explanation: CONFIG remains until both engines are not running, center tank quantity is less than 363 kg, or one center pump switch is ON. · FCOM 12.10.6

question: The Crossfeed valve must be:
options: Open for Takeoff
Closed for Takeoff and Landing
Closed for Cruise
Open for Takeoff and Landing
explanation: Normal configuration: crossfeed CLOSED (VALVE OPEN light extinguished) — it is opened only for fuel balancing or a non-normal. Not stated as a limitation in the FCOM. · FCOM NP / 12.10.2

question: The electrically driven fuel pumps for the centre tank discharge at a higher pressure than the main tanks so that the centre tank fuel is used first
options: To reduce the bending load at the root of the wing
To keep the CofG as far forward as possible to improve stability
To reduce the risk of fuel contamination
To reduce the fire risk for the passengers
explanation: FCOM gives the mechanism (center pumps at higher pressure). The reason — keeping fuel in the wings as long as possible to relieve wing root bending — is general design knowledge. · FCOM 12.20.2

question: The maximum fuel temperature is
options: 69 degrees
59 degrees
49 degrees
94 degrees
explanation: AFM limitation: maximum tank fuel temperature is 49°C. · FCOM L.10.9

question: There are CDS fuel alerts indications for:
options: Fuel quantity low in main tank, impending fuel filter bypass, excessive fuel flow difference between engines
Any fuel pump producing low or no pressure with the pump switch on, impending fuel filter bypass, excessive fuel quantity difference between main tanks
Fuel quantity low in main tank, both center tank fuel pumps producing low or no pressure with fuel in center tank, excessive fuel quantity difference between main tanks
Fuel quantity low in center or main tank, either center tank fuel pump producing low or no pressure with fuel in center tank, excessive fuel flow difference between engines.
explanation: CDS fuel alerts: LOW (main tank < 453 kg), CONFIG (fuel in center with center pumps not supplying), IMBAL (main tanks differ by > 453 kg). · FCOM 12.10.5 / 12.10.6

question: True or false - With the Centre (CTR) tank FUEL PUMP switches ON, if an amber LOW PRESSURE light illuminates during the takeoff roll, no other warnings will illuminate.
options: True
False
explanation: False. With CTR switches ON, continuous illumination of one LOW PRESSURE light for 10 seconds illuminates MASTER CAUTION and FUEL (also during the takeoff roll). · FCOM 12.10.2

question: What does the fuel scavenge system do?
options: Transfers any remaining fuel in the centre tank to main tank number 1 as long as the fwd main tank 1 pump is operating and the main tank number one is half-full or less
Allows fuel from either Main Tank to be transferred to the Centre Tank
Transfers fuel from Main Tank 2 to Main Tank 1
Defuels the aircraft
explanation: With main tank No.1 FWD pump ON, the scavenge jet pump transfers remaining center tank fuel to main tank 1, starting when tank 1 is about half full, and continues for the rest of the flight. · FCOM 12.20.3

question: What is the correct sequence regarding the SPAR VALVE CLOSED light during a normal engine start procedure after the START LEVER is positioned to IDLE detent?
options: Transitions from extinguished, to bright and then dim.
Transitions from extinguished to bright.
Transitions from dim, to bright and then extinguishes.
Transitions from extinguished to dim.
explanation: Start lever to IDLE: SPAR VALVE CLOSED dim → bright → extinguished. (At CUTOFF it is the reverse: extinguished → bright → dim.) · FCOM SP.12.2

question: What is the minimum in-flight tank fuel temperature?
options: 3°C above the fuel freezing point or -43°C, whichever is highe
3°C below the fuel freezing point or -49°C, whichever is higher
explanation: –43°C or 3°C above the fuel freezing point, whichever is higher. · FCOM L.10.10

question: What may be an indication of a fuel leak during the cruise?
options: A CONFIG alert or pump LOW PRESSURE alert
Engine OVHT warning
An IMBAL alert, excessive fuel flow to one engine or total fuel being considerably less than planned fuel
Abnormally high EGT or fluctuating N1
explanation: Fuel leak clues: IMBAL, unusual fuel flow to one engine, or total fuel considerably less than planned (fuel used + remaining doesn't add up). · FCOM QRH FUEL LEAK / 12.10.6

question: What may the failure of a single Centre Tank pump in flight with all fuel pumps switched ON lead to?
options: Flameout
A LOW alert
A CONFIG alert
A fuel IMBAL
explanation: With one CTR pump failed (crossfeed closed) that engine feeds from its own main tank while the other feeds from the center, so a main tank IMBAL develops. · FCOM 12.20.2

question: When ALL of the AC fuel pumps are switched on and operating and there is fuel in each tank, which tank would fuel for the APU normally be supplied from?
options: Main tank No.1
The right hand side of the fuel manifold
Main tank No.2
The Centre tank
explanation: APU fuel comes from the left side of the fuel manifold when AC pumps run. With fuel in the center and all pumps on, the higher-pressure center pumps supply the manifold — so it is center tank fuel. (No AC pumps: suction fed from main tank 1.) · FCOM 12.20.3 / 12.20.2

question: When would a fuel LOW indication be displayed?
options: When a main tank pump output pressure is low
When the fuel supply pressure to an engine is low
When a main tank quantity is less than 453Kg
When a main tank quantity is less than 762Kg
explanation: Fuel LOW (amber): main tank quantity less than 453 kg; remains until the tank is increased to 567 kg. · FCOM 12.10.5

question: When would you see the Fuel CONFIG alert?
options: More than 726 kg of fuel in the Centre Tank and the Centre Tank Pump switches are OFF
Only one of the Main Tank pump switches are ON
Less than 453 kg of fuel in the Centre Tank
explanation: CONFIG: either engine running, center tank more than 726 kg and both center tank pump switches OFF. · FCOM 12.10.5

question: Which of these Fuel System alerts has the highest priority?
options: Fuel CONFIG
Fuel LOW
Fuel IMBAL
explanation: IMBAL is inhibited by a fuel LOW indication when both exist, so LOW has priority. · FCOM 12.10.6

question: Which statement is correct when the aircraft is in flight, with 2500 kgs of fuel in main tank No.1 and 3060 kgs of fuel in main tank No.2 ?
options: The fuel quantity digits for main tank No.2 turn amber
This will cause an amber LOW alert below main tank No.1 accompanied by MASTER CAUTION lights and a System Annunciation light for FUEL
This will cause an amber IMBAL alert below main tank No.1. The fuel quantity digits for the tank also turn amber
This will cause an amber IMBAL indication below main tank No.1 accompanied by MASTER CAUTION lights and a System Annunciation Light for FUEL
explanation: 560 kg difference (> 453 kg): amber IMBAL below the lower tank (No.1) and its digits turn amber (arc too on YA573–YW063). No Master Caution. · FCOM 12.10.6

question: Which statement is correct when the CROSSFEED selector is positioned in the closed position and the crossfeed valve is closed?
options: Crossfeed VALVE OPEN light illuminated
Crossfeed VALVE OPEN light extinguished
Crossfeed VALVE OPEN light illuminated dim blue
Crossfeed VALVE OPEN caption on lower DU
explanation: Crossfeed VALVE OPEN light extinguished = valve closed. Dim blue = open; bright blue = in transit or disagrees with the selector. · FCOM 12.10.2

question: With the engines running, the fuel CONFIG alert will be displayed when the Centre tank quantity is 762kg and the Centre tank pump switches are on
options: False
True
explanation: False. CONFIG needs BOTH center pump switches OFF (plus engine running and > 726 kg). With the switches on there is no CONFIG. · FCOM 12.10.5

question: Hydraulic System A powers which hydraulic system components?
options: Ground spoilers, trailing edge flaps and the power transfer unit (PTU)
Landing gear, normal nose wheel steering and the power transfer unit (PTU)
Alternate nose wheel steering, Alternate brakes and ground spoilers
Ground spoilers, normal nose wheel steering and the Landing Gear Transfer Unit
explanation: System A powers: ailerons, rudder, elevator & feel, flight spoilers 2,4,9,11, ground spoilers, alternate brakes, No.1 thrust reverser, autopilot A, normal nose wheel steering, landing gear and the PTU. TE flaps, the landing gear transfer valve and alternate NWS are System B. · FCOM 13.20.2

question: While airborne and with flaps retracted, if hydraulic System A or System B loose pressure does the Standby hydraulic system automatically activate?
options: No, automatic activation only occurs if both System A and System B loose pressure and flaps are extended.
Yes, failure of either System A or System B will cause automatic activation of the Standby hydraulic system.
Yes, but only if both System A and System B loose pressure.
No, automatic activation only occurs if either System A or System B loose pressure and flaps are extended.
explanation: Automatic standby operation needs: loss of system A or B AND flaps extended AND airborne or wheel speed > 60 kt AND the FLT CONTROL switch ON — OR the main PCU Force Fight Monitor trips. With flaps up it will not start on a single-system loss. · FCOM 13.20.5

question: The amber LOW PRESSURE Light for System B Electric Hydraulic Pump illuminates. What are the other indications?
options: MASTER CAUTION, HYD annunciator and System B Flight Control LOW PRESSURE Lights illuminate
System B hydraulic pressure drops to 1000 psi
MASTER CAUTION and HYD annunciator lights illuminate
System B brake pressure drops to 1000 psi
explanation: A pump LOW PRESSURE light means only that pump's output is low; it brings on MASTER CAUTION and HYD. The flight control LOW PRESSURE light only comes on when the whole system pressure to ailerons, elevator and rudder is low, and system pressure is still held by the other pump. · FCOM 13.10.1 / 15.20

question: Which conditions must exist when airborne for the landing gear transfer unit to operate?
options: No. 1 engine driven pump (EDP) fails, landing gear lever is positioned up, either main landing gear is not up and locked
No. 1 engine RPM drops below a limit value, landing gear lever is positioned up, either main landing gear is not up and locked
No. 1 engine RPM drops below a limit value, landing gear lever is positioned up, any landing gear is not up and locked
No. 1 engine driven pump (EDP) pressure below limits, landing gear lever is positioned up, any main landing gear is not up and locked
explanation: Landing gear transfer valve conditions: airborne, No.1 engine RPM drops below a limit value, LANDING GEAR lever UP, and either main gear not up and locked. System B EDP then supplies the volume to raise the gear. · FCOM 13.20.4 / 14.20.2

question: (RF) Indication is displayed to the right of the hydraulic system quantity:
options: Only during MASTER CAUTION system recall
When hydraulic quantity is below 76% in either system A or B
At all times
When hydraulic quantity is less than 88% in either system A or B
explanation: RF (white) = hydraulic quantity below 76%. Valid only on the ground with both engines shut down, or after landing with flaps up during taxi-in. · FCOM 13.10.2

question: How is hydraulic oil pressure stopped from entering the system when the Engine Driven Pumps (EDPs) are switched to OFF?
options: A blocking valve in the pump is energised allowing it to close and stop pressure entering the system.
The EDPs are mechanically disengaged from the engine external gearbox by means of a electronic clutch.
The EDPs are mechanically disengaged from the engine external gearbox by means of a Sprag clutch.
A blocking valve in the pump is de-energised allowing it to close and stop pressure entering the system.
explanation: ENGINE HYDRAULIC PUMP switch ON de-energizes the blocking valve (pressure enters system). OFF energizes the blocking valve to block pump output. The pump keeps turning with the engine. Leave switches ON at shutdown to prolong solenoid life. · FCOM 13.10.1

question: Hydraulic pressure from system B will be used to retract the landing gear:
options: After a failure of the No 1 engine hydraulic pump with landing gear still down and the landing gear lever is positioned up
When the ALTERNATE NOSE WHEEL switch is positioned ON
When system A pressure is low and the landing lever is positioned up
After failure of the No 1 engine with the landing gear still down and the landing lever is positioned up
explanation: System B EDP raises the gear through the landing gear transfer valve when airborne, No.1 engine RPM below a limit, gear lever UP and either main gear not up and locked. It is triggered by engine 1 RPM, not by a pump failure. · FCOM 13.20.4

question: The Power Transfer Unit (PTU) supplies pressure to which flight controls if the System B Engine Driven Pump (EDP) pressure drops below limits?
options: The landing gear
Trailing Edge (TE) flaps
The Autoslat system and all leading edge devices
Trailing Edge (TE) flaps and Leading Edge (LE) flaps
explanation: The PTU supplies the extra volume to operate the autoslats and LE flaps and slats at the normal rate when the system B EDP is inoperative. It uses system A pressure to drive a pump that pressurizes system B fluid. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: The Power Transfer Unit provides a backup source of hydraulic pressure to operate the:
options: Outboard spoilers
Trailing edge flaps
Landing gear
Autoslats
explanation: PTU = backup volume for the autoslats and the LE flaps and slats (normal rate) when the system B EDP pressure is low. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: The purpose of the landing gear transfer unit is to:
options: Automatically use hydraulic system B for landing gear retraction if hydraulic system A engine driven pump fails and the landing gear lever is positioned up
Automatically use hydraulic system B for gear retraction if No 1 engine is lost and the landing gear lever is positioned up
Allow the use of nose wheel steering in the event of hydraulic system A fails
Allow landing gear retraction if hydraulic system B is lost during takeoff
explanation: The transfer valve supplies volume to raise the gear at the normal rate when system A EDP volume is lost. It operates when airborne, No.1 engine RPM drops below a limit, gear lever UP and either main gear not up and locked. · FCOM 13.20.4

question: What effect will a leak in system B downstream of the EDP have on the Power Transfer Unit (PTU)?
options: A leak in system B has no effect as the PTU only uses oil from system A to operate.
It will function as normal as it is part of the standby system and powered by system A oil pressure.
It will continue to function if required due to oil in the system B reservoir below the standpipe level.
It will cease to function as it requires oil from system B to operate.
explanation: System B reservoir has one standpipe feeding both pumps. With fluid at the top of the standpipe, the fluid left in the system B reservoir is sufficient for PTU operation. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: What is the maximum hydraulic system pressure.
explanation: Hydraulic pressure indication: normal 3000 psi, maximum 3500 psi. With both pumps OFF it may read reservoir pressure, normally below 100 psi. · FCOM 13.10.2

question: Which statement is true regarding Hydraulic System A failure? The Standby hydraulic system, powered by a single electric-motor driven pump, has been manually activated.
options: Ground spoiler are inoperative, increasing landing distance. Half of the flight spoilers on each wing are inoperative, reducing roll rate. Engine 1 thrust reverser will deploy and retract at a slower rate and some asymmetry can be anticipated during thrust reverser deployment.

Ground spoiler are inoperative, increasing landing distance. Half of the flight spoilers on each wing are inop, reducing roll rate. Both thrust reversers are powered by the Standby system to avoid asymmetry during thrust reverser deployment.

Ground spoiler are inoperative, increasing landing distance. Half of the flight spoilers on each wing are powered by the Standby hydraulic system. Engine 1 thrust reverser will deploy and retract at a slower rate and some asymmetry can be anticipated during thrust reverser deployment.

Ground spoilers are powered by the Standby system and are operative. Half of the flight spoilers on each wing are inoperative, reducing roll rate. Engine 1 thrust reverser will deploy and retract at a slower rate and some asymmetry can be anticipated during thrust reverser deployment.
explanation: System A powers the ground spoilers and flight spoilers 2,4,9,11, so with system A lost the ground spoilers are inoperative and half the flight spoilers are lost. The standby system powers the No.1 reverser at a slower rate (some asymmetry). Standby does not power any spoilers. · FCOM 13.20.2 / 7.20.13

question: Which statement is true regarding thrust reverser operation with a failure of hydraulic System A?
options: The No.1 thrust reverser will automatically operate using the Standby System.
The No.1 thrust reverser will operate normally from System B via the PTU.
The No.1 thrust reverser will operate using the Standby System if the Standby System has been manually or automatically activated.
The No.1 thrust reverser will be inoperative.
explanation: If system A and/or B fails, alternate operation of the affected reverser is available through the standby hydraulic system (when it is selected or auto-activated). The affected reverser deploys and retracts at a slower rate. · FCOM 7.20.13

question: A leak in standby hydraulic system will cause system B fluid indication decrease to approximately:
options: Zero
Has no effect on system B quantity
explanation: Standby system leak: standby reservoir goes to zero (LOW QUANTITY light at about half empty). System B keeps operating normally, but its quantity indication decreases and stabilizes at approximately 70% full (closest option: 72%). · FCOM 13.20.7

question: A leak in the No. 2 engine driven hydraulic pump or associated lines can result in a total loss of hydraulic system B pressure:
options: only if Standby hydraulic pump is on
yes, if Elec pump is on
yes, but PTU operation is still available
no
explanation: System B: a leak in either pump, line or component takes the quantity to approximately zero and system B pressure is lost (one standpipe feeds both pumps). The fluid left in the reservoir is still enough for PTU operation. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: Alternate brakes are operated by:-
options: system B via PTU
system A
system B
Standby system
explanation: Normal brakes = System B. Alternate brakes = System A. Brake accumulator as backup. · FCOM 13.20.2 / 14.20.4

question: Alternate nose wheel steering (NWS) is powered by system A, and normal NWS is powered by system B.
options: True
False
