explanation: False. Normal nose wheel steering is System A; alternate nose wheel steering is System B. · FCOM 14.20.1

question: An engine-driven hydraulic pump supplies approximately ___ times the fluid volume of an electric motor-driven hydraulic pump?
explanation: FCOM: an engine-driven hydraulic pump supplies approximately 6 times the fluid volume of the related electric motor-driven pump. (One bank version shows 4 — that is wrong.) · FCOM 13.20.2

question: An OVERHEAT light on the hydraulic panel illuminates inflight - what does this mean?
options: The hydraulic fluid or the related electric- or engine-driven pump have overheated
The hydraulic fluid used to cool & lubricate the related electric-driven pump has overheated or the pump itself has overheated
The hydraulic fluid has overheated
The hydraulic fluid used to cool & lubricate the engine-driven pumps has overheated or the pump itself has overheated
explanation: Electric hydraulic pump OVERHEAT light: the fluid used to cool and lubricate the corresponding electric motor-driven pump has overheated, or the pump itself has overheated. There is no overheat light for the engine-driven pumps. · FCOM 13.10.1

question: Automatic operation of the Standby Hydraulic System is initiated when:-
options: System B fails and flaps are less than 15 but not up
The main rudder PCU Force Fight Monitor (FFM) trips
Positioning either FLT CONTROL switch to STBY RUD
System B fails and wheel speed > 50kts
explanation: Automatic standby: loss of A or B + flaps extended + airborne or wheel speed > 60 kt + FLT CONTROL switch ON, OR the main rudder PCU Force Fight Monitor trips. Selecting STBY RUD is manual operation, not automatic. · FCOM 13.20.5

question: During flight with hydraulic system B inoperative (no fluid in system B):
options: The standby hydraulic system operates the trailing edge flaps normally
The autoslat system is still functional through the operation of the PTU
Trim is available for the stabiliser and rudder only Aileron trim is inoperative with the autopilots disengaged
The standby hydraulic system operates the leading edge slats and leading edge flaps to fully extended position only
explanation: Standby system powers the LE flaps and slats (extend only) via ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM. With no fluid in system B the PTU cannot work (it pressurizes system B fluid), so no autoslats. TE flaps are electric in alternate mode. · FCOM 13.20.4 / 13.20.5

question: During normal operations, hydraulic quantity indications vary when:
options: It will never vary
Raising or lowering the landing gear or leading edge devices
Nose wheel is active
Turning the steering wheel
explanation: Quantity varies when the system is pressurized after engine start, when raising or lowering the gear or leading edge devices, and with cold soaking in long cruise. Little effect on operation. · FCOM 13.20.7

question: If a leak develops in the hydraulic System A reservoir, which associated pump(s) will have hydraulic fluid available from below the standpipe?
options: The AC electric motor-driven pump
Neither pump
Both the the engine driven pump (EDP) and the AC electric motor-driven pump
The engine driven pump
explanation: System A: a leak in the EDP or its lines stops at the standpipe (~20% indicated) and system A pressure is maintained by the electric motor-driven pump, which draws from below the standpipe. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: If hydraulic system A develops a leak the engine driven pump (EDP) in system A is starved of oil before the electrical motor driven pump.  If system B develops a leak, the electrical motor driven pump in system B is the first to be starved of oil?
options: True
False
explanation: False. System A: the EDP is starved first (standpipe), the electric pump keeps pressure. System B has one standpipe feeding BOTH pumps, so a B leak takes both pumps and the quantity to about zero together. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: If Hydraulic System B were to simultaneously show a LOW PRESSURE warning for the engine driven pump and the electrically driven pump, will the STANDBY system be affected at the same time?
options: Yes, as these symptoms would indicate a loss of AC Transfer Bus 2
Yes. The symptoms would indicate a fluid leak. The Standby system is connected to System B
No, as the Standby System has it's own reservoir
Yes, as this would indicate a failure of Engine 2
explanation: The standby reservoir is connected to the system B reservoir only for pressurization and servicing. FCOM: a leak in system B does not affect the operation of the standby hydraulic system. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: If the nose gear steering lockout pin is not installed for pushback or towing:
options: System B HYDRAULIC PUMPS must be switched off
System B HYDRAULIC PUMPS must be switched on
System A HYDRAULIC PUMPS must be switched off
System A HYDRAULIC ELEC PUMP may be switched on
explanation: RYR: engine start when the nose gear steering lockout pin is not installed — before tug/towbar connection, HYDRAULIC PUMP A switches (both) OFF. Normal nose wheel steering is System A; the lockout pin normally depressurizes steering so the systems need not be depressurized. · FCOM SP.7.5 / 14.20.3

question: In addition to hydraulic system A and B, the rudder can also be powered by the standby hydraulic system through the:
options: System B Standby Rudder PCU
Standby Rudder PCU
System A standby Rudder PCU
Main rudder PCU
explanation: The standby rudder PCU is powered by the standby hydraulic system (STBY RUD selected or automatic activation). · FCOM 9.20.13

question: Minimum fuel for ground operation of the electric motor-driven hydraulic pumps is:
options: 760 kgs in the related main tank
726 kgs in the related main tank
760 kgs in any tank
No restriction
explanation: CAUTION: minimum fuel for ground operation of the electric motor-driven pumps is 760 kg in the related main tank (the heat exchangers are in main tanks 1 and 2). · FCOM 13.20.3

question: Moving the STBY RUD switch to ON activates the standby pump and opens the standby rudder shutoff valve to pressurise the standby power control unit.
options: True
False
explanation: False as worded: there is no STBY RUD 'ON' switch. The FLIGHT CONTROL switch positions are STBY RUD / OFF / ON (guarded). It is STBY RUD that activates the standby pump and opens the standby rudder shutoff valve; ON is just the normal position. · FCOM 13.10.3

question: Positioning an engine-driven hydraulic pump switch to OFF:-
options: Isolates the hydraulic fluid flow from the system components, but the pump keeps rotating as long as the engine is running
Closes the related hydraulic shut off valve and disconnects the related engine-driven pump from the accessory gearbox.
Opens the related hydraulic bypass valve and routes the output of the pump directly to the input.
Isolates the reservoir from the system components and disconnects the related pump
explanation: Positioning the ENG pump switch to OFF isolates fluid flow from the system components. However, the engine-driven pump continues to rotate as long as the engine is operating. · FCOM 13.20.2

question: Pulling the No 2 ENGINE FIRE SWITCH shuts off hydraulic fluid to the:
options: Electric pump in system A
Engine driven pump in system A
Electric pump in system B
Engine driven pump in system B
explanation: Pulling an engine fire switch shuts off fluid flow to that engine's driven pump and deactivates its LOW PRESSURE light. Engine 2 drives the System B EDP. · FCOM 13.20.2

question: Refer to the RF indication to the right of the hydraulic system quantity indication. This indication is displayed:
options: Only during MASTER CAUTION system recall
At all times
Only when hydraulic quantity is below 76% in either system A or B and the aircraft is on the ground with both engines shutdown or after landing with flaps up during taxi-in
Automatically when the hydraulic quantity is below 88% in either system A or B
explanation: RF (white): hydraulic quantity below 76%. Valid only on the ground with both engines shut down, or after landing with flaps up during taxi-in. · FCOM 13.10.2

question: The amber FEEL DIFF PRESS light illuminates when the:
options: Captains pilot system fails
Flaps are not up and a pressure imbalance between Hydraulic system B and Standby system is detected.
Flaps are up and a pressure imbalance between Hydraulic Systems A and Standby system is detected.
Flaps are up or down and a hydraulic pressure imbalance is detected between hydraulic system A and B or if one of the elevator pilot systems fails
explanation: When either hydraulic system or an elevator feel pitot system fails, excessive differential hydraulic pressure is sensed in the elevator feel computer and FEEL DIFF PRESS illuminates (flaps up or down). · FCOM 9.20.6

question: The amber Standby Hydraulic System LOW PRESSURE Light is armed:
options: Only when the ALTERNATE FLAPS Switch is moved to ARM
Only when standby pump operation has been selected or automatic standby function is activated
At all times
Only when either FLT CONTROL Switch is moved to STBY RUD
explanation: STANDBY HYDRAULIC LOW PRESSURE light: output pressure of the standby pump is low. Armed only when standby pump operation has been selected or the automatic standby function is activated. (The LOW QUANTITY light is always armed.) · FCOM 13.10.4

question: The AUTOSLAT system:
options: Uses Hydraulic System A fluid
Uses Standby Hydraulic system fluid
Uses Hydraulic System A pressure
Is normally powered by Hydraulic System B
explanation: Autoslat operation is normally powered by hydraulic system B. Alternate power comes from system A through the PTU if pressure from the system B EDP is lost (the PTU pressurizes system B fluid). · FCOM 9.20.21

question: The electric motor driven hydraulic pumps are cooled and lubricated by hydraulic oil passing through them - this oil is then cooled by passing through a fuel cooled oil cooler located in each main tank.  What quantity of fuel must there be in each main tank to operate the electric driven pumps on the ground?
options: 760 kg
453 kg
726 kg
363 kg
explanation: Heat exchangers: system A in main tank 1, system B in main tank 2. CAUTION: minimum fuel for ground operation of the electric pumps is 760 kg in the related main tank. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: The engine hydraulic pump (ENG 1 and ENG 2) switches are switch ON:
options: They de-energize the blocking valve to allow pump pressure to enter the system. The switches should remain OFF at shutdown to prolong solenoid life.
They energize the blocking valve to allow pump pressure to enter the system. The switches should remain OFF at shutdown to prolong solenoid life.
They energize the blocking valve to allow pump pressure to enter the system. The switches should remain ON at shutdown to prolong solenoid life.
They de-energize the blocking valve to allow pump pressure to enter the system. The switches should remain ON at shutdown to prolong solenoid life.
explanation: ENG pump switch ON de-energizes the blocking valve so pump pressure enters the system. It should remain ON at shutdown to prolong solenoid life. OFF energizes the blocking valve. · FCOM 13.10.1

question: The hydraulic brake pressure indicator displays accumulator nitrogen pre-charge pressure of 1000 psi and:
options: Brake pressure from hydraulic system B if it is greater than 1000 psi
Brake pressure from the PTU
Brake pressure from standby hydraulic system
Brake pressure from hydraulic system A if it is greater than 1000 psi
explanation: The HYD BRAKE PRESS indicator shows brake accumulator pressure: normal precharge 1000 psi, normal 2900–3600 psi, maximum 3600–4000 psi. The accumulator is charged by System B (normal brakes). · FCOM 14.10.7 / 14.20.4

question: The hydraulic system quantity is displayed on the lower DU by digital indication from 0 to 100%.
options: True
False
explanation: False. Hydraulic quantity is shown as a digital percentage from 0% to 106%, so it can read above 100%. · FCOM 13.10.2

question: The maximum hydraulic system pressure indication would be:-
options: 3500psi in amber
3500psi in white
3000psi in white
3000psi in amber
explanation: Hydraulic system pressure indications are white: normal 3000 psi, maximum 3500 psi. · FCOM 13.10.2

question: The Power Transfer Unit provides an alternate source of power for the Autoslat System if:
options: The Alternate Flaps Position Switch is momentarily held down
Hydraulic System A engine driven pump is inoperative
A loss of Hydraulic System A pressure is sensed
A loss of pressure from the Hydraulic System B engine pump is sensed
explanation: Alternate autoslat power comes from system A through the PTU if a loss of pressure is sensed from the higher-volume system B engine-driven pump. · FCOM 9.20.21

question: The purpose of the Power Transfer Unit (PTU) is to supply system A with the volume of hydraulic fluid from system B to raise the landing gear at the normal rate when system A Engine Driven Pump volume is lost.
options: True
False
explanation: False. That describes the LANDING GEAR TRANSFER VALVE (system B volume to raise the gear when system A EDP volume is lost). The PTU uses system A pressure to give system B the volume for autoslats and LE devices. · FCOM 13.20.3 / 13.20.4

question: Under certain conditions the power transfer unit (PTU) will supply additional volume of hydraulic fluid needed to operate specific equipment. The PTU operates automatically when which of the following conditions exist?
options: Airborne, Flaps are less than 15 but not up and No. 1 engine RPM drops below a limit value
Airborne, Flaps are less than 15 and No. 2 engine RPM drops below a limit value
Airborne, Flaps are less than 15 but not up and SYS B engine–driven hydraulic pump drops below limits
Airborne, Flaps are less than 15 and System A engine–driven hydraulic pump pressure drops below limits
explanation: PTU runs automatically when: system B EDP pressure drops below limits, airborne, and flaps less than 15 but not up (YA573–YW097). On YW098–YW164 the flap condition is simply 'flaps not up'. · FCOM 13.20.3 / 13.20.4

question: What is one indication of a leak in the Standby Hydraulic System?
options: Decrease in System A quantity
Illumination of the System A LOW PRESSURE Lights
Decrease in System B quantity
Illumination of the System B LOW PRESSURE Lights
explanation: Standby leak: standby reservoir goes to zero (LOW QUANTITY at about half empty), and the system B quantity indication decreases and stabilizes at about 70% because the standby reservoir is serviced from system B. · FCOM 13.20.7

question: What is the effect on the Standby Hydraulic System, if there is a leak in system B?
options: The level in the standby system will also decrease as it is linked to system B.
No effect as the standby system has its own accumulator.
The standby system will decrease but only a limited amount due to the standpipe in system B reservoir.
No effect as the standby system is supplied from system A.
explanation: FCOM: a leak in system B does not affect the operation of the standby hydraulic system. (The 'own accumulator' wording is loose — the standby system has its own reservoir, connected to B only for pressurization/servicing — but 'no effect' is the point.) · FCOM 13.20.3

question: What system normally provides hydraulic pressure for Nose Wheel Steering?
options: System B
System A
Standby System
Nose wheel steering accumulator
explanation: NOSE WHEEL STEERING switch NORM (guarded): system A powers steering. ALT: system B powers steering. · FCOM 14.10.8 / 14.20.1

question: Where is the heat exchanger for hydraulic system A fluid located?
options: In the standby hydraulic tank.
In the System A hydraulic tank.
In main fuel tank No.1.
In the centre fuel tank.
explanation: Pump case-drain fluid passes through a heat exchanger before returning to the reservoir: system A in main fuel tank No.1, system B in main fuel tank No.2. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: Which controls operate the nose wheel steering system?
options: The steering wheel and the rudder pedals (on the ground)
The control wheel
The thrust levers
The control column
explanation: Nose wheel steering is controlled by the steering wheel (tiller) and, on the ground, by the rudder pedals (pedal steering up to 7° either side; deactivated as the nose strut extends). · FCOM 14.10.7 / 14.20.3

question: Which hydraulic system normally powers the thrust reversers?
options: Standby system
System A for engine No 1 and system B for engine No 2
System B
System A
explanation: Hydraulic pressure for engine No.1 and No.2 thrust reversers comes from systems A and B respectively, with standby as the alternate source. · FCOM 7.20.13

question: Which of these is indicated by the hydraulic Brake Pressure Indicator?
options: Maximum pressure 3500psi in amber
Minimum pressure 3000psi in white
Maximum pressure 3500psi in white
Minimum pressure 3000psi in amber
explanation: Poorly written bank question. 3500 psi (white) is the maximum HYDRAULIC SYSTEM pressure on the lower DU. The HYD BRAKE PRESS indicator itself shows: precharge 1000 psi, normal 2900–3600 psi, maximum 3600–4000 psi. · FCOM 14.10.7 / 13.10.2

question: Which systems are powered by the hydraulic system?
options: Flight controls, autothrottles, wheel brakes, leading and trailing edge flaps, leading edge slats, nose wheel steering, landing gear, thrust reversers.
Yaw damper, autopilot and autothrottle, flight controls, brakes, landing gear, trailing edge flaps and slats, nose wheel steering, tiller, power transfer unit, landing gear transfer unit.
Flight controls, Anti-skid, trailing edge flaps and slats, nose wheel steering, landing gear, thrust reversers, autopilots.
Flight controls, wheel brakes, leading and trailing edge flaps, leading edge slats, nose wheel steering, landing gear, thrust reversers, autopilots.
explanation: Hydraulic systems power: flight controls, wheel brakes, LE flaps and slats, nose wheel steering, TE flaps, thrust reversers, landing gear, autopilots. · FCOM 13.20.1

question: With the loss of hydraulic system B, (system A operating normally):
options: Standby yaw damper functions are available as long as hydraulic system A is providing normal pressure and the yaw damper switch is ON
Main and standby yaw damper functions are lost
Main yaw damper functions are available as long as hydraulic system A is providing normal pressure and the yaw damper switch is ON
Standby yaw damper functions are available if the FLT CONTROL B switch is placed to STBY RUD and the YAW DAMPER switch is reset to ON
explanation: The main yaw damper uses system B, so it is lost; the YAW DAMPER switch can't be reset when B FLT CONTROL is OFF or STBY RUD. The standby yaw damper is only used in manual reversion (A and B lost, both switches STBY RUD). · FCOM 9.20.14

question: If hydraulic system A develops a leak, the output from the engine driven hydraulic pump and the electrically driven hydraulic pump will stop at the same time
options: False
True
explanation: False. A leak in the system A EDP or its lines stops at the standpipe (~20%) and the electric pump keeps pressure. Only a leak in the electric pump/lines or common components takes the quantity to zero and all system A pressure. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: In case of LOSS OF SYSTEM A
options: Alternate Nose wheel steering is not available
A/P B is not available
Nose wheel steering is not available
Autoslats are not available
explanation: Normal nose wheel steering is system A, so it is lost (alternate steering from system B can be selected with the NOSE WHEEL STEERING switch to ALT). Autopilot B and autoslats are system B; autopilot A is lost. · FCOM 14.20.1 / 14.20.3

question: In normal operation, which hydraulic system powers the No 1 engine thrust reverser?
options: System A
System B
Standby system
Systems A and B
explanation: No.1 thrust reverser = system A; No.2 = system B; standby is the alternate for either. · FCOM 7.20.13

question: Prior to starting the engines, what position must the Engine Driven Hydraulic Pump switches be set to?
options: Either ON or OFF
ON
OFF
explanation: ENG pump switches stay ON — they 'should remain ON at shutdown to prolong solenoid life', so they are already ON for the next engine start. · FCOM 13.10.1

question: The amber LOW PRESSURE Light for the No 1 Engine Driven Hydraulic Pump illuminates. What should you do?
options: Select STBY RUD with FLT CONTROL switch A
Position the pump switch to OFF
Start the Elec pump
Monitor System A and B pressures
explanation: QRH HYDRAULIC PUMP LOW PRESSURE: position the affected pump switch OFF. FCOM 13.10.1: the light means output pressure of that pump is low. · FCOM QRH / 13.10.1

question: The electric motor driven hydraulic pumps are cooled and lubricated by hydraulic fluid passing through them - this fluid is then cooled by passing through a cooler located in each main tank.  What quantity of fuel is required in each main tank to operate the electric driven pumps on the ground?
options: 453 kg
760 kg
363 kg
explanation: CAUTION: minimum fuel for ground operation of the electric motor-driven hydraulic pumps is 760 kg in the related main tank (heat exchanger: system A in tank 1, system B in tank 2). · FCOM 13.20.3

question: The hydraulic system quantity is displayed on the lower DU. It will never read greater than 100%
options: False
True
explanation: False. Hydraulic quantity is a digital percentage from 0% to 106%. · FCOM 13.10.2

question: The Standby Hydraulic System powers the:
options: Inboard spoilers, rudder and thrust reversers
Alternate brakes, rudder and thrust reversers
Outboard spoilers, rudder and thrust reversers
Leading edge devices, rudder and thrust reversers
explanation: The standby system's single electric pump powers: thrust reversers, rudder, LE flaps and slats (extend only) and the standby yaw damper. No spoilers, no brakes. · FCOM 13.20.4

question: What does the lower DU show when the SYS switch is pushed on the Multifunction Display (MFD) on a 737-800 aircraft?
options: Hydraulic pressure, hydraulic quantity and flight control positions
Duct temperatures, cabin temperatures and brake temperatures
Hydraulic pressure and quantity only
Brake temperature on all four main wheels
explanation: MFD SYS switch: displays hydraulic indications (quantity % and pressure for A and B) on the lower DU, or the inboard DU if MAIN PANEL DUs is set to INBD MFD. Second push removes them. · FCOM 13.10.2

question: What is the minimum fuel quantity limitation for ground operation of the electric motor-driven hydraulic pumps?
options: 363 Kgs in the related main tank
There is no minimum fuel quantity limitation on the ground
453 Kgs in the related main tank
760 Kgs in the related main tank
explanation: CAUTION: minimum fuel for ground operation of the electric motor-driven pumps is 760 kg in the related main tank. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: What quantity of fuel is required in each main tank to operate the electric driven pumps on the ground?
options: 363 kg
760 kg
453 kg
explanation: 760 kg in the related main tank — the pump cooling fluid passes through a heat exchanger in main tank 1 (sys A) and main tank 2 (sys B). · FCOM 13.20.3

question: What would be the result of a fluid leak from the outlet side of the System A electric motor-driven pump?
options: System A reservoir fluid quantity decreases to approximately 20% full and System A pressure is maintained
System A reservoir fluid quantity decreases to approximately 20% full and alternate brakes and steering must be used
System A reservoir fluid quantity decreases to zero and all System A pressure is lost
System A reservoir fluid quantity decreases to zero but system pressure is maintained by the Landing Gear Transfer Unit
explanation: A leak in the electric motor-driven pump or its lines (or components common to both pumps) makes the reservoir quantity steadily decrease to zero and all system A pressure is lost. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: What would you expect to see when the standby hydraulic system is automatically activated?
options: Master Caution and FLT CONT light only
No indications of automatic operation
STBY RUD ON with no Master Caution
Illumination of the STBY RUD ON, Master Caution, and FLT CONT lights
explanation: Automatic standby operation activates the standby pump, opens the standby rudder shutoff valve and illuminates the STBY RUD ON, Master Caution and FLT CONT lights. · FCOM 13.20.5

question: When is the STANDBY HYDRAULIC LOW QUANTITY light armed?
options: Only when both FLT CONTROL switches are selected to STBY RUD
Only when the Yaw Damper is selected on
Only in the event of the loss of System A or System B
At all times
explanation: STANDBY HYDRAULIC LOW QUANTITY light: low quantity in the standby reservoir — always armed. (The standby LOW PRESSURE light is the one armed only when standby is selected/active.) · FCOM 13.10.4

question: When will the amber LOW PRESSURE Lights for the Engine Driven Hydraulic Pumps (EDP) extinguish?
options: Normally when the respective engine has been started
When the Electric Motor Driven pumps are running
When the switch is positioned to OFF
Whenever the engines are shut down
explanation: The EDP LOW PRESSURE light shows low output pressure from that pump, so it goes out once the engine is running and the pump produces pressure. It is also deactivated when the engine fire switch is pulled. · FCOM 13.10.1

question: Which hydraulic system normally powers the AUTOSLAT system?
options: Normally powered by Hydraulic System B
The Standby Hydraulic System
Hydraulic System A
Neither. They are electrically powered
explanation: Autoslats are normally powered by hydraulic system B; alternate power from system A via the PTU if the system B EDP pressure is lost. · FCOM 9.20.21

question: Which of the following are powered by the Standby Hydraulic system?
options: Leading edge devices, rudder, thrust reversers and standby yaw damper
Inboard spoilers, rudder and thrust reversers
Alternate brakes, thrust reversers and standby yaw damper
Outboard spoilers, rudder and thrust reversers
explanation: Standby system powers: thrust reversers, rudder (standby PCU), LE flaps and slats (extend only), standby yaw damper. · FCOM 13.20.4

question: Which services does the STANDBY HYDRAULIC SYSTEM supply?
options: Rudder, Thrust Reversers, Leading Edge Flaps and Slats
Rudder, Ailerons, Autoslats, Trailing Edge Flaps
Rudder, Thrust Reversers, Landing Gear
Rudder, Thrust Reversers, Brakes, Autopilot B
explanation: Standby supplies the rudder, thrust reversers and the LE flaps and slats (extend only) — plus the standby yaw damper. · FCOM 13.20.4

question: Which system provides hydraulic pressure for normal Nose Wheel Steering?
options: Hydraulic Standby System
Hydraulic System A and System B
Hydraulic System B
Hydraulic System A
explanation: Normal (NORM) nose wheel steering = hydraulic system A. ALT = system B. · FCOM 14.10.8

question: With a loss of system B pressure the standby system can be used to extend and retract the leading edge devices
options: False
True
explanation: False. Standby powers the LE flaps and slats to EXTEND ONLY — they cannot be retracted with standby pressure. · FCOM 13.20.4

question: With a loss of system B pressure the standby system can be used to extend the leading and trailing edge devices, the leading edge devices cannot be retracted again once extended by the standby system, but the trailing edge flaps can be retracted by electric motors using the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch, but no asymmetry or skew protection is then provided.
options: True
False
explanation: False. Standby only extends the LE devices (extend only). The TE flaps are never driven by standby hydraulics — in alternate mode they move by an electric motor (ALTERNATE FLAPS switch), with no asymmetry or skew protection. · FCOM 13.20.4 / 9.20.22

question: With the No 1 engine running, what is the effect of switching ENG 1 hydraulic pump OFF?
options: Pump continues to run and output is diverted to Electric hydraulic pump
Pump drive is disconnected
Pump continues to be driven by the engine, but it's output is isolated from the rest of the hydraulic system.
Transfers system to ENG 2 pump output
explanation: Switch OFF isolates the EDP's fluid flow from the system, but the pump continues to rotate as long as the engine is operating. · FCOM 13.20.2

question: Which of the following statements is true, when the landing gear Manual Extension Access Door is open?
options: Normal landing gear extension is possible if Hydraulic system A operational.
The landing gear cannot be retracted.
The landing gear can be manually lowered with the lnding gear lever in ANY position.
All of the above are true
explanation: With the manual extension access door open: manual gear extension is possible with the LANDING GEAR lever in any position; normal extension is still possible if system A pressure is available; landing gear retraction is disabled. So all three are true. · FCOM 14.10.3 / 14.20.2

question: With RTO selected, the system will automatically apply maximum brake pressure when the thrust levers have been retarded to idle with speed at or above 90 kts.
options: True
False
explanation: False — the figure is 88 kt, not 90. RTO automatically applies maximum brake pressure when the thrust levers are retarded to idle at or above 88 knots. (One bank marks this True; that's wrong.) · FCOM 14.10.4

question: Other than moving the Autobrake selector to OFF, how else can Autobraking be cancelled?
options: Applying manual brakes
Applying manual brakes, Moving Speed Brake lever to DOWN detent or Advancing forward thrust levers immediately after touchdown.
Advancing forward thrust levers immediately after touchdown or Applying manual brakes
Applying manual brakes or Moving Speed Brake lever to DOWN detent.
explanation: After braking starts, autobrake disarms (DISARM light on) by: SPEED BRAKE lever to DOWN detent, advancing forward thrust lever(s) — EXCEPT during the first 3 seconds after touchdown — or applying manual brakes. 'Advancing immediately after touchdown' does not disarm it. · FCOM 14.20.5

question: Which of the following statements are true for the Nose Wheel Steering system
options: If alternate nose wheel steering is activated then the standby hydraulic system operates the nose wheel steering.

Nose wheel steering is normally powered by hydraulic system A, If alternate nose wheel steering is activated then the standby hydraulic system operates the nose wheel steering and As well as being in the down position, the nose landing gear must be compressed for nose wheel steering to be available.
Nose wheel steering is normally powered by hydraulic system A and as well as being in the down position, the nose landing gear must be compressed for nose wheel steering to be available.

If alternate nose wheel steering is activated then the standby hydraulic system operates the nose wheel steering and as well as being in the down position, the nose landing gear must be compressed for nose wheel steering to be available.
explanation: Nose wheel steering is normally system A and is available only when the nose gear is down AND compressed by the weight of the airplane. Alternate steering is system B, not standby. · FCOM 14.20.3

question: How far must you pull the emergency gear release handle before the related landing gear uplock is released?
options: Approximately 6cm.
Released as soon as handle pulled.
Approximately 16cm
Approximately 61cm
explanation: Each gear uplock is released when its manual gear extension handle is pulled to its limit, approximately 24 inches (61 cm). · FCOM 14.10.3

question: Which of the following statements are false for Antiskid Protection.
options: The Antiskid system provides skid, locked wheel, touchdown and hydroplane protection in both normal and alternate braking.
Each wheel is provided with individual Antiskid protection in normal and alternate braking
All of the above are false.
Antiskid protection is provided for both normal and alternate brake systems.
explanation: False statement: individual wheel antiskid is only in the NORMAL system. The alternate system applies antiskid to main gear wheel PAIRS. Both systems provide skid, locked wheel, touchdown and hydroplane protection. · FCOM 14.20.4

question: If both normal and alternative brake system pressure is lost it is still possible to use the brakes to bring the aircraft to a complete stop after landing?
options: True
False
explanation: True. The brake accumulator (pressurized by system B) traps pressure: if both normal and alternate brake pressure is lost it can still provide several braking applications or a parking brake application. · FCOM 14.20.3

question: If the parking brake is set and then all electrical and hydraulic power is removed from the aircraft, will the brakes still be applied?
options: Yes.
Only if the landing gear pins are inserted.
No. The aircraft must have chocks inserted.
Yes, but only if the nosewheel steering bypass pin has been removed.
explanation: Yes. If systems A and B are not pressurized, parking brake pressure is maintained by the brake accumulator (shown on HYD BRAKE PRESS). (Verify accumulator pressure — it can be insufficient.) · FCOM 14.20.6

question: If you see that the Nose Gear green light above the landing gear lever is not illuminated, but the corresponding light on the aft overhead panel is illuminated, is the nose gear down and locked?
options: Yes
No. Both lights must be illuminated for the gear to be considered down and locked.
Not possible to tell. You will need to look through the inspection window in the floor.
explanation: Yes. FCOM: landing gear is down and locked as long as one green light (centre panel or overhead panel) for each gear is illuminated. · FCOM 14.10.2 / 14.10.3

question: The brake pressure accumulator provides pressure to the brake system and:
options: Parking brake system
Nose wheel steering system
Landing gear system
Flap system
explanation: The accumulator (system B) can provide several braking applications or the parking brake application if normal and alternate brake pressure are lost. · FCOM 14.20.3

question: The landing gear lights on the main centre panel all indicate green, but the lights on the aft overhead panel show the LEFT GEAR is not locked and down. Can you consider the landing gear down and locked?
options: True
False
explanation: True. One green light per gear, on either the centre panel or the aft overhead panel, means that gear is down and locked. · FCOM 14.10.2

question: The red landing gear indication lights are illuminated under which of the following conditions?
options: Landing gear is not down and locked (with either or both thrust levers retarded to idle, and below 800 feet AGL)
Landing gear is up and locked with the LANDING GEAR lever UP or OFF
Both; Landing gear is in disagreement with LANDING GEAR lever position, and Landing gear is not down and locked (with either or both thrust levers retarded to idle, and below 800 feet AGL).
Landing gear is in disagreement with LANDING GEAR lever position
explanation: Red lights: gear not down and locked with either or both forward thrust levers at idle below 800 ft AGL, AND/OR related gear in disagreement with lever position (in transit or unsafe). · FCOM 14.10.1

question: When the manual gear extension access door is open:
options: Normal landing gear extension is not possible
The landing gear may be retracted by moving the landing gear lever to the UP position only if hydraulic system A pressure is available
Manual landing gear extension may be accomplished with the landing gear handle in the UP position
Landing gear uplocks are released
explanation: Door open: manual extension possible with the lever in ANY position (including UP); normal extension still possible with system A pressure; retraction disabled. Opening the door does not release the uplocks — the handles do. · FCOM 14.10.3

question: Which hydraulic system operates the parking brake?
options: Brake accumulator
All of the above.
Hydraulic system A
Hydraulic system B
explanation: The parking brake can be set with either A or B pressurized; if neither is pressurized the parking brake pressure is maintained by the brake accumulator. · FCOM 14.20.6

question: Which of the following statements is true for Antiskid Protection.
options: The antiskid system disengages when manual braking is applied
Each individual wheel is provided with Antiskid protection in normal and alternate braking.
Antiskid protection is provided for both normal and alternate brake systems.
The Antiskid system does not provide touchdown protection in alternate braking.
explanation: Antiskid is provided in both normal and alternate systems (individual wheels in normal, wheel pairs in alternate). Both give skid, locked wheel, touchdown and hydroplane protection. · FCOM 14.20.4

question: You select the AUTO BRAKE to RTO on the ground, and the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates for 2 seconds then extinguishes.  What is the fault?
options: The Auto Brake has failed the self test and should be re-cycled to off then back to RTO, if the light does not illuminate this time the system is serviceable.
Autobrake is unavailable.
You do not have the parking brake set.
The system has passed the self test and there is NO fault.
explanation: Selecting RTO on the ground: AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates for one to two seconds then extinguishes, indicating a successful automatic self-test. · FCOM 14.20.4

question: For which brake system is the AUTO BRAKE function available?
options: Normal and Alternate
Alternate only
Normal, Alternate and when using the Brake Accumulator in the event of a loss of Hydraulic System A and B
Normal only
explanation: Antiskid is provided on both brake systems, but the autobrake system is available only with the normal brake system (system B pressure). · FCOM 14.20.1 / 14.20.4

question: Is it still possible to use the brakes to bring the aircraft to a complete stop after landing if Hydraulic Systems A and B are both unavailable?
options: True
False
explanation: True. Trapped pressure in the brake accumulator can still give several braking applications (or a parking brake application). · FCOM 14.20.3

question: The landing gear lights on the main centre panel all indicate green, but the lights on the aft overhead panel show the LEFT GEAR is not locked and down.   You can ignore this situation as one green light, on either panel, for each landing gear, means the gear is down and locked.
options: True
False
explanation: True. Gear is down and locked as long as one green light (centre or overhead panel) for each gear is illuminated. · FCOM 14.10.2

question: What could cause the amber ANTISKID INOP Light to illuminate?
options: Brake accumulator pressure is in the red band
System B pressure is low
AUTO BRAKE select switch OFF
A fault in the parking brake system
explanation: FCOM: a fault in the parking brake system may cause the ANTISKID INOP light to illuminate. (Normally the light means a fault detected by the antiskid monitoring system.) · FCOM 14.20.6

question: What is the purpose of the Nose Wheel Steering Lockout Pin (Bypass Pin)?
options: Isolates Rudder Pedal nose wheel steering, limiting nose wheel steering to the Tiller only
Depressurises the nose wheel braking system, to prevent damage to the tow bar
Depressurises hydraulic system B
Depressurises nose wheel steering allowing pushback or towing without having to depressurise the hydraulic systems
explanation: A lockout pin in the towing lever depressurizes nose wheel steering, allowing pushback or towing without depressurizing the hydraulic systems. · FCOM 14.20.3

question: What protection is provided during alternate brake operation?
options: No protection is provided during alternate brake operation
Skid, and hydroplane only
Skid, locked wheel and hydroplane only
Skid, locked wheel, touchdown and hydroplane
explanation: Both normal and alternate brake systems provide skid, locked wheel, touchdown and hydroplane protection (alternate works on wheel pairs). Antiskid is available even with loss of both hydraulic systems. · FCOM 14.20.4

question: When disarming the Autobrake System which of the following does NOT cause the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light to illuminate?
options: Positioning the AUTO BRAKE select switch to OFF
Advancing the forward thrust levers after the first 3 seconds after touchdown
Applying manual brakes
Moving the SPEED BRAKE lever to the DOWN detent
explanation: Moving the selector to OFF disarms autobrake WITHOUT illuminating the DISARM light. Speed brake to DOWN, manual brakes, or thrust levers advanced (after the first 3 s) all illuminate it. · FCOM 14.20.5

question: Which of the following conditions must exist to arm the RTO mode prior to takeoff?
options: Forward thrust levers positioned to IDLE
AUTO BRAKE select switch OFF
AUTOBRAKE switch to MAX
Wheel speed greater than 60 knots
explanation: To arm RTO: on the ground, antiskid and autobrake operational, AUTO BRAKE switch to RTO, wheel speed less than 60 kt, forward thrust levers at IDLE. · FCOM 14.20.4

question: Which statement is correct when selecting a landing autobrake setting after touchdown?
options: Autobrakes will initiate if selected prior to decelerating through 30 knots of groundspeed
Autobrake action will occur only when thrust reverse is selected
Autobrakes will arm after decelerating through 60 knots groundspeed
The AUTO BRAKE DISARM light will illuminate and autobrake application will not occur
explanation: Landing autobrake settings may be selected after touchdown prior to decelerating through 30 kt groundspeed; braking starts immediately if the other conditions (thrust levers idle, wheel spin-up) are met. · FCOM 14.20.5

question: Which statement is true?
options: Hydraulic System B pressure is bypassed with the lockout pin installed in the steering depressurisation valve
Rudder pedal steering is deactivated as the nose gear strut extends
Rudder pedal steering overrides the steering wheel inputs
Rudder pedal steering allow 37 degrees of steering in either direction
explanation: Rudder pedal steering is deactivated as the nose gear strut extends. The steering wheel overrides pedal steering; pedals give up to 7° each way; the lockout pin depressurizes nose wheel steering (system A). · FCOM 14.20.3 / 14.10.8

question: With the NOSE WHEEL STEERING switch in the ALT position, which Hydraulic System powers the Nose Wheel Steering?
options: Standby Hydraulic System
Hydraulic System A
Hydraulic System A or Hydraulic System
Hydraulic System B
explanation: NOSE WHEEL STEERING switch ALT: hydraulic system B powers nose wheel steering. NORM (guarded): system A. · FCOM 14.10.8

question: You select the AUTO BRAKE to RTO on the ground, and the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates for 2 seconds then extinguishes. Is there a fault, and if so what is it?
options: This is a warning that the system is unavailable
This means that the Brake Accumulator pressure is low
This indicates that the Parking Brake is still set
There is no fault. This just means that the Autobrake System has passed the self-test
explanation: RTO selection on the ground: the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates for one to two seconds and then extinguishes, indicating that the automatic self-test has been successfully accomplished. · FCOM 14.20.4

question: When carrying out the Stall Warning Test, which of the following statements is correct?
options: The test cannot be completed until the AC Transfer Busses have been powered for up to 4 minutes.
The test can be completed once AC power is available
The test can be completed on DC power
The test cannot be completed until the DC Standby system is powered
explanation: Note in the preflight procedure: the stall warning test requires that the AC transfer busses are powered for up to 4 minutes. Each switch tests its own SMYD; either shaker vibrates both columns. · FCOM NP.21.8 / 15.10.4

question: Altitude alerting occurs when approaching or departing from the MCP selected altitude.  When is the altitude alerting system inhibited?
options: Glide slope is captured, or trailing edge flaps are extended to 25 or greater.
Flaps set to 15 or less and the landing gear is extended.
Landing gear is down and locked.
Flaps set to10 or less
explanation: Altitude alerting is inhibited when trailing edge flaps are extended to 25 or greater, or while G/S is captured. · FCOM 15.20.9

question: At what altitude are the TCAS INCREASE DESCENT RAs inhibited?
options: 1,100 feet AGL.
1200 feet AGL
1500 feet RA.
1,100 feet RA.
explanation: INCREASE DESCENT RAs inhibited below ~1,500 ft RA; DESCEND RAs below ~1,100 ft RA; all RAs and voice below ~1,000 ft RA (TA ONLY automatically); all voice below ~500 ft RA. · FCOM 15.20.32

question: How can the Fire Warning Bell be silenced on the flight deck?
options: Push the master fire warn lights, push fire warning bell cutout switch.
Push the master fire warn lights, press the horn cutout of the APU ground control panel, push fire warning bell cutout switch.
Fire bell can only be silenced by pressing either master fire warn light.
Push the Master Fire Warn lights, press the Horn Cutout of the APU Ground Control Panel.
explanation: Push either master FIRE WARN light or the fire warning BELL CUTOUT switch: extinguishes both master FIRE WARN lights, silences the bell (and the remote APU horn) and resets for further warnings. · FCOM 15.10.1 / 15.20.2

question: When will the landing gear config warning horn give an intermittent warning sound?
options: Flaps 1 through 10, below 800 feet RA, either forward thrust lever at 20 degrees or less (or less than 34 degrees if only 1 engine running).
Flaps greater than 25, below 800 feet RA, regardless of forward thrust lever position.
Never.
Flaps up through 10, below 800 feet RA, either forward thrust lever at 20 degrees or less (or less than 34 degrees if only 1 engine running).
explanation: Never. The landing gear configuration warning is a STEADY horn. The intermittent horn is for takeoff configuration and cabin altitude. · FCOM 15.20.1 / 15.20.7

question: Altitude alerting, consisting of a tone and highlighted boxes, occurs at a set distance before reaching the selected attitude.  How many feet before the selected altitude do the altitude alert highlighted boxes no longer show?
options: 900 feet
3000 fpm with 3000 feet to go, 2000 fpm with 2000 feet to go, 1000 fpm with 1000 feet to go.
300 feet
600 feet
explanation: 900 ft before the selected altitude a white box appears and a momentary tone sounds; at 300 ft from the selected altitude the box no longer shows (YF501–YW164). · FCOM 15.20.9 / 15.10.6

question: Crew are warned of exceeding the maximum allowed airspeed by which of the following?
options: Horn and stick shaker
Stick shaker.
Aural Clacker, speedtape red and black band.
Bell, and the speed tape turns red
explanation: Vmo/Mmo exceedance: aural clacker (silenced only by reducing speed below Vmo/Mmo) and the red/black maximum airspeed band on the speed tape. Stick shaker is for stall. · FCOM 15.20.8

question: How are crew alerted to a deviation from the selected altitude?
options: A warning tone sounds once deviation is 300 feet from selected altitude, the current altitude box turns red and begins to flash.
A warning tone sounds once deviation is 900 feet from selected altitude, the current altitude box turns red and begins to flash.
A warning tone sounds once deviation is 300 feet from selected altitude, the current altitude box turns amber and begins to flash.
A warning tone sounds once deviation is 300 feet from selected altitude, the current altitude box begins to flash.
explanation: Deviation alert (YF501–YW164): when deviating 300 ft from the selected altitude a momentary tone sounds and the current altitude box turns amber and flashes. (YA573: 200 ft.) · FCOM 15.20.9

question: How far from projected impact will the "TERRAIN, TERRAIN, PULL UP" aural warning be given?
options: 1.2 nm to 1.5 nm
Whenever descending below unsafe RA while too far from any airport in the terrain database.
20 to 30 seconds.
1.2nm to 1.5nm or 40 to 60 seconds whichever limit occurs first.
explanation: Look-ahead TERRAIN, TERRAIN, PULL UP: 20 to 30 seconds from projected impact (red). The CAUTION TERRAIN alert is 40 to 60 seconds (amber). · FCOM 15.20.13

question: Once an alert has occurred for deviating from the selected altitude, how is it cancelled?
options: Press ALT INT to select next FMC target altitude.
Return to within 200 feet of selected altitude.
Return to within 200 feet of selected altitude and press the HORN CUTOUT button on the Control Stand.
return to within 300 feet of selected altitude or deviate by more than 900 feet from selected altitude, or select a new altitude.
explanation: Amber flashing continues until deviation is less than 300 ft, more than 900 ft, or a new altitude is selected (YF501–YW164; YA573 uses 200 ft). · FCOM 15.20.9

question: Refer to the Cabin/Flight Altitude placard. At a cruise altitude FL290, the cabin altitude should read:
options: A pressure differential of 50 psi
Cannot be determined from this placard
Approximately 6000 feet
Slightly less than FL220
explanation: The CABIN/FLIGHT ALTITUDE placard (used for manual pressurization) gives the target cabin altitude for each flight altitude — about 6,000 ft at FL290 (bank answer; the placard values are not reproduced in the FCOM text). · FCOM SP.2.3

question: TCAS TA Only mode is enabled automatically:
options: Above 1000ft when TA/RA mode is selected
Below 1000ft RA when TA/RA mode is selected
Below 1000ft RA when the TXPDR is to ALT OFF
During a high altitude descent
explanation: Below 1,000 ft RA with TA/RA selected, TA ONLY mode is enabled automatically and TA ONLY is shown on the ND. · FCOM 15.20.32

question: The GPWS will provide an aural alert of "BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE" under which of the following circumstances?
options: When the bank angle exceeds 35, 40 and 45 degrees.
Whenever trailing edge flaps are at 1 or greater and roll angle exceeds 30 degrees.
Whenever the bank angle exceeds the setting on the Bank Angle Selector by 5 degrees
When the bank angle exceeds the maximum of 67 degrees, which gives the equivalent of 2.5g
explanation: BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE when roll exceeds 35°, 40° and 45°. Each sounds once and resets when bank is reduced to 30° or less. · FCOM 15.20.28

question: The predictive windshear symbol radials, which extend from the predictive winsdshear symbol to help identify the location of a windshear event, are displayed in what colours?
options: Amber.
Displayed amber when a predictive winshear caution is active, and displayed red when a predictive windshear warning is active.
Red and Black banded.
Red.
explanation: Predictive windshear symbol radials are amber; they extend from the symbol to help locate the windshear event. · FCOM 15.10.15

question: The PSEU light, located on the forward overhead panel, will illuminate on the ground if a fault is detected in the PSEU or if an overwing exit flight lock fails to disengage when commanded.
options: True
False
explanation: False because of the location: the PSEU light is on the AFT overhead panel. The conditions are right — on the ground it shows a PSEU fault or an overwing exit flight lock failing to disengage. · FCOM 15.10.2 / 15.20.7

question: The Stall Warning is generated from which system component?
options: The SMYD Computers.
Captain's IRS
The PSEU
The ADIRUs.
explanation: The SMYD computers provide outputs for all stall warning (stick shaker, pitch limit indicator, airspeed displays) and GPWS windshear detection. · FCOM 15.20.9

question: The TCAS symbol for proximity traffic is:
options: A white solid diamond
A red square
An amber circle
A hollow white diamond
explanation: Proximate traffic (within 6 nm and 1,200 ft, no TA/RA expected) = solid white diamond. Other traffic = hollow white diamond; TA = amber circle; RA = red square. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: The TCAS system generates a Traffic Advisory, whenever another aircraft is what distance from point of closest approach?
options: 40 seconds.
<6 nm separation with < 1200 feet vertical separation.
25 seconds.
>6 nm separation with >1200 feet vertical separation.
explanation: TA when the other airplane is about 40 seconds from the point of closest approach; RA at about 25 seconds. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: What is significant about the layout of the Annunciator Panel lights?
options: The lights are arranged in no significant order.
The lights on the Captain's side show the systems that the Captain is responsible for monitoring, and the lights of the F/Os side show the systems the F/O is responsible for monitoring.
The lights are arranged in order of priority to be dealt with in case of multiple system failures.
The lights are arranged to reflect the relative position of the systems panels on the Overhead Panels.
explanation: The system annunciator panels only include systems on the forward overhead, aft overhead and fire control panels, laid out to match where those panels are. · FCOM 15.20.2

question: What is the first Radio Altitude Callout given during the approach?
options: 2450 feet - "Twenty Five Hundred".
1000 feet - "One Thousand".
2500 feet  - "Twenty Five Hundred".
50 feet - "Fifty".
explanation: GPWS approach callouts start at 2,500 ft – TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED, then 1,000, 500 (smart), etc. · FCOM 15.20.29

question: Which of the following statements is true for the CABIN ALTITUDE Warning?
options: An intermittent warning horn sounds and the amber CABIN ALTITUDE warning lights illuminate when the cabin altitude exceeds 8000 feet
A steady warning horn sounds and the amber CABIN ALTITUDE lights illuminate when the cabin altitude exceeds 14000 feet.
A steady warning horn sounds and the red CABIN ALTITUDE warning lights illuminate when the cabin altitude exceeds 14000 feet.
An intermittent warning horn sounds and the red CABIN ALTITUDE lights illuminate when the cabin altitude exceeds 10000 feet
explanation: Cabin altitude above 10,000 ft: intermittent horn and red CABIN ALTITUDE lights. · FCOM 15.10.3 / 15.20.6

question: Which two displays cannot be selected and shown simultaneously on the Navigation DU?
options: Weather and Data.
TCAS and Airport.
Weather and Terrain.
Terrain and TCAS.
explanation: Terrain and weather radar cannot show together on a display. · FCOM 15.20.12

question: With both engines operating and one forward thrust lever set below approximately 20 degrees thrust lever angle, the landing gear warning horn can be silenced with the landing gear warning HORN CUTOUT switch:
options: with flaps UP through 10 if below 800 feet RA and above 200 feet RA
with flaps UP through 25 if below 800 feet RA and above 200 feet RA
with flaps UP through 10 if below 800 feet RA and above 300 feet RA
it cannot be silenced if the thrust lever angle is less than 20 degrees.
explanation: The gear warning horn can be silenced with HORN CUTOUT at flaps up through 10, above 200 ft RA (warning active below 800 ft RA). Below 200 ft RA, or flaps 15+, it cannot be silenced. · FCOM 15.10.6 / 15.20.7

question: An amber ALT DISAGREE in the bottom of the altimeter tape is an indication of:
options: The standby altimeter has failed
The Captains and First Officers altitude indications differ more than 50 feet for more than 5 seconds
The Captains and First Officers altitude indications differ more than 200 feet for more than 5 seconds
There is a difference of more than 10 HP between the selected QNHs
explanation: ALT DISAGREE (amber): Captain's and F/O's altitudes disagree by more than 200 ft for more than 5 continuous seconds. · FCOM 10.11.34

question: An amber ROLL displayed in the lower portion of the altitude indicator on the PFD means:
options: The airplane is experiencing an uncommented roll
No flight director or autopilot mode engaged
The airplane has exceeded 36 degrees of bank
The captains and first officers roll angle display differ by more than 5 degrees
explanation: Amber ROLL (or PITCH) comparator: Captain's and F/O's roll (pitch) displays differ by more than 5°. Flashes for 10 s then steady. · FCOM 10.11.28

question: True or False - As well as providing outputs for all stall warnings, the SMYD computers also provide outputs for GPWS Windshear Detection and Alert.
options: True
False
explanation: True. SMYD outputs: all stall warning (stick shaker, PLI, airspeed displays) and the GPWS windshear detection and alert. · FCOM 15.20.9

question: At what altitude (in feet) do the RA callouts begin?
options: ONE THOUSAND.
TWO THOUSAND
FIFTEEN HUNDRED.
TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED.
explanation: The first radio altitude callout is TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED at 2,500 ft. · FCOM 15.20.29

question: During descent from altitude you need to decrease your airspeed by using your speed brakes. What is the limit of the SPEED BRAKE LEVER position?
options: ARMED
STOWED
GROUND DETENT
FLIGHT DETENT
explanation: In flight the SPEED BRAKE lever is limited to the FLIGHT DETENT; moving it beyond causes buffeting and is prohibited in flight. · FCOM 9.20.16

question: Elevator feel system is provided by the elevator feel computer. This computer receives inputs of:
options: Only System A hydraulic pressure
Airspeed and stabiliser position
Elevator balance tabs position
Altitude and elevator position
explanation: The elevator feel computer simulates aerodynamic forces using airspeed (elevator pitot system) and stabilizer position. · FCOM 9.20.6

question: If spoilers became jammed:
options: The first officer's control wheel operates the ailerons
The captain's control wheel will also become jammed
The captain's control wheel operates the ailerons
The first officer's control wheel operates the spoilers through another cable
explanation: If the spoiler system is jammed, force on the Captain's control wheel gives roll control from the ailerons (spoilers and F/O wheel inoperative). If the ailerons are jammed, force on the F/O's wheel gives roll control from the spoilers. · FCOM 9.20.3

question: In Flight, the Intuvue radar will provide a windshear warning from 0.5nm to 3nm ahead of the aircraft.
options: True
False
explanation: False. IntuVue in flight: predictive windshear WARNING area is 0.5 to 1.5 nm ahead (±25°); the CAUTION area extends to 3 nm. · FCOM 15.20.28

question: On the ground, for primary ATC communication:
options: Always use no. 1 VHF radio
No. 1 VHF for outbound and no. 2 VHF for inbound flights
Always use the no.2 VHF radio
Monitor the VHF radio connected to the lower antenna
explanation: Non-AFM operational information: use the VHF radio connected to the top-of-fuselage antenna for primary ATC communications on the ground — VHF 1. · FCOM L.10.6

question: Pushing the ground proximity BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT light cancels or inhibits the alert when below 1,000 feet RA.
options: True
False
explanation: True. Pushing the BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT light cancels or inhibits the GLIDESLOPE alert below 1,000 ft RA. · FCOM 15.20.14 / 15.10.7

question: Some of the indications for an engine fire warning are: MASTER CAUTION and OVHT/DET annunciator lights, ENG OVERHEAT light, Master FIRE WARN lights and the red fire switch light. There is one more indication?
options: A FAULT light illuminates
A red ENG OVERHEAT light illuminates
The APU DET INOP light illuminates
The fire warning bell rings
explanation: Engine fire indications: fire warning bell, both master FIRE WARN lights, the engine fire switch light, plus the overheat indications (MASTER CAUTION, OVHT/DET, ENG OVERHEAT). · FCOM 8.20.2

question: The air/ground system receives logic signals from:
options: Six sensors, two on each landing gear
A teleflex cable on the right main landing gear
The cabin pressure controllers
The altimeter
explanation: The air/ground system receives logic signals from six sensors, two on each landing gear. · FCOM 14.20.6

question: The airspeed range for speed trim operation is:
options: 100 KIAS - Mach 0.5
100 KIAS - Mach 0.6
explanation: Speed trim operates between 100 KIAS and Mach 0.60 (with fadeout to zero by Mach 0.68), autopilot not engaged, 10 s after takeoff, etc. · FCOM 9.20.9

question: The Captain observes the word ROLL displayed in amber in the lower portion of the PFD during takeoff. This means:
options: No F/D or autopilot roll mode has been engaged
The Captains and First Officers roll angle displays differ by 5 degrees or more
The aircraft has exceeded 40 degrees of bank
The Captains roll attitude is more than 3 degrees in error
explanation: Amber ROLL: Captain's and F/O's roll angle displays differ by more than 5°. It flashes for 10 s then stays steady. · FCOM 10.11.28

question: The cross bus tie relay automatically opens at glide slope capture to:
options: Provide more power to the AC standby bus
Ensure that the standby DC bus is powered
Provide more power to DC bus 1
Prevent a single bus failure from affecting both navigation receivers and flight control computers
explanation: At glide slope capture (F/D or A/P ILS approach) the cross bus tie relay opens to isolate DC bus 1 from DC bus 2, preventing a single failure from affecting both navigation receivers and flight control computers. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: The EGPWS contains a terrain database, which it uses for look-ahead terrain alerting.  Which of the following statements is correct for this terrain database?
options: All EGPWS terrain databases account for man-made obstructions over 100 feet high, in the more detailed areas of the database near major airports.
All man-made obstructions are accounted for in the detailed areas of the EGPWS terrain database in areas close to major airports.
All EGPWS terrain databases account for man-made obstructions over 100 feet high, throughout the whole database area.
Man-made obstructions are not accounted for in all EGPWS terrain databases
explanation: On some airplanes (YA573, YJ827–YK879) the FCOM notes that the EGPWS terrain database, look-ahead alerting and terrain display do NOT account for man-made obstructions — so not all databases include them. · FCOM 15.20.12

question: The EGPWS displays terrain within 2,500 feet of the aircraft barometric altitude on the Navigation display.
options: True
False
explanation: False. Terrain within 2,000 ft of airplane barometric altitude shows on the ND (terrain more than 2,000 ft below is not shown). · FCOM 15.20.12

question: The End of Descent altitude on the PATH DES page is:
options: The field elevation
The altitude restriction for the end of descent waypoint
The airport reference point elevation
The runway threshold elevation
explanation: DES page E/D ALT: the altitude restriction for the E/D waypoint (blank if no path descent). For an approach ending at RWxx it is the TCH, 50 ft above the runway. · FCOM 11.43.4

question: The First Officer observes the word PITCH displayed in amber in the lower portion of the PFD during an ILS approach. This means:
options: The First Officers pitch display is more than 3 degrees in error
The Captains and First Officers pitch displays differ by 5 degrees or more
Glide slope is not being tracked
The autopilot has defaulted to CWS pitch
explanation: Amber PITCH: Captain's and F/O's pitch angle displays differ by more than 5°. · FCOM 10.11.28

question: The landing gear configuration warning horn will activate anytime a gear is not down and locked:
options: With flaps set to 30, the horn can be silenced
There is no horn in the landing gear configuration system
With flaps set to 15, one thrust lever at idle and the other at a high power setting (above 34 degrees)
With flaps set to 15, one thrust lever at idle and the other at low power setting (below 34 degrees)
explanation: Flaps 15 through 25: the steady horn sounds if either thrust lever is below ~20°, or one engine is not operating and the other lever is below 34° — and it cannot be silenced. Flaps 30/40: horn regardless of thrust, cannot be silenced. · FCOM 15.20.7

question: The landing gear indicator lights found on the center panel will illuminate red when:
options: All landing gear are DN, and the gear handle in OFF position
One of the 6 green lights are faulty
All landing gear are UP, and the gear handle in OFF position
There are no red lights
explanation: Red light = related gear in disagreement with the LANDING GEAR lever (in transit or unsafe), or gear not down and locked with a thrust lever at idle below 800 ft. Lights are out with gear down and the lever DN, or gear up with the lever UP/OFF — so gear DN with the lever at OFF gives red. · FCOM 14.10.1

question: The Look-Ahead Terrain alerting system will show for terrain:
options: Within 2000 feet barometric altitude
Within 2000 feet RA
Below 1000 feet barometric altitude
Above 1000 feet RA
explanation: Terrain within 2,000 ft of airplane barometric altitude shows on the navigation display. · FCOM 15.20.12

question: The mach/airspeed warning system can only be checked on the ground:
options: Yes, together with IRS test
Yes
No
Yes, with Flaps extended only
explanation: MACH AIRSPEED WARNING TEST switches: push to sound the clacker — inhibited while airborne, so ground only. · FCOM 15.10.4

question: The predictive windshear aural alerts will be heard through flightdeck speakers and the headsets at a pre-set volume.  They cannot be controlled or turned off by the crew.
options: True
False
explanation: Audio warnings for GPWS, altitude alert, TCAS and radar predictive windshear are heard through speakers and headsets at preset volumes; they cannot be controlled or turned off by the crew. · FCOM 5.20.1

question: The PSEU light will illuminate along with a Master Caution and an OVERHEAD annunciator light, under which of the following situations?
options: Illuminates whenever ground/air system senses air mode, and an emergency exit flight lock has failed locked.
Illuminates 30 seconds after the ground/air system senses ground mode, if an emergency exit flight lock has failed locked or a fault is detected.
Illuminates as soon as the ground/air system senses ground mode, if an emergency exit flight lock has failed locked or a fault is detected.
Illuminates 30 seconds after the ground/air system senses air mode, if an emergency exit flight lock has failed locked or a fault is detected.
explanation: In flight the PSEU light is inhibited from thrust lever advance for takeoff until 30 seconds after landing. So a failed-locked flight lock or a detected fault shows 30 s after the air/ground system senses ground mode. · FCOM 15.10.2 / 1.40.51

question: The ram air system deflector doors:
options: Extend on the ground only
Prior to landing
Extend on the ground and during slow flight
During slow flight with the flaps extended
explanation: Deflector doors are forward of the ram air inlets to prevent slush ingestion before liftoff and after touchdown — they extend on the ground. · FCOM 2.30.2

question: The SMYD computers receive inputs from:
options: Anti-ice controls only
FMC, Thrust reverser
ADIRUs only
Anti-ice controls, ADIRUs, alpha vane output, wing configuration, air/ground sensing, thrust and FMC outputs
explanation: The SMYDs use alpha vane angle of attack, ADIRU outputs, anti-ice controls, wing configuration, air/ground sensing, thrust and FMC outputs. · FCOM 15.20.8

question: The stall warning test can only be carried out on the ground, the No1 and No2 systems must be carried out separately to ensure the clacker sounds when each system is tested.
options: True
False
explanation: False. The test is ground-only, but it checks the stick shakers: No.1 shakes the Captain's column, No.2 the F/O's (both columns vibrate through the interconnect). The clacker belongs to the Mach/airspeed test. · FCOM 15.10.4 / 15.20.9

question: The Takeoff Configuration Warning Horn sounds if:
options: Parking brake not set
Trailing edge flaps in the 5 pos
TOGA not pressed
Stabiliser trim is not in the green band
explanation: Takeoff config warning: flaps not in the 1–25 takeoff range (or skew/asymmetry), LE devices not configured, speed brake lever not DOWN, spoilers not down, parking brake SET, or stabilizer trim not in the takeoff range (green band). · FCOM 15.20.6

question: The window heat PWR TEST:
options: Provides a confidence test
Must be tested before each flight
Also tests the overheat protection system
Can be used if all green lights are on
explanation: PWR TEST: provides a confidence test (see SP for the window heat test procedures). · FCOM 3.10.2

question: There is a second set of landing gear indicator lights on the aft overhead panel. These lights:
options: Illuminate red when the relating landing gear is not down and either thrust lever is retarded to idle at a radio altitude of 800 feet or less
Illuminate green when the landing gear is in agreement with the landing gear lever
Illuminate red when the related landing gear is not down and locked and the gear handle is down
Are a redundant but separate set of landing gear indicator circuits and green lights
explanation: The aft overhead lights are a redundant but separate set of landing gear indicator circuits and lights (green only). · FCOM 14.10.2

question: What happens to the digital readout of the radio alt when descending below minimums?
options: The dial and numbers of the radio altimeter flash green for 5 seconds
The dial and numbers of the radio altimeter flash amber for 5 seconds
The dial and pointer of the radio altimeter flash amber for 3 seconds
The dial and pointer of the radio altimeter flash green for 5 seconds
explanation: Below radio altitude minimums the remaining dial perimeter and pointer turn amber and flash for 3 seconds; the numeric readout does not flash. · FCOM 10.11.19

question: When an Annunciator Panel is pressed, all lights on both annunciator panels initially illuminate as a confidence check that all the lights are working.
options: True
False
explanation: When the MASTER CAUTION recall is pressed, all twelve system lights should illuminate while the press-to-test is held. · FCOM 15.20.2

question: When configured for landing, the GPWS will NOT alert if attempting an off-airport landing.
options: True
False
explanation: False: EGPWS TOO LOW TERRAIN alerts for descent below unsafe altitude while too far from any airport, whatever the configuration (FCOM 15.20.13). · FCOM 15.20.13

question: When control wheel pressure is released during CWS roll operation, the aircraft will roll wings level when the bank angle is:
options: 15 degrees or less
8 degrees or less
6 degrees or less
10 degrees or less
explanation: CWS: when control pressure is released the A/P holds the existing attitude. If aileron pressure is released with 6° or less bank, the A/P rolls wings level and holds the existing heading. · FCOM 4.10.19

question: When descending, what is the first Radio Altitude callout that you will hear?
options: TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED.
FIFTEEN HUNDRED.
TWO THOUSAND
ONE THOUSAND.
explanation: First GPWS radio altitude callout on approach: TWENTY FIVE HUNDRED at 2,500 ft. · FCOM 15.20.29

question: While flying an ILS approach below 1,000 feet Radio Altitude, a BELOW G/S alert occurs. To cancel the alert:
options: Press recall
The alert cannot be cancelled
Select another mode on MCP
Press either pilots BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT Light, or correct the flight path back to the glide slope
explanation: Push either pilot's BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT light (below 1,000 ft RA) or correct back towards the glideslope. Repetition rate increases as deviation increases. · FCOM 15.20.14 / 15.10.7

question: While performing the APPROACH chekclist the PSEU light illuminates on recall, this indicates:
options: The landing gear configuration warning horn will sound upon landing
A problem exists in the PSEU system because this light should be inhibited in flight
A normal condition
A fault is detected in the landing gear locking system or the air/ground sensing system
explanation: The PSEU light is inhibited in flight (and from takeoff thrust until 30 s after landing). Seeing it on recall during the approach checklist suggests a PSEU problem. The correct check is on the ground after landing: > 30 s after landing push RECALL; report PSEU/EEC to engineering. · FCOM 15.20.8

question: ZONE TEMP amber light illumination for CONT CAB indicates:
options: Both a duct temperature overheat, or a failure of both temperature controllers.
Failure of both flight deck primary and standby temperature controller
An overtemp in the control cabin zone
A duct temperature overheat
explanation: ZONE TEMP CONT CAB: duct temperature overheat OR failure of the flight deck primary and standby temperature control. FWD/AFT CAB: duct overheat only. · FCOM 2.10.9

question: A TCAS Resolution Advisory is generated when:
options: the conflicting aircraft is 25 seconds from point of closest approach
the conflicting aircraft is 45 seconds from point of closest approach
the conflicting aircraft is likely to collide with you
the conflicting aircraft is 1000ft above you
explanation: TA at about 40 s and RA at about 25 s from the point of closest approach. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: After a normal take-off, what pitch command can you expect from the F/D?
options: V2
explanation: After lift-off the F/D pitch command stays at 15° until a sufficient rate of climb is acquired, then commands MCP speed (normally V2) + 20 kt. Engine failure: V2, existing speed between V2 and V2+20, or V2+20. · FCOM 4.20.11

question: Below what height are predictive WINSHEAR warnings annunciated to crew?
options: 2300ft RA
1200ft RA
500ft RA
2500ft RA
explanation: The windshear mode runs in flight below 1,800 ft RA, but predictive windshear alerts are issued below 1,200 ft RA. · FCOM 15.20.26

question: Below what height are TCAS Resolution Advisories inhibited?
options: 1000ft Radio Altitude
TCAS RAs are not inhibited at any time
2500ft Radio Altitude
1200ft Radio Altitude
explanation: All TCAS RAs and voice are inhibited below about 1,000 ft RA (TA ONLY automatically). INCREASE DESCENT below 1,500 ft, DESCEND below 1,100 ft. · FCOM 15.20.32

question: Dual angle-airflow sensors (alpha vanes) provide angle-of-attack information to the stall warning system, autothrottle, autopilot and autoslats are anti-iced:
options: Whenever wing anti-ice is being used
By switching on the LEFT and RIGHT FWD window heat switch
By switching on the PROBE HEAT switches
Whenever the alternate static ports are heated
explanation: The alpha vanes are electrically heated with the probes, controlled by the PROBE HEAT switches. · FCOM 3.20 / 15.20.8

question: During the ILS approach on the radio altimeter remaining perimeter and pointer turns amber and flashes for 3 seconds. This means:
options: The airplane has descended below 1,000 ft radio
The airplane has descended below the selected radio altitude
There is difference of more than 10 feet between the captains and first officers radio altimeters
Radio altitude data is unreliable
explanation: Remaining perimeter and pointer turn amber and flash for 3 s when below the selected radio altitude minimums (readout does not flash). · FCOM 10.11.19

question: For RAs to be generated, the other airplane must have which equipment installed and working?
options: Navigation Radar
Mode C or S transponder
Mode A transponder
TCAS system
explanation: TCAS interrogates transponders; altitude and vertical motion (needed for RAs) come only if the other airplane is using a Mode S or C transponder. With Mode A only you get TAs without altitude, no RAs. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: How can the Overspeed Warning (clacker) be silenced?
options: Reducing airspeed to below Vmo / Mmo
Pushing the control column forward
Pressing HORN CUTOUT
Operate the EGPWS FLAP INHIBIT switch
explanation: The clackers can be silenced only by reducing airspeed below Vmo/Mmo. · FCOM 15.20.8

question: How can you silence the CABIN ALTITUDE warning?
options: Press the ALT HORN CUTOUT switch next to the pressurisation panel
Descend to below 14,000ft
This warning cannot be silenced until the cabin altitude descends to below 10,000ft
Put the Pressurisation Panel into MAN mode
explanation: The intermittent cabin altitude horn may be silenced by momentarily pressing ALT HORN CUTOUT on the cabin altitude panel; the red light stays on until the cabin is below 10,000 ft. · FCOM 15.20.6

question: How can you silence the Mach/airspeed warning in flight?
options: Press the Mach/airspeed warning test switch
Press the Mach/airspeed warning reset switch
Descend to a lower altitude
Slow the aircraft speed to below Vmo/Mmo
explanation: Only by reducing airspeed below Vmo/Mmo. · FCOM 15.20.8

question: How far below the aircraft's altitude will the EGPWS display terrain?
options: 2500ft and displayed as solid red
5000ft and displayed as solid green
2000ft and displayed as dotted green
explanation: Dotted green: terrain from 2,000 ft below to 500 ft (250 ft gear down) below the airplane. Terrain more than 2,000 ft below is not shown. · FCOM 15.10.12

question: If the PSEU light illuminates, can the flight crew reset it?
options: Yes. Pulling and resetting of the PSEU PRI and PSEU ALTN circuit breakers will reset the indication
Yes. Advancing the thrust levers fully forward before engine start and retarding them will trigger a PSEU reset
No. Only a BITE reset or the clearing of the fault will extinguish the light
Yes. Pressing the PSEU light will reset it
explanation: The PSEU light can be reset following a maintenance BITE check or repair of the fault. (Exception: a 'simple fault' seen only on recall is cleared by resetting the MASTER CAUTION.) · FCOM 15.20.7

question: If you press only the No. 1 STALL WARNING TEST button on the AFT overhead panel, why can you feel the stick shaker on both the FOs and Captain's Flight Control Columns?
options: Each switch operates both stick shakers simultaneously, but uses a different power supply.
Only the stick shaker motor on the Captain's column operates, but the two columns are mechanically connected.
The No. 1 switch operates the FO's stick shaker and the No. 2 switch operates Captain's stick shaker.
explanation: No.1 test activates the Captain's stick shaker, No.2 the F/O's. Either stick shaker vibrates both columns through the column interconnect. · FCOM 15.20.9

question: Illumination of the PSEU fault light on the aft overhead panel will indicate:
options: It will only come ON during the light test
A single PSEU fault in flight only
FWD entry door not closed
An overwing exit flight lock fails to disengage on the ground
explanation: PSEU light on the ground: a PSEU fault, or an overwing exit flight lock fails to disengage when commanded. Inhibited in flight. · FCOM 15.10.2

question: In AUTO, the FASTEN BELTS and RETURN TO SEAT signs:
options: illuminate when descending through 15,000ft
illuminate when descending through 10,000ft
illuminate when flap or gear are extended
illuminate when flap is selected higher than 1 degree
explanation: AUTO: FASTEN BELTS and RETURN TO SEAT signs illuminate when flaps or gear are extended and extinguish when both are retracted. · FCOM 1.40.5

question: In flight, the Predictive Windshear Warning:
options: will activate if windshear is detected up to 7nm ahead of the aircraft
is inhibited below 1500ft
is operated by the EGPWS
will activate for windshear up to 1.5nm ahead of the aircraft
explanation: In flight the predictive windshear WARNING area is 0.5–1.5 nm ahead (±25°); cautions out to 3 nm. It comes from the weather radar, not the EGPWS. · FCOM 15.20.28

question: In flight, when will a Predictive Windshear Warning Alert be activated?
options: Will activate for windshear up to 1.5NM ahead of the aircraft
Is inhibited below 1800ft RA
Will cause amber WINDSHEAR message on both ND's
Will activate for windshear up to 3NM ahead of the aircraft
