explanation: Warning area in flight: up to 1.5 nm ahead (from 0.5 nm). Cautions to 3 nm. Red WINDSHEAR on PFD/ND for warnings, amber on ND for cautions; alerts below 1,200 ft RA. · FCOM 15.20.28

question: In what mode will the TCAS automatically show if a TA/RA occurs and the TFC switches are selected OFF?
options: MAP, CTR MAP, VOR, APP
MAP, VOR, APP, CTR APP
VOR, APP, CTR APP
MAP, CTR VOR, CTR APP
explanation: TCAS display shows automatically (TA ONLY or TA/RA selected, neither pilot has TFC on) in MAP, center MAP, VOR or APP modes. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: In what modes will a TCAS Traffic Alert message be displayed on the ND whenever a TA or RA is active (the EFIS control panel TFC switch does not have to be selected on)?
options: All modes
PLAN, MAP, VOR, APP
MAP CTR, VOR, APP
MAP, MAP CTR, VOR, APP
explanation: The TRAFFIC alert message is displayed in all ND modes whenever a TA or RA is active, even without TFC selected. · FCOM 10.41.22

question: Logo lights are installed on:
options: Left wingtip
Right wingtip
Top of both horizontal stablizers
Both wingtips
explanation: Logo lights are on the top of each horizontal stabilizer, lighting both sides of the vertical stabilizer. · FCOM 1.40.2

question: Number 1 DRIVE light illuminates amber. This is directly caused by:
options: IDG failure
engine shutdown
low oil pressure in the IDG
IDG auto disconnect due to high oil temperature
explanation: The DRIVE light is directly caused by IDG low oil pressure — which itself can be due to IDG failure, engine shutdown, or IDG disconnect. · FCOM 6.10.5 / 6.20.6

question: On takeoff the config warning sounds. What can be the cause?
options: Takeoff power not set on both engines
Trailing edge flaps are in a skew condition
Stabilizer set in the takeoff range
Trailing edge flaps set to 2
explanation: Takeoff config warning includes TE flaps outside 1–25, or TE flaps in a skew/asymmetry or uncommanded motion; plus LE, speed brake, spoilers, parking brake, stab trim. 'Flaps 2' is not a flap position. · FCOM 15.20.5

question: On the B737-800, which system(s) does the Proximity Switch Electronic Unit (PSEU) monitor?
options: Overwing door locks
Spoiler deflection
Landing Gear position, Takeoff/Landing, Configuration Warnings and Air/Ground sensing
Autobrake and Anti-Skid
explanation: The PSEU monitors takeoff configuration warnings, landing configuration warnings, landing gear and air/ground sensing (and overwing exit flight locks). · FCOM 15.20.7

question: Pushing VHF TEST swtich on the radio tuning panel:
options: Will test all VHF units installed
Performs the self-test function of the respective VHF radio
Will result in the 'VHF TEST COMPLETE' aural notification
Improves reception of weak signals
explanation: VHF TEST: removes automatic squelch (background noise heard, testing the receiver) and improves reception of weak signals. · FCOM 5.10.2

question: The alpha vanes provide angle-of-attack information to the stall warning system, auto throttle, auto pilot, auto slats and are anti-iced:
options: Whenever the alternate static ports are heated
By independent 115V AC heating elements, controlled by the PROBE HEAT switches
By LEFT or RIGHT FWD window heat switches
Whenever engine anti-icing is being used
explanation: The alpha vanes have their own electric heaters, powered when the PROBE HEAT switches are ON (AUTO on some airplanes). · FCOM 3.10.3 / 3.20

question: The aural alert for excessive bank angle is:
options: BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE
WINGS LEVEL
BANK ANGLE
DON'T SINK
explanation: GPWS aural: BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE at 35°, 40° and 45° of roll. · FCOM 15.20.28

question: The elevator control column override mechanism allows:
options: Forces from either control column to be transferred to the stabiliser
The control columns to be physically separated in the event of an elevator jam
The elevator feel and centering unit to transfer proper aerodynamic forces to the control columns
The elevator feel and centering unit to transfer the source of power for elevator actuators to hydraulic systems A or B, depending upon which is producing higher pressure
explanation: In a control column jam, an override mechanism allows the columns to be physically separated: force against the jam breaks out either column, and whichever moves freely provides elevator control. · FCOM 9.20.6

question: The Ground Proximity Warning System Test:
options: Can be performed only on the ground
Can be performed only above 1,000 Radio Altitude
Can be performed any time
Is inhibited from lift-off to 1,000 feet Radio Altitude
explanation: Ground proximity SYS TEST: momentarily push on the ground; system test is inhibited in flight. · FCOM 15.10.8

question: The Predictive Windshear alerts are available:
options: When TERR switch on EFIS control panel is pressed
Automatically below 2300 feet RA
Automatically below 1200 feet RA
When WPT switch on EFIS control panel is pressed
explanation: Predictive windshear runs automatically (in flight below 1,800 ft RA, or with takeoff thrust set); alerts are issued below 1,200 ft RA. No switch selection is needed. · FCOM 15.20.26

question: The RA aural alert "CLIMB-CLIMB NOW" means:
options: Increase your rate of climb now
Start climbing as soon as possible
Reversal maneuvour from initial descent RA
Reversal maneuvour from initial climb RA
explanation: CLIMB – CLIMB NOW: reversal maneuver from an initial descent RA. (DESCEND – DESCEND NOW: reversal from an initial climb RA.) · FCOM 15.20.33

question: The Stall Warning requirement is determined by what system component?
options: Two independent ADIRUs.
The Captain's or F/O's Alpha Vane.
A single stall management configuration computer.
Two independent SMYD Computers.
explanation: Two independent, identical SMYD computers determine when stall warning is required (alpha vanes, ADIRUs, anti-ice, configuration, air/ground, thrust). · FCOM 15.20.8

question: The Stall Warning System Stick Shaker can be tested by pressing the STALL WARNING TEST buttons on the AFT overhead panel.  Pressing No1 switch will activate the Captain's Stick Shaker and the Captain's column will vibrate.  Pressing N02 switch will activate the FO's Stick Shaker and the FO's column will vibrate.
options: True
False
explanation: False. No.1 activates the Captain's shaker and No.2 the F/O's, but either shaker vibrates BOTH columns through the column interconnect. · FCOM 15.20.9

question: Up to what range are predictive windshear alerts generated?
options: 0.5 to 1nm in flight  -  0.5 to 2nm on the ground
0.5 to 1.5nm in flight  -  0.5 to 3nm on the ground
0.1 to 1nm
0.5 to 5nm
explanation: Predictive windshear alert area: in flight warnings 0.5–1.5 nm (cautions to 3 nm); on the ground 0.5–3 nm, ±25°. · FCOM 15.20.28

question: What does the TCAS symbol shown below (an AMBER CIRCLE) indicate?
options: Results in aural alert of "TRAFFIC, TRAFFIC" when within 6nm with 1200 feet or less of vertical separation of other traffic.
Advises of traffic with potential impact on 25 seconds.
Advises that the proximate traffic is descending at more than 500 fpm.
Advises of traffic with potential impact in 40 seconds.
explanation: Solid amber circle = Traffic Advisory, generated about 40 seconds from the point of closest approach (RA red square at about 25 s). · FCOM 15.20.31

question: What effect does pushing the ground proximity BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT light have?
options: Has no effect if already within 1 dot of the localiser
Cancels or inhibits the Glideslope alert when below 1,000 feet RA.
Has no effect if already within 1 dot of the glideslope
Inhibits all GPWS warnings when below 1500ft RA
explanation: BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT: pushing it inhibits the ground proximity GLIDESLOPE alert when below 1,000 ft RA. · FCOM 15.10.7

question: What GPWS callout is given at 100ft above DH/MDA?
options: MINIMUMS
The actual RA
PLUS HUNDRED
DECIDE
explanation: DH/MDA callouts (from the Captain's MINS selector, RADIO or BARO): PLUS HUNDRED at DH/MDA + 100 ft, MINIMUMS at DH/MDA. · FCOM 15.20.30

question: What is the correct aural alert for excessive bank angle?
options: An intermittent horn
'BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE'
'ATTITUDE, ATTITUDE'
'CAUTION BANK'
explanation: BANK ANGLE, BANK ANGLE (at 35°, 40°, 45°). · FCOM 15.20.28

question: What is the maximum airspeed limit according MEL, when WINDOW HEAT is inoperative for window nr 4?
options: 280 KIAS
250 KIAS
250 KIAS below 10,000 feet MSL
280 KIAS below 10,000 MSL
explanation: Window heat test: if any ON light remains extinguished the window heat system is inoperative — observe the maximum airspeed limit of 250 kt below 10,000 ft. · FCOM SP.3.5

question: What will occur if the aircraft pitch altitude reaches the Pitch Limit Indication (PLI) on the PFD during slow speed manoeuvring?
options: The aircraft will experience initial stall buffet
The aircraft stalls
The stick nudger pushes the control column forward
The stick shaker warning activates
explanation: The pitch limit indicator shows the pitch attitude for stick shaker activation in the existing flight conditions (SMYD output). · FCOM 10.11 / 15.20.9

question: When are all TCAS alerts inhibited?
options: Below approximately 1,100 feet radio altitude
By GPWS and windshear warnings
Below approximately 1,000 feet radio altitude
Until the flaps are fully retracted after takeoff
explanation: All TCAS alerts are inhibited by GPWS and windshear warnings. (RAs and voice are inhibited below ~1,000 ft RA; all voice below ~500 ft RA.) · FCOM 15.20.32

question: When is a resolution advisory (RA) generated?
options: When the other aircraft is approximately 25 seconds from the point of closest approach
When the other aircraft is less than 6 nm from the point of closest approach
When the other aircraft is approximately 1200 feet from the point of closest approach
When the other aircraft is approximately 40 seconds from the point of closest approach
explanation: RA at about 25 seconds from the point of closest approach (TA at about 40 s). · FCOM 15.20.31

question: When is the Proximity Switch Electronic Unit (PSEU) light inhibited?
options: For 30 seconds after landing only
When the thrust levers are advanced toward takeoff power only
At all times in flight, when the thrust levers are advanced toward takeoff power at any time, and for 30 seconds after landing
In flight, but never on the ground
explanation: The PSEU light is inhibited in flight, when the thrust levers are advanced toward takeoff power, and for 30 seconds after landing. · FCOM 15.20.8

question: When testing the Mach/Airspeed warning system in flight, the No1 and No2 systems must be tested separately to identify that the clacker sounds for both systems independently.
options: True
False
explanation: False. The Mach/airspeed warning test is inhibited while airborne — it can only be done on the ground. · FCOM 15.10.4

question: When you initially turn on the battery, what indications will the Master Caution and Warning System give?
options: The Master Caution will illuminate, along with some of the system annunciators
There will be no warnings or lights, as the system is suppressed for 4 minutes
The Master Fire Warning will illuminate and the Fire Bell will sound
explanation: On initial power-up, systems not yet powered/configured show their caution lights, so MASTER CAUTION illuminates with some system annunciators. Bank answer. · FCOM 15.10.2

question: Which is the ND symbol for a traffic advisory?
options: Outline white diamond
Solid red square
Outline blue square
Solid amber circle
explanation: TA = solid amber circle. RA = solid red square; proximate = solid white diamond; other traffic = hollow white diamond. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: Which of the following will cause activation of the takeoff configuration warning system?
options: SPEED BRAKE lever in the DOWN position
Spoilers partially extended
Leading edge slats in the extend position and trailing edge flaps at flaps 5
Leading edge slat in the full extend position and trailing edge at flaps 15
explanation: Takeoff config warning (on the ground, thrust advanced) includes spoilers not down and speed brake lever not in DOWN, flaps outside 1–25, LE devices not correctly set, parking brake set, stab trim outside the takeoff range. · FCOM 15.20.5

question: Which statement is correct for TCAS, proximate traffic?
options: It is only shown as 'OFFSCALE'
It is within 6 miles and 1200ft vertically
It is not indicated
It is always a TA
explanation: Proximate traffic is within 6 nm and 1,200 ft vertically but is not expected to cause a TA or RA (solid white diamond). · FCOM 15.20.31

question: Which statement is correct in relation to the predictive windshear aural alerts?
options: The predictive windshear aural alerts will be heard through flightdeck speakers and the headsets at a pre-set volume.  They cannot be controlled or turned off by the crew.
They cannot be deselected on the Captain's and FO's Audio Control Panel, but the volume can be adjusted
They can be deselected on the Captain's and FO's Audio Control Panel, but the volume cannot be adjusted
They can be deselected on the Captain's and FO's Audio Control Panel, and the volume can be adjusted.
explanation: GPWS, altitude alert, TCAS and radar predictive windshear audio are heard through speakers and headsets at preset volumes and cannot be controlled or turned off by the crew. · FCOM 5.20.1

question: Which statement is correct in relation to the testing the Mach/Airspeed warning system
options: The test will only function correctly whilst airborne, as it needs an airspeed to be indicating.
The test is only required on the outbound leg.
On the ground, the No1 and No2 systems must be tested separately to identify that the clacker sounds for both systems independently.
In flight, the system should be tested as part of the Airspeed Unreliable checklist to determine which ADIRU is functioning correctly
explanation: Each MACH AIRSPEED WARNING TEST switch tests its own system (clacker sounds); test inhibited while airborne, so done on the ground, one system at a time. · FCOM 15.10.4

question: Which systems does the Proximity Switch Electronic Unit (PSEU) monitor
options: Air/Ground sensing, Landing Gear and Anti-Skid.
Air/Ground sensing, Landing Gear and Air/Ground sensing.
Takeoff/Landing Configuration Warnings, Landing Gear and Air/Ground sensing.
Takeoff/Landing Configuration Warnings, Landing Gear and Anti-Skid
explanation: The PSEU monitors takeoff configuration warnings, landing configuration warnings, landing gear and air/ground sensing. · FCOM 15.20.7

question: With TCAS, proximate traffic is:
options: Displayed as an amber square
Within 12 miles horizontally and 1200ft vertically
Within 1.5 nm
Within 6 miles horizontally and 1200ft vertically
explanation: Proximate traffic: within 6 nm and 1,200 ft vertically, not expected to cause a TA or RA (solid white diamond). · FCOM 15.20.31

question: With the Captains ACP is operating in degraded mode, at that station:
options: Altitude alert, GPWS and Windshear audio warnings are not heard
The Captain can transmit on VHF2
PA functions are still available
The flight interphone is still available
explanation: ACP degraded mode: audio warnings for altitude alert, GPWS and windshear are not heard at that station. Only one radio is available (Captain VHF-1, F/O VHF-2); PA, interphone and hand mic are not usable. · FCOM 5.20.3

question: A takeoff should be rejected if a flight deck window opens on takeoff below 80kt.
options: True
False
explanation: Below 80 kt reject for any significant problem (e.g. a flight deck window opening). Above 80 kt RYR rejects only for fire/fire warning, engine failure, predictive windshear warning, or airplane unsafe/unable to fly. · FCOM NP.21.38

question: When are crew alerted to a deviation from the selected altitude?
options: 1000 feet from selected altitude.
500 feet from selected altitude.
300 feet from selected altitude.
50 feet from selected altitude.
explanation: Deviation alert: 300 ft from the selected altitude → momentary tone + current altitude box amber and flashing. · FCOM 15.20.9

question: What does the amber INSTR SWITCH annunciation (shown on the PFD/ND heading display) indicate?
options: Captain's and First Officer's displays are using seperate sources of IRU data.
The IRS switch on the Forward Overhead panel is not selected to NORMAL
Captain's and First Officer's displays are using the same source of IRU data with the IRS switch selected to OFF.
The IRS position for each IRS is in disagreement
explanation: INSTR SWITCH (amber): both the Captain's and First Officer's displays are using the same source of IRU data. Displayed when the IRS switch on the overhead panel is not in the NORMAL position. · FCOM 10.11.32

question: What precaution should be taken when responding to a CONFIG alert?
options: The checklist should not be actioned if fuel quantity in the centre tank is greater than 726Kg
Do not accomplish the checklist until established in a level flight attitude
Ensure that all main tank pump switches are in the ON position.
Retard the thrust levers to idle
explanation: In a nose-up climb the centre pump LOW PRESSURE lights can come on with fuel still in the centre tank, so the pumps get switched OFF and CONFIG appears. RYR: when established in a LEVEL FLIGHT ATTITUDE, if the centre tank contains usable fuel and a centre pump switch is OFF, set it ON again. So the CONFIG response is done once in level flight. · FCOM NP.21.87 / 12.10.5

question: Where do you read the flight crew oxygen pressure?
options: On the crew oxygen pressure indicator on the aft overhead panel
At each crew station
At the the flight crew
At the oxygen cylinder
explanation: Crew oxygen pressure is read on the CREW OXYGEN pressure indicator on the aft overhead panel. · FCOM NP.21.9

question: Which systems use engine bleed air during operation?
options: Engine and wing anti-icing, air conditioning, cabin pressurisation, emergency gear extension.
Engine starting, air conditioning, cabin pressurisation, wing anti-icing, hydraulic reservoir pressurisation, water tank pressurisation.
Engine and wing anti-icing, APU starting, air conditioning, cabin pressurisation, hydraulic reservoir pressurisation.
Engine and wing anti-icing, thrust reverser deployment, cabin pressurisation, hydraulic reservoir pressurisation.
explanation: Systems relying on bleed air: air conditioning/pressurization, wing and engine thermal anti-icing, engine starting, hydraulic reservoir pressurization, water tank pressurization (and the nitrogen generation system on later airplanes). · FCOM 2.20.1

question: Which systems use engine bleed air for operation?
options: APU, engine starting, Air con/Press, Hydraulic tanks
Air con/press, Wing Anti-ice, Fuel tanks
Wing Anti-ice, engine starting, water tank
Engine starting, Air con/Press, Wing and Engine anti-ice, Hydraulic and water tanks pressurization
explanation: Systems relying on bleed air: air conditioning/pressurization, wing and engine thermal anti-icing, engine starting, hydraulic reservoir pressurization, water tank pressurization (and the nitrogen generation system on later airplanes). · FCOM 2.20.1

question: What is the result if all temperature zone selectors are positioned to OFF?
options: The packs will attempt to maintain an average temperature across all zones.
Both packs will shut down
Left pack will produce 24 degrees centigrade and right pack will produce 18 degrees centigrade.
explanation: All temperature selectors OFF: the packs produce fixed temperatures, left pack 24 °C (75 °F) and right pack 18 °C (65 °F). · FCOM 2.10.5 / 2.30.x

question: If all TEMPERATURE ZONE SELECTORS are positioned to OFF:
options: the left pack maintains 18 degrees, the right 24
the packs turn off automatically
the left pack maintains 24 degrees, the right 18 degrees
the packs maintain the average temperature demanded by the coolest part of the cabin
explanation: All temperature selectors OFF: the packs produce fixed temperatures, left pack 24 °C (75 °F) and right pack 18 °C (65 °F). · FCOM 2.10.5 / 2.30.x

question: What is the result if all temperature zone selectors are positioned to OFF
options: Left pack will produce 24 degrees centigrade and right pack will produce 18 degrees centigrade
None of the answers are correct
Both packs will shut down
The packs will attempt to maintain an average temperature across all zones
explanation: All temperature selectors OFF: the packs produce fixed temperatures, left pack 24 °C (75 °F) and right pack 18 °C (65 °F). · FCOM 2.10.5 / 2.30.x

question: Due to a malfunction you are required to return to the airport of departure. To avoid the OFF SCHED DESCENT warning you reset the FLT ALT. What can you expect?
options: The pressurization will increase its ventilation and possibly pressurization will be lost
The automatic abort capability for the departure airport is lost
The system will be recalculating the pressurization for the departure airport
Nothing will happen and you will still get the OFF SCHED DESCENT warning
explanation: If the FLT ALT is reset in flight, the controller no longer recognises the departure field, so the automatic abort (return to takeoff field elevation) capability is lost. · FCOM 2.40.5 / 2.40.6

question: The amber OFF SCHEDULE DESCENT light illuminates. What does it indicate?
options: The pressurization controller has failed and will automatically shift to manual
The aircraft has descended before reaching the planned cruise altitude set in the flight altitude window
The pressurization standby controller has failed and will automatically shift to STANDBY
The main pressurization controller is unable to maintain pressurization and has to be manually shifted to manual
explanation: OFF SCHED DESCENT (amber): the airplane started to descend before reaching the planned cruise altitude set in the FLT ALT window. · FCOM 2.10.14 / 2.40.5

question: The wing body overheat light comes on. What is the related master caution warning?
options: OVERHEAD
OVHT /DET
AIR COND
As the light is in the proximity of the pilot’s perception there is no master caution for this condition
explanation: WING-BODY OVERHEAT is an AIR COND system annunciator (master caution). · FCOM 15.20.3

question: What happens when the WING BODY OVHT TEST switch is pressed?
options: The amber BLEED TRIP OFF Lights illuminate
All of the answers are correct
The amber PACK TRIP OFF Lights illuminate
The amber WING-BODY OVERHEAT Lights illuminate
explanation: WING-BODY OVHT TEST: illuminates both WING-BODY OVERHEAT lights (tests the overheat circuits). · FCOM 2.10.x

question: What is the function of the Dual Bleed Light?
options: Illuminates to warn whenever both engines are providing bleed air and the engines are at different thrust settings.
Illuminates whenever pressure in APU rises above a pre-set value.
Illuminates when the APU bleed air valve, engine bleed air valves and the isolation valve are in a position to permit possible backpressure of the APU.
Illuminates whenever the APU is running and no engine bleed air valves are open
explanation: DUAL BLEED: the APU bleed air valve is open and the engine No 1 bleed switch is ON, or engine No 2 bleed is ON with the isolation valve open, i.e. a position that permits possible backpressure of the APU. · FCOM 2.10.x

question: What is the result if one pack fails in-flight?
options: The remaining pack will operate in LOW flow
The packs will automatically switch off, and cabin temperature is controlled by the mix manifold and the recirculation fans
The remaining pack is capable of maintaining pressurisation and acceptable cabin temperatures up to 41,000 feet
The remaining pack when selected to AUTO will be capable of maintaining pressurisation up to aircraft ceiling, only if all Zone Temperature Controllers are selected to OFF
explanation: One pack is capable of maintaining pressurization and acceptable temperatures throughout the airplane up to 41,000 ft (max certified ceiling). · FCOM 2.30.x

question: What does illumination of an amber COWL ANTI-ICE light indicate?
options: An over temperature in the duct upstream of the engine cowl anti ice valve
An over temperature or over pressure condition in the duct downstream of the engine cowl anti-ice valve
An over pressure in the duct downstream of the engine cowl anti-ice valve
The respective cowl anti-ice valve is open
explanation: COWL ANTI-ICE light (amber): overpressure condition in the duct downstream of the engine cowl anti-ice valve. · FCOM 3.10.x

question: Which statement is correct for when the window heat Test Switch is put into the OVHT position?
options: Simulates an overheat condition in order to test the system
Can only be used if all green lights are on
Performs a voltage check of the power supplies
Checks for the presence of the window heat elements
explanation: Window heat TEST switch OVHT: simulates an overheat condition to test the system (OVERHEAT lights illuminate, ON lights extinguish). PWR TEST forces heat to full power. · FCOM 3.10.x

question: In flight, with Autopilot engaged in CMD B, which FCC controls the flight directors on the Captain's PFD?
options: Both FCCs
Neither FCC
FCC B
FCC A
explanation: Master FCC: with one or both A/Ps engaged in CMD, the FCC for the first A/P in CMD is the master FCC, regardless of which F/D is turned on first. CMD B → FCC B is master and drives both F/Ds (MA light illuminated). · FCOM 4.20.3

question: How many independent Flight Control Computers (FCCs) are there in the AFDS?
options: Three
Four
Two
One
explanation: The AFDS is a dual system consisting of two individual flight control computers (FCCs A and B) and a single mode control panel. · FCOM 4.20.1

question: Other than by selecting N1 mode by pressing the N1 switch on the MCP, when else will N1 mode automatically engage.
options: Never, N1 mode is only ever manually selected and engaged.
VNAV engaged prior to liftoff.
LVL CHG engaged in climb more than 2.5 minutes after takeoff or VNAV engaged in climb.
LVL CHG engaged within first 1.5 minutes after takeoff.
explanation: N1 mode engages automatically when engaging LVL CHG in climb (except during the 2 1/2 minute inhibit period after lift-off) and when engaging VNAV in climb. · FCOM 4.10.3

question: Two independent radio altimeters provide radio altitude to the respective FCC's. How will the Autopilot System be affected if one Radio Altimeter becomes inoperative?
options: The autopilot will continue as normal
The autopilot will continue to command the aircraft down to minimums
The autopilot will disconnect as soon as the failure is detected
The autopilot will disconnect two seconds after LOC and G/S capture
explanation: With a radio altimeter inoperative, the autopilot will disengage two seconds after LOC and GS capture. · FCOM 4.20.3

question: Which A/T modes permit manual thrust change without A/T interference?
options: GA & ARM
THR HLD & ARM
Only THR HLD
N1 & ARM
explanation: THR HLD: thrust lever servos inhibited, the pilot can set the thrust levers manually. ARM: no A/T mode engaged, servos inhibited, manual thrust setting (minimum speed protection provided). · FCOM 4.20.5

question: After lift-off the A/T remains in THR HLD until which altitude?
options: 400 feet Radio Altitude and 18 seconds after lift-off
800 feet Radio Altitude and 18 seconds after lift-off
800 feet above Field Elevation
400 feet Radio Altitude
explanation: The A/T remains in THR HLD until 800 feet above field elevation, then changes to ARM. · FCOM 4.20.11

question: Normally, N1 limits and target N1 values are provided to the A/T by the?
options: A/T computer
The pilot
FMC
IRUs
explanation: The FMC provides N1 limits and target N1 for the A/T, and command airspeeds for the A/T and AFDS. · FCOM 4.20.1 / 4.20.8

question: The Automatic Flight System (AFS) consists of?
options: The Flight Directors (F/D)
All of the answers are correct
The Autothrottles (A/T)
The autopilots (A/P)
explanation: The automatic flight system (AFS) consists of the autopilot flight director system (AFDS) and the autothrottle (A/T). · FCOM 4.20.1

question: What happens to the IAS/MACH display on the MCP if the SPD INTV switch is pushed during VNAV operation?
options: The display opens up and shows 100 kts
The display opens up and shows FMC target speed
The display becomes blank
The display opens up and shows dashes
explanation: SPD INTV with VNAV engaged: the IAS/MACH display opens showing the current FMC target speed, which can then be changed with the selector. · FCOM 4.10.4 / SP.4.3

question: With the STANDBY POWER switch (located on the Generator Drive and Standby Power Panel)  in the AUTO position, will the loss of a single AC Transfer Bus result in automatic switching from normal to alternate power?
options: Only if power from AC Transfer Bus 1 is lost
No, for automatic switching to occur power must be lost from both AC Transfer Busses
Only if power from AC Transfer Bus 1 is lost, or power from DC Bus 1 is lost
Only if power from AC Transfer Bus 2 is lost
explanation: Standby power switch AUTO: automatic switching from normal to alternate power occurs if power from either AC transfer bus 1 or DC bus 1 is lost. · FCOM 6.20.11

question: What is the normal source of power for the AC Standby Bus?
options: AC Transfer Bus 1
AC Transfer Bus 2
Ground Service Bus 1
The Static Inverter
explanation: Normally the DC standby bus is powered by TR1, TR2 and TR3 (AC standby bus from AC transfer bus 1). With all AC lost: battery. · FCOM 6.10.6 / 6.20.11

question: In the event of the loss of all engine and APU IDGs, the Standby Power system will provide what electrical power?
options: AC power and DC power
28 Volts DC power only
12 Volts DC
AC power only
explanation: The standby system provides 115V AC (static inverter) and 24V DC to essential systems after loss of all engine or APU-driven AC power. · FCOM 6.20.11

question: Under what conditions are DC bus 1 and DC bus 2 isolated
options: At glide slope capture during a a flight director or autopilot ILS approach
Switching the Bus Transfer switch to OFF
All of the answers are correct
When the cross bus tie relay opens
explanation: The cross bus tie relay opens (isolating DC bus 1 from DC bus 2) at glide slope capture on an F/D or A/P ILS approach, or with the BUS TRANSFER switch OFF. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: What is the effect of selecting the Drive Disconnect switch to DISCONNECT?
options: AC Standby Bus is subsequently powered by the Inverter from the batteries.
IDG is mechanically disconnected from the engine and the DRIVE light illuminates.
No effects take place until STANDBY POWER switch is also moved to BAT.
DRIVE light illuminates, AC electrical power is lost on associated Transfer Bus, AC Standby Bus powered from opposite Transfer Bus.
explanation: Generator drive DISCONNECT disconnects the IDG from the engine (if the engine is running) and the DRIVE light illuminates. It cannot be reconnected in the air. · FCOM 6.10.5 / 6.20.6

question: What is the source of power for the AC Standby bus if all AC power is lost
options: The Battery Charger
The DC Standby Bus
The Static Inverter
The TRs
explanation: The static inverter converts 24V DC from the battery to 115V AC for the AC standby bus when normal power is lost. · FCOM 6.20.12

question: Why are the covers on the Drive DISCONNECT switches red?
options: To identify that operation of this switch in flight is irreversible.
To identify a NNP memory item.
For easy identification in low light conditions.
To identify an emergency operation switch.
explanation: Red guard: the DISCONNECT action can't be undone in flight — the IDG cannot be reconnected in the air. · FCOM 6.10.5

question: Where is the right IRS electrically powered from?
options: Normally AC Transfer Bus 2 - if AC power is not normal from the switched hot battery bus for a maximum of 5 minutes
Normally AC Transfer Bus 1 - if AC power is not normal DC power from the switched hot battery bus
Normally AC Transfer Bus 2 - if AC power is not normal from the hot battery bus
Normally AC Transfer Bus 2 - if AC power is not normal from the battery bus
explanation: Right IRS: normally AC transfer bus 2; backup from the switched hot battery bus for only about 5 minutes (left IRS: AC standby bus, with switched hot battery backup). · FCOM 11.20.6

question: On the ground with the Battery Master switch selected to ON, but no AC Power available, what would you expect the battery voltage to be?
options: Exactly equal to 28 Volts
None of the answers are correct.
Less than 28 Volts
Greater than 28 Volts
explanation: Batteries are two 24 V Ni-Cd units; battery voltage range is 22–30 V. With no AC (no charger), the battery reads below the 28 V TR/charger output. The FCOM gives only the 22–30 V range, not this exact case. · FCOM 6.20.8

question: On the ground, with the BATTERY switch OFF and STANDBY POWER Switch in BAT, the switched hot battery bus is:
options: Powered by the Hot Battery Bus
Powered by the switched hot Battery Bus
Powered by the Battery
Not powered
explanation: STANDBY POWER switch BAT puts the AC standby, DC standby and battery bus on battery power; the battery switch may be ON or OFF. If the battery switch is OFF, the switched hot battery bus is not powered. · FCOM 6.20.11

question: What is the voltage of the DC Busses in normal flight?
explanation: 28 volt DC power is supplied by three TR units (115V AC → 28V DC). · FCOM 6.20.7 / 6.20.8

question: Fuel for the APU is normally supplied from the:
options: no 1 main tank
aux Tank
no 2 main tank
center Tank
explanation: APU fuel comes from the left side of the fuel manifold when the AC fuel pumps are operating; with no AC pumps it is suction fed from main tank No.1. · FCOM 7.30.1 / 12.20.3

question: During an In-flight start, if a wet start is detected, will the EEC turn off ignition and fuel to the engine? If so, when?
options: 10 seconds after start lever moved to Idle.
As soon as the wet start is detected by the EEC.
15 seconds after start lever moved to Idle if the EGT does not rise
There is no in-flight abnormal start protection.
explanation: Abnormal start protection is for GROUND STARTS ONLY. In flight there is no automatic wet/hot start cutoff — the crew monitors. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: On a ground start, if a Wet start is detected, when will the EEC turn off ignition and shut off fuel to the engine?.
options: 10 seconds after start lever moved to idle
The EEC does not turn off ignition and fuel. The crew must monitor these carefully and close the start lever if the EGT does not rise.
5 seconds after thrust lever moved to Idle
15 seconds after the start lever was moved to Idle
explanation: Ground start: if a wet start (no EGT rise) is detected, the EEC turns off ignition and shuts off fuel 15 seconds after the start lever is moved to IDLE. · FCOM 7.20.9

question: Can an engine be started if the aircraft does not have AC power applied?
options: Only if the APU is running
No
Yes, even if the battery switch is placed OFF
Yes, provided an air source is available for starting
42 QUESTIONS
explanation: Yes — a battery start is possible with a pneumatic source: the start switch uses battery power to open the start valve, and the EEC is powered by its alternator once N2 exceeds 15%. · FCOM 7.20.3 / 7.20.9

question: If an outboard display unit fails, where will the PFD be automatically displayed?
options: On the inboard display unit
It will not automatically display. It can only be displayed manually with the MAIN PANEL DU selectors
On the ENGINE SECONDARY display
On the ENGINE PRIMARY display
explanation: If an outboard DU fails, the PFD is automatically displayed on the inboard DU and the outboard DU blanks. · FCOM 10.21.5

question: The display selector on the IRS Display Unit (ISDU) is moved to position HDG/STS during alignment. What is displayed in the right window?
options: True track
Minutes remaining until alignment is complete
Ground speed
Wind speed
explanation: ISDU HDG/STS: left window true heading; right window maintenance status codes — during alignment, minutes remaining until alignment is complete (shows 15 until 14 minutes remain). · FCOM 11.10.18

question: Which window(s) are heated with the LEFT FWD WINDOW HEAT Switch ON?
options: L2, L3
L1, L2
L1 only
explanation: FWD WINDOW HEAT switches control window No.1; SIDE switches control window No.2. Window No.3 is not electrically heated. · FCOM 3.20.2

question: With the APU running, how can it be stopped immediately?
options: Rotate APU FIRE switch
Switch the battery off
All of the answers are correct
Move the APU START switch to OFF
explanation: Moving the battery switch to OFF automatically shuts down the APU (power loss to the ECU) — immediately. APU switch OFF has a 60 s cooling delay. · FCOM 7.30.2

question: What is the maximum flap extension altitude?
options: 10,000ft if below 250kts
explanation: To prevent excessive structural loads from increased Mach at higher altitude, flap extension above 20,000 feet should not be attempted. · FCOM 9.20.19 / L.10.x

question: What does the SPEED BRAKE DO NOT ARM light (located on the left forward panel) indicate when illuminated amber?
options: The speed brakes must not be extended as airspeed currently too high for safe operation.
Indicates that the wheel speed is above 60 kts on landing and the speedbrake lever has not been moved to the up position.
Illuminated whenever forward thrust levers are advanced beyond takeoff thrust whilst aircraft on the ground
Indicates an abnormal condition, a test input in the speed brake system or that the wheel speed has dropped below 60 kts on landing and the speedbrake lever has not been moved to the down position.
explanation: SPEED BRAKE DO NOT ARM (amber): abnormal condition or test inputs to the automatic speed brake system, OR during landing wheel speed below 60 kt with the speedbrake lever not moved to DOWN. · FCOM 9.10.11

question: What happens to the speed brakes if the SPEED BRAKE lever is left in the DOWN position during landing.
options: The speed brake lever will automatically move to the up position and the spoilers will deploy as normal if all other required conditions are met.
The flight spoilers will deploy on landing if all other conditions are met, but ground spoilers will not deploy.
The spoilers will not deploy.
The ground spoilers will deploy on landing if all other conditions are met, but flight spoilers will not deploy.
explanation: Lever DOWN at landing: if the thrust reversers are raised (both reverse thrust levers), the SPEED BRAKE lever automatically moves UP and the spoilers deploy (with the other conditions met). · FCOM 9.20.16

question: Selecting the ALTERNATE FLAPS master switch to...
options: STBY, activates the standby pump and arms ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch
OFF, activates the PTU and arms the primary flap selector
ARM, closes trailing edge flap bypass valve, activates standby pump and arms ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch
ON, activates the standby pump and arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch
explanation: ALTERNATE FLAPS master ARM: closes the TE flap bypass valve, activates the standby pump and arms the ALTERNATE FLAPS position switch. Guard is red because LE devices extended by the standby system cannot be retracted. · FCOM 9.10.x / 9.20.x

question: What does the Magenta figure displayed above the Speed Tape signify?
options: Maximum airspeed for current flap settings
Airspeed manually selected in the IAS/MACH window or the FMC computed airspeed if the IAS/MACH window is blank
Current or next speed restriction in the FMC
explanation: Selected speed readout (magenta) above the speed tape: speed selected in the MCP IAS/MACH window, or the FMC computed speed when the window is blank. · FCOM 10.11.x

question: What does the Magenta figure displayed above the Speed Tape signify?
options: Airspeed manually selected in the IAS/MACH window and FMC computed airspeed if the IAS/MACH window is blank
Current or next speed restriction in the FMC
Maximum airspeed for current flap settings
FMC computed airspeed if the IAS/MACH window is blank
explanation: Selected speed readout (magenta) above the speed tape: speed selected in the MCP IAS/MACH window, or the FMC computed speed when the window is blank. · FCOM 10.11.x

question: If IRS alignment is lost in flight, what action can be taken?
options: IRS mode selector can be selected to ALIGN for 30 seconds then back to NAV to reset the system.
The navigation mode remains unavailable for the rest of the flight, but ATT mode can be selected to provide attitude reference.
The IRS mode selectors must be moved to OFF to allow FMC to hold all GPS and navigation data for remainder of the flight.
ALIGN mode can be selected to provide attitude reference. After 2 minutes in level flight, NAV mode will be available again

ATT mode can be selected to relevel the system and attain attitude reference, the system can then be returned to ALIGN for the 30 second Fast Align, then returned to NAV once the ALIGN light extinguishes.
explanation: If alignment is lost in flight, the navigation mode (present position and ground speed) is inoperative for the remainder of the flight. Selecting ATT allows the attitude mode to provide an attitude reference after about 30 s of straight, level, unaccelerated flight. · FCOM 11.20.5

question: If IRS alignment is lost in flight, what action can be taken?
options: ATT mode can be selected to relevel the system and attain attitude reference, the system can then be returned to ALIGN for the 30 second Fast Align, then returned to NAV once the ALIGN light extinguishes
ALIGN mode can be selected to provide attitude reference. After 2 minutes in level flight, NAV mode will be available again
The navigation mode remains unavailable for the rest of the flight, but ATT mode can be selected to provide attitude reference
IRS mode selector can be selected to ALIGN for 30 seconds then back to NAV to reset the system
explanation: If alignment is lost in flight, the navigation mode (present position and ground speed) is inoperative for the remainder of the flight. Selecting ATT allows the attitude mode to provide an attitude reference after about 30 s of straight, level, unaccelerated flight. · FCOM 11.20.5

question: After performing the FMC/CDU preflight, the flight crew notices that the ACTIVE navigation database has expired and must be changed. What will the RTE page look like after the navigation database change?
options: Unchanged, no action required
Route discontinuity will be gone, everything else remains the same
The route will need to be reloaded
The navigation database never expires
explanation: The navigation database date can be changed only on the ground. Changing the navigation database removes all previously entered route data, so the RTE page is blank and the route must be re-entered. · FCOM 11.40.7

question: Below what altitude are windshear alerts available for aircraft fitted with IntuVue weather radar?
options: 1200 feet RA and below.
2500 feet RA and below.
FL100 and below.
1500 feet AGL and below.
explanation: Predictive windshear alerting below 1,200 ft RA. IntuVue: windshear detection operates automatically below 1800 ft AGL, with alerts available at 1200 ft and below. · FCOM 11.20.11 / 11.20.13

question: Which statement is correct if during VNAV operations the Fuel Quantity Indicating System fails?
options: VNAV operation is not possible
The scratchpad message: CHECK FMC FUEL QUANTITY is displayed
The flight crew manually enter (and periodically update) estimated fuel weight on the FMC PERF INIT page to keep gross weight current and performance data valid
VNAV disengages
explanation: VERIFY GW AND FUEL: fuel data invalid, the PERF INIT fuel value is replaced with dashes. Enter fuel weight on PERF INIT 1/2; periodic update of fuel weight is required to keep gross weight and performance data valid. · FCOM 11.60.13 / 11.32.4

question: For the IntuVue  Radar, Predictive Windshear mode is automatically turned on in which of the following specific aircraft conditions?
options: In flight below 1800 feet AGL or on the ground with thrust levers set for takeoff.
In flight above 1500 feet AGL
Whenever the Air/Ground logic is in Air mode.
In flight above 1200 feet RA, on ground after first engine start
explanation: IntuVue automatic windshear activation: in the air below 1800 ft AGL, or on the ground with the thrust levers set for takeoff. · FCOM 11.10.36

question: How can the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) be erased?
options: Pushing the ERASE switch for 2 seconds when the aircraft is on ground and parking brake is set
Pushing the ERASE switch for 2 seconds when the aircraft is in flight
Pushing the ERASE switch for 2 seconds when the aircraft is on ground with parking brake is released
Pushing the ERASE switch for 2 seconds when the aircraft is in flight and parking brake is set
explanation: CVR ERASE switch (red), push 2 seconds: all four channels erased; operative only when the airplane is on the ground and the parking brake is set. · FCOM 5.10.11

question: What does the FMC Advisory Message BUFFET ALERT indicate?
options: Current conditions result in a manoeuvre margin less than specified
The airplane is in partial or full stall
Flaps need to be retracted because airspeed is greater than Vfe
Encountering turbulence will cause initial buffet
explanation: BUFFET ALERT (only with flaps retracted): current conditions result in a maneuver margin less than specified. Bring the airplane back within the operating envelope. · FCOM 11.60.18

question: What are the LNAV engagement criteria within 3 miles of the active route?
options: The aircraft must be on an intercept heading prior to the next waypoint
The aircraft must be on an intercept heading after the next waypoint
The aircraft must be on an intercept heading at least 5 miles before the next waypoint
The aircraft can be on any heading
explanation: LNAV engages within 3 NM of the active leg on any heading. Outside 3 NM, it engages if on an intercept heading of 90° or less and the intercept will occur before the active waypoint. · FCOM 11.31.10 / 4.10.13

question: What information is available with the IRS mode selector in ATT?
options: Heading information only
Attitude information only
Attitude, heading and position
Attitude and heading information
explanation: IRS mode selector ATT: provides only attitude and heading information. Heading is available after entry of the initial magnetic heading (POS INIT SET HDG or ISDU). · FCOM 11.10.21

question: How many fuel measuring sticks are installed?
explanation: Six fuel measuring sticks in each main tank and four in the center tank = 16. · FCOM 12.10.8

question: In flight a fuel imbalance between No1 and No2 tanks can be corrected by:
options: A Fuel imbalance cannot be rectified in flight, as fuel transfer between tanks can only be carried out on the ground using the Ground Refuelling Panel switches.
Increase thrust setting on the side with higher amount of fuel and decrease thrust setting on side with lower amount of fuel.
Open the Crossfeed valve, turn off the pumps on the low side until the Fuel Quantity Indicators are balanced.
Open the crossfeed valve, turn OFF the fuel pumps for the tank with higher fuel level.
explanation: QRH: open the CROSSFEED and switch OFF the fuel pumps of the LOW tank, so both engines feed from the high tank until balanced, then restore. Fuel is not 'transferred' into the other tank — the high tank just feeds both engines. (FCOM 12.20.2: crossfeed lets one main tank feed both engines.) · FCOM QRH FUEL IMBALANCE / 12.20.2

question: How many fuel pumps does each tank have, and where are they located?
options: The centre tank has 2 AC pumps located on the forward wall of the centre tank. The No1 main tank has 1 AC pump located on the rear wall of the No1 tank. The No2 main tank has 1 AC pump located on the rear wall of the No2 tank

The centre tank has 1 AC fuel pump on the front wall of the centre tank and 1 on the rear wall of the centre tank. The No1 main tank has 1 pump on the rear wall of the No1 tank and 1 pump on the front wall of the No1 tank.

The centre tank has 2 AC pumps located on the forward wall of the centre tank. The No1 main tank has 2 AC pumps located on the rear wall of the No1 tank. The No2 main tank has 2 AC pumps located on the rear wall of the No2 tank
The centre tank has 2 AC fuel pumps mounted on the rear wall of the centre tank. The No1 and No2 tank have 2 AC pumps mounted in the centre tank - 1 on the front wall and one one the rear wall.
explanation: FCOM confirms each tank has two AC pumps and a center tank scavenge jet pump feeding main tank 1; pump mounting locations are not given in the FCOM — answer from the banks. · FCOM 12.20.2 / 12.20.3

question: In-flight, if the two fuel pump LOW PRESSURE Lights for main tank No.1 illuminate. What happens to the No.1 engine?
options: It receives fuel from main tank No. 2 automatically
It will shut down due to fuel starvation
It receives fuel from main tank No.1 through a suction feed line that bypasses the pumps
It continues to operate due to the Cross Feed valve automatically opening
explanation: With both pumps in a main tank failed, the engine is suction-fed from its own tank through the bypass valve (high altitude may cause thrust deterioration or flameout). · FCOM 12.20.x

question: Pulling the engine fire warning switch up:
options: Closes the spar fuel shutoff valve. The engine fuel shutoff valve must be closed using the engine start lever
Closes the engine fuel shutoff valve. The spar fuel shutoff valve must be closed using the engine start lever
Closes both the engine fuel shutoff valve and the spar fuel shutoff valve
Closes both the engine fuel shutoff valve and the spar fuel shutoff valve if the battery switch is OFF
explanation: Pulling the engine fire switch closes both the engine fuel shutoff valve and the spar fuel shutoff valve (same as start lever to CUTOFF). Discharge needs the switch to be rotated. · FCOM 8.20.2 / 12.20.3

question: In flight one centre tank fuel pump selected OFF with more than 760 kg remaining in the centre tank, and both main tanks are full. What will be displayed on the Upper Display Unit?
options: No indication initially. If left in this position, eventually IMBAL will be displayed
A fuel LOW alert indication below the centre tank contents gauge
A CONFIG alert under the centre fuel contents gauge
The related centre tank pump LOW PRESSURE light will be illuminated
explanation: CONFIG: either engine running, center tank more than 726 kg and both center pump switches OFF → amber CONFIG at the center tank indicator. · FCOM 12.10.5

question: When does the center tank fuel scavenge jet pump operate?
options: The center fuel tank is about 3/4 full and all AC fuel pump switches are selected to ON
The No. 1 main fuel tank is about 1/2 full and the No. 1 tank FWD pump switch is selected to ON
Both Center Tank Fuel Pump Switches are turned OFF
When either engine is operating
explanation: The centre tank scavenge jet pump operates when the No 1 main tank is about 1/2 full, transferring remaining centre tank fuel into tank 1. · FCOM 12.20.x

question: With all fuel tanks full and all electrically driven fuel pumps switched on, which tank feeds which engine?
options: Number 1 engine fed by the right tank, Number 2 engine fed by the left tank
Both engines will be fed by the centre tank
Number 1 engine fed by the left tank, Number 2 engine fed by the right tank
Fuel is fed depending on the fuel pressure from the tanks
explanation: Both engines are normally pressure fed from the center tank until it is near zero (center pumps produce higher pressure), then each engine from its own main tank. · FCOM 12.20.1

question: Hydraulic System A powers which hydraulic system components?
options: Alternate nose wheel steering, Alternate brakes and ground spoilers
Alternate nose wheel steering, Alternate brakes and ground spoilers
None of the other answers are correct
Ground spoilers, trailing edge flaps and the power transfer unit (PTU)
explanation: System A powers: ailerons, rudder, elevator & feel, flight spoilers 2,4,9,11, ground spoilers, alternate brakes, No.1 thrust reverser, autopilot A, normal nose wheel steering, landing gear and the PTU. TE flaps, the landing gear transfer valve and alternate NWS are System B. · FCOM 13.20.2

question: Hydraulic System A powers which hydraulic system components?
options: Alternate nose wheel steering, Alternate brakes and ground spoilers
Ground spoilers, trailing edge flaps and the power transfer unit (PTU)
None of the other answers are correct
Ground spoilers, normal nose wheel steering and the Landing Gear Transfer Unit
explanation: System A powers: ailerons, rudder, elevator & feel, flight spoilers 2,4,9,11, ground spoilers, alternate brakes, No.1 thrust reverser, autopilot A, normal nose wheel steering, landing gear and the PTU. TE flaps, the landing gear transfer valve and alternate NWS are System B. · FCOM 13.20.2

question: Which conditions must exist when airborne for the landing gear transfer unit to operate?
options: Landing gear lever is positioned up, any landing gear is not up and locked
No. 1 engine driven pump (EDP) pressure below limits, landing gear lever is positioned down, any main landing gear is not down and locked
No. 2 engine driven pump (EDP) fails, landing gear lever is positioned up, either main landing gear is not up and locked
No. 1 engine RPM drops below a limit value, landing gear lever is positioned up, either main landing gear is not up and locked
explanation: Landing gear transfer valve conditions: airborne, No.1 engine RPM drops below a limit value, LANDING GEAR lever UP, and either main gear not up and locked. System B EDP then supplies the volume to raise the gear. · FCOM 13.20.4 / 14.20.2

question: When is the 'RF' Indication displayed to the right of hydraulic system quantity?
options: Only during MASTER CAUTION system recall
When hydraulic quantity is below 76% in either system A or B on the ground with engines shut down
When hydraulic quantity is less than 72% in either system A or B at any time
When hydraulic quantity is below 76% in either system A or B in flight or on the ground
explanation: RF (white) = hydraulic quantity below 76%. Valid only on the ground with both engines shut down, or after landing with flaps up during taxi-in. · FCOM 13.10.2

question: When will hydraulic pressure from System B be used to retract the landing gear?
options: Number 1 engine RPM drops below limit value, with either main landing gear still down and the landing gear lever is positioned Up
When the ALTERNATE NOSE WHEEL Switch is positioned ON
When System A pressure is zero and the landing lever is positioned UP
After a failure of the number 1 engine hydraulic pump with the landing gear still down and the landing gear lever is positioned UP
explanation: System B EDP raises the gear through the landing gear transfer valve when airborne, No.1 engine RPM below a limit, gear lever UP and either main gear not up and locked. It is triggered by engine 1 RPM, not by a pump failure. · FCOM 13.20.4

question: What is the purpose of the Landing Gear Transfer Unit?
options: Ensures System A can operate leading edge flaps and slats when System B is lost
Ensures that the landing gear can be raised at the normal rate if the output from System A is insufficient
Ensures System A can raise the gear on loss of System B
Is used to lower the gear on loss of System A
explanation: The transfer valve supplies volume to raise the gear at the normal rate when system A EDP volume is lost. It operates when airborne, No.1 engine RPM drops below a limit, gear lever UP and either main gear not up and locked. · FCOM 13.20.4

question: What effect will a leak in system B downstream of the EDP have on the Power Transfer Unit (PTU)?
options: It will cease to function as it requires fluid from system B to operate.
A leak in system B has no effect as the PTU only uses fluid from system A to operate.
It will continue to function if required, due the feed to the PTU being below the level of the EDP standpipe level.
It will function as normal as it is part of the standby system and powered by system A fluid pressure.
explanation: System B reservoir has one standpipe feeding both pumps. With fluid at the top of the standpipe, the fluid left in the system B reservoir is sufficient for PTU operation. · FCOM 13.20.3

question: A leak in standby hydraulic system will cause system B fluid indication decrease to approximately
options: Has no effect on system B quantity
Zero
explanation: Standby system leak: standby reservoir goes to zero (LOW QUANTITY light at about half empty). System B keeps operating normally, but its quantity indication decreases and stabilizes at approximately 70% full (closest option: 72%). · FCOM 13.20.7

question: An engine-driven hydraulic pump supplies approximately ___ times the fluid volume of an electric motor-driven hydraulic pump?
explanation: FCOM: an engine-driven hydraulic pump supplies approximately 6 times the fluid volume of the related electric motor-driven pump. (One bank version shows 4 — that is wrong.) · FCOM 13.20.2

question: Positioning an engine-driven hydraulic pump switch to OFF
options: Isolates the fluid flow from the system components and deactivates the related pump
Closes the related hydraulic shut off valve and deactivates the related engine-driven pump
Opens the related hydraulic shut off valve but the pump keeps rotating as long as the engine is running
Isolates the hydraulic fluid flow from the system components, but the pump keeps rotating as long as the engine is running
explanation: Positioning the ENG pump switch to OFF isolates fluid flow from the system components. However, the engine-driven pump continues to rotate as long as the engine is operating. · FCOM 13.20.2

question: What is the effect on the Standby Hydraulic System, if there is a leak in system B?
options: No effect as the standby system is supplied from system A
The standby system will decrease but only a limited amount due to the standpipe in system B reservoir
A leak in system B does not affect the operation of the standby hydraulic system
The level in the standby system will also decrease as it is linked to system B
explanation: FCOM: a leak in system B does not affect the operation of the standby hydraulic system. (The 'own accumulator' wording is loose — the standby system has its own reservoir, connected to B only for pressurization/servicing — but 'no effect' is the point.) · FCOM 13.20.3

question: Which of these pressures can be indicated by the Hydraulic Brake Pressure Indicator?
options: Normal precharge of 2800 psi
Maximum pressure of 3500 psi
Normal precharge of 1200 psi
Maximum pressure of 2800 psi
explanation: Poorly written bank question. 3500 psi (white) is the maximum HYDRAULIC SYSTEM pressure on the lower DU. The HYD BRAKE PRESS indicator itself shows: precharge 1000 psi, normal 2900–3600 psi, maximum 3600–4000 psi. · FCOM 14.10.7 / 13.10.2

question: Which of the following statements is true, when the landing gear Manual Extension Access Door is open?
options: The landing gear can be manually lowered, but the landing gear lever must be in the DOWN position
The landing gear can be retracted.
Landing gear extension is not possible if Hydraulic system A is not available.
The landing gear can be manually lowered with the landing gear lever in ANY position.
explanation: With the manual extension access door open: manual gear extension is possible with the LANDING GEAR lever in any position; normal extension is still possible if system A pressure is available; landing gear retraction is disabled. So all three are true. · FCOM 14.10.3 / 14.20.2

question: Which statement is true when the landing gear Manual Extension Access Door is open?
options: Landing gear retraction is enabled
Normal gear extension is possible if hydraulic system B pressure is available
Manual landing gear extension is possible with landing gear lever in any position
Normal landing gear extension is possible with the loss of hydraulic system A
explanation: With the manual extension access door open: manual gear extension is possible with the LANDING GEAR lever in any position; normal extension is still possible if system A pressure is available; landing gear retraction is disabled. So all three are true. · FCOM 14.10.3 / 14.20.2

question: Other than moving the Autobrake selector to OFF, how else can Autobraking be cancelled?
options: Advancing forward thrust levers within one second after touchdown.
All of the other answers are correct
Full rudder deflection.
Moving Speed Brake lever to the DOWN detent or applying manual brakes.
explanation: After braking starts, autobrake disarms (DISARM light on) by: SPEED BRAKE lever to DOWN detent, advancing forward thrust lever(s) — EXCEPT during the first 3 seconds after touchdown — or applying manual brakes. 'Advancing immediately after touchdown' does not disarm it. · FCOM 14.20.5

question: Which of the following statements are true for the Nose Wheel Steering system:
options: As soon as the nose gear is in the down position, nose wheel steering becomes active.
Nose wheel steering is normally powered by hydraulic system A.
All of the other answers are true.
If alternate nose wheel steering is activated, then the standby hydraulic system operates the nose wheel steering.
explanation: Nose wheel steering is normally system A and is available only when the nose gear is down AND compressed by the weight of the airplane. Alternate steering is system B, not standby. · FCOM 14.20.3

question: Which of the following statements are true for the Nose Wheel Steering system?
options: Nose wheel steering is normally powered by hydraulic system A and as well as being in the down position, the nose landing gear must be compressed for nose wheel steering to be available

If alternate nose wheel steering is activated then the standby hydraulic system operates the nose wheel steering and as well as being in the down position, the nose landing gear must be compressed for nose wheel steering
If alternate nose wheel steering is activated then the standby hydraulic system operates the nose wheel steering
Nose wheel steering is normally powered by hydraulic system A, If alternate nose wheel steering is activated then the standby hydraulic system operates the nose wheel steering
explanation: Nose wheel steering is normally system A and is available only when the nose gear is down AND compressed by the weight of the airplane. Alternate steering is system B, not standby. · FCOM 14.20.3

question: How far must you pull the handle before the related landing gear uplock is released?
options: Approximately 6cm.
Approximately 1cm
Released as soon as handle pulled.
Approximately 61cm
You select the AUTO BRAKE to RTO on the ground, and the AUTO BRAKE DISARM light illuminates for 2 seconds then extinguishes.
explanation: Each gear uplock is released when its manual gear extension handle is pulled to its limit, approximately 24 inches (61 cm). · FCOM 14.10.3

question: If you see that the Nose Gear green light above the landing gear lever is not illuminated, but the corresponding light on the aft overhead panel is illuminated, is the nose gear down and locked? Select one:
options: Not possible to tell. You will need to look through the inspection window in the floor
No. Both lights must be illuminated for the gear to be considered down and locked
Yes
No. You will have to request from tower to confirm the position on the nose landing gear
explanation: Yes. FCOM: landing gear is down and locked as long as one green light (centre panel or overhead panel) for each gear is illuminated. · FCOM 14.10.2 / 14.10.3

question: Altitude alerting occurs when approaching or departing from the MCP selected altitude. When is the altitude alerting system inhibited?
options: Landing gear is down and locked
Flaps not up and the landing gear is extended
Flaps not up
Glide slope is captured, or trailing edge flaps are extended to 25 or greater
explanation: Altitude alerting is inhibited when trailing edge flaps are extended to 25 or greater, or while G/S is captured. · FCOM 15.20.9

question: TA ONLY mode is enabled automatically
options: Below 1,000ft RA when TA/RA mode is selected.
None of the answers are correct.
Below approximately 1,100 feet radio altitude.
Below 2,000ft RA when TA/RA mode is selected.
explanation: Below 1,000 ft RA with TA/RA selected, TA ONLY mode is enabled automatically and TA ONLY is shown on the ND. · FCOM 15.20.32

question: What is the TCAS symbol for proximate traffic?
options: A white solid diamond
A white hollow diamond
An amber circle
A red square
explanation: Proximate traffic (within 6 nm and 1,200 ft, no TA/RA expected) = solid white diamond. Other traffic = hollow white diamond; TA = amber circle; RA = red square. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: The TCAS system generates a Traffic Advisory, whenever another aircraft is what distance from point of closest approach?
options: 25 seconds.
<6 nm separation with < 1200 feet vertical separation.
>6 nm separation with >1200 feet vertical separation.
40 seconds.
Symbol; Amber circle
explanation: TA when the other airplane is about 40 seconds from the point of closest approach; RA at about 25 seconds. · FCOM 15.20.31

question: What does an amber ALT DISAGREE in the bottom of the altimeter tape indicate?
options: The captains and first officer's altitude indications differ more than 50 feet for more than 5 seconds
The captains altitude reading and the standby altimeter disagree by more than 200ft for more than 5 seconds
The captain's and first officer's altitude indications differ more than 200 feet for more than 5 seconds
There is a difference of more than 10 HPa between the selected QNH's
explanation: ALT DISAGREE (amber): Captain's and F/O's altitudes disagree by more than 200 ft for more than 5 continuous seconds. · FCOM 10.11.34

question: What does an amber ROLL displayed in the lower portion of the attitude indicator on the PFD mean?
options: No flight director or autopilot roll mode engaged
The Captain's and F/O's attitude displays differ by more than 5 degrees in roll
The airplane has exceeded 46 degrees of bank
The airplane is experiencing an uncommanded roll
explanation: Amber ROLL (or PITCH) comparator: Captain's and F/O's roll (pitch) displays differ by more than 5°. Flashes for 10 s then steady. · FCOM 10.11.28

question: Which radio is used on the ground, for primary ATC communication?
options: Always use the VHF-1 radio
Monitor the VHF radio connected to the lower antenna
Always use the VHF-2 radio
Use the VHF-1 radio for outbound and the VHF-2 radio for inbound flights
explanation: Non-AFM operational information: use the VHF radio connected to the top-of-fuselage antenna for primary ATC communications on the ground — VHF 1. · FCOM L.10.6

question: The First Officer observes the word PITCH displayed in amber in the lower portion of the PFD during an ILS approach. What does this mean?
options: The Captain's and First Officer's pitch angle displays differ by more than 5 degrees
Glide slope information is not being followed
The First Officer's pitch angle display has failed
The autopilot has defaulted to CWS pitch
explanation: Amber PITCH: Captain's and F/O's pitch angle displays differ by more than 5°. · FCOM 10.11.28

question: The PSEU light will illuminate along with a Master Caution and an OVERHEAD annunciator light, under which of the following situations?
options: Illuminates 30 seconds after the ground/air system senses ground mode, if an emergency exit flight lock has failed locked or a fault is detected
Illuminates as soon as the ground/air system senses ground mode, if a fault is detected
Illuminates 60 seconds after the ground/air system senses air mode, if an emergency exit flight lock has failed locked or a fault is detected
Illuminates whenever ground/air system senses air mode, and an emergency exit flight lock has failed in the locked position
explanation: In flight the PSEU light is inhibited from thrust lever advance for takeoff until 30 seconds after landing. So a failed-locked flight lock or a detected fault shows 30 s after the air/ground system senses ground mode. · FCOM 15.10.2 / 1.40.51

question: When will the Takeoff Configuration Warning horn sound?
options: TE flaps set to position 5
If the parking brake is not set
If stabilizer trim is not in the green band when throttles advanced for takeoff
TOGA not pressed
explanation: Takeoff config warning: flaps not in the 1–25 takeoff range (or skew/asymmetry), LE devices not configured, speed brake lever not DOWN, spoilers not down, parking brake SET, or stabilizer trim not in the takeoff range (green band). · FCOM 15.20.6

question: During an ILS approach below 1,000 feet Radio Altitude, a BELOW G/S alert occurs. To cancel the alert
options: The alert cannot be cancelled
Reset the Master Caution
Press either pilots BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT Light, or correct the flight path back to the glide slope
Select another mode on MCP
explanation: Push either pilot's BELOW G/S P-INHIBIT light (below 1,000 ft RA) or correct back towards the glideslope. Repetition rate increases as deviation increases. · FCOM 15.20.14 / 15.10.7

question: Before takeoff thrust is set, what does the PM call when the thrust levers have been advanced to about 40% N1 and the engines are stable?
options: "STABILIZED"
"THRUST SET"
"ENGINES NORMAL"
"N1 CHECKED"
explanation: Takeoff: thrust levers to about 40% N1, observe engines stabilized and normal; PM calls "STABILIZED", then the PF pushes TO/GA and calls "SET TAKEOFF THRUST". · FCOM NP.40.2 / NP.21.68

question: After TO/GA is pushed on the takeoff roll, what does the PF call?
options: "SET TAKEOFF THRUST"
"TAKEOFF THRUST SET"
"STABILIZED"
"GO"
explanation: PF: "SET TAKEOFF THRUST". PM then calls "TAKEOFF THRUST SET" and "INDICATIONS NORMAL". · FCOM NP.40.2

question: What is the PM callout at 80 knots on the takeoff roll, and the PF response?
options: PM "80 KNOTS" – PF "CHECK"
PM "80 KNOTS" – PF "80 KNOTS"
PF "80 KNOTS" – PM "CHECK"
No callout at 80 knots
explanation: 80 kt: PM "80 KNOTS", PF "CHECK" (Note 1: incapacitation check / instrument crosscheck). · FCOM NP.40.2

question: At positive climb after takeoff, which calls are made?
options: PM "POSITIVE RATE" – PF "GEAR UP"
PF "POSITIVE RATE, GEAR UP"
PM "GEAR UP" – PF "CHECK"
PM "V2" – PF "GEAR UP"
explanation: Positive climb: PM "POSITIVE RATE", PF "GEAR UP". · FCOM NP.40.2

question: At what height after takeoff is the roll mode (LNAV or HDG SEL) called?
options: 400 ft radio altitude
1000 ft AAL
50 ft RA
1500 ft AAL
explanation: 400 ft radio: "LNAV" or "HDG SEL". · FCOM NP.40.2

question: At 1000 ft AAL after takeoff, what does the PF call?
options: "COMMAND A OR B"
"BUG UP"
"CLIMB THRUST"
"AFTER TAKEOFF CHECKLIST"
explanation: At 1000 ft AAL select CMD A or B and call "COMMAND A or B"; PM "CHECKED". · FCOM NP.40.2 / NP.21.71

question: When is "BUG UP" called with NADP 1?
options: 3000 ft AAL
1000 ft AAL
1500 ft AAL
400 ft RA
explanation: BUG UP: 1000 ft AAL (NADP 2) or 3000 ft AAL (NADP 1). · FCOM NP.40.2

question: During NADP 1, what minimum speed is maintained during the initial climb?
options: V2 + 15 kt (up to V2 + 25 at light weight)
V2
V2 + 10 kt
V2 + 20 kt minimum
explanation: NADP 1: maintain a minimum of V2 + 15 kt; at light weight up to V2 + 25 to match F/D pitch. Do not exceed 20° nose up. · FCOM NP.21.71

question: What is the maximum pitch attitude during the initial climb (NADP 1)?
options: 20° nose up
15° nose up
25° nose up
30° nose up
explanation: Do not exceed 20 degrees nose up. · FCOM NP.21.71

question: At 1500 ft AAL after takeoff, what should be verified?
options: FMA shows N1 and automatic thrust reduction to climb thrust
Flaps up
Gear up and off
Altimeters set to STD
explanation: At 1500 ft AAL verify FMA displays N1 and automatic thrust reduction to climb thrust. · FCOM NP.21.71

question: After flaps up, what are the calls?
options: PM "FLAPS UP – NO LIGHTS" – PF "AFTER TAKEOFF CHECKLIST"
PF "FLAPS UP" – PM "CHECK"
PM "CLEAN" – PF "CHECKLIST"
PM "FLAPS UP" – PF "VNAV"
explanation: Flaps up: PM "FLAPS UP – NO LIGHTS", PF "AFTER TAKEOFF CHECKLIST"; then "VNAV". · FCOM NP.40.3

question: What is the callout 1,000 ft before the cleared altitude?
options: PM "ONE TO GO" – PF "CHECK"
PF "1000 TO GO" – PM "CHECK"
PM "ALTITUDE" – PF "CHECK"
No callout
explanation: 1,000 ft to cleared altitude: PM "ONE TO GO", PF "CHECK". · FCOM NP.40.3

question: Passing FL100 in climb, what does the PF call?
options: "PASSING FL___ CLIMBING ___, TEN CHECKS"
"TEN THOUSAND"
"LIGHTS OFF"
"ALTIMETERS"
explanation: FL100: PM "ALTIMETERS", PF "PASSING FL___ CLIMBING ___, TEN CHECKS" (altimeter crosscheck). · FCOM NP.40.3

question: When cleared to the final cruising level, what is the PF call?
options: "FL___ SET, THREE TIMES" (CRZ page, MCP and FLT ALT)
"CRUISE SET"
"LEVEL SET"
"FL___ CHECKED"
explanation: Final cruising level: PF "FL ___ SET, THREE TIMES" checking CRZ page, MCP and FLT ALT; PM "CHECK". · FCOM NP.40.3

question: When is the SEAT BELT SIGN ON call made in descent?
options: FL150 or 15 minutes to landing
FL100
Top of descent
Transition level
explanation: FL150 / 15 minutes to landing: PM "SEAT BELT SIGN ON". · FCOM NP.40.3

question: How is unnecessary conversation restricted on the flight deck?
options: Prohibited from engine start to top of climb and from top of descent to engine shutdown
Only below 10,000 ft
Only during takeoff and landing
Only below FL100 in descent
explanation: Unnecessary conversation is prohibited from engine start to Top of Climb, and from Top of Descent to engine shutdown. · FCOM NP.40.1

question: If the PM does not make a required callout, what should happen?
options: The PF should make it
Nothing; it is optional
The Captain must take control
Go around immediately
explanation: If the PM does not make the required callout, the PF should make it. A missing callout may indicate a system malfunction or incapacitation. · FCOM NP.40.1

question: What does the EGPWS "2500" callout on approach require?
options: PF "TERRAIN NOTED"
PM "CHECK"
No response
PF "RADIO ALIVE"
explanation: EGPWS "2500": PF "TERRAIN NOTED" (also in climb/cruise, confirming TERRAIN on the F/O ND). · FCOM NP.40.4 / NP.21.71

question: At what distance are gear down and flaps 15 normally selected on approach (IMC)?
options: 5 NM (4 NM in VMC)
3 NM
6 NM
10 NM
explanation: All approaches: LG down and Flap 15 at 5 NM (IMC) / 4 NM (VMC); V/S NPAs at 5 NM (IMC/VMC). · FCOM NP.21.102 / NP.40.4

question: By what height must the aircraft be stable in landing configuration in IMC?
options: 1000 ft AAL
500 ft AAL
1500 ft AAL
300 ft AAL
explanation: Stable at 1000 ft AAL (white bar) in IMC and 500 ft AAL (amber bar) in VMC. · FCOM NP.21.102

question: For the "500 CONTINUE" call, what speed range is required?
options: VREF+5 to VREF+15 (min VREF, max VREF+20)
VREF to VREF+5
VREF+10 to VREF+30
VREF+20 exactly
explanation: Target approach speed VREF+5 to VREF+15 knots (minimum VREF, maximum VREF+20). · FCOM NP.21.102

question: For the "500 CONTINUE" call on an ILS, what deviation is acceptable?
options: ±1 dot G/S and ±1 dot LOC
±2 dots G/S
±½ dot LOC only
Any, if visual
explanation: On glidepath ±1 dot (or 3 reds/3 whites) and on localizer ±1 dot. · FCOM NP.21.102

question: What is the maximum vertical speed for a stabilized approach at 500 ft (unless briefed)?
options: 1000 fpm
800 fpm
1500 fpm
700 fpm
explanation: Vertical speed proportional to the approach, but not more than 1000 fpm unless briefed. · FCOM NP.21.102

question: If any stabilized approach criterion cannot be confirmed at 500 ft, what is called?
options: "500 GO-AROUND"
"500 CONTINUE"
"MINIMUMS"
"UNSTABLE"
explanation: If any parameter cannot be confirmed, the call shall be "500 GO-AROUND". · FCOM NP.21.102

question: By what height must lateral maneuvering be completed on circling or side-step approaches?
options: 300 ft AAL
500 ft AAL
200 ft AAL
1000 ft AAL
explanation: Lateral maneuvering to align with the extended centreline must be completed by 300 ft AAL (exceptions in OMC AFB). · FCOM NP.21.102

question: What is the landing checklist status required for the 500 CONTINUE call?
options: Completed (except landing lights)
Not required
Completed including landing lights
Only gear checked
explanation: Landing checklist completed (except landing lights). · FCOM NP.21.102

question: Where is the missed approach altitude normally set on a non-precision approach?
options: At 1000 ft AAL; if MDA/DA ≥ 900 ft AAL, set when 300 ft above MDA/DA
Immediately at the FAF
At MDA
At 500 ft AAL
explanation: Set the MAA at 1000 ft AAL. If MDA/DA ≥ 900 ft AAL, set when 300 ft above MDA/DA to avoid inadvertent ALT ACQ. · FCOM NP.21.122

question: At minimums ("MINIMUMS"), when must the go-around be initiated if no visual reference?
options: By DA, without delay
At the MAP only
After searching for visual cues
At 100 ft below DA
explanation: The go-around must be initiated by DA; at the minimums call the PF goes around without delay — no need to search for visual cues; the PM calls visual cues. · FCOM NP.21.116

question: On the go-around at 400 ft radio, what is called?
options: "LNAV or HDG SEL, SPEED CHECKS, FLAPS 5"
"GEAR UP"
"COMMAND A"
"FLAPS UP"
explanation: Go-around 400 ft: PM "LNAV or HDG SEL, SPEED CHECKS, FLAPS 5"; PF repeats; "TUNE RADIOS FOR MISSED APPROACH". · FCOM NP.40.5

question: What does the RYR acronym RIBETS stand for?
options: Route check, Instrument crosscheck, takeoff Briefing, Emergency briefing, Taxi routing, SID briefing
Radios, Instruments, Brakes, Engines, Trim, Speeds
Runway, Instruments, Briefing, Engines, Taxi, Speeds
Route, ILS, Brakes, Emergency, Takeoff, Securing
explanation: RIBETS: Route Check, Instrument Crosscheck, Takeoff Briefing, Initial Emergency Briefing (when appropriate), Taxi Routing and SID Briefing. · FCOM NP.21.35

question: If the SID changes during taxi, what must the crew do?
options: Stop the aircraft; not continue or accept line-up/takeoff until re-briefed and FMC entries re-confirmed
Brief it while taxiing
Ask ATC for the old SID
Brief it after takeoff
explanation: Crews must stop the aircraft and NOT recommence taxi or accept line-up/takeoff clearance until re-briefing and re-confirming SID FMC entries (performance, NAVAIDs, MCP); re-do RIBETS. · FCOM NP.21.56

question: What is the maximum taxi ground speed on a taxiway (unless published otherwise)?
options: 30 kt
20 kt
15 kt
50 kt
explanation: Max ground speeds: contaminated 5 kt, turns 10 kt, aprons 15 kt, taxiway 30 kt, backtrack on runway 50 kt. · FCOM NP.21.57

question: What is the maximum taxi speed in turns?
options: 10 kt
5 kt
15 kt
20 kt
explanation: Turns – 10 kt (contaminated 5, aprons 15, taxiway 30, backtrack 50). · FCOM NP.21.57

question: What is the maximum taxi speed on aprons?
options: 15 kt
10 kt
20 kt
30 kt
explanation: Aprons – 15 kt. · FCOM NP.21.57

question: What must be completed before crossing or entering any runway during taxi?
options: The "Two Phase Call"
The before takeoff checklist
A PA to the cabin
Strobes ON only
explanation: Complete the "Two Phase Call" prior to crossing or entering any active or non-active runway. · FCOM NP.21.56

question: Taxi light and marshaller: when should the taxi light be turned on when being marshalled off stand?
options: After the nose wheels are deflected away from the marshaller
Before pushback
Immediately at engine start
Never during taxi
explanation: Delay turning on the taxi light if being marshalled off stand until the nose wheels are deflected away from the marshaller. · FCOM NP.21.55
