question: Assumed temperature reduction is NOT allowed when the crosswind exceeds:
options: 10 kt
15 kt
20 kt
25 kt
explanation: If the crosswind exceeds 10 kt, no assumed temperature reduction is allowed (full rated or required derate). · FCOM NP.21.33 / NP.21.66

question: Who flies a flaps 1 departure?
options: The Captain (performance reasons only)
Either pilot
The F/O only
The pilot with most experience on type
explanation: Flaps 1 departures are only authorized for performance purposes and shall be flown by the Captain. · FCOM NP.21.66

question: During the takeoff roll, what control column input is applied until 80 knots?
options: Slight forward pressure, relaxed to neutral above 80 kt
Full back pressure
Neutral throughout
Full forward until V1
explanation: Slight forward pressure until 80 kt, then relax towards neutral; smooth continuous rotation at VR. · FCOM NP.21.65

question: During single-engine taxi in, what thrust limit should be respected?
options: Avoid more than 40% N1
Avoid more than 30% N1
No limit
Avoid more than 60% N1
explanation: Engine-out taxi: avoid thrust levels in excess of 40% N1; acceleration takes about twice as long. · FCOM NP.21.142 / NP.21.143

question: What is the maximum actual gross weight for engine-out taxi after landing?
explanation: EOT after landing conditions include actual gross weight ≤ 63,000 kg, no LVP, no freezing conditions, no contamination. · FCOM NP.21.142

question: Engine-out taxi after landing is NOT permitted when:
options: Low visibility procedures are in force
The APU is running
It is daytime
The aircraft is below 63,000 kg
explanation: EOT not permitted with LVP, freezing conditions, contamination, GW above 63,000 kg or conflicting NNC. · FCOM NP.21.142

question: On rollout after an autoland, what must the F/O do?
options: Stay on instruments until reaching taxi speed
Look outside to assist
Disarm the autobrake
Stow the reversers
explanation: The F/O remains on instruments until taxi speed. · FCOM NP.40.7 / NP.21.114

question: At 500 ft RA in an autoland, what does the F/O call?
options: "PASSING ___ RADIO, FLARE ARMED"
"STABLE"
"LAND 3"
explanation: Autoland 500 ft RA: F/O "PASSING ___ RADIO, FLARE ARMED"; Captain responds "500 RADIO FLARE ARMED". · FCOM NP.40.6

question: What does the PM call after the reversers deploy on landing?
options: "REVERSERS NORMAL" (or "NO REVERSER ENGINE 1/2")
"REVERSE GREEN"
"DECEL"
Nothing
explanation: Landing roll: "SPEEDBRAKES UP/NOT UP", "REVERSERS NORMAL" or "NO REVERSER ENGINE 1/2" or "NO REVERSERS", ___%, 100, 80, 60 (IAS), "AUTOBRAKE DISARM". · FCOM NP.40.5

question: Visual approach: where should the aircraft be established with gear down and flaps 15?
options: At a point not less than 4 NM from the runway
At 2 NM
At 1000 ft AAL
At the FAF only
explanation: The PF identifies a point not less than 4 NM from the runway and plans to be established at or before it with gear down and flaps 15. · FCOM NP.21.106

question: If there is any doubt about terrain clearance on a visual approach, the crew must:
options: Refuse the visual approach
Continue using the EGPWS
Descend to MSA then continue
Ask ATC for vectors and continue visually
explanation: If any doubt about terrain clearance exists, the visual approach must be refused. · FCOM NP.21.107

question: After an EGPWS "2500" callout in climb or cruise, what is required?
options: PF "TERRAIN NOTED" and confirm TERRAIN on the F/O's ND
Ignore it in climb
Immediate climb
Select both NDs to WXR
explanation: PF calls "TERRAIN NOTED", confirms TERRAIN on the F/O's ND, and checks routing vs terrain; if in doubt turn away from high ground. · FCOM NP.21.71

question: Before using the APU as a bleed air source, how long should it run?
options: Two full minutes
30 seconds
One minute
Five minutes
explanation: Run the APU for two full minutes before using it as a bleed air source. · FCOM NP.21.6

question: Why does the F/O select the transponder to ALT OFF before requesting push and start?
options: To show the aircraft position to ATC
To test TCAS
Because TA/RA is not allowed on stand
To save power
explanation: F/O selects the transponder to 'ALT OFF' to indicate aircraft position to ATC prior to requesting push and start clearance. · FCOM NP.21.45

question: When is the transponder set to TA/RA?
options: Before takeoff (with LNAV/HDG SEL armed and TERR on the F/O's ND)
At engine start
On pushback
Passing 1000 ft
explanation: Before takeoff items: A/T ARM, arm LNAV or HDG SEL, confirm TERR on the F/O's ND, transponder to TA/RA. · FCOM NP.21.64

question: How does the Captain ensure the weather radar is ON for takeoff?
options: Includes it in the scan when responding to the "MCP" item of the BEFORE TAKEOFF checklist
It switches on automatically
The F/O checks it at 1000 ft
It is not used for takeoff
explanation: The Captain includes the weather radar in the scan when responding to the "MCP" check on the BEFORE TAKEOFF CHECKLIST BELOW THE LINE. · FCOM NP.21.64

question: What is the recommended engine cool-down before shutdown?
options: At least 3 minutes at taxi thrust
1 minute
No cool-down needed
5 minutes at idle reverse
explanation: Run the engines at least 3 minutes at a taxi thrust setting; routine cool-down of less than 3 minutes is not recommended. · FCOM NP.21.142 / NP.21.144

question: After placing the start levers to CUTOFF at shutdown, what must both pilots verify?
options: A reduction in N2
EGT increase
Oil pressure increase
Fuel flow increase
explanation: After placing the start lever(s) to cutoff, both pilots must verify a reduction in N2. · FCOM NP.21.144

question: Who reads the BEFORE START checklist BELOW THE LINE and who actions the items?
options: PF actions the items and calls for it; PM completes the checklist
PM actions and PF reads
Captain alone
Nobody, it is a flow only
explanation: Once clearance is received, the PF actions the below the line items and calls "BEFORE START CHECKLIST BELOW THE LINE"; the PM completes it. · FCOM NP.21.45

question: Who actions the BEFORE TAKEOFF checklist BELOW THE LINE items?
options: The F/O actions the items before reading the checklist aloud
The Captain
The PF
Cabin crew
explanation: The F/O actions the BELOW THE LINE checklist items before reading the checklist aloud. · FCOM NP.21.64

question: Who calls "CLEAR LEFT" and "CLEAR RIGHT" before taxi?
options: Captain "CLEAR LEFT", F/O "CLEAR RIGHT"
Both call "CLEAR"
F/O both sides
Ground crew
explanation: The F/O confirms right side clear ("CLEAR RIGHT"); the Captain confirms left side clear ("CLEAR LEFT") and selects taxi and turnoff lights on. · FCOM NP.21.55

question: Where does the F/O record taxi instructions?
options: In the FMC CDU scratchpad
On the PLOG only
On paper
Not recorded
explanation: The first officer types all taxi instructions in the scratchpad on the FMC CDU and displays the taxi chart on the EFB. · FCOM NP.21.55

question: What does the RYR 'Progressive Taxi' SOP mean?
options: The PM (right seat) adopts active monitoring during taxi
Taxi speed increases progressively
ATC gives progressive clearances only
Captain taxis with one engine
explanation: Progressive Taxi: the Pilot Monitoring (right hand seat) should adopt an 'active pilot monitoring' approach to the taxi phase. · FCOM NP.21.55

question: When should checklists NOT be performed during taxi?
options: Approaching or during turns
On straight taxiways
When stopped
At the holding point
explanation: Conduct checklists when safety and TEM permit; avoid challenge/response items approaching or during turns. · FCOM NP.21.56

question: Transponder code change at RYR (on the ground) — who does what?
options: PM enters in scratchpad, PF crosschecks, PM sets transponder, PF verifies
PF sets it alone
PM sets it without crosscheck
ATC sets it
explanation: Transponder codes: PM enters into CDU scratchpad, PF crosschecks, PM enters into transponder, PF verifies. · FCOM NP.21.56

question: What is the maximum taxi speed when backtracking on the runway?
options: 50 kt
30 kt
40 kt
60 kt
explanation: Backtracking on runway – 50 kt. · FCOM NP.21.57

question: What is the maximum taxi speed on contaminated or slippery surfaces?
options: 5 kt
10 kt
15 kt
3 kt
explanation: Contaminated and slippery taxiways or runways – 5 kt. · FCOM NP.21.57

question: Prior to spool-up on the runway (RAAS fitted), what is called?
options: RAAS "On Runway ___" then PF "TIMING"
"LINED UP"
"CLEARED FOR TAKEOFF"
"BRAKES RELEASED"
explanation: Prior to spool-up: RAAS "On runway ___" (or without RAAS "XXX/XXX" track/runway heading) and "TIMING", start CHR and ET. · FCOM NP.40.2 / NP.21.68

question: During the takeoff roll, what must the Captain's hand do?
options: Guard the thrust levers
Hold the tiller until V1
Rest on the parking brake
Hold the speedbrake lever
explanation: The Captain's hand must be guarding the thrust levers (until V1). · FCOM NP.21.68

question: Descending through transition level, what does the PF call?
options: "SET QNH ___, PASSING ___, DESCENDING ___ FT, ___ FLAGS, STANDBY ALTIMETER SET"
"QNH SET"
"ALTIMETERS"
"TRANSITION"
explanation: Transition level / cleared to altitude: PM "CHECK", PF "SET QNH ___, PASSING ___, DESCENDING ___FT, ___FLAGS, STANDBY ALTIMETER SET". · FCOM NP.40.3

question: When is the VOR/LOC armed callout made?
options: When cleared to intercept VOR/LOC: PF "VOR/LOC ARMED"
At glideslope alive
At 10 NM always
After capture
explanation: When cleared to intercept: PM "CHECK", PF "VOR/LOC ARMED". · FCOM NP.40.4

question: At localizer capture, what does the PF call?
options: "CHECK, RUNWAY HEADING ___ SET" (or "SET RUNWAY HEADING ___")
"LOC ALIVE"
"CAPTURED"
Nothing
explanation: VOR/LOC capture: PM "VOR or LOC CAPTURE", PF "CHECK, RUNWAY HEADING ___ SET" or "SET RUNWAY HEADING ___". · FCOM NP.40.4

question: At glideslope capture, what does the PF call?
options: "CHECK, ___ FEET SET" (missed approach altitude)
"GLIDESLOPE"
"FLAPS 30"
"LANDING CHECKLIST"
explanation: G/S capture: PM "GLIDESLOPE CAPTURE", PF "CHECK, ___ FEET SET". · FCOM NP.40.5

question: At 4–5 NM, what does the PF call?
options: "GEAR DOWN, FLAPS 15, LANDING CHECKLIST TO FLAPS"
"FLAPS 30"
"GEAR DOWN" only
"APPROACH CHECKLIST"
explanation: 4/5 NM: PM "SPEED CHECKS, GEAR DOWN, FLAPS 15", PF "GEAR DOWN, FLAPS 15, LANDING CHECKLIST TO FLAPS". · FCOM NP.40.4

question: What does the PM call at the outer marker / FAF?
options: "ALTITUDE CHECKS, ___ FEET, FLAGS/NO FLAGS"
"OUTER MARKER"
"FAF"
explanation: Outer marker: PM "ALTITUDE CHECKS, FLAGS / NO FLAGS"; PF "OUTER MARKER ___ FEET, FLAGS / NO FLAGS". · FCOM NP.40.5

question: At the EGPWS "1000" callout on approach, what is the PF response?
options: "CHECK"
"STABLE"
"CONTINUE"
No response
explanation: EGPWS "1000": PF "CHECK". · FCOM NP.40.5

question: At EGPWS "MINIMUMS" with the runway in sight, what is the PF call?
options: "CONTINUE"
"LAND"
"VISUAL"
"MINIMUMS"
explanation: At MINIMUMS: PM "LIGHTS / RWY IN SIGHT" (or "GO-AROUND"); PF "CONTINUE" or "GO–AROUND, FLAPS__". · FCOM NP.40.5

question: On the go-around at positive climb, what calls are made?
options: PM "POSITIVE RATE" – PF "GEAR UP"
PF "GEAR UP" before positive rate
PM "GO AROUND THRUST SET" only
No calls
explanation: Go-around: PF "GO-AROUND, FLAPS__", "SET GO AROUND THRUST"; PM "FLAPS__", "GO AROUND THRUST SET"; at positive climb PM "POSITIVE RATE", PF "GEAR UP". · FCOM NP.40.5

question: During the landing roll, at which speeds does the PM call?
options: ___%, 100, 80, 60 (IAS) then "AUTOBRAKE DISARM"
100 and 60 only
80 only
Every 10 kt
explanation: Landing roll PM: "SPEEDBRAKES UP/NOT UP", "REVERSERS NORMAL"..., "___%, 100, 80, 60 (IAS)", "AUTOBRAKE DISARM". · FCOM NP.40.5

question: When are the autobrakes normally disarmed on landing rollout?
options: Prior to taxi speed, using manual brakes
At 100 kt
After vacating the runway
Never; they disarm automatically
explanation: Prior to taxi speed, disarm the autobrake using manual brakes and continue manual braking as required. · FCOM NP.21.138

question: When should the reverse thrust levers reach reverse idle on rollout?
options: By taxi speed
At 100 kt
At 60 kt exactly
After vacating the runway
explanation: Reverse thrust levers should be at reverse idle by taxi speed, then full down after the engines decelerate to idle; verify REV extinguished. · FCOM NP.21.138

question: Approaching the VNAV descent point (2 NM before), what does the PM call?
options: "APPROACHING DESCENT"
"TOP OF DESCENT"
"VNAV PATH"
"DESCEND NOW"
explanation: Additional VNAV callouts: 2 NM before descent point PM "APPROACHING DESCENT"; PF "XXX FEET SET". · FCOM NP.40.7

question: On a CPDLC uplink, who reads the message aloud?
options: The PM
The PF
Both silently
ATC by voice
explanation: PM reads the message out loud; PF calls WILCO/UNABLE/STBY; PM presses the response. · FCOM NP.40.11 / NP.40.12

question: When is the "VERTICAL SPEED" call made in the last 1000 ft?
options: Less than 300 fpm or more than 1000 fpm
More than 1500 fpm
Less than 500 fpm
Any change
explanation: "VERTICAL SPEED": less than 300 fpm or greater than 1000 fpm in the last 1000 ft AGL. · FCOM NP.40.14

question: When is the "SPEED" deviation call made?
options: IAS less than Vref or greater than Vfly + 10 kt (or trend to exceed)
IAS greater than Vref + 5
Only below Vref
Only above Vfly + 20
explanation: "SPEED": whenever IAS is less than Vref or greater than Vfly + 10 kt, or the trend shows a significant tendency to exceed them. · FCOM NP.40.13 / NP.40.14

question: What does "verify" mean in RYR procedures?
options: Visually confirm correct operation; no verbal response required
Must call aloud
Must write it down
Ask the other pilot
explanation: "Verify" instructs a crewmember to visually confirm correct operation; it does not require a verbal response. · FCOM NP.40.14

question: If an optional EGPWS voice callout is not heard when expected on approach, who makes it?
options: The PM
The PF
Nobody
ATC
explanation: If the normally expected electronic voice callout is not heard, the PM should make the callout; the PF acknowledges EGPWS callouts. · FCOM NP.40.1
